If the seers are the believers, then the seen are the disbelievers; and if the seers are the disbelievers, then the seen are the believers. Let us consider the matter under both meanings:

If it is the disbelievers who see the believers, then they see them as twice their number, that is, double their number; and the number of disbelievers was close to a thousand. Thus the disbelievers see the believers as double themselves, that is, two thousand. The meaning may also lead to the believers seeing the disbelievers as double their actual number. It may also be said that the meaning leads to the disbelievers seeing the believers as double their number, and the number of believers was close to three hundred and fourteen, and double this number is six hundred and twenty-eight fighters.

If we take the meaning of "mithlayhim" as the number of the believers, then the disbelievers see them as about six hundred and twenty-eight fighters; and if we take the meaning of "mithlayhim" as the number of the disbelievers, then the disbelievers see the believers as about two thousand. And what is the purpose of this? The Truth, glory be to Him, speaks of the confrontation between disbelief and faith, in which Allah grants victory to faith over disbelief. Some of those who hunt for faults in the Qur'an say: how can the Qur'an say ﴿They see them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾ when it says in another place:

﴿When Allah shows them to you in your dream as few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed about the matter, but Allah saved (you). Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts. * And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and He made you appear few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah are returned [all] matters.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 43-44].

This verse establishes multitude, whether the multitude of the believers or the multitude of the disbelievers, while the verse that we are now addressing with faith-inspired reflections establishes fewness. The skeptics about the Qur'an say: how does the Qur'an treat one battle with two different matters? We say to these skeptics: you have little discernment, for there is a difference between courage in advancing into battle and the moral and spiritual spirit that dominates the fighter during the battle. Allah, glory be to Him, has spoken of both states: the Truth made these appear few in the eyes of those, and made those appear few in the eyes of these, because when the believers see the disbelievers as few, they are provisioned with boldness and the energy of faith to achieve victory.

And when the disbelievers see the believers as few, they belittle them and grow slack when confronting them. But when the battle is joined, what happens? They have all entered the battle hoping for the fewness of the opposing numbers, so what happens in their nerves? The believer enters the battle with intense readiness to confront the disbelievers, while the nerves of the disbeliever weaken because the number has become other than what he expected. Thus the Truth says:

﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and He made you appear few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah are returned [all] matters.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 44].

This depicts the state before the battle, because Allah does not want one side to be daunted so that the battle does not arise. But as soon as the battle begins, the Truth reverses matters into their opposite; He transfers a thing from one opposite to its opposite, and the transfer of a thing from one opposite to another is a notice that a higher power directs feelings and sensations, and a high power can produce in feelings whatever it wills.

The Truth first made the numbers appear few so that they would not be daunted by the battle, and at the time of the battle Allah made them appear numerous in each other's eyes, so each group sees the other side as numerous, and the energies of believing courage burst forth from the souls of the believers, so they advance to fight with zeal, while the souls of the disbelievers weaken when they face numbers greater than they expected. And the Truth, glory and exaltation be to Him, says:

﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two hosts that met: one host fighting in the way of Allah, and another, disbelieving; they see them as twice their number with their own eyes. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13]

This verse is a good tiding to every believer of victory, and at the same time a warning to every disbeliever that defeat will befall him if he confronts the believing group. So beware of measuring matters by the standards of causes: the causes required of you are those within human capacity, and you must leave the completion of all of that to destiny. Let not the believing group become weak before a large number, and do not deceive yourselves, O disbelievers, with your great numbers; for the precedent before you confirms that a small number of believers has overcome a large number of disbelievers.

Among the meanings of the verse also: the disbelievers see the believers as twice the number of the disbelievers, that is, double their number. Among its meanings, thirdly, is that the disbelievers see the believers as double the actual number of the believers. Among its meanings, fourthly, is that the Muslims see the disbelievers as twice their number, that is, twice the number of the believers, i.e., six hundred men and a few more, and in that case the number of the disbelievers in the eyes of the believers would be less than the actual number of those disbelievers. So what is the story of this "mithlayhim"? Allah promised the believers His victory when He said:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 65].

The ratio here is that one believer goes out against ten of the disbelievers and defeats them; that is Allah's promise. And when Allah wished to lighten it, the Truth said:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾ [Al-Anfal: 66].

Allah has lightened the ratio, so one believer overcomes two disbelievers. The believers are promised by Allah victory even when they are weak. And the Truth says, in the verse that gives good tidings to the believers and warns the disbelievers, which we are now addressing: ﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.﴾

We hear the word "ibrah" (lesson) often, and its root indicates passing from one place to another; so it is said of it "‘ubūr" (crossing). In our ordinary life we designate on streets places for the crossing of pedestrians, that is, the distance through which pedestrians can pass from one side of the street to the other side of the same street. And "‘ubūr al-bahr" (crossing the sea) is passing from one shore to another shore.

So the root "‘ubūr" indicates passing from place to place, and "‘ibrah" means a tear, because it falls from its place in the eye onto the cheek. And "‘ibārah" means a sentence that we speak, for it passes from the mouth to the ear, and it is also a crossing. And "‘abīr" means a fine scent that passes from a rose a little distant from a person to reach his nose. So the root "‘ubūr" indicates "passing through."

When the Truth says: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson﴾, that is, it transfers you from a matter that may frighten you, O believers, because you are few and they are many, it transfers you to the victory of Allah, O believers, and transfers you, O disbelievers, to

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires...﴾

The place where this noble verse occurs is the context of mentioning the Islamic battle, which Allah made a continuing and perpetual sign, to clarify for us that battles of faith require devotion to Allah and require the believing person to step out of the habit that grants him every pleasure. Battles of faith make the sincere believer sacrifice much of his wealth in equipping himself and equipping others as well.

So the one who holds back from war is a person overcome by the desires of this world. Therefore Allah brings this verse after the verse that outlines the path of continuous victories for the people of faith, lest the desires of life take us away from the enjoyment of fighting in the way of Allah and of raising His word. He says: "Beautified for people is the love of desires," and the word "zuyyina" (beautified) gives us a distinction between the enjoyment that Allah makes lawful and the enjoyment that Allah does not approve of, because adornment is usually something above the essence. A woman is beautiful in herself, and afterwards she adorns herself, so her adornment is something above the essence of her beauty.

It is as if Allah wants us to take life and not reject it, but not to take it with its adornment and glitter; rather, we take it in its essential reality of sustenance, so He says: "Beautified for people is the love of desires among women." And what is shahwa (desire)? Shahwa is the strong inclination of the soul towards any action whatsoever.

When we look at the verse, we find that it clarifies for us that inclination, if it is something that confirms the reality of sustaining life, is required and accepted, but if a person takes the matter beyond that, this is what is detested.

We have previously given the example of the most intense of human instincts, the instinct of sex, and that the animal surpasses the human in it. The animal takes the sexual act for the preservation of the species, as evidenced by the fact that the female animal, once it has been impregnated by a male, does not allow another male to mount her. And the male too, if he comes to a female who is pregnant, does not approach her. So animals have taken the instinct of sex as a means of sustaining life, and have not taken it, like humans, as a renewed pleasure.

Nevertheless, we humans wrong the animals, and we say in describing a human's desire: "So-and-so has bestial desire." Would that it were truly bestial desire, for the beast takes it only to the necessary measure; but we have philosophized it. So your going beyond what could be permissible and lawful in the matter is called the baseness of the desire of the soul.

Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to guarantee the continuance of the universe, and continuance has two kinds: that a person sustains his life through food and drink, and that the life of the human species is sustained through marriage.

But if you look at the matter, you find the Creator is wise and all-knowing. He knows that the childhood of any animal is simple in relation to its father and mother. For example, the dove feeds its chick until it is able to fly, then it does not know where its chick went. But the outcome of the union between man and woman, which Allah willed to produce children, needs toil until the child reaches maturity, so that there is a balance and proportion between what a person eagerly desires of desire and what he bears of hardships and troubles in the effort to enjoy it and sustain it.

So the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted: "Beautified for people is the love of desires among women." Who is it that beautifies? If it is in the matter beyond the necessities of the matter, then this is the work of Satan; and if it is in the regular matter that guarantees the continuance of the species, then this is from Allah.

We find that the Truth adds "sons" to the domain of desires, and by it He means males, and He did not say daughters. Why? Because sons are the ones who are always sought for support, as they say, and no shame comes from them, and the Arabs used to bury daughters and feared shame; and what is beloved to a man in begetting, even until now, is begetting sons. Even those who speak of women's rights and call for them, whether a man or a woman, if Allah has not granted them a male child, then he or she wants a male child.

And He adds to the domain of desires: ﴿and heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾. The qanatir are the plural of qintar (a hundredweight-type unit of weight), and the qintar is a unit of weight, and this weight was determined by the density of gold. However, the qintar, before it was a weight, was a volume; but they saw that this volume weighs a certain quantity, so they moved from volume to weight.

In ancient times, the sign of great wealth was that they would bring the hide of an ox after skinning it and fill it with gold, and filling the ox-hide with gold they called a qintar, and this was a primitive process. Afterwards they took the filled hide of gold and weighed it, and it became a weight. So its origin was volume, and it became weight. When you hear ﴿and heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾, He wants to realize the qintariyya in it, meaning that the muqantar (heaped-up) qintar is the qintar of full weight, not merely an approximate qintar, just as we also say: "dinars mudannara" (minted dinars). It is a habit in the Arabic language to find a word that comes from the same root, joined to it in order to give it strength, so it is said "zill zaleel" (a dense shade), meaning a thick shadow, and it is said "layl alyal" (a pitch-dark night), meaning the night is in intense darkness, an exaggeration in the density of darkness.

Darkness, for example, veils the sun, and what veils the sun from you may be one veil, or the thing that shades you may be above something else which also shades it, so the shade becomes a dense shade. That is why the shade under trees is pleasant, because one leaf screens the sun and another leaf screens the first leaf, and so on, thus producing a natural air-conditioning.

For this reason they now make air-conditioned tents made of cloth with another cloth above it and a gap between them, so there is cloth shading another shade; and if they place a third piece of cloth shading the first two, the shade becomes dense. That is why we said: the shade of trees is a dense shade, containing tenderness; every leaf that shades a person is itself shaded by another leaf, and the leaves of the tree that shade one another are of different positions, and they give the breeze an opportunity to pass, whereas tents block the breeze.

And the poet, when he wanted to describe a garden, said:
"It blocks the sun wherever it faces, so it veils it and permits the breeze."

So when Allah described the qanatir as muqantara, that means the precisely balanced qanatir, and they are heaped-up qanatir of what? ﴿of gold and silver and horses branded/marked﴾. Horses were the instrument of honour and a sign and indication of greatness, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection."

The saying of the Truth: ﴿and branded horses﴾ — we see in it that a single word radiates into multiple domains of meaning. Musawwama (branded/pastured) derives from sawwamaha, meaning that these horses have pastures from which they eat as they wish, and are not horses tied to being fed only what is provided to them. Musawwama also means that these horses have marks: this horse is white-faced, that one is black, and that one is chestnut.

Musawwama also means that they are trained, tamed, and taught; the original state of horses is not domesticated but wild, so they must be broken in so that a person may benefit from them. So how many meanings did the word "musawwama" give?

Sa'ima: grazing, eating according to their appetite and not according to the fodder we give them. Mu'allama: having marks like the white blaze and the white stockings; this is a black steed, and that a chestnut steed; or that they are marked, meaning trained. So what does war require?

War requires separation from family, so the desire of the soul must not be a barrier, whether it is desire for women, or the desire for the pride of sons and their care, or the desire for wealth; the believer spends it in the way of Allah, and horses too a person uses in fighting to raise the word of Allah.

We note that this verse, which enumerates the kinds of adornment, came after the verse speaking of jihad in the way of Allah, in which the Blessed and Exalted Truth says:

﴿There has already been for you a sign in the two armies that met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving, who saw them as twice their number with their own eyes. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.﴾ [Al-Imran: 13]

This is to guide us that the believing person should not sacrifice his true desire, which is attaining martyrdom in the way of Allah or victory over the enemy, for the sake of passing desires that are represented in women, in sons, in heaped-up qanatir of gold and silver, in branded horses and livestock. And Allah said about livestock in Surat al-An'am:

﴿Eight pairs: of the sheep two and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge if you are truthful. And of the camels two and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah commanded you this? Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ [Al-An'am: 143-144]

The calculation of that is two of the sheep, two of the goats, two of the camels, and two of the cattle, that is, eight pairs. It cannot be counted as sixteen as some said in the past; no. The zawj (pair) does not mean two of a thing, but the zawj is one, provided it is with another of its kind. Another example is the word "tawam" (twin): the tawam is one with another, and they are two twins, and they are tawa'im if the number is more than two.

And the Truth says in the domain of the adornment of desires: "Beautified for people is the love of desires among women and sons and heaped-up piles of gold and silver and branded horses and livestock and tilth." And when you hear the word "al-harth" (tilth), understand that what is meant here is crops; but Allah, glorified and exalted, wants you to know that when Allah causes things to grow for you without your treatment, He also wants you to cultivate things by your treatment, and this is achieved only through the process of tilling.

Tilling (harth) is stirring up the soil; the earth is hard, so a person must stir it by tilling, that is, loosen its dryness and the cohesion of its particles, because the cohesion of soil particles is not suitable to be an environment for plants, since plants need water and need air, and need from man to prepare the way for the small rootlets to emerge and find easy soil in which to move until they grow strong.

So tilling stirs the earth and makes it soft and crumbly so that the seed can grow; because Allah has deposited in the two cotyledons of every seed the components of life until a root grows to take the components of life from the earth, and as the root strengthens in the plant, the two cotyledons shrink and become merely two leaves. Where has the volume of the two cotyledons gone?

The two cotyledons have nourished the plantlet until the plantlet was able to feed itself from the earth, and this cannot happen unless the earth has been tilled. That is why they say: clay soil that is black is difficult and not fertile, and it is said that sandy soil is also not fertile. Why?

Because we want two qualities in the soil: the first quality is...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 15:

Then Allah makes clear the goodness of the final return in His saying, may He be glorified: ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something better than that?..."﴾

When you hear the phrase "Shall I inform you" (a'unabbi'ukum), what follows it is not ordinary speech; rather, it is a momentous announcement, one that is said only about great events. No one says to another, "I will inform you that you will eat such-and-such at lunch." Instead one says, "I inform you that you have won a great prize." This is at the human level, so what of Allah, the Supreme Creator? This is why the True God says:

﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾ [An-Naba': 1–2].

It is the matter that overturns the whole structure of this world. So when the Truth says, ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something better than that?"﴾, the meaning is that Allah informs us of a thing better than these things. From this we know that Allah has made these things a measure. Why?

Because it is a measure that can be perceived by the senses. He also clarified for us how the ascent works, saying: ﴿For those who are mindful of God, with their Lord﴾. The believer looks with confidence at the phrase ﴿with their Lord﴾, meaning the Lord who takes charge of nurturing, and who looks after the one being nurtured until he reaches the degree of perfection required of him.

The "with-ness" here is with the Supreme Lord. So what has the Supreme Nurturer prepared for the mindful? He has prepared for them ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Let us observe the excellence of these gardens. In this world they correspond to tilth and crops, and we have said that when the Truth speaks of crops He describes them as "tilth" (harth), so that we may know that crops require movement and labour from us.

In the Hereafter, however, the gardens are ready-made; they demand no movement or toil from the believer. And the matter does not stop there: these gardens have rivers flowing beneath them, and in them is for the believing human what Allah has promised him: ﴿abiding therein forever, and purified spouses﴾. It is the eternity that never perishes, which a person does not leave and which does not leave him.

The purified spouses are a promise from Allah to the believers. Whoever loves women in this world knows that a woman in this world undergoes changes that may repel: either in her natural creation or in her character. There are times when a man does not want to approach his wife, and she may have some bad trait, so that a person dislikes her beauty.

Therefore a man may be deceived by a woman's outward appearance in this world, and a person may fall in love with one woman only to find in her a trait that makes him hate her. In the Hereafter, however, the matter is different: they are ﴿purified spouses﴾, that is, purified from every defect that afflicts the women of this world, so the believer takes their beauty, and there is in them none of the evils of this world, for Allah has purified them of these.

﴿And purified spouses﴾: purified by whom? It is Allah Himself, may He be glorified, who purified them in creation and in character. A man in this world may desire a woman, and her freshness lasts fifteen years, attracting and drawing him, then wrinkles, sagging and aversion begin. In the Hereafter, however, the woman is purified of everything and remains in her freshness and beauty forever. Is this not an ascent to good?

We note that the Truth, glorified be He, mentioned here two matters:

The first: gardens beneath which rivers flow, which we compare with tilth in this world.

The second: purified spouses, which we also compare with women in this world. The Truth did not mention anything about the rest of the things. Where are the heaped-up hoards of gold? Where are the horses? Where are the cattle and the children?

We notice that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, placed the two adorned matters, one with which the verse begins and the other that comes at its end. Let us recite the verse in which adornment is mentioned: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: of women and children, heaped-up hoards of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilth﴾.

The beginning is women; that is the first arc, and the end is tilth, which is the second arc. Between the two arcs are the rest of the adorned things. Allah has given us in place of the two arcs, and has clarified for us that they are the elevated good, and He did not mention the rest of the adorned things. This means that we should understand it in light of the principle that provision is that by which one benefits. That is, everything from which a person benefits is provision: good character is provision, hearing knowledge is provision, a person's manners are provision, a person's forbearance is provision, a person's truthfulness is provision. But provision comes sometimes directly, so that one benefits from it immediately, and sometimes provision comes but does not benefit directly; rather, it may be a means and a route to what benefits directly.

An example of this is bread: it is direct provision. Money is also provision, but it is indirect provision, because a person may be hungry while owning a mountain of gold; if someone said to this person, "Take a loaf in exchange for a mountain of gold," the hungry person would give the mountain of gold for the loaf, because a person does not eat gold. Likewise a cup of water is for the thirsty.

So there is provision that is not sought for its own sake, but is sought because it is a means to something else. A means to something else you will not need in the Hereafter, because you will live by the exertion of causes, by the Truth's saying: "Be!" A person in Paradise will not need wealth or heaped-up hoards of gold and silver, because whatever the soul desires you will find. And in the Hereafter you will not need branded horses, because you will not fight upon them or take pleasure and delight in riding them.

Everything you do not need in the Hereafter, Allah gave you in this world so that you might strive through causes. Allah did not mention it in His saying: ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who are mindful of God, with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah; and Allah is Seeing of [His] servants."﴾ He did not mention them in the noble text, because Allah's giving in the Hereafter is direct provision, whereas the things for which a person strives in this world to obtain direct provision He did not mention, since there is no need for them in the Hereafter. We love wealth, and why? Because it enables us to buy things. We love branded horses because they give us the capacity to fight and strive in the way of Allah,

and cattle, to give us enjoyment.

As for Paradise in the Hereafter, the believer finds in it everything the souls desire, and whatever occurs to the mind of one whom Allah grants Paradise he will find; intermediaries are then of no use. Therefore the Truth spoke of direct things, mentioning for us the gardens beneath which rivers flow, and mentioning for us the purified spouses.

When we reflect on the Truth's saying: ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something better than that?"﴾, someone may say: Would it not have been more logical for the Truth to inform us directly of what He wishes to tell us, rather than asking us whether He should inform us of this good or not?

We say: You have not noticed the excitement created by the beautiful style, and Allah's tenderness toward His creation. He, glorified and exalted, is saying to us: Do you not want me to tell you of things that surpass those that delight you in this world? It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted, has alerted the one who did not pay attention. And the Truth did not wait for us to say to Him, "Tell us, O Lord."

No, He tells us without our asking, and this style is called in the language "interrogation for affirmation" (istifham li-taqrir). When a person hears ﴿Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾, the mind becomes preoccupied; if the news is not heard, the mind will remain preoccupied with the news, and the answer comes with longing, and so it takes firm hold of the believer's soul.

The news comes ﴿for those who are mindful﴾. When we consider carefully the desires mentioned earlier, namely women, children, heaped-up hoards of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilth, is it not fitting that a person should be mindful of his Lord within their domain?

Mindfulness of Allah regarding these things is obligatory. That is why we said earlier something by which we respond to those who want to make life into asceticism and withdrawal from action, and who want to confine life to worship in matters of prayer and fasting, and to abandon everything. To these we say: No; your movement in life helps you toward mindfulness, because we have learned that the meaning of taqwa is that a person places a barrier between himself and the Fire, and that you place between yourself and your Lord's anger a shield. When you take Allah's blessings to spend them in light of Allah's method, this is the good use of blessings.

I explained earlier that taqwa, when it comes in the Truth's saying ﴿Be mindful of Allah (ittaqu Allah)﴾ and comes again as ﴿Be mindful of the Fire (ittaqu al-nar)﴾, the two meet: guarding against the Fire so that a person is not struck by harm, and when a person is mindful of Allah he is guarding against Allah's anger, because Allah's anger brings punishment, and punishment is among the soldiers of the Fire. So those who are mindful of Allah do not suppose that they have renounced this life for its own sake, but for the sake of what is higher than it: the desire for the everlasting bliss of the Hereafter.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, makes clear: you will not enjoy yourselves in the Hereafter out of a need for enjoyment, such that when blessing comes to you, you rejoice in it. The matter is not confined to that; rather, it extends to your wishing, O believers, only to see the Bestower. As long as the believer who enters Paradise finds everything he desires, indeed he does not even desire anything until it comes to him, and he enjoys according to Allah's giving and His capacities.

If a person does not desire fruits or women in Paradise, and becomes occupied with seeing his Lord, then his place is a garden of the gardens called "Illiyyin," and there is nothing in "Illiyyin" of what you hear about Paradise; there is in it nothing but meeting Allah. Provision and blessings are not for the sake of sustaining life in Paradise; rather, a person will have eternity there, so what a person needs is the approval (ridwan) of Allah.

Indeed, the approval of Allah is greater than everything. Allah has informed us of what is in the gardens, and has informed us of the good in all of that. Allah has informed us that His greatest approval is that the believer be assured of attaining the sight of his Lord. This is what is said about Allah:

﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 22–23].

Thus there are ascending degrees in Paradise. Then the Truth tells us: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾, meaning that Allah will give each person according to his position regarding the method of his Lord. Whoever obeys Allah out of desire for the bliss of Paradise receives Allah's Paradise, and whoever obeys Allah because the Essence of Allah is worthy of being obeyed, Allah gives him the enjoyment and delight of looking at Him, glorified be He. Rabi'a al-'Adawiyya says regarding this meaning:

"They all worship out of fear of the Fire, and see salvation as a generous portion.
As for me, I am not like them, and for this reason I do not seek any substitute for the One I love."

She also said: "O Allah, if You know that I worship You out of fear of Your Fire, then cast me into it; and if You know that I worship You out of desire for Your Paradise, then deprive me of it. I worship You only because You deserve to be worshipped."

So, "﴿Allah is Seeing of [His] servants﴾" means that He will give each servant according to his movement and intention in movement. Whoever loves what is with Allah of blessing, let him take the blessing, and let Allah pour it out upon him. As for whoever loves Allah, even if blessing is taken from him, Allah gives him the fullest giving; and this is the field of Allah's boasting before His angels. Among the strongest proofs of faith and its perfection is preferring the love of Allah and His Messenger over everything in existence:

From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: "Whoever has three qualities will find in them the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else; that he loves a person only for Allah's sake; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has rescued him from it, just as he hates to be thrown into the Fire."

There is the servant who loves Allah for His own essence, because His essence, glorified be He,

The Almighty then says: ﴿Those who say: "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins..."﴾

Their saying ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have believed﴾ is the first rank for entering the door of God. It is as if faith in God requires that the one who has received the obligation attend to the movement of his own self, because faith has a right that calls for this. It is as if the believer says: "I, with my humanity, cannot fulfil the right of faith in You. So, O Lord, forgive me for whatever heedlessness, slip, arrogance, or outburst of the self has befallen me in it."

This supplication is evidence that he knew what faith requires, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) explained to us in his clarification of the meaning of ihsan (excellence in worship), when he said: "Ihsan is that you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you."

That is, you summon God into every deed, because He sees you.

Can any human dare to transgress against the sacred things of One whom he sees with his own eyes? At that point the believer recalls what has come down to us of transmitted speech, so it is as if the Almighty, exalted is He, addresses us: "O My servants, if you believe that I do not see you, then the flaw is in your faith; and if you believe that I see you, then why have you made Me the least of those who look at you?"

It is as if the Almighty says to the servant: "Am I less than My servants? Would you be able to wrong someone while he is watching you? Then how do you dare to wrong your Creator?"

The saying of the believers ﴿Indeed we have believed, so forgive us﴾ is evidence that they knew that the demands of faith are difficult. ﴿Those who say: "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins"﴾. Let us see upon what they based the forgiveness of sins. They based the request for forgiveness of sins upon faith. Why? Because, since the Almighty has legislated repentance and legislated the forgiveness of sins, this means that He, glory be to Him, has known from eternity that His servants' selves may betray them, so they deviate from the way of God.

The Almighty concludes the verse, on the tongues of the believers, with His saying: ﴿And protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, because at the moment that I know the Almighty has guaranteed me, through the vastness of His forgiveness, that He will cover my sin, a servant may be ashamed of committing a sin, or hasten to seek forgiveness.

And why should His saying ﴿so forgive us our sins﴾ not mean: "Cover them, O Lord, from us, so that they never come to us"? And if they come, they are the occasion for seeking forgiveness and repentance. So if I commit a sin, and I seek forgiveness from my Lord, and I know that my Lord has permitted forgiveness, because He said:

﴿So I said: "Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving"﴾ [Nuh: 10].

Then fear is withdrawn, and dread departs from me, and I turn to God with love for His obligations, and I compel my self to apply the whole way of God. Therefore, when God, the Almighty, exalted is He, legislated repentance for creation, that was another mercy. And this other mercy becomes manifest in its opposite and contrary.

Suppose God had not legislated repentance, and one person committed a sin, and the moment he committed a sin he left God's mercy. What would then befall society from him? All evils would strike society from this person, because he would have lost hope in himself. But when God opens the door of repentance for him, if the servant commits a sin while heedless of his religion, he returns to his Lord.

This is the realism of the Islamic religion. Religion is not merely words said; rather, it is a religion that takes account of human reality. He, glory be to Him, knows that the servants will commit sins, so He also lays out for them the path of seeking forgiveness. When the servants commit sins, the Truth requires them to repent of them and to seek forgiveness from God. If repentance stings them when they recall the sin, then every time this sting bites them, God gives them a good deed.

It is as if the forgiveness of sin is one thing, and protection from the Fire is another. How? Because at the moment the servant knows that the Almighty has guaranteed him His forgiveness, and He is the Creator and Sustainer, the servant goes to God seeking forgiveness, hoping for forgiveness and mercy. This is the call of the believers, if they had forgotten to seek forgiveness for themselves. Why? Because seeking forgiveness for sin is an obligation from God. As we have said: a human may forget some of the obligations, so he may be heedless of seeking forgiveness. Therefore the Truth says, on the tongues of His believing servants: ﴿And protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾.

The meaning of taqwa (God-consciousness, piety) is that you place between yourself and the Fire a shield, or you place between yourself and the anger of your Lord a shield. So when you take the blessings from God to spend them in the way of God, they become a good deed for you. We have said that "fear God" (ittaqu Allah) and "fear the Fire" (ittaqu al-nar) meet, because the meaning of "fear the Fire" is so that it does not harm you, and "fear God" means that we place between ourselves and the anger of God a shield, because the anger of God will come.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 17:

And after that the Truth says: ﴿the patient, the truthful, the obedient, and those who spend﴾....

These are all attributes of those who have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah. Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, and purified spouses, and the pleasure of Allah, which is greater. They are patient, truthful, obedient (qanitun), those who spend in the way of Allah, and those who seek forgiveness at the hours before dawn.

And patient in what? They are patient in carrying out the obligations of Allah. For when we first hear of an obligation (taklif), we should know that it contains cost and hardship, and the legal obligations (al-takalif al-shar'iyyah) involve hardship because they restrict the freedom of the servant.

The Truth created you with a nature fit to do such-and-such or not to do it. When He says to you, "Do," He has closed off for you the door of "Do not," and when the Truth says to you, "Do not," He has closed off for you the door of "Do." Thus the restriction of your movement occurs, and the restriction of the created being, in the form of choice, involves hardship. So when the command of Allah comes with "Do," the act itself may be difficult in its essence. If you endure the hardship of the act that came by way of "Do," then you are patient, because you have been patient in obedience. And you may also be patient in refraining from disobedience, when something that carries the anger of Allah insistently presses upon you, and you refuse to commit the sin; then you have been patient in refraining from committing the sin.

So in "Do" there is patience over its hardship, and in "Do not" there is patience by refraining from it. The patient therefore have two directions, because the obligation is either with "Do" or with "Do not." When the obligation comes with "Do," the hardship may come; and when you carry out the obligation with "Do," you have been patient through the hardship. And when the obligation comes with "Do not," like the command of the Truth to refrain from drinking wine, or "Do not steal," you have been patient in refraining from it. Thus "Do" and "Do not" together encompass both types of obligation. There remain, after that, events that do not fall within the scope of "Do" or "Do not," and these are what descends upon you by divine decree (qadar), without choice on your part, but rather are compulsion and coercion.

For when it is required of you to act, that is, He has created you fit not to act, as we said before, except if you are compelled to act only. And likewise if the Truth says to you, "Do not." And the matter of decree in which there is no room for choice, what does the believer do with it? He is patient with pains and hardships, because he has believed in Allah as Lord, and the Lord is the one who undertakes the upbringing of the one being raised until he reaches the perfection desired for him. So if the Truth brings you a matter in which you have no choice, such as illness or sudden calamities, like a stone falling from above or being struck by a stray bullet, all of these are matters in which neither "Do" nor "Do not" has any part.

There, patience with such matters is the faith in the wisdom of the One who inflicted them upon you. For the one who inflicted them is the Lord, and He is the one who created me, so I am His handiwork.

And we have never seen anyone spoil his handiwork at all. So when a matter comes upon a person without his choice, the One who brought it upon him has wisdom in it, and if the person is patient with these pains, he enters the category of the patient.

So the patient are of kinds: the patient in obedience and its hardships, the patient in refraining from sins and their enticements, and the patient in the events of decree that descend upon him without his choice. And if you see a person who has been patient in the matter of obedience, patient in refraining from the desire for sin, and patient in the decrees that descend upon him, then know his love for his Lord and his Lord's pleasure with him.

Next we come to another description in which Allah says: ﴿the patient﴾ ﴿and the truthful﴾.

Truthfulness (al-sidq), as we know, is opposed by falsehood (al-kadhib), and truthfulness, as we know its reality, comes when the verbal statement (al-nisbah al-kalamiyyah) that a person utters corresponds to the other, external statement (al-nisbah al-kharijiyyah) that exists in the cosmos.

If you say, "Such-and-such happened," then that is a verbal statement issued by a speaker. If reality agrees with it, that such-and-such did indeed happen, the speaker is truthful. And if reality does not agree with the occurrence of what he reported, the speaker is a liar. Why? Because the speech of a rational speaker must have three statements:

The first is the mental statement (al-nisbah al-dhihniyyah). Before I speak, I present the matter to my mind, and my mind gives the signal to my tongue to speak. This is the first statement, and it is called "the statement of the mind." It may occur to me that the mental statement comes and then I turn away from it and do not speak, so the mental statement has come into existence while the verbal statement has not come into existence.

And I may insist on bringing the mind's signal onto my tongue, so I say the verbal statement. After the verbal statement we come to see: is it the case that what happened and what I spoke of did occur or did not occur? If it occurred, the speech from me is truthful. And if it did not occur, and the external statement was contrary to what I reported, we say: "This is a false statement." So truthfulness is that the verbal statement corresponds to reality, and falsehood is that the verbal statement does not correspond to reality. Often people err in understanding reality and find contradiction in some styles of expression.

An example of that: when some orientalists addressed the saying of the Truth, may He be glorified and exalted:

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1]. That is a verbal statement issued by them. Is it in agreement with reality or contrary to it? It is in agreement with reality. And the Truth confirms that by His saying:

﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

After that the Truth, may He be glorified, says:

﴿And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

So in what did the hypocrites lie? Did they lie in their saying: ﴿that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾? No. The Truth did not declare them liars in their saying ﴿that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾, because Allah has affirmed this reality by His saying ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger﴾.

But Allah declared them liars regarding what the critical orientalist overlooked when they said: ﴿We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾. Allah declared them liars in their testimony, not in the thing testified to, which is that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a messenger from Allah. Allah knows that Muhammad is His messenger, sent by Him as a mercy to the worlds, but the lie was in their own testimony.

The speech of the hypocrites is rejected by Allah. Why? Because testimony (al-shahadah) means that the tongue agrees with and conforms to the heart. Their saying was a testimony that did not conform to their hearts, and this means their lying.

So the rejection is directed at their testimony. Had they said ﴿that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾ without "We bear witness," their saying would have been a "sound" proposition. That is why Allah's rejection concerned their testimony, and from here we perceive the secret in the saying of Allah: ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger﴾. The Truth affirms the matter testified to, which is the sending of Muhammad as a messenger from the Truth, and after that the Truth brings His own testimony that the hypocrites are liars in their saying "We bear witness." So truthfulness is that the verbal statement corresponds to reality. And truthfulness, as we said before, is truth, and truth does not have multiple forms. We gave an example before: a person whom we ask to narrate an event he witnessed with his own eyes, and to recount it truthfully, will never change his account, however often the telling is repeated or the number of times the testimony is given. But if the event was a lie, the one narrating it becomes confused by his lies, and narrates the event in various colors without coherence, and the lying narrator may forget what he said the first time, and thus the secret of the lie is revealed. But the narrator of an observed reality who speaks truthfully is the one who recounts, and his narrations do not differ each time from the previous one, but rather coincide.

So when we say, "Zayd is diligent," this means that Zayd's diligence has occurred first. Then there comes to the mind of the one who saw Zayd's diligence the intention to report the matter of his diligence, and then he speaks about Zayd's diligence. The external matter, which is Zayd's diligence, occurred first, and after that comes the mental statement, and after that the verbal statement.

But composition (al-insha'), which is the opposite of report (al-khabar), is that we request someone to create a matter that has no reality yet, as when we say to someone, "Strive!" Before we say to a person, "Strive," this means that striving was a matter in the mind of the speaker, and when he utters it, it becomes a "verbal statement." After that the reality occurs, after the mental statement and the verbal statement, and this is composition.

Requesting composition (al-insha' al-talabi) means that the external statement occurs after the verbal statement. And the truthful are those whom Allah wished to praise. Why? And where is the field of their truthfulness? They are those whose movement conforms to the method of Allah, because when they said, "There is no god but Allah," and believed in Him, they committed themselves to all the requirements of faith to the extent of their ability. The meaning of "There is no god but Allah" is: there is no one worshipped but Allah. And the meaning of "but Allah" is: there is no obedience but to Allah.

And obedience, as we know, is compliance with a command and compliance with a prohibition.

So the field of "There is no god but Allah" includes that there is no one worthy of worship but Allah, and no one obeyed in His obligations but Allah, and no compliance with a command or a prohibition except the command coming from Allah. If a person complies with a command from Allah after saying "There is no god but Allah," that person is truthful in his saying "There is no god but Allah."

This is the truthfulness of the summit: that all the conduct of the one who says "There is no god but Allah" conforms to this statement. The true believer is the one who builds all his conduct in agreement with the method of Allah. This is the truthful person. As for the one who says with his tongue, "There is no god but Allah, no one worthy of worship but Allah," and then opposes his Lord by disobeying Him, we may say to him: you are a liar in your saying "There is no god but Allah." Why? Because he has not conformed to the statement he uttered. If this person believes in any obligation and then does what contradicts it, we say to him: you are a hypocrite. Why? Because when we spoke at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah about the hypocrites, we said that the believer, when he believes in Allah, is truthful with himself, because he says "There is no god but Allah" and believes in it, and the unbeliever, when he denies divinity, is also truthful with himself.

As for the hypocrite, he is not truthful with himself, nor truthful with people; he is wavering between these and those. The hypocrite lacks truthfulness with himself, and therefore the Truth describes them:

﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ [al-Nisa': 143].

The unbeliever has truthfulness with himself: he does not say "There is no god but Allah," because he does not believe it. But the hypocrite has said "There is no god but Allah," while it does not match his conduct, so he is not truthful with himself, nor truthful with his Lord. Thus the saying of the Truth ﴿and the truthful﴾ refers to those people who in all their movements proceed from the method of Allah, so they do not believe in one matter and do another. Therefore the Truth, may He be glorified and exalted, says:

﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 2–3].

That is, when the saying is something different from the doing, the statement does not conform. The truthful are those who are truthful in their conduct with the word of tawhid, in all that this word requires in this chain: "There is no god but Allah, no one worthy of worship but Allah," that is, no one obeyed in a command or prohibition except Allah. If you come and obey someone in what Allah has not legislated, the believers have the right to say to you: you are a liar in your saying "There is no god but Allah."

"On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, nor does the thief steal while he is a believer, nor does the drinker drink wine while he is a believer."

This is the exalted nature of faith in the believer: the believer cannot lie or contravene the requirements of his creed, because the believer in all his conduct is subject to his faith that there is no god but Allah.

Then the Truth says: ﴿and the obedient (al-qanitin)﴾. Al-qanit is the one who worships with humility, tranquility, and constancy. The qanit is truthful with himself. Why? Because the Truth, may He be glorified and exalted, when He imposes obligations on the servants... all these things are from taqwa, and the acknowledgment of faith, and seeking forgiveness for sins, and seeking protection from the punishment of the Fire, and patience, and truthfulness, and qunut, and spending in the way of Allah, and seeking forgiveness at the hours before dawn, all of that is a result of the first taqwa.

It is the fruit of "There is no god but Allah." And since this is the fruit of "There is no god but Allah," let every person know that Allah has not left you to derive it yourself from nothing; rather, know that Allah has testified that there is no god but Him, and sufficient is Allah as a witness. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels...﴾.

All these things are from taqwa (God-consciousness): acknowledging faith, asking forgiveness for sins, asking to be protected from the Fire, patience, truthfulness, devotion (qunut), spending in the way of God, and seeking forgiveness at dawn. All of this is the result of the first taqwa.

It is the fruit of "there is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illa Allah). Since this is the fruit of "there is no god but Allah," every person should know that God has not left you to derive it yourself from something that is absent. Rather, know that God Himself has testified that there is no god but Allah, and God suffices as a witness. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge...﴾

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, standing firmly in justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

Let us take the first clause of the noble verse in its meaning: Allah has borne witness that there is no god but He, that is, the Truth has informed us of what He has seen and witnessed, or what stands in place of that. Indeed, "shahida" (bore witness) means "knew" ('alima).

It is the Truth who set up the proofs in existence for His self-subsistence (qayyumiyya) and for His being one God. Is this not an establishment of proof that He is the one God? And who created the proofs and brought them? It is Allah.

So Allah has borne witness that there is no god but He. We have said that Allah's witness that there is no god but He is the witness of the Essence to the Essence, and the witness of the Essence to the Essence means that it is a word that is empowered. So when the Truth says: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 117].

By Allah, if He had not borne witness to Himself that there is no god but He, and there were no one opposing His purpose, would He have gambled by saying it? He is the Supreme Truth who witnessed that there is no god but He, so at the moment He says "Be," He knows that there is no other god who says "Do not be." The Truth must assure us that there is no god but He; therefore it was necessary that He bear witness to Himself that He believes there is no god but He, and that He issues the command, and the governing decree (al-hukm al-taskhiri, the decree of subjugation), and knows that there is no god opposing Him.

Was it not also among the requirements of the Messenger ﷺ that he bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed and said in his prayer: "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." If he had not borne witness to this for himself, how would he gamble with the things he says? That is why our master Abu Bakr, when news of Muhammad's being sent as a messenger reached him, said something to the effect of: "Did Muhammad say it? He is truthful, and since he has said it, it is true."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was certain of the record that preceded Muhammad's being sent with the message. In history we see a woman for whom the cause of her Islam was a glimpse of the biography of the Messenger ﷺ. This woman read that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had guards from among the believers who protected him from the disbelievers. Then one day the Messenger ﷺ dismissed these guards and said to them something to the effect of: "Allah has protected me from the people, so go yourselves."

We have read this incident many times, but the opening came from the Truth to a woman, and this matter occupied her, and she asked herself: Were not these guards protecting him out of fear for his life? Why then did he say to them, "Do not guard me," because Allah is the one who guards me? If the Messenger of Allah had deceived the whole world, could he have deceived himself during his lifetime?

The woman answered herself: It is impossible. The Messenger of Allah must have been fully certain that Allah had informed him of the matter of his protection, as evidenced by his dismissing the guards; otherwise, how would he feel secure that someone might come to kill him? The woman said: By Allah, if he had deceived all the people, he did not deceive himself during his lifetime. "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

The Islam of this woman came about from a slight breath of the biography of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

So, ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He﴾ is the witness of the Essence to the Essence, and God suffices as a witness. The angels also bore witness, and the angels are the unseen realm hidden from us, who receive commands from the Truth. The angels did not see anyone else giving them orders; He is the one God, the Capable. This is the witness of the presence (shahada al-mashhad, witnessing by direct vision). To the angels is added ﴿and those of knowledge﴾, who are the ones who look at the proofs and sit deriving from God's creation proofs that there is no god but Allah.

This is the greatest witness to the greatest thing witnessed by the greatest witnesses: Allah at the summit, Muhammad ﷺ, the angels, and those of knowledge. Those of knowledge have attained a great rank because God has linked them with the angels.

The Truth, glory be to Him, informs us that He has scattered in His creation many wondrous signs, and whoever sits, reflects, ponders, perceives and looks, he will extract the proofs that there is no god but He. As we said before, this is the simplest way to demonstrate this truth. If "there is no god but Allah" is true, then we are sufficed. If it is not true, then where is the god from whom Allah took this universe, and who did not inform us that he is the owner of the universe? Either this other god did not know, or he knew and cannot do anything; so it is not right for him to be a god contending with the Truth who informed us that there is no god but He.

"There is no god but Allah" remains for its speaker, exalted is He: "Allah bears witness that there is no god but He." In every movement of life we find that acting alone in the performance of a movement may give elevation, or it may give arrogance. Therefore we say: Here is the Supreme Creator, "there is no god but He," informing us that He stands firmly in justice. And although no one is able to overtake Allah, He assures us that He stands firmly in justice.

Let us note here a beautiful point in the wording: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, standing firmly in justice﴾. Why did God not say that the angels and the people of knowledge, who bore witness that there is no god but He, are "standing" in justice? Allah has borne witness that there is no god but He, standing in justice, and the angels witnessed this matter, and the scholars also witnessed this matter. Why? Because if God had said "standing in justice" of them, then Allah would have been the one witnessed upon by them, whereas the witness here is for Him alone, that He is standing in justice and equity.

Because He, glory be to Him, created the angels with justice, and if they had been with Him in that, the affair would not be right. The people of knowledge are also created with justice, because God has distributed the movement of life among people: some people work with their minds, others work with their hearts, and others work with their limbs. This is one aspect of Allah's justice. Otherwise, would anyone claim that a person has gathered in himself all the talents life requires? No. This is from the justice of the Most Merciful.

Among the justice of the Truth is that He distributed talents among human beings. Instead of a person depending on himself for making clothing, food and drink, Allah made skills distributed among people. A group of people mastered the craft of farming to produce the food that suffices them and meets the needs of others, and they likewise exchanged benefits with others. A person alone cannot grow cotton, gather it, spin it and weave it to wear, and a person cannot grow wheat, harvest it, grind it and then bake it.

Allah did not create people so that each individual would satisfy the diverse needs of his own self; rather, God distributed talents so that these talents would interlock and human society would be complete. One person farms the land, a second spins cotton, a third weaves cloth, and a fourth makes tools. This is a great justice, because human capacity cannot bear to carry out all of life's requirements. Therefore the Truth made this diversity of talents in order to bind people to people by compulsion over people, and He did not give anyone preference over anyone else. Since one person is known in one field and another is not known in that field, the one who is not known needs the other, and so people exchange benefits despite themselves.

Therefore we find the universe integrated. Let each of us look at his life and count how many angles of knowledge, how many angles of capacities, and how many angles of talents are required so that the movement of life is served.

These angles are distributed among all people so that together they serve the movement of life. This is the peak of justice. And so that the Truth may clarify for us the value of justice and how justice is established in creating love and respect among human beings, let each of us look at the other person far from him, and ask himself within: Does this man far from me work for my sake? And the answer is: Yes.

So when a person sees someone excelling in some craft, let him say: His excellence in his craft returns to me, and his excellence in his talent returns to me. In this way Allah, through justice, prevented resentment and envy, and made people supportive of one another by compulsion, not by their own choice. So each person who strives in the movement of life is in fact establishing himself in one corner of life's corners. It is remarkable that the field a person excels in is where his own need is least. Therefore we find the rural proverb: "The carpenter's door is the loose one," so that a person knows that a talent someone else has will benefit him, as evidenced by the fact that the talent you have has benefited you only a little.

Thus among people there spreads the conviction that each individual's talent returns benefit to all of them, and love and respect take the place of envy and resentment. When one of the witty men was asked: "And why is the carpenter's door the loose one?" One of the witty men replied: "Because it is the only door for which the carpenter will not take a fee to repair it." We also turn to the wonders in the common wisdom: we find specialist physicians in various kinds of illness who became leaders in their fields of specialization, and the Truth, glory be to Him, wills that they are afflicted only with what they excelled in, as though what they excelled in did not benefit themselves at all, but benefited others. Let us look at the verse as a whole: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, standing firmly in justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ God began it by saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, standing firmly in justice﴾, then He said after that: ﴿There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ It is as if the verse is telling us: If the witness of the Essence to the Essence is established, and the witness of the presence from the angels, and the witness of inference from the scholars, then the principle is firmly and conclusively settled beyond doubt, so take it as a settled premise: "There is no god but He."

And since there is "no god but He," let your reliance be on Him alone, and know that if you rely on Him alone as God, you have relied on the Mighty who is not overcome in His command.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the whole nation gathered to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something Allah had already written for you; and if they gathered to harm you, they would not harm you except with something Allah had already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried."

No one can enter into dispute with Allah. Rather, the creatures of Allah enter into disagreement or struggle with one another, but no one dares to enter into struggle with Allah, because He is the Mighty who is not overcome. If you believe in Him alone, then success is yours. The word "alone" may appear, on its surface, to diminish the support you rely on in human reckoning, so it is said: "I take refuge in so-and-so alone." But when you are a refuge to twenty, are you not stronger? Here, however, there is no comparison between seeking refuge in Allah alone and seeking refuge in a created being. Here you take refuge in the Supreme Creator, in whose hand are the keys of everything, and He is capable of everything. So the word "alone" here suffices you and spares you from all others. Act for one face, and it will suffice you for all faces, and know that there is no one who can overcome His command.

The greatness of the Truth is that He is One, the Unique, the single, the Self-Sufficient (al-Samad), the Mighty who is not overcome in His command, and the possessor of all wisdom in placing things in their proper positions, such that when you come to know the wisdom of what Allah, glory be to Him, brings about upon His creation, you marvel at the greatness of Allah's power, because wisdom is placing a thing in its place. And when you have placed a thing in its place, there is no unease; and when a thing is placed in its place, it is settled; and as long as the thing

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 19:

The Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam...﴾.

After He told us that He is one God, and that He upholds justice, it follows logically from His being one God. So His saying ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ is a consequence of His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice﴾. Why? Because there is no submission to anyone except Allah, and since Allah is one God, there is no other god who shares with Him. The Exalted says:

﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any other god. [If there were], each god would have take off with what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91].

And since it has been established that He is the one God, what is it that prevents you, O human, from submitting to what He wills of you? So the Exalted's saying after that, ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾, is a matter entirely logical, which every rational person must arrive at. Yet Allah, glorified and exalted, has shown us mercy by sending us messengers to alert us to the matter of cause and effect, of the caused and the causer, of premise and conclusion: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam.﴾

If we ask: what is religion (ad-din)? The answer: the word din has multiple usages. It derives from "dāna": you say, "I submitted to so-and-so": I returned to him, surrendered myself to him, and obeyed his command. The word din is also applied to recompense (al-jaza'), so the Exalted says of the Day of Judgment: "the Day of Din," which is the day of recompense for obedience and for disobedience, and for the believing person having submitted to the command of Allah. All of these meet in the Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam.﴾ It makes us aware that there may exist religions to which people submit, but they are not religions with Allah. Did not the Exalted say:

﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun: 6].

This means that there is a religion for other than Allah, in which there is submission and surrender, and in which commands are carried out, but it is not a religion of Allah, nor a religion with Allah. The religion acknowledged by Allah is Islam. The word din is applied at times to the millah (creed/community) and at other times to the shari'ah (law). If the believer wants the required rulings, you may call them shari'ah; if the believer wants obedience, submission, and what follows from them of recompense, let the believer call it din; and if a person wants everything that encompasses these, let him call it millah.

So His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ means that there is no religion with Allah except Islam. The word "Islam" is derived from the root sin, lam, and mim. The letters sin, lam, and mim have a meaning that revolves through all its derivations and ends at safety from corruption. The meaning also ends at reconciliation between a person and himself, between a person and his Lord, between a person and the cosmos, and between a person and his brothers. It is soundness and the absence of corruption; the root sin-lam-mim all indicates this. And since the root from which the word "Islam" is formed indicates this, why would we not follow it?

We have said previously: a person does not submit to his peer unless he is convinced by what he says. A person says to an equal who commands him: "Why do you want me to carry out your orders? You must convince me of the wisdom of that command." But when a person believes in one God who upholds justice, and a command issues from this God, then it is incumbent upon the person to obey.

So, Islam means submission and surrender with dignity and understanding, with dignity and rationality; for there is a servitude of reason when a person stops at the superficial meaning, and there is a dignity of reason when a person stops at the meaning "which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it." This is the dignity of the intellect, so that nothing charms it except submission to the fixed command that never contradicts itself.

So, since Allah is one God upholding justice, I, as a servant of His servants, when I believe in Him and take from Him, this is dignity in understanding, dignity in rationality, and dignity in servitude as well, because I worship Allah who is above all creatures and beings, and I do not worship an equal to me. Whoever worships his equal has nothing but the pride and zeal of the humiliated. And since Islam is submission and surrender to Allah, it is submission to one who is not an equal. "Aslama" means he entered into peace (salm), that is, entered into reconciliation, non-contradiction, safety and comfort; he freed himself from everything except the face of Allah. Therefore the Exalted says:

﴿Allah presents an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison? All praise is due to Allah; but most of them do not know﴾ [az-Zumar: 29].

It is as if Allah wants to clarify for us the difference between one who submits to the command of a single master and one who submits to many masters. Allah has struck for us an example from a matter well known among us, saying what means: suppose a slave has ten masters, and each master has a request from him; what will that slave do? Another slave has a single master: this slave is at rest because he has one master, whereas the other, owned by ten, has his life torn by the conflicting commands of his ten masters.

So the slave owned by partners is wretched, because the partners do not agree; they are mutually contentious. When his master sees him doing a task for another master, he orders him to the opposite, and thus the slave's effort is dissipated and his fatigue multiplies. But the man who belongs wholly to one man is at rest. Likewise monotheism: the Exalted has brought an example from our reality to bring us close to the sweetness of tawhid. The believer in one God praises Allah because he submits to one God. So, since Islam is submission and surrender, and its meaning is entering into peace (salm) with a kasra on the sin, or entering into peace (salm) with a fatha on the sin, the Exalted says:

﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and rely upon Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [al-Anfal: 61].

This submission is not to an equal, but to one higher. The higher one to whom we submit is the one who created us, and He is the highest, who supplies us with His self-subsistence in everything.

So when a person submits, this Islam has a price, which is the reward from Allah. It is in a person's interest to submit. ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam.﴾ And since the religion acknowledged by Allah is Islam, it is the religion upon which reward is bestowed. Islam is the religion of all the messengers, and all of them believed in it. Abraham, the friend of the Merciful, said:

﴿Our Lord, make us Muslims [in submission] to You, and of our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 128].

Ya'qub, peace be upon him, is reported by the Exalted in His saying to his sons and their answer to him:

﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133].

And He says, majestic is He:

﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the creed of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists." Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He; and this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims [in submission]"﴾ [al-An'am: 161-163].

So Islam is a common religion, and "Muslims" is a common term among the religions; thus Islam does not stop at the message of our master Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, alone. Rather, Islam is the submission of a creature to a God in a method brought by messengers supported by miracles. However, Islam, with respect to these messages, was a description, but the Muhammadan community (ummah) was distinguished by the permanence of the description of its religion, as was the case for the nations of the earlier messengers. Islam also became a proper name for the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, because the message of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, contained the utmost of what exists of submission on earth, so nothing more can be added to it, and the community of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was singled out in that Islam became its name.

So Islam among the earlier nations was a description, while with respect to the message of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, it became a proper name, since no religion came after it. Its Islam is universal Islam. Therefore, with this religion we say: "We are Muslims." As for the adherents of other religions, they too are Muslims, but only by description. We who follow the final religion are named by Allah in His Book "the Muslims"; this is one of the miraculous aspects of the naming, in which the friend of Allah, Abraham, peace be upon him, agreed with the will of his Lord:

﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty; the millah of your father Abraham. He named you "the Muslims" before, and [also] in this [Revelation], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; how excellent is the protector and how excellent the helper﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

Islam has become the name of the community of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; and this description is not used as a name except for one who has fully attained submission.

How? We know that the word "Allah" is a proper name for the Necessarily Existent, and we know that "Hayy" (Living) is an attribute of Allah, the Exalted. But the word "Hayy" became a name of Allah's names, because Allah has complete, eternal life. So an attribute does not become a name unless the description in it attains permanence and absoluteness. By this analogy, the messengers before Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the nations before the Islamic community, were Muslims, and were nations that were Muslim by description. But the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was distinguished by Islam as description and as proper name; so the matter became, with respect to it, a name, and since nothing will come after it, the Islam of the Messenger of Allah's community became a "proper name." Abraham, peace be upon him, had already given good news of this matter: ﴿the millah of your father Abraham; He named you "the Muslims"﴾ [al-Hajj: 78]. Allah has relayed on the tongue of Abraham, with complete clarity, ﴿He named you the Muslims﴾, and Allah did not say, "He described you as Muslims." No, He said ﴿He named you the Muslims﴾, because the earlier nations were described with Islam, whereas the community of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is named with Islam. And among the miraculous aspects of the naming: we find that adherents of other religions have names other than Islam. The Jews call themselves Jews, after Yahuda. They call themselves "Mosaics," after Musa, peace be upon him. Christians call themselves that after the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. We, the community of the Messenger of Allah, have not said of ourselves, "We are Muhammadans"; rather we have said of ourselves, "We are Muslims." This designation has come on the tongue of no one ever except for the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the name Islam has become an honor for us.
