Therefore, the word of Allah, the Truth: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ means that, if it is permissible for a messenger or for the followers of a messenger to have the description of Islam, a messenger may yet come with something new that the earlier nations did not have, and we add it through submission; and through our addition—we the Muslims—of this submission, submission was sealed with us, the community of the Messenger of Allah...

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi on Surah 3, verse 20:

And then the Truth says: ﴿So if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to God...﴾

﴿So if they argue with you﴾. This statement shows that the Truth, glory be to Him, places His method upon the Seal of the Messengers and gives him the reality in which he lives. The Messenger (ﷺ) faced three camps. The first camp was the polytheists of Quraysh, whose disbelief was at its peak. The second camp was that of the Jews and the Christians, who are grouped together because they are People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab). The third camp was that of the hypocrites (munafiqun). The argument came from the second camp, because the disbelievers of Quraysh did not claim that they had a religion sent down from heaven. As for the People of the Book, they claim that they have a religion sent down from heaven. When polytheism (shirk, the association of partners with God) clashes with a religion, this is understandable. But when the people of a religion sent down from heaven clash with a messenger who has brought a final religion from heaven, this is a matter that deserves our pause.

The meaning of ﴿they argue with you﴾ is that they dispute with the Messenger (ﷺ), and the two similar letters, the two "jim"s, have been assimilated (idgham) so that the word would not be heavy on the tongue. The meaning of argument (muhajja) is that each of the two opponents presents his proof. This means debate. As long as there is debate between truth and falsehood, God does not leave His Messenger (ﷺ) alone, but says to him: ﴿if they argue with you﴾, that is, if they debate with you about the matter of Islam which you have brought as a final religion that contradicts the idolatry or polytheism of Quraysh, and contradicts what the People of the Book have altered from the will of God, then say, O Muhammad: ﴿I have submitted my face to God﴾. We have said before that when we hear the words of the Truth ﴿say﴾, it would have been permissible for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to limit himself to the content of the saying. We gave an example of this: when a father says to his son, "Go to your uncle and tell him: such and such," and when the son goes to the uncle, he says to him, "The matter is such and such," the son does not say to his uncle, "Tell your uncle such and such..." But the Messenger (ﷺ) preserved the text that came to him from his Lord, because the text is clear. ﴿So if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to God﴾. Is this a response by argument? Yes, this is the response, because among the People of the Book and the disbelievers of Quraysh there comes the saying:

﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 9].

And there comes the wise saying:

﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: "God." So how are they deluded?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 87].

The universe, as we know, is "makan" (place) and "makin" (one who is established). The "makan" is the heavens and the earth. The "makin" is the human being. Both the place and the one established in it are created by God. It is logical that we submit our faces to the One who created them.

So the words of the Truth ﴿say: I have submitted my face to God﴾ mean: pay attention, O people, I have not gone outside the circle of faith in the One God, which you also believe in. He is the One who created, and He is the One who brought the universe into existence.

After that, if there is submission in Islam, the Truth brings the most noble thing in the human being to be the manifestation of submission. The face is the distinguishing mark of highest rank, and it is the thing upon which the emotional reactions to events in the universe appear, whether joy or sorrow. It shows whether you prostrated while hating prostration, or prostrated while drawing near to God, glory be to Him, so the face fills with cheerfulness and radiance.

The saying of the Truth ﴿I have submitted my face to God﴾ means that the face, which is the most noble thing in the human being, has submitted to the Truth. It is as if the noble saying did not attribute submission to the body but to the most noble thing in the human being, which is the face. The face is sometimes used to mean the whole self. So when a person says ﴿I have submitted my face﴾, he means "I have submitted my self," with everything the self possesses of limbs and organs. Let us recite the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Everything will perish except His Face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 88].

That is, everything will perish except His Self, glory be to Him. This is what is meant by ﴿except His Face﴾. If we take "face" to mean only the face, someone may say: does God not have a hand, for example? We say that He has a hand within the scope of ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾, and therefore God's hand does not perish, nor does anything in Him perish. His Face means His Self within the scope of ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾. The face is used to refer to the Self, because the face is what identifies the self. No one can distinguish one body's limbs from another body's limbs; distinction comes through the features of the face, because they are the distinguishing mark. In the saying of the Truth to His Messenger, ﴿So say: I have submitted my face to God, and whoever follows me﴾, it shows that the Messenger has submitted his face to God, because God addressed him through revelation, and revelation came directly to him (ﷺ). But when He says ﴿and whoever follows me﴾, the address extends to whoever follows me, even if he is not addressed directly by God.

So there is no room for anyone to say to the Messenger (ﷺ): "You submitted your face to God because He addressed you alone." It is as if the speaker of this claim wants an address to every believer. He, glory be to Him, said ﴿and whoever follows me﴾. Whoever follows the Messenger believes that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a truthful messenger who conveys from God a true method. There is no room for requiring the conveyance to reach each individual, because the message has already reached them through faith in what God sent down to His noble Messenger. The Truth, glory be to Him, commands His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered: Have you submitted?﴾

When you read or hear a style that contains the interrogative hamza, you should know that the question seeks to make the truth known, as when a person says to another: "Do you have Muhammad?" or "Did so-and-so visit you?" This is a question meant to establish understanding of the reality. Sometimes the question means merely an instruction to do something. For example, a guest comes and you sit with him, and your father enters and says to you: "Did you make coffee for your guest?" This is a directive to you: if you have not performed the duty of hospitality, you must hasten to perform it.

On this basis we understand the saying of the Truth: ﴿Have you submitted?﴾. Therefore, after speaking of wine, we read the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling, and to hinder you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 91].

The saying of the Truth ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ contains a question, and the question here means a command to desist. In the context of the verse we are reflecting upon, we find the saying of the Truth ﴿Have you submitted?﴾, which means a call to Islam, that is, "Submit." Then comes the noble saying of the Truth: ﴿If they submit, then they are guided﴾. The meaning of "they are guided" is that they have recognised the path that leads to the purpose for which God created the human being. Here we must know that the word "Islam" has come to indicate submission,

and submission is not observed except in one who submits, and the process of submission is known through movement and conduct, not only through belief. For this reason, Imam Ali (may God ennoble his face), who was given something of the breath of prophethood in the expression of faith with beautiful eloquence, said to his brothers: "I will attribute Islam a lineage that no one before me has attributed: Islam is certainty (yaqin), certainty is affirmation (tasdiq), affirmation is acknowledgment (iqrar), acknowledgment is performance (ada'), performance is action (amal), and the believer is known by his faith through his action." In our ordinary life we ask: "What is so-and-so's lineage?"

That is, we ask "Whose son is he?" The word "nassabah" among the Arabs means the man who knows the chain of lineage: who is the son of whom, so-and-so son of so-and-so son of so-and-so. Imam Ali (may God ennoble his face), when he attributes Islam, actually attributes it to a lineage that no one before him had attributed. And Imam Ali (may God ennoble his face) concludes by attributing Islam to action.

He said:

"The believer is known by his faith through his action, so the correct proof of a believer's faith is his action." Imam Ali (may God ennoble his face) adds: "The disbeliever is known by his disbelief through denial. The believer has taken his religion from his Lord and has not taken it by his own opinion. The bad deed in Islam is better than the good deed in other religions, because the bad deed in Islam is forgiven, while the good deed in other religions is not accepted, since disbelief accompanies it with God (i.e., associating partners with God)." Is there a lineage for Islam more wonderful than this? Thus we find the noble saying: ﴿If they submit, then they are guided.﴾ The opposite of Islam comes after that: ﴿But if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey.﴾ The opposite is "turn away," that is, they did not submit. It is the Truth alerting His Messenger not to grieve and not to be sorrowful if they turn away, as in His noble saying:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 6].

Why? Because the Messenger (ﷺ) has only the duty of conveyance. Since the verse begins with ﴿I have submitted my face to God and whoever follows me﴾, the conveyance also includes the Prophet (ﷺ) and whoever follows him. For this reason another verse comes to explain this matter of faith, to keep the message within his community (ﷺ), and to inform us why there is no longer any need for prophets after the Messenger of God (ﷺ), trustworthy ones to correct corruption of conduct in the universe. The world no longer needs new prophets, and for this reason the Messenger (ﷺ) said:

"The scholars are the heirs of the prophets."

So from ﴿then your duty is conveyance﴾ we take the clear understanding that the duty of conveyance does not end with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), but includes every scholar of the conveyance of what reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and was believed in. They had in the Messenger of God an excellent example. The Truth clarifies this in another verse:

﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and believing in God. If the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiant transgressors.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110].

The Truth says in another verse:

﴿And strive for God with the striving due to Him...﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78]. The meaning is that you bear witness before the people that you have conveyed to them the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Whoever does not convey the message of the Messenger of God to people has not taken the inheritance of prophethood. The inheritance of prophethood is both the honour of conveying and also endurance and bearing. The inheritance of prophethood is sometimes the attainment of the honour of conveying the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and sometimes the inheritance of prophethood is the steadfastness of bearing, in the cause of performing the message. Steadfastness in bearing is the quality that the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ) must have. Whenever we Muslims inherit the honour of prophethood, we also inherit steadfastness in bearing. This is the meaning of the true saying:

﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you, and you may be witnesses over the people.﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78].

So what is the meaning of the exemplar (uswa)? The exemplar in the Messenger of God (ﷺ) requires that, since he bore with steadfastness the conveying of the message to people, we too should follow his example. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) struggled, and the followers of the Messenger of God must struggle in the cause of spreading the call. If you see the people of religion in laxity, flabbiness, and unable to struggle in conveying the message of God, know that these people will not take the inheritance of prophethood. For this reason, if you see a scholar of Islam who has no enemies, know that his inheritance from the inheritance of the prophets is deficient.

Why

Then the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah...﴾.

We have said that when the Truth says ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, it means those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah in general, and there is a difference between disbelieving in the signs of Allah and disbelieving in Allah. Why? Because belief in Allah requires the clear proofs that point to Allah, and the clear proofs of the existence of Allah are present in the universe.

So the proofs are evident. Whoever disbelieves in Allah has already disbelieved in the evidence that points to the existence of the Creator. The Truth did not say here "those who disbelieve in Allah," in order to show us that the Truth is unseen, but the clear signs are manifest in the universe. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets﴾. We should note here that the word "killing" always comes with the prophets. That is, it does not come with those who took a status beyond the mission of the prophet, who is the messenger. It is not reasonable that Allah sends a messenger to convey a method from Allah and then empowers His creation to kill the messenger. Rather, Allah sends the prophets to be behavioral examples for the believers, and none of them brings new legislation. As for the messenger, Allah sends him bearing a method from Allah. It is not reasonable that Allah chooses a servant of His servants, selects him to convey His method, and then empowers some of His creation to kill this messenger.

The creation cannot prevail against a messenger whom Allah has sent, but they may prevail against the prophets. Each of the prophets is a behavioral example, and that is why we find that each prophet worships according to the religion of the messenger before him. So why would the creation kill the behavioral example, since the prophet among them came only to be an example and did not bring a new religion? If the prophet among them had brought a new religion, we would say that fanaticism toward the religion before him is what made them kill him. But the prophet is an example in conduct, so why the killing? The prophet among them performs worship in a way that makes the people notice that the conduct the prophet practices does not come in accordance with their desires.

The people who kill the prophets are the people who refuse to conduct themselves in the Islamic manner, which means subjecting their limbs and movements to the logic of religion and the logic of Islam. Why? Because the prophet, being committed to the law of the messenger before him, when he commits to the religion of Allah among a community of non-committed people, his conduct becomes a reproach to the non-committed.

The presence of a prophet who holds fast to the law of Allah, who subjects his limbs and conduct to the method of Allah, among a community that claims to follow the religion of Allah but does not hold fast to the method of Allah, leads them to say: Why does the prophet behave in this upright way, and why does he subject his limbs to the logic of faith while we are not committed as he is? This question stirs rage and hatred toward the prophet among this community that is not committed to the religion of Allah, even if they openly declare their commitment to the religion.

They hate the prophet because he elevates himself through his Muslim conduct, and they cannot elevate themselves to be like him.

Through his conduct subject to the method of Allah, the prophet becomes a clear and manifest example, by which the difference becomes apparent between merely declaring belief in the method of Allah and behavioral commitment to the method of Allah, and the prophet's example belittles their deeds. Therefore, when we find a person committed to the religion of Allah and His method, we find the non-committed person targeting the committed one with mockery and ridicule. Why? Because the non-committed person is filled with rage and hatred toward the committed one who is able to subject himself to the method of Allah. The non-committed person asks himself:

Why is this person able to control himself and subject himself to the method of Allah while I am not able to do so? The non-committed person tries to push the committed one aside and remove him from in front of him. Why? Because the non-committed person diminishes in his own eyes and in the eyes of others when he compares himself to the one committed to the method of Allah. When others compare the conduct of the one committed to the method of Allah with the conduct of the non-committed one, they do not respect the non-committed one, so he feels psychological inferiority before the committed one and before the people, and he tries to remove the committed one and push him out of his way. Indeed, those who are not committed to the method of Allah mock and wink at those committed to the method of Allah, as the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as observers over them.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-33].

Do those clear verses not illustrate for us what the non-committed people in some of our societies say to those committed to the method of Allah? Do we not hear the words of the non-committed to the one committed to the method of Allah: "Take us under your wing"? These non-committed people fit the word of the Truth:

﴿And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided."﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 30-32].

Indeed, one of the non-committed may rejoice because he has managed to mock a believer committed to Allah. And one of the non-committed may accuse a committed person that commitment is misguidance. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, responds to this accusation with the noble words:

﴿But they had not been sent as observers over them.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 33].

The Truth responds to those who mock those committed to the method of Allah, so on the Day of Resurrection the believers will laugh at the disbelievers, and the Truth, in the majesty of His power and the completeness of His dominion, says:

﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, [reclining] on adorned couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34-36].

Thus the non-committed receive their punishment. But what of those who kill the prophets unjustly? We may ask: why did Allah describe the killing of the prophets as "unjustly," and is there any killing of a prophet that is just? There can be no just killing of a prophet. And since Allah said: ﴿and kill the prophets unjustly﴾, this noble statement came to describe a reality. He, glory be to Him, says after that, in the chain of deeds of those who kill the prophets unjustly: ﴿and kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾. They did not content themselves with killing the prophets; they also kill those among the believers who defend this prophet. How? Because when a prophet is killed, those who committed to the prophet's method and were with him must become angry and grieved.

The followers of the prophet are moved by the event of the prophet's killing. If they are able to prevent that killing, they would do so. If the followers of the prophet cannot prevent the killing of the prophet, then at the least they should enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. But the killers' tyranny goes beyond them, so they do not only kill the prophets. If someone says to them, disapproving of their behavior: "Why do you kill the prophets?", they kill him too. As for our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), we know that his enemies devised things with him by which they intended to assassinate him, and that indicates the foolishness of those who planned that assassination.

Why? Because they did not consider his situation (ﷺ). He was not only a prophet but also a messenger. And since he was a messenger, he was at once an example and a bearer of a method. Had Muhammad (ﷺ) been only a prophet, they could have killed him as they had killed the prophets before. But he is a messenger from Allah, and they saw him bearing a new method, and this method makes their dreams foolish and exposes their falsehoods, including their alteration of the scriptures revealed to them.

Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a messenger bearing a message and a method, and when they wanted to kill him as a prophet, they overlooked that he was a messenger. That is why the Truth, reassuring us and addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), said:

﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

The noble Messenger is thus a bearer of a message and protected by Allah from his enemies. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has related the account of those who kill the prophets, and wanted to reassure the believers and to reassure the Messenger about himself, and to let the opponents of the Messenger of Allah know that there is no path to killing him. So the Truth says:

﴿Say, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91].

Why does Allah use the phrase "before" here? He is making clear to us, to the Messenger, and to the enemies of Muhammad (ﷺ), that the matter of killing the prophets could have happened before the Messenger of Allah, but that this matter has come to an end, and no one dares to practice it against Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. In this way, the Truth reassured the believers and reassured the Messenger of Allah that no one would harm him. That is why the Truth said:

﴿And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

And the Truth despaired those who want to kill the Messenger of Allah, for He said to them:

﴿Say, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91].

Had the matter been one of prophethood alone, with the message of the Messenger of Allah not entering into their considerations, and their denial of his message being mere obstinacy, they would have said: "The matter of killing the prophets does not stop at 'before,' because we will make it 'after' as well," and they would have gathered their strength and killed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But Allah, glory be to Him, despaired them and dispirited them from that, and this is within the scope of the power of Allah.

If the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, speaks of a matter concerning the killing of the prophets and the killing of those who enjoin justice, was that contemporary with this statement of the Messenger, or to whom was this speech addressed? It is addressed to some of the People of the Book. It is addressed to those who believed in following those who killed the prophets before, and killed those who enjoin justice. They believed as the predecessors among the killers of the prophets believed, and they killed those who enjoin justice.

This is a rebuke to those who followed in belief a people who killed the prophets before and killed those who enjoin justice. It is a rebuke and a questioning: How do you believe as those who killed the prophets believe? And how do you follow those who did such things? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related that the Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at once, and then one hundred and seventy of the followers of the prophets stood up to denounce them for that, and they were killed. This is the meaning of this noble verse:

﴿and they kill the prophets unjustly and kill those who enjoin justice among the people, so give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 21].

Why does the Truth give them the tidings of a painful punishment? Is not the meaning of "tidings" the announcement of something pleasing within a time in which the pleasing act can be done? Tidings are always for an act that pleases, like the Truth's tidings to the believers of Paradise. The meaning of tidings of Paradise is that Allah informs the believer of something that pleases him, and the Truth gives the believer the opportunity to implement the method of Allah so that he may receive the reward and the glad tidings.

Why is the address of glad tidings directed to the sons of those who did that? Because we know that those who killed the prophets and killed those who enjoined justice among the people were not contemporaries of the revelation of this verse. The contemporaries among the People of the Book at the revelation of this verse are the sons of those who killed the prophets and killed those who enjoined

Then the Almighty says: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter...﴾.

They are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of God, and killed the prophets without right, and killed those who commanded justice among people. For these there is a painful punishment, and for them too the deed is rendered void in this world and the Hereafter, and likewise for whoever follows their path. The meaning of "habitat" (ḥabiṭat, "rendered void") is that there is no hoped-for fruit from the deed. Every deed that a sane person performs must have an aim he intends. Any deed that has no purpose is like the blow of a madman, which has no target. The sane person, before doing any action, should know its end: what benefit will it achieve? Is this benefit the best and most lasting benefit, or is it less than that?

On the basis of these measures, the sane person determines his deed. When the Almighty says: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter﴾, He, glory be to Him, wants to inform us that a person may perform an act which, outwardly, is good. So beware, O believer, of being deceived into thinking that he has done good. Why? Because an act of goodness is only credited to a person when it is accompanied by faith in the One who will reward it. If a person performs an act through which his worldly affairs may be set right, then it is a good act. So why would the deeds of these people be worthless in this world and in the Hereafter? They are worthless by the measures of faith, and the deed is worthless because it did not proceed from a believer, since that person performed the deed trusting in its outcome, not trusting in the Supreme Command.

When the believer performs a deed, he performs it trusting in the Supreme Command. Some people in our age object to Islam that it does not give a good reward to disbelievers who performed useful works for humanity. One of them says: Can anyone reasonably believe that Pasteur, who discovered microbes, and the other scientist who discovered rays, and all these scientists, go to Hell? To these we say: Yes, the Truth, in His justice, willed that; and let us and you refer to the customs of people. The one who seeks a wage for a work, from whom does he seek it? He seeks the wage from the one for whom he performed it. Was God in the minds of these scientists while they were doing these works? Their minds were occupied with humanity, and humanity gave them immortality and other worldly gains. What applies to them is the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The first of people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought forward, and God will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. He will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I fought for You until I was martyred.' He will say: 'You lie; rather you fought so that it might be said, "He is brave," and it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire. And a man who learned knowledge and taught it and recited the Qur'an, will be brought forward, and He will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. He will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I learned knowledge and taught it, and I recited the Qur'an for You.' He will say: 'You lie; rather you learned knowledge so that it might be said, "He is a scholar," and you recited the Qur'an so that it might be said, "He is a reciter," and it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire. And a man whom God made wealthy and gave of all kinds of wealth, will be brought forward, and He will make him recognise His blessings, and he will recognise them. He will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I did not leave any path in which You would love money to be spent except that I spent in it for You.' He will say: 'You lie; rather you did it so that it might be said, "He is generous," and it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face, and then thrown into the Fire."

So if the reward is from God, we may ask: was God in the minds of these scientists when they produced their inventions? God was not in their minds. Whoever seeks a wage, seeks it from the one for whom he worked. God did not waste the fruit of their works; rather their deeds yielded them remembrance, rank and elevation. God does not waste the reward of one who does good work.

﴿Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tillage; and whoever desires the tillage of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20].

I have told you before: remember the surprise that befalls one who performs an act which is outwardly good, but whose Lord was not in his mind. This applies to him the saying of the Almighty:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks to be water, until when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full. And God is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

He is surprised by the existence of God, and this God was not in his mind at the time he performed this act which is outwardly good. It is as if God says to the doer of such an act: "I was not in your mind when you performed this deed, so take your reward from the one who was in your mind." ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they have no helpers﴾. Their deeds were rendered void in this world because they may perform deeds intended to plot against Islam, so God does not enable them to do so, but rather forsakes them all. The religion of God has triumphed despite the scarcity of its means. These people have no helpers: that is, there is no one who will come and see them defeated before their adversary and come to their aid. They will not find a helper if God defeats them, for there is no one with God besides Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 23:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?...﴾

We know that when we hear the words of the Truth, ﴿Have you not seen﴾, here is the interrogative hamza, here is the negative particle "lam", and here is "tara" (see), whose meaning is that a person uses the instrument of sight, which is the eye. So when God says to His Messenger: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are called to the Book of God that it may judge between them, then a party of them turn away, while they are averse﴾, this is a call to a clear matter. But sometimes ﴿Have you not seen﴾ comes about an event whose time was before his (ﷺ) mission, so the Messenger of God did not see it, as the Truth says:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ [al-Fil: 1].

The Prophet (ﷺ) did not see the companions of the elephant. Therefore, when you hear ﴿Have you not seen﴾, if its event is contemporary, it may be a sight, and sight leads to certain knowledge, because it is the seeing of something witnessed. But if ﴿Have you not seen﴾ comes about a matter that happened earlier, or a matter that has not yet happened, it means "Have you not known?", because sight is the chief of proofs. So when God, glorified and exalted, says to His Messenger about an event the Messenger did not witness: "Have you not seen?", this means: "Have you not known?"

And someone may say: why did He not say "know" (ta'lam) and instead say "see" (tara)? Because the chief of proofs is the visible proof, so God wants to inform us with ﴿Have you not seen﴾ that we should take the information from God as if it were seen, and let your Lord be more trustworthy to you than your eye. You may not actually see this matter that God informs you of, but because the speaker is God, and there is no power that can make what God says other than what God says. Thus we have said that when God expresses a future matter that will come later, He may express it in the past tense. The Truth has said:

﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate﴾ [al-Nahl: 1].

Does His saying ﴿The command of God has come﴾ harmonize with ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾? The matter that God informs us of has come, so how can it be not hastened? "Has come" means that the matter has occurred before He spoke. We must therefore know that the One who said "has come" is able to bring it about, so it is as an actual event, a matter that needs no dispute, because no power can contend with God to bring forth a matter He willed other than as He willed. So His saying, the Truth, ﴿Have you not seen﴾, if it relates an event whose time has passed, what comes from it is knowledge, because it is the report of God; and if it relates a contemporary event, what comes from it is also knowledge, because it issues from seeing and witnessing.

And when the Truth says: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾

"Were given" (utu) draws our attention to a people to whom a method was sent down from on high. That is why the mention of the method in the Qur'an comes with "nazala" (sent down) and "anzala" (caused to descend), so that we feel the loftiness of the station from which the method descended. And what is the portion (naseeb)? We call the portion "the share" or "the lot", like someone who has twenty dinars and divides them among four, so each gets five; those five dinars are what is called a "portion" or "share", and the naseeb is a "share" or "allotment" that is attributed to the one who received it.

So why does the Truth say ﴿those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾? It is a beautiful allusion: the whole Scripture did not remain for them; what reached them and ended with them is only a small part of the Scripture. So this word alerts the Messenger and those who hear him to excuse these people, since only a small part of the Scripture reached them; only a portion of the Scripture is what reached them.

The Truth explains this in other verses:

﴿So for their breaking their covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard; they distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

The forgotten part of the Scripture was not taken by the contemporaries of the Messenger of God. We have also said: the Truth has clarified that some of them concealed part of the Scripture.

﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their sons, but indeed a party of them conceal the truth while they know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 146].

And since some of them concealed part of the Scripture, that means its concealment from their contemporaries; some of them were deceived. So part of the Scripture was forgotten, and thus erased from memory, and part of the Scripture was concealed, so it became known to some and unknown to others. Even what they did not conceal came with the wise saying:

﴿And indeed among them is a party who distort their tongues with the Scripture so that you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture; and they say, "It is from God," but it is not from God; and they speak falsehood about God while they know﴾ [Al 'Imran: 78].

So the Scripture that was sent down to them from God has been subjected to more than one aggression from them, and only a portion of the Scripture remained. This portion of the Scripture is what the Qur'an argues with these people. The Qur'an does not argue with them about what was altered among them by the deeds of their earlier rabbis and monks, but it argues with them by the portion they were given.

The Truth says: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are called to the Book of God that it may judge between them, then a party of them turn away, while they are averse.﴾ About which Book of God does this verse speak? Does it speak of the Qur'an? If it were about the Qur'an, it would have been made the judge in a matter between them and the Messenger of God. But those who were given a portion of the Scripture differed among themselves, and why do they differ among themselves? The cause is also a kind of transgression (baghy) among them.

And if the Scripture is the Qur'an, is not the Qur'an confirming what is with them?

So when they are called to have what is in their books confirmed, the call here is for the rule of the Qur'an to prevail. And what is the meaning of ﴿they are called to the Book of God﴾? The caller is the Messenger (ﷺ), and they are the ones called. And since the Truth has said ﴿were given a portion of the Scripture﴾, was their dispute over the portion in their hands or over the missing portion? It is a dispute among them over the portion in their hands, so that it is a proof that they are not trustworthy even regarding what reached them and what is written with them. When the scholars spoke about this matter, they cited an incident for it. They differed regarding Prophet Abraham, and some said: Abraham was a Jew; and some said: he was a Christian. And the Qur'an came decisively:

﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a upright Muslim (hanif musliman), and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [Al 'Imran: 67].

Why? Because the words "Jew" and "Christian" came after Abraham, and they had to free themselves from lack of discernment and arrange events according to their times. So in what matter did they differ? Did they differ over the affair of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)? Did they differ over a ruling present with them in the Torah? The call was directed to them about what? They are ﴿called to the Book of God that it may judge between them﴾, and this indicates that the word:

﴿out of transgression among themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19]

is a common condition among them. Why? Because the scholars, when they mentioned the incident in which they were called to be judged by the Book of God, said: two persons from the Jews of Khaybar, a woman of Khaybar and a man of Khaybar, had committed adultery, and both were of the nobility of the people. Those who would judge in this matter by the Torah did not want to display God's ruling that came in the Torah, which is stoning, so they devised a stratagem, which was to go to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). And why would they go in this particular matter to the Messenger of God (ﷺ)? We take the mere going to the Messenger of God as acceptance of his judgment.

But why did they not accept from the beginning everything the Messenger of God brought? They wanted to go, perhaps finding benefit in a matter they desired; otherwise they did not go to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The mere fact of their going to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gives us an idea about them: they wanted a lighter ruling other than stoning. The adulterer, who was from Khaybar, and the adulteress from Khaybar, wanted to rescue themselves from the Torah's ruling of stoning; they were of the nobility of Khaybar, and because the Jews had at that time created for themselves a temporal authority, the adulterer and the adulteress went, together with the rabbis who wanted to twist God's ruling previously sent down in the Torah, which is stoning.

When they entered upon the Messenger of God, there was one named "al-Nu'man ibn Awfa" and one named "Bahri ibn 'Amr", and they said: "O Messenger, judge between these." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, in meaning: "Do you not have a ruling?" And the Messenger added, in meaning: "I will take as judge the Torah, which is your book." What did they say? They said: "You have been just with us."

The Messenger of God had explained to them the ruling of Islam regarding adultery, which is stoning, and the remaining part of the Torah in their possession was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which contains the binding ruling, as evidence that God informed him of things that had not been in anyone's mind. He called for a section of the Torah and said, in meaning: "Which of you is most knowledgeable in the Torah?" They said a person named Abdullah ibn Suriya, so they brought him, and he was given the Torah, and was told: "Read." Abdullah ibn Suriya read, and when he passed the verse of stoning he placed his palm over it to conceal it, and read what was other than it. Abdullah ibn Salam was present, and said: "O Messenger of God, did you not see that he covered a verse with his palm and read what came after it?" Ibn Salam moved the man's palm aside and read, and behold, it was the verse of stoning.

This matter shows us that the ruling in the Holy Qur'an is the ruling in the Torah regarding adultery, and it also shows us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was blessed by God with inspirations, so he brought the part of the Torah that contains this text. Then there came after that a soldier of God's soldiers, Abdullah ibn Salam, who was a Jew who had embraced Islam, to show the people's desire for falsification and forgery.

The Islam of Abdullah ibn Salam has a remarkable story: after faith had matured in his heart, he came to the Messenger of God saying: "God has opened my breast to Islam and I have pronounced the words 'There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God'; but I love, before I announce my Islam, that you summon the chiefs of the Jews and ask them their opinion of me, for the Jews are 'a people of slander' (qawm buhtan), in them is fabrication, in them is lying, in them is misguidance." When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked the chiefs of the Jews about their opinion of Abdullah ibn Salam, they said: "Our master, son of our master, our rabbi..." etc., and they expanded in attributes of praise, eulogy and esteem. Then Abdullah ibn Salam said before them: "Now I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." The chiefs of the Jews turned around and said of Abdullah ibn Salam the opposite of what they had said first: they said, "He is our wicked one and son of our wicked one..." etc.

They turned praise into blame. Abdullah ibn Salam said: "O Messenger of God, did I not tell you that they are a people of slander? By God, I wanted to inform you of their opinion of me before I embraced Islam." That is the

This is the commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 24:

﴿That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days." And what they used to fabricate has deluded them in their religion.﴾

They turned away while they were averse to the judgment of God. They supposed that the Fire would not touch them except for a few numbered days. We should understand the meaning of "deluded" (gharrahum), and we should ask: what is ghurur (delusion)? Ghurur is aspiration toward what is not valid and will not be attained. When you say to someone, God forbid, "You are deluded (maghrur)," you mean that he is following a path that will not lead him to the desired goal. So ghurur is aspiration toward what is not valid and will not be attained, and for this reason God calls Satan "al-Gharur" (the Deluder).

﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deluder delude you concerning God. Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ [Fatir: 5-6].

It is Satan who makes certain matters seem attractive to people and urges creation to aspire to their occurrence. When they occur, there is no correctness in them, for they are among what Satan adorned; therefore their outcome does not match the aspiration toward them. The Truthful, glorified is He, says about the worldly life:

﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and competition in wealth and children, like the example of a rain whose plant pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from God and approval. And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ [al-Hadid: 20].

It is said of a man who has no experience that he is "ghirr" (naive), so he acts without experience, and therefore he gains nothing from it, and it is not valid. Thus, all of the root of "ghurur" derives from aspiration toward what is not valid and will not be attained. For this reason God named Satan "al-Gharur," because he makes us humans aspire to things that are not valid and do not occur. Hence Satan will come on the Day of Resurrection to disown those who followed him and accuse them of foolishness:

﴿And Satan will say when the matter is decided: "Indeed, God promised you a promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieved in your association of me [with God] before. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment."﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

What is the meaning of ﴿I had no authority over you﴾? Sultan (authority) is the power that convinces a person to do a certain act. It is either the authority of argument, which persuades you to do something so you do it, or the authority of force, which compels you to act. Authority, therefore, is of two kinds: the authority of argument and the authority of overpowering force. The difference between the authority of argument and the authority of overpowering force over an act is that the authority of argument persuades you to act while you remain convinced, whereas the authority of overpowering force does not persuade a person but compels him to do something. Hence Satan declares to his followers on the Day of Resurrection: "I had no authority over you; I had no argument with which to persuade you to commit sins, nor any force to compel you to act. But you were on the edge of committing sins, and I called you, and you responded to me."

﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

That is, Satan affirms that he will not come to the aid of any of those who followed him to rescue them. The word "yusrikh" means that one comes to the aid of someone in response to a call or a plea for help. Satan, then, will not rescue anyone from God's punishment, and no one will rescue Satan from God's punishment. Thus some of the People of the Book went into delusion in the religion of God, fabricating statements against God that never came from Him, and they believed their own fabrications. Would that their delusion had not been in religion, for delusion in matters other than religion has an easy calamity, but delusion in religion is the greatest calamity. Why? Because delusion in any matter follows a clear law, namely that the timing of every event is fixed by its nature. But delusion in matters of religion is different. Why? Because the event of religion is not bounded by the nature of time; it is continuous, because it is a sound method that came from the Truth to creation. If one is deluded about any particular part of worldly affairs and fails, the failure stops at that particular part alone and does not extend to the rest of time. But delusion in religion causes one's whole life to be lost, because the person has not followed the true method, and the loss and punishment extend into the second life, which is life in the Hereafter. The Truth says:

﴿And what they used to fabricate has deluded them in their religion﴾ [Al 'Imran: 24].

Fabrication (iftira') is deliberately lying. God clarifies the meaning for them, saying: if this happened from you, and you turned away from the judgment of God to which you were called in the Book of God, and you justified that by saying the Fire would not touch you except for a few numbered days, and you falsely claimed that the numbered days were the days of your worship of the calf, and you claimed that you are the sons and beloved of God, all of that is delusion and fabrications. Would that they had known the truth of these fabrications, but they are the ones who said them while knowing they are lies.

Then if that is permitted for them in this world, what will their position and condition be when God gathers them on a Day about which there is no doubt? On this the Truth says: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾

Their lying will be exposed on this Day. The Fadiha (the Exposer) has come, and the Fadiha is the Resurrection. It exposes every liar, every deceiver, and every caller to other than the truth. The Truth asks: how will they act in that life in which We gave them choice, so that they do what they want and do not do what they do not want? All of this happens from them while they know that the Truth has made the reward for those who follow God's commands, and the punishment for those who depart from God's will. How will they conduct themselves when the Truth strips them of choice and the Day of Resurrection arrives? In the world they possessed God's gift of the power to choose between alternatives, and God established in their make-up that all their limbs are subject to their will as humans created by God. Some of them are able to use their limbs in what pleases God, while others use their limbs, which were subjected to them by God's favour, in what does not please God. As we all know, the limbs are subject to the human will, and it is the human will that chooses between alternatives. But what will these people do on the Day of Resurrection? The limbs that used to obey those who departed from God's method in action will not obey them on this great Day, because obedience is a choice to act and to obey, and on the Day of Resurrection the limbs will not be compelled to the human will. On the Day of Resurrection the quality of compulsion and subjection to the human will will be dissolved from the limbs, and the limbs will return to their own nature:

﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do. On that Day God will pay them their due reckoning in full, and they will know that God is the Manifest Truth.﴾ [al-Nur: 24-25].

The tongue was the instrument of declaring disbelief, and on the Day of Resurrection it will testify against the disbeliever. The hand was the instrument of disobedience to God, and on the Day of Resurrection it will testify against its owner. The skins will also testify. The limbs were subject to the will of their owners and did what they wanted them to do, but they were performing the act that disobeys God while disliking that act. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 25].

How their condition will be on the Day when God gathers them for requital, on a Day about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty regarding its coming. This Day is certainly coming, because the proofs of its existence are established, despite their hostility toward God. God, the Just and the True, does not wrong them; rather He will take them to account by the measures of justice.

As soon as you hear the word "malik" (king/owner), you should know that there is the word "mulk" with a ḍamma on the mīm (مُلك), and another word "milk" with a kasra on the mīm (مِلك). The word مِلك means that a person has ownership of some things, such as a person's ownership of his clothes, his books and his belongings. But the one who possesses the owner of this milk, you call him مُلك. If this ownership is in what is apparent to us, we call it "the realm of mulk" (ʿālam al-mulk), which is the observable world. If this ownership is in what is hidden, we call it "the realm of malakūt" (ʿālam al-malakūt, the unseen dominion). So here we are faced with مِلك, مُلك and مَلكوت. Therefore, when Allah the Exalted revealed Himself to our master Ibrahim, Khalil al-Rahman (the Friend of the Most Merciful), and disclosed to him what is hidden from the eyes and what is manifest, He said, glorified is He:

﴿And thus did We show Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain (in faith).﴾ [al-An'am: 75]

That is, Allah the Exalted willed that our master Ibrahim should witness the malakūt in the heavens and the earth, that is, all things, the apparent and the hidden, concealed from the eyes of the servants. Thus we see the stages of possession as follows: مِلك, meaning that a person owns something, and we call him an owner (mālik) of things, so he is the owner of his possessions and the owner of his goods. As for the one who possesses the person who possesses things, we call him مُلك, meaning that he owns the one who owns things. What is apparent in the first case we call مِلك, for every person has ownership of some things. After that, one inclines toward the more general, so that the ownership of the owners of properties is attributed to one king. Thus ownership with regard to a human being comes down to this: a person owns something and becomes an owner, and another person whom Allah appoints over a group of people becomes a king (malik). This is in the human sphere.

As for the divine sphere, we ascend to see who owns every owner and king, and that is Allah the Exalted. No one should suppose that a person has come to own anything, or any rank in this world, without Allah's will in it. Every person owns by what Allah wills for him of a mission. If the servants go astray, Allah must set over them an unjust king. Why? Because the righteous may not know how to train people well.

﴿And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn.﴾ [al-An'am: 129]

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is saying: "O you good one (al-khayyir, with the yāʾ doubled), place one foot upon the other and do not defile your hand by taking revenge on the wrongdoer. I will set the authority of a greater wrongdoer over this lesser wrongdoer. I hold you too high to do that, and I will avenge you. And you, O good one, are free of committing wrongs in My sight." That is why we find the saying of the Truth:

﴿And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn.﴾ [al-An'am: 129]

We all know the common saying: "Allah sets the wrongdoers over the wrongdoers." If those who were wronged were empowered over those who wronged them, they would not do to them what the wrongdoers do to one another. The Truth sets wrongdoers over wrongdoers, and spares the people of goodness from the position of taking revenge on those who wronged them.

So in this life we find "mālik" and "malik", and above all that there is "Mālik al-Mulk" (Owner of the Kingdom). Allah did not say "Malik al-Mulk" (King of the Kingdom), because if we examine the matter of ownership carefully, we will find no owner except Allah. ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty﴾. He is the one who disposes of His dominion. Beware of supposing that anyone has ruled over the creation of Allah without Allah's will. Rather, when people depart from obedience to Allah, Allah sets over them a tyrannical ruler. That is why the Truth, glorified is He, says in His sacred hadith:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will fold the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then He will take them in His right hand, then He will say: 'I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?' Then He will fold the earth in His left hand, then He will say: 'I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?'"

Beware, O believer, of supposing that anyone has taken kingship out of anger from Allah. Rather, kingship is what Allah wills for whoever disciplines the servants by it. If the king is unjust in his discipline, Allah sends someone to wrong him. And whoever sees the injustice of this king or that ruler, it is possible that Allah will show him that this king or that ruler is himself wronged. This is the wise word that confirms to us that He, glorified is He, alone is the Owner of the Kingdom.

The Truth, glorified is He, commands His noble Messenger: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty﴾. The word "Allahumma" alone contains one of the linguistic wonders. The Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic tongue, and the Arab people were eloquent in speech, expression and rhetoric. The Truth willed that the divine name "Allah" have a unique distinction in the Arabic language.

Arabic establishes a clear rule: one does not address with "yā" a noun that carries the definite article (al-), such as "al-rajul" (the man). So one does not say "yā rajul", but says "yā ayyuhā al-rajul" (O you, the man). But the language that Allah made easy for His servants singles out the name of Majesty (Allah) for sanctification, so it is permissible for the servants to say "yā Allah". This name, in its majesty, has distinction even in its pronunciation.

We may observe that the Arabs, the Quraysh unbelievers, who were people of eloquence, did not notice this. It is as if Allah compels even the unbelievers by making the name of Majesty distinctive even on their tongues, so they say along with the believers "yā Allah". As for the other names preceded by the definite article, you cannot say "yā al-rajul" or "yā al-ʿAbbās", but you must say "yā ayyuhā al-rajul" or "yā ayyuhā al-ʿAbbās", and you do not even say in addressing the Prophet "yā al-Nabī", but rather "yā ayyuhā al-Nabī".

But when addressing Allah with a call, we say "yā Allah". It is a distinction that the Truth, glorified is He, draws our attention to, by which He alone is singled out. Also, we have not seen in the Arabic language a proper name to which the particle "tāʾ" is attached as the particle of oath except Allah: we say "tallāhi" (by Allah). We have never found anyone saying "tazayd" or "taʿamr".

We find the tāʾ as a particle of oath only with the word Allah, and we also find no proper name in the Arabic language from which the "yā" of the vocative is dropped and replaced with the mīm, except the name Allah, so we say "Allahumma". All this is to indicate that the word in itself has the distinction of what it names. "Qul Allahumma" (Say: O Allah). It is as if the omission of the vocative particle here teaches us that Allah alone is the one called without a vocative particle: "Allahumma". In some dialects they combine the yā and the mīm, as in the words of the poet:

*"Innī idhā mā ḥādithun alammā*
*aqūlu yā Allahumma yā Allahumma"*

It is a distinction belonging to the One who has the highest distinction. ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty﴾. Someone might ask why the Truth did not say "Malik al-Mulk" (King of the Kingdom). Here we must know that a day will come when no one will have any ownership except Allah, the sole Owner. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Exalted in degrees, Lord of the Throne; He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that He may warn of the Day of Meeting. The day they will come out, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. "To whom belongs dominion this Day?" "To Allah, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 15-16]

The Truth's saying here, "Owner of sovereignty", makes clear to us that the ownership of Allah, which is everlasting and capable, is evident, manifest and affirmed. If Allah had described His essence as "King of the Kingdom", that would mean that there are humans who own alongside Allah. No, He is the Truth alone, the Owner of sovereignty. Since Allah is the Owner of sovereignty, He gives it to whom He wills and takes it from whom He wills. And here we note that the Truth's saying that He is the Owner of sovereignty, who gives sovereignty to whom He wills and takes it from whom He wills, comes after the process of argument, and after some of the People of the Book fled from applying the judgment of Allah after they were called to it. A faction of them turned away and withdrew from the judgment of Allah, and they justified that by claiming that they are the sons of Allah and His beloved, and that the Fire would not touch them except for a few counted days.

All these are choices of the kindness of Allah placed before these servants: choices between following the judgment of Allah or following the judgment of desire. But they chose only the bad choice, the judgment of desire. That is why Allah brings the report of the Day that will come, when no one will have any power or choice.

The right of choice exists for us in this world, and we must choose well in light of the method of Allah.

Let us reflect on this example that the pure Prophetic biography (al-sīra al-nabawiyya) has related to us: when the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwat al-Aḥzāb) came, in which all the adversaries of the call gathered, and the Jews busied themselves with intrigue and sowing discord, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on the advice of Salman al-Farisi, decided to dig a trench (khandaq) around the city of Medina. The meaning of "khandaq" is a stretch of land dug in a way that obstructs advance. The fighters knew that the horse could leap a certain distance of meters.

While digging the trench, the believers tried to make it wider than the reach of the horses. Let us look at the precision of the administration of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Salman al-Farisi suggested that the trench be dug, and it appears that he took the idea from his environment; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted the idea and approved it, and the Muslims carried it out.

Thus not everything the unbelievers did was rejected by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Rather, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted the application of all beneficial works, whether or not the unbelievers had done them before. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that the digging was exhausting because of the hardness of the earth and its rockiness in some places. Therefore he set a portion of forty cubits for every ten of the Companions, and in this way the noble Messenger distributed the work and the responsibility, and he did not leave the matter to each group, lest they rely on others.

Distributing responsibility means that each group knows the clear measure of work it shares with the other groups. Someone might ask: why did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not assign the task to each individual on his own? We say: it is the wisdom of administration and firmness that made the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recognize a clear truth, namely that the Companions who were digging were not equal in ability and effort. Therefore he wanted every weak one to be supported by nine of the Companions.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not make the matter common property, but there was a definition of responsibility. Yet he did not make the responsibility specified in an initial and fixed way for each individual, so that the strong would help the weak among them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) covered the weak with the strength of his brothers, and whenever a weak person is among ten brothers who carry for him and dig, his attitude toward his companions becomes love and affection, and the strong has poured out his bounty upon the weak.

Among the group of ten was ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, and Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him). When they came to dig, they encountered an area called "al-Kaʾūd", and the meaning of "al-Kaʾūd" is the place which is hard while digging. The digger, when he digs the earth, may find the earth soft and continue digging; but if he meets a hard piece in the earth, he cannot break it with his pickaxe because it is solid rock, so it is said of him: "akdā al-ḥāfir" (the digger has been stopped).

When ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, Salman al-Farisi, al-Mughira and others encountered this hard rock, they said to Salman: "Go and raise our matter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." From this we learn a lesson, which is that the one assigned by the one who assigns him a task, when he finds something that prevents him from performing the

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) brings evidence from the laws of the cosmos and the signs of God in existence to confirm the matter of ﴿Indeed, You are over all things Competent﴾. He says, and His word is the truth: ﴿You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night, and You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account.﴾

The Truth tells us: you have a phenomenon that you observe, namely night and day, and another phenomenon, namely life and death. The phenomenon of night and day is known to all of us, because it is one of the wondrous signs. The Truth says about it: ﴿You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night.﴾ The Truth did not create the day with a fixed amount of time, the same every time. No. He, glorified is He, willed that the night should sometimes fall short of the day by five hours, and sometimes the day should exceed the night by five hours.

We may ask ourselves: Do the five hours decrease from the night or the day all at once and suddenly? Does the day surprise us after being twelve hours to become seventeen hours? Does the night surprise us in its length or shortness? No. The matter comes gradually, by cycle, so that you do not perceive it. There is a kind of movement called the "ratchet movement" (al-harakah al-tarsiyyah). When we look at the clock, do we see the whole time? No. Each gear has a moment in which it stops, and when it stops we push it so that it repeats its cycle and works. If we look carefully at the minute hand, we can notice this.

So there is a period of stopping and stillness between the movement of the minute hand from one minute to another. This kind of movement we call "ratchet movement." There is another movement, which we call "flowing movement" (al-harakah al-insiyabiyyah), in which every part of time has movement, as happens in the phenomenon of growth in humans, plants and animals.

A newborn child does not grow from morning to evening in a noticeable or perceptible way. He grows in fact without our noticing it. He may increase by a millimeter in height, and this millimeter is spread across every fraction of seconds of the day. The child does not remain at the same weight and height for twenty-four hours of the day and then suddenly grow at the end of the day. No. The growth of the child each day takes place in a manner in which the power of growth pervades every fraction of seconds of the day. This process requires extreme precision in distributing the particles of the event over the particles of time. This is the greatness of the Creating Power, which man remains unable to attain forever.

I have told you once: if one of you looks at his newborn son, and keeps looking at him throughout his life, he will never notice his son growing at all. But when a person is absent from his son for a month or months, and then returns, he sees in his son the sum of the growth of the months during which he was away, and it has become clear. If a person plants a certain plant and sits watching it, he will never see that plant grow. Why? Because the particles grow without the ability of a person to perceive how they grow.

We should know that everything that grows also shrinks, and there is no ability in man for direct observation of that. There are other examples in life. We take this example: when scientists photographed the earth from artificial satellites, the first images of New York City were of a simple point. When scientists enlarged this image, the details appeared, such as the streets and other things. Where were the streets in this small point? The streets had shrunk during the photographing to a degree that makes it impossible for the human faculties of perception to see them. Therefore it is necessary to enlarge this image so that man can see them. We see a distant thing as small, and the closer we bring it, the larger it appears to us.

So God's saying ﴿You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night﴾ is a call to human attention that night and day are not separated by a sharp boundary that gives each of them an equal share. No. By His power, the Truth makes the night enter into the day and the day enter into the night. The meaning of "tuliju" (cause to enter) is "tudkhilu" (cause to enter). An example of this: the muezzin calls for the Maghrib prayer on one day at five o'clock, and on other days the muezzin calls for the Maghrib prayer at seven o'clock. This does not happen suddenly, and Maghrib does not leap from five to seven. Rather it happens smoothly and gradually. From this we receive the lesson and the example.

O servant, if you see a kingdom established on a rooted civilization, know that there are subtle factors, which you cannot see with the eye, that gnaw at this kingdom until the day comes when this kingdom ends. Thus civilizations collapse after reaching the peak of advancement, when people attain enormous preparations and immense capabilities, because the factors of collapse gnaw inside these civilizations.

The Truth, by drawing our attention to the majesty of His power and the greatness of the precision of His craftsmanship, uses the example of the night and day: ﴿You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night.﴾ Then the Supreme Truth brings us another example, saying: ﴿And You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living,﴾ which is absolute power without causes.

This pause here makes us see how we have been guided by what God has bestowed upon some of His creatures of discovering some of His secrets in His cosmos. Science has reached the knowledge that everything has a specific life. We see that a leaf of a plant has reactions and a specific life, and we see that the atom has reactions and a specific life. Reaction means movement, and life, as you know, is manifested by movement. The only difference is that there is a difference in perceiving life between the common people and the elite. The common man does not know that the sperm has life, and that the seed has life; only the elite among the people of knowledge know that.

The common people do not know that the seed has visible life, and that hidden growth exists in it, and the common people do not know that there is a difference between a living thing and something capable of living.

An example of this is the date pit, which we take and plant so that a palm tree grows from it. It is a pit that remains merely a pit until a person takes it and places it in its environment, so that a palm tree grows from it.

So the pit is capable of life. When we look at grains of soil, we cannot place them in an environment to make something from them, yet the grain of soil has movement. Scientists say that the movement present in the heads of a single box of matches is enough to run an electric train that could go around the earth for a number of years.

These are matters known to the elite and not to the common people. When we look at the common people, when they hear the true word ﴿And You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living﴾, they would say: the example of this is the date pit, and they knew that the palm tree grows from the pit. But the elite investigated and discovered that inside the pit there is life, and they came to know how it grows. Scientists came to know that everything in existence has a life suited to its mission. Life is not only the apparent movement and the clear growth before the eye. No, there is life in everything.

The common people can find a clear example that God brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. As for the elite, they know God's power through their knowledge that everything has life. If we take some soil in an isolated place where we place seed, nothing will come out of it. This soil is what scientists describe as "dead in the first degree." As for the pit that you can take and place in this soil, scientists describe it as "dead of the second degree."

When we place the "dead in the first degree" to become an environmental medium for the "dead of the second degree," results appear that demonstrate the life of both the soil and the pit together. The Qur'an has touched on this with delicate touch, because when the Qur'an addresses things where minds may stand puzzled, it deals with them in a way that every mind can accept. The mind of the elite accepts it and the mind of the common people accepts it too, because when the Qur'an touches any matter, it touches it with a comprehensive, elevated expression that everyone accepts; then the human mind discovers new details in this matter.

For example, the Qur'an did not tell us that the atom has movement and life and that it contains charges of a certain kind of energy. Rather, the Qur'an dealt with the atom and other things with divine, capable explanation, especially since these things did not give rise to disagreement over ruling or method. If a person at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an had known that the atom has life, what would that add to the rulings? And if someone had proven that the atom has no life, what would that reduce from the rulings of the faithful method? The matter, in terms of rulings, would neither increase nor decrease. When we take the Qur'an as those who are mindful of it, and understand the indications of its words, we find that the word "life" has an opposite, which is "death." The Truth, glorified is He, left the word "death" in some places of the Noble Book and mentioned another word, which is "perishing" (al-halak). The Truth, glorified is He, said:

{So that whoever perishes would perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives would live upon clear evidence. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.} [al-Anfal: 42].

"Perishing" here is the opposite of life. Why did the Truth not mention the word "death" here? Because He is the Creator, the most knowing of His servants. He knows that servants may differ over the matter of "death." Some of them define the dead as that which has no movement, no sensation, and no growth. But this dead thing has a life suited to it, like the life of an atom, or the life of a grain of sand, or the life of any dead thing. Thus we learned from the previous verse that life is opposed by perishing. The Truth, glorified is He, says about the Hereafter, to clarify for us what will happen on the Day of Resurrection:

{Everything is perishing except His Face} [al-Qasas: 88].

The Truth made an exception for the Face, or the Divine Self, and everything else is perishing. Since everything is perishing, this means that everything was alive, even if we do not perceive its life. So true life exists in everything in a manner suited to it: sometimes you perceive it, and sometimes you do not.

Thus His noble saying ﴿And You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living﴾ may be taken in the general custom, or it may be taken in the specialized custom, that is, the custom of the scholars. Since this is an apparent matter in existence, like the entering of the night into the day and the entering of the day into the night, that is, the Truth causes the day to enter the night and the night to enter the day. In the language, they call a man's inner circle, that is, his closest friends, "al-waliyjah" (the intimate). Why? Because they penetrate him. For if you want to know the secret of a person, sit with a friend of his or with some of his friends who are close to him.

Therefore the matter of the night entering into the day and the day entering into the night came with complete clarity, and the matter of life and death came in words that both the common people and the elite can understand. If these phenomena are some of God's capabilities, then who would deem it great for God to have His power, in that He gives sovereignty to whom He wills, honors whom He wills, takes away sovereignty from whom He wills, and humbles whom He wills? The proof has come from the cosmic signs, and we see it every day with our own eyes. {Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will, You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will; in Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are}

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 28:

﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, unless you but fear a danger from them. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

You do not take the disbeliever as an ally (wali) except when the signs of strength in him are clear to you, and the signs of weakness in you are clear.
