When you reflect on the meaning of the word "wali", you find that its meaning is "helper" (mu'in). When you say "Allah is the Wali", we use the word here in its absolute sense. The word wali is attributed to Allah absolutely, and it is attributed in a relative and limited sense to the creation of Allah. The Almighty says:

﴿Allah is the Wali of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257].

Allah is Wali in an absolute sense, and the Almighty says:

﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [Yunus: 62].

The singular of "awliya' Allah" (allies of Allah) is "wali Allah", so the believer is the wali of Allah, and the Almighty says:

﴿There, guardianship belongs to Allah, the Truth. He is best in reward and best in outcome.﴾ [al-Kahf: 44].

Thus we observe that wilaya is sometimes attributed to Allah and sometimes to the creation of Allah. Allah is the Wali of the believer, and this is understood. We may ask: how can the believer be the wali of Allah? We can understand this meaning as follows: Allah is the helper of the believing servants, so Allah is the Wali of those who believe, that is, their helper and strengthener. And the awliya' of Allah are those who support Allah, so Allah supports them – He, the Exalted, is the Truth who said:

﴿O you who believe, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm.﴾ [Muhammad: 7].

Was Allah not able to take revenge on the disbelievers once and finish with them? But the Almighty said:

﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them, and give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14].

Indeed, if the Truth were to fight them, His fighting them would be a hidden matter, and they might say that these are cosmic matters in existence. Therefore He brings fighting for the believers whom the disbelievers have oppressed. So at one time "wali" is used and what is meant is "helper" (mu'in), and at another time the word "wali" is used and what is meant is "one who is helped" (ma'an). For if you are a wali of Allah, and Allah is your wali, then He, the Truth, is your "helper" (mu'in), and you are the "one helped" (ma'an).

The Almighty wills that His method prevail through the faith of His creation in it; otherwise the Almighty would have used the absoluteness of His power to compel people to be obedient, for none can escape the power of Allah. Man must think clearly and know that his life is between two brackets: the bracket of his birth and the bracket of his death, and man controls neither of the two brackets, so why does he try to control the distance between the two brackets? Thus the cosmic mechanisms are in the hand of Allah and move like a clock. He, the Exalted, says:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

Nothing has departed from the will of the Supreme Creator. Rather, the Almighty took these matters in the movement of the heavens and the earth by the force of His dominance and the power of His might, so nothing escapes from His hand. As for the servants, He, the Exalted, wills to take a people by the love of their hearts.

Faith is a path left to the choice of man. It is true that the Truth is able to bring people as believers, but He wills to see who comes to Him while being free to choose not to come.

The subjugation of things shows us the attribute of Allah's complete power, and the choices of man are what show the attribute of being loved by Allah. Allah wants us to see His power, and wants from us that we turn to Him with love. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers.﴾ Why? Because the disbelievers, even if they pretend to be your allies, O believer, they try to make you feel secure with them and at ease with them, and perhaps they infiltrate subtly and delicately, entering upon you through the gate of affection, while they are not sincere in that, for as long as they are disbelievers, there is fundamentally no meeting between faith and disbelief. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah.﴾

Whoever takes these people as his allies has no share in the help of Allah. Why? Because he believed that these disbelievers are able to do something for him. Therefore Allah warns us and makes the meaning clearer, meaning: beware of being deceived by the strength of the disbelievers and taking them as allies. Do not say, O believer: "What shall I do?" For Allah does not require of you anything except that you exert what effort you can, and therefore He, the Exalted, said:

﴿Prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know but whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.﴾ [al-Anfal: 60].

The Truth did not say: "Prepare against them what will overcome them," but He said: ﴿Prepare against them what you are able﴾. The believer must do what is within his ability and leave the rest to Allah. Therefore there is a matter at which the intellect may stop, but Allah reassures us; that is: do not fear, and do not think that their large numbers are able to defeat you, and do not ask: "What shall I do, O Allah?" The Truth has taught us not to say that, and has taught us what protects us from this situation, so He said:

﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved; so strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip.﴾ [al-Anfal: 12].

So when Allah casts terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, what can they do, whatever their number or equipment? Is that not an end to the matter? Terror is a soldier among the soldiers of Allah, and therefore the believer must not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Why? So that the saying of the Truth does not apply to him: "Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah." Then the Truth gives the exception: ﴿unless you but fear a danger from them, and Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

The Almighty Allah gives the method to man, and He is His creation, glory be to Him; He knows all his instincts, emotions and thoughts, and that circumstances may come upon him that are stronger than his capacity. Therefore the Truth treats man as a creature of limited capabilities. In another place the Truth gave another exception, saying:

﴿Whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless he is turning aside for battle or withdrawing to a company, has certainly drawn anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [al-Anfal: 16].

The Truth says in this place of Surat Ali 'Imran: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except that you but fear a danger from them.﴾

"Taqah" is derived from "wiqayah" (protection). They may be extremely strong, and the believer may not, by strong probability, be able to overcome them, and they are the disbelievers, so there is no objection to the believer guarding himself against their evil.

Taqiyya is a concession from Allah. It is related that Musaylima the Liar brought two men from among the Muslims and said to one of them: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" The believer said: "Yes." Musaylima said: "And do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" The believer said: "Yes." Musaylima then brought the other Muslim and said to him: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" The believer said: "Yes." Musaylima said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" The second believer said: "I am deaf." How did the believer answer with a claim of deafness? Musaylima knew that he was feigning deafness, so he seized him and killed him, and the matter was referred to our master the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and what did he say? He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "As for the one who was killed, he proclaimed the truth, so good tidings to him; and as for the other, he took the concession of Allah." So taqiyya is a concession, and openly declaring the truth is a virtue.

'Ammar ibn Yasir took the concession, and Bilal ibn Rabah adhered to steadfastness.

Let us look at the wisdom of legislation in this matter. Every principle of good comes to confront a phenomenon of evil in existence, and this principle needs a method that comes from a Wise One above it, and it requires firmness of certainty and strength of resolve, as well as the endurance of a method. Endurance is for the sake of the method remaining for people, and resolve is for the sake of the believer confronting the adversaries. Had Allah not legislated taqiyya by His saying:

﴿except one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith﴾ [al-Nahl: 106].

We would indeed realize the self-sacrifice that ransoms the methods of truth by sacrificing life cheaply in the cause of Allah. But suppose every believer took that stance; who then would carry the knowledge of Allah to others? Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, legislates taqiyya so that those who carry the method remain. He establishes for us sacrifice for the creed, and legislates for us taqiyya for the survival of the creed. The Truth has brought both matters: the matter of standing against falsehood by martyrdom in the cause of truth, and the matter of taqiyya as protection for some of the creation, so that the true method is not lost should a tyrant come and uproot all the believers. Therefore the Truth legislates what keeps a people for sacrifice and keeps a people for survival, to carry the method of Allah. Have we now understood why taqiyya came? Because the Truth, glory be to Him, wills a method that populates the earth and is inherited by successive generations. Had the Truth not legislated taqiyya by His saying:

﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief – except one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith – but those who open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾

[al-Nahl: 106].

Self-sacrifice in belief would have been established, and if self-sacrifice alone were established, the matter of the method would be exposed to vanish, and no other people would inherit it. Therefore Allah legislated taqiyya so that some people remain around the candle of faith, preserving its light; perhaps one will take from its flame and it will shine forth light. Therefore there is no alliance from a believer with a disbelieving people except that he guards himself from them with caution, why? Because Allah warns us of Himself by His saying: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

Beware of embracing with an open heart the conduct that the disbelievers place before you and saying: "I am practising taqiyya." Rather, the matter must be clear in your soul, and you must know why you practised taqiyya: did you do it to keep the method of good in existence, or for other than that? Did you do it so as not to bring all the soldiers of good to extinction, or otherwise? If you practise taqiyya consciously and preserve yourself for the task of preserving the faith-based method, then you are people of faith, and you must know well that the Truth has said:

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return.﴾ It is the Truth saying to the believers: beware of clothing taqiyya with something your souls desire, why? Because the Truth has defined it: { Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief – except one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith – but whoever opens his breast to disbelief

Then, after that, the Truth says: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and Allah has power over all things.﴾

Because a person may practice taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation) as a mere outward formality, but the believer never does that at all. Why? Because the warning is clear in this verse. Here someone might say: concealing what is in the breast is what Allah knows, but disclosing what is in the breast is something another than Allah has also known. So why did this statement come? This wise statement came because it may occur to you that Allah is the Unseen, so He knows only the unseen and does not know the witnessed. But Allah is not veiled from one place by another, or one time from another time. So beware of believing that Allah is the Unseen and therefore knows only the unseen. Indeed, the Truth knows the unseen and knows what has come forth into existence.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 30:

Then after that the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿On the Day when every soul will find whatever good it has done brought forward...﴾

Action in itself is a phenomenon that occurs and then ends. How, then, will a person come on the Day of Resurrection and find his deeds? Undoubtedly he will find the recompense for his deeds. Until now we have been saying this, but when God opens to some minds, and they discover secrets of the secrets of the universe, the explanation of this verse may go beyond what we say. They are now able to film a recording of some action, and after a period of time one person says to another: "Look at what you did and what you said." The action recorded on the tape is present and depicted. If we human beings can do this by our own means, then what of the means of God, glory be to Him? They must surpass us in power. He, the Truth, knows everything, in the breast, or in the heavens or on the earth. The divine judgment encompasses the whole universe, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a clear register.﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

The Truth concludes this verse with His saying: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ He is the Capable who knows our heedlessness, so He always alerts us to the perfection of His power, as He said in a verse before it: ﴿Indeed, You are over all things competent.﴾ We are created by Allah, and He is the Supreme Capable, capable of everything, and He brings to each of us the book of his reckoning on the Day of Reckoning:

﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record!"﴾ [al-Haqqah: 19].

So whoever has this matter fixed in his mind, let him say: ﴿Whatever good it has done, brought forward﴾, meaning that he finds the recompense for his deed. As for what the soul has done of evil, it wishes that between it and that there were a long distance, that is, a far-off limit, and the person says to himself: "Would that it had not come!" And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants.﴾ The Truth, glory be to Him, repeats the warning so that we may keep in mind His absolute power, but He is also Kind and Merciful toward us.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 31:

After that, the Truth (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: If you truly love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins.…﴾

We should know that every "Qul" (say) in the Qur'an comes as evidence that what follows it is a conveyance (balagh) from the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from his Lord: a conveyance of the command and of the thing commanded. Some of those in whose hearts is deviation (zaygh) say: "It would have been possible for the Messenger to say: ﴿If you love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you﴾ without the 'Say'." To these we say: If the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had done that, he would have conveyed "the thing commanded" but would not have conveyed the command in its entirety. Why? Because the command is in "Say", and the thing commanded is ﴿If you truly love Allah﴾. It is as if the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in every conveyance from Allah that began with "Say", was conveying "the command" and conveying "the thing commanded," which indicates that he is a conveyer from Allah of everything he conveys from Allah.

As for those who say: "Let 'Say' be deleted from the Qur'an, and instead of saying ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾, let us pronounce it: 'Allah is One'." To these we say: You want the Messenger to have conveyed "the thing commanded" but not to have conveyed "the command."

The Truth says: ﴿Say: If you truly love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾. What does this verse indicate? They must have claimed that they love Allah, but they did not follow Allah in what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought. It is as if they made love for Allah one thing and following the obligation (taklif) another thing. Allah, glorified and exalted, has over His creation existence (ijad) and provision (imdad), and that is a blessing; and Allah has over His creation the favour of obligation (taklif), because if the obligation returns benefit to the one obligated (al-mukallaf, with a fatha on the kaf and a shadda on the lam) and nothing returns from it to the one who obligates (al-mukallif, with a kasra on the kaf), then this is a blessing from the one who obligates.

The Truth, glorified is He, has no need of anyone or from anyone. When the Truth, glorified is He, obligates us, He wishes us only to follow the law for preserving human life. We have struck the example — and to Allah belongs the highest example — of the machine made by human hands. The engineer who designed it sets for it a maintenance law and a list of instructions on how to use it; these are summed up in "do this" and "do not do that," and he chooses for this machine a specific place and an organized method of use.

So, placing a list of the laws for the maintenance and use of a machine and printing it in a small booklet is for the benefit of the one who uses the product. This is in the realm of human craftsmanship; how much more so the craftsmanship of Allah, mighty and majestic. Allah has existence for the human being, Allah has provision for the human being, and Allah has obligation for the human being, and the Truth has made obligation in the service of existence and provision. If the Truth had not given us the system of the movement of life in "do" and "do not do," our existence and provision would have been corrupted for us. Among the completeness of the Truth's blessing upon creation is that He brought obligation into being. And if the servant has recognized Allah's worth and loves Him for existence and provision, then the servant should also recognize his Lord's favour upon him in accepting the obligations, and that the servant should love his Lord because He imposed upon him the obligations of faith.

You may love Allah, but you must notice the difference between your loving Allah and Allah's loving you. Obligation may appear hard upon you, so you neglect it; therefore we say to you: It is not enough that you love Allah for the blessing of His creating and provisioning you, because by that you have neglected the blessing of His obligation, which returns to you with good. The blessing of obligation returns to you with all good when you perform it, O human being, so do not neglect it. It is possible to find servants who love Allah because He created them and provided them with all the means of life, but Allah's love for His servant depends on the servant knowing His blessing — glorified is He — in the obligation. Allah loves the servant who knows the value of the blessing in the obligation.

In our human realm we see a person loving another person who does not reciprocate the affection, and al-Mutanabbi said: "You are the beloved, but I seek refuge in Him from being a beloved who is not loved."

Al-Mutanabbi seeks refuge from loving one who does not return his love. So too those who claim that they love Allah, because they are slaves to His goodness in existence and provision, and then afterwards they disdain, or are unable to bring their souls to perform the obligation — to these we say: You have withheld half of love for Allah, because Allah does not obligate you for His benefit, but He obligates you for your benefit, since obligation is no less than existence and provision.

Why? Because obligation contains the welfare of existence and provision. Love, as we know, is the affection of the heart, and when you measure the heart's affection toward Allah, we see its effects and its work: pardon, mercy, and good pleasure.

When you measure the heart's affection from the servant to Allah, it is in obedience. The love which is the heart's affection is within every person's capacity, but the Truth requires from the heart's affection the affection of the body (qalib), and the human being must seek out Allah's obligations to perform them, out of obedience and love for Allah, so that he receives Allah's love for him in its effects: pardon, mercy, and good pleasure.

The love that is required by the Sharia differs from love in its narrow conception. I say this so that we all may know that the Truth, glorified is He, is established in justice (qa'im bil-qist), so He does not burden with excess, nor impose beyond capacity or beyond ability. The love intended for Allah in the obligation is rational love ("al-hubb al-'aqli"), and we must distinguish between rational love and emotional love. Emotional love has no fixed law. I do not say to you, "You must love so-and-so with emotional love," because that emotional love has no law. A person loves his son even if he is of little intelligence or afflicted with a defect; he loves him with his emotion, and he dislikes the one of little intelligence with his reason.

And when a person sees the son of his neighbour, or even the son of his enemy, and he is outstanding, he loves the neighbour's son or the enemy's son with his reason, but he does not love the neighbour's or the enemy's son with his emotion. The proof of this is that when a person has beautiful things, he gives them to his own son, not to the sons of the neighbours. There is, then, a difference between love of the reason and love of the emotion.

Obligation always falls within the scope of what can be done, and that is rational love. Along with rational love, a person may ask himself: what would my life be, and how, if I had not embraced this religion? And what would the world be, and how, if not for Allah's mercy upon us when He honoured us with this religion and sent us this noble Messenger? This is the discourse of reason and the love of reason.

Love may rise up and become emotional as well, but what is obligated is rational love, not emotional love. Therefore we must pay attention to what is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his child, his father, and all people."

Our master Umar stopped at this point and said: "Is it reasonable that love for you should be more than for my own self? I love you more than my wealth, or my child, but not more than my self — for in the self there is something." Thus we see the sincerity of Umar ibn al-Khattab's faith-response, may Allah be pleased with him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, repeated it a second and a third time, and our master Umar understood that it had become an obligation, and understood that it must be from the love that is within capacity, which is rational love, not emotional love. Then Umar said: "Now, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Now, O Umar" — meaning: your faith is now complete. That is, our master Umar had understood the intended meaning of this love, which is rational love.

Here we want to give an example so that this matter does not become an obstacle in hearts or minds — we say, and to Allah belongs the highest example: a person looks at a medicine that is bitter in taste and asks himself, "Do I love it or not?" A person loves this medicine with his reason, not with his emotion.

Rational love, then, is the affection of one who knows that a thing is good for you and beneficial to you, even if your self abhors it; and when the limits of a thing's benefit become clear to you, you love it with your emotion. So what is required for the faith-obligation is "rational love," and after that it rises to become "emotional love." Thus is the Truth's word: ﴿If you truly love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾. And this love is not a mere claim. When a person among us claims that he loves another person, everything connected to that person becomes beloved to him. Did not the poet say: "And everything the beloved does is beloved"? So if you truly love the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then follow him by carrying out the faith-obligations. And let us attend to the difference between "follow me" (ittabi'uni) and "listen to me" (is-tami' li).

Following occurs only in conduct. If you love the Messenger of Allah, then you must see what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to do, and do likewise. But if you claim this love and do not do as the Messenger of Allah did, then this is a lack of sincerity in love. The proof of your sincerity in the love you claim is that you follow the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. If we follow the Messenger of Allah, we have taken the obligation from Allah as a blessing, and we turn it from Allah along with the hardship it has for us, so Allah loves us, because we have preferred His obligation despite the hardship in the obligation.

Understanding this verse requires that we know the Truth is alerting us, as if He is saying to us: You loved Allah for existence and provision, and afterwards you stopped at the obligation because it is heavy upon you. Here we say: "Look at the obligation: is it for the benefit of the one who imposes it, or for the benefit of the one who receives the obligation?" It is for the benefit of the mukallaf, that is, the one who receives the obligations.

Thus we must join the obligation to the blessings, so that the blessings become "the blessing of existence," "of provision," and "of obligation." If you love Allah for existence and provision, this requires that you love Him also for the obligation, and the proof of the truth of love is the servant's standing by the obligation. And since you have expressed the sincerity of your feelings by your love for Allah, then Allah must love you. Every one of us knows that his love for Allah does not advance or delay, but Allah's love for you advances and delays.

As for the word of the Truth, glorified and exalted, in what He teaches His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ — that is, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent from Allah, came with all that Allah sent down and concealed nothing of what he was commanded to convey. It is not sound for anyone to place a distinction between the Messenger of Allah and Allah, because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, conveys from Allah everything that was sent down to him.

Then the Truth says: ﴿And He will forgive you your sins﴾. The matter of this ﴿and He will forgive you﴾ includes what human laws call retroactive effect. Whoever has not had this matter in mind — which is the love of Allah and following the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace — must know that he bears the responsibility to begin in this matter immediately, to follow the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and to carry out the faith-obligation, and Allah will forgive him what has already passed. And what sins does Allah forgive here? They are the sins from which some servants fled from following the Messenger, so the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came with the ruling concerning them.

Thus we know and are certain that the justice of Allah is that He, glorified is He, will not punish anyone for a past sin as long as the servant has accepted to carry out the faith-obligation. Those to whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, conveyed had to become aware with their reason of what the Messenger announced to them. This matter does not become a proof except after it has become a conveyance, and the conveyance has come; therefore Allah forgives the sins that preceded the conveyance. Then the Truth says: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. We know that forgiveness is from Allah and mercy is from Him as well.

After that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger...﴾

I have said before, regarding the command to obey, that it comes in the Noble Qur'an in three forms. Sometimes the Truth says: ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾, as in this verse that we are now considering with our faith-inspired reflections. We observe here that the All-Glorious did not repeat the command to obey. Rather, He made the command a single one, "obey," so if we ask, "Whom is obeyed?" the answer is: Allah and the Messenger together.

So the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ), conveying from Allah, ﴿Follow me, and Allah will love you﴾, means that the obedience of the believers to the Messenger is obedience to Allah. The Messenger (ﷺ) did not command us to obey him for his own sake, but he commands us to obey Allah. For this reason the Truth did not repeat the command to obey. Here the Truth unifies the command to obey, making it for Allah and for the Messenger together. He links the second obeyed one to the first obeyed one, who is Allah, with a second obeyed one, the Messenger (ﷺ). The Truth says in His Mighty Book:

﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if they turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ [An-Nur: 54].

The Truth mentions the command to obey three times: once the command to obey is for Allah, a second time it is for the Messenger (ﷺ), and a third time the Truth says:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority (ulil-amr) among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should be believers in Allah and the Last Day. That is best and most suitable in outcome.﴾ [An-Nisa: 59].

What is the matter of these commands to obey? It is obedience in the various kinds and types of legal obligation (taklif). The rulings that the believers are required to obey are of two kinds: sometimes the command comes from Allah and the Messenger has confirmed it by his words and conduct. When the believer obeys in this one matter, he obeys Allah and the Messenger together. Other times a ruling comes from Allah in general terms, and the Messenger comes to explain it in detail.

﴿And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ [An-Nur: 56].

None of us knew how many prayers there are in a day, nor the number of units (rak'ah) in each prayer, nor how they are performed. But the Messenger (ﷺ) explained the matter for us in every prayer. So the believer obeys Allah in the general command, and obeys the Messenger in the detail of the command. We must notice that there are two obediences here: the first is obedience to Allah, and the second is obedience to the Messenger. In a single matter, obedience is to Allah and the Messenger, because it is one command. As for the command that came from Allah in general terms, Allah left its explanation to the Messenger (ﷺ). So the believer obeys Allah in the general command, such as the command to pray and to establish it, and obeys the Messenger in the detailed explanation of the prayer and its manner. Sometimes a ruling comes with a higher delegation from Allah to the Messenger, so Allah tells His Messenger, in effect, that you are the one who decides in these matters, as the Truth said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7].

The All-Glorious left it to the Messenger to issue the legislation necessary "for the uprightness of the believers' lives." He gave him the general delegation, and since the All-Glorious has given the Messenger (ﷺ) the general delegation, the believer's obedience is to the Messenger in what the Messenger says, even if Allah has not said it. For example, we do not find in the Qur'an evidence that the dawn prayer is two units. Rather, the Messenger (ﷺ) explained the prayer to us, so we know that dawn is two units, noon is four units, afternoon is like noon, sunset is three units, and night is four units. The evidence is the explanation of the Messenger, and the saying of the Truth: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7].

This is evidence from the Noble Qur'an. Thus we know that the command to obey came in the Qur'an in three forms. The first form: when the one obeyed is one, "Allah and the Messenger," where the mention of the Messenger here is joined to the Supreme Divine Name. The second form: obedience to Allah in the general command and obedience to the Messenger in the detailed explanation of that command, as the Truth says: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾. The third form: that for which Allah has no specific ruling, but which falls under the general delegation to the Messenger, by the saying of the Truth: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from﴾. This is obedience to the Messenger. Then in the command to obey those in authority, the Truth says:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should be believers in Allah and the Last Day. That is best and most suitable in outcome.﴾ [An-Nisa: 59].

The Truth did not mention the obedience of those in authority merged into the obedience to Allah and the Messenger, to make it one obedience. No. The Truth mentioned the obedience of those in authority in the verse where He distinguishes between the obedience to Allah and the obedience to the Messenger, and then from within the obedience to the Messenger comes the obedience of those in authority. Why? Because there is no independent obedience due to those in authority, since the Messenger (ﷺ) has independent obedience. The obedience of those in authority is derived from their obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and there is no obedience to those in authority in what does not involve obedience to Allah and to the Messenger (ﷺ).

The Truth says: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾ Allah instructs the Messenger to convey to those who claim that they love Allah, under the conditions by which the Truth may reciprocate love with His servants, so that the benefit may be realized for mankind, because the love of Allah surpasses whatever love people offer. Following the Messenger and carrying out the obligation of obedience to Allah and the Messenger is the manner by which the servants express their love for Allah and for the Messenger (ﷺ). As for "if they turn away," meaning they did not listen to you, O Muhammad, and did not follow you, then their position—God forbid—moves toward disbelief (kufr), because the Truth says of those who turn away from Allah and the Messenger: ﴿But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾

There is no more severe warning than this.

The word "turned away" suggests that those who heard the commands of the Truth recoiled and withdrew. They did not take Allah's ruling and then laziness prevented them from carrying it out. No. They turned away from Allah's ruling, God forbid. For this reason I have said, and I still say: let those who oppose the commands of Allah beware of separating between a command that is accepted as the true ruling and the forcing of the self to follow and carry out the ruling.

Beware, O Muslim, of denying a ruling that you cannot bring yourself to follow or are unable to perform. If you deny it, you move yourself from the circle of Islam into the circle of disbelief, God forbid. Rather, you must affirm the ruling and say: "It is the ruling of Allah and it is right, but I am unable to compel myself." This makes failure to carry out the ruling merely a sin. After the Truth—glory be to Him—had explained to us the foundations of belief in His saying:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 18].

And after the Truth gave the believers good news that He—glory be to Him and exalted be He—grants them the sovereignty of faith, that He is the capable God, and that the absoluteness of His power causes the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and after He—glorified be He—laid out the path of His love: if you have loved Allah for His creation and provision, and you want Him to love you, then you must obey Allah and the Messenger (ﷺ) in carrying out the obligations.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 33:

After Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, has set down the principles of faith, both doctrinal and legislative, after this and that, He gives us practical models of human conduct. This is because there is a difference between theories being laid down and the command coming for application, only to find no one who applies it. Indeed, the Truth does not impose burdens without purpose or in vain. Allah says to us: "I have imposed the duties of faith, and among created beings like you are those who are able to walk upon them and carry them out." Therefore, the Truth presents to us the models that make this clear.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent to an unlettered nation (ummah ummiyyah), and Islam was new to them. For this reason, the Truth presents ancient models, and these models confirm for us that in the religion of Islam we do not find fanaticism (ta'assub), because the religion that came from Allah upon Adam (peace be upon him) is the religion that Abraham (peace be upon him) brought from Allah, and it is the religion that was revealed to the family of Imran, Moses (peace be upon him) and Jesus (peace be upon him).

Indeed, the Truth bestows the attributes of honour upon the people of religions who are ascribed to what Allah revealed to them of a method (manhaj). Islam came to abrogate (naskh) some of what came in those earlier messages and to place them into one enduring method that remains until the Day of Resurrection, namely the method of Islam, which is absolutely magnificent. Here the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds﴾.

This is the justice of the Noble Qur'an, the just Truth that descends upon the Messenger as a clear message, reminding the sons of the purity of the origins of their fathers, and it is a loss if the sons end up as they are. ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam﴾. The word ﴿chose (iṣṭafā)﴾ indicates a choice that is pleasing. And we may ask: Did the Truth choose these messengers, Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran, so that they were obedient, or did the Truth know eternally (azalan) that they would be obedient, so He chose them? The eternal knowledge of the Truth is eternal, and His knowledge is not dependent upon everything. When you bring your human law and look keenly into a person and entrust him with a matter, and he succeeds in it, you congratulate yourself that your insight was right, by the knowledge and power of Allah?

Those whom Allah chose are those whom Allah knew eternally would be obedient. Someone may say: they are obedient to Allah through being chosen. To such a person we reply: they are obedient through the general human disposition (al-nafs al-'āmmah), and they become in greater obedience after they take on the specific duty (al-nafs al-khāṣṣah). They were obedient before they received the matters of duty, and had the Truth left them to the rational faculties, they would have been guided to His obedience. And when the command of duty came to them and Allah chose them, they became messengers and bearers of a heavenly method.

When a person hears the words of the Truth: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam﴾, he may wonder about its meaning, because from Allah's choosing of Adam there comes to mind the meaning of "singling him out" with Himself, or taking him as the elite from others. So how was Adam chosen, when there was no one before him or with him, since he was the first creation? We can know by ordinary reason that Allah's choosing of Noah (peace be upon him) was a choosing from among existing humans, and likewise the choosing of Abraham the Friend of the Merciful and the rest of the prophets.

So then, how was Adam chosen? The meaning of ﴿Allah chose Adam﴾, as we have said, is that Allah has selected him, or that "the one chosen" (al-muṣṭafā 'alayhi) comes from him and from his offspring. Yes, and indeed the chosen one came from his offspring, and this meaning is valid, and the preceding meaning is also valid. The Truth says: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾, and we know that our master Noah (peace be upon him) faced a group of disbelievers in him, so Allah drowned them in the flood, and Noah and those with him were saved by the command of Allah.

﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven gushed forth, We said: Load into it two of every kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe. And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud: 40].

Those who remained after Noah (peace be upon him) were believers, then they were exposed to changes (aghyār). These changes came in their wake, and so disbelief and faith arose. Why? Because when Allah created Adam (peace be upon him), He set for him the trial of duty in the Garden, and it was obligatory that he transmit to his children what Allah had taught him.

Adam conveyed to them the matters of preserving their physical needs and taught them how to eat, how to drink, and other things.

And the values had to be with them too. Adam (peace be upon him) fulfilled this, and taught his children how to preserve their physical needs and also taught them values, but with the passage of time, some of Adam's children kept lightening the burdens of duty until they were effaced and vanished. Out of Allah's mercy toward His creation, He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, renews the message by sending a new messenger.

The new message gives what existed first regarding beliefs and reports and things that do not change, and the new message brings rulings suitable for the time of that message. If humans could amend the policies of humans, the matter would remain as it is; if one person committed a wrong and his people struck his hand, the affair of the message would be upright and this nation would remain upon goodness. Why? Because the refining-filters of certainty (maṣāfī al-yaqīn) in the human soul exist, and we see them and feel them. There is someone in whom you find the filters of certainty within himself, and who may not be able to control himself, so he commits sin, and his own soul blames him, so he turns back from the sin.

Again, we find another person who does not find the filters of certainty within himself, but they exist in others, so we find someone who commands him to good and forbids him from evil. If the individual filters of faith are withheld, and likewise the communal filters of faith in society are withheld, then there is no hope there, and therefore a new messenger must come and alert people with some miracle.

The will of the Truth, glory be to Him, has decreed that no other messenger should come after our master Muhammad (ﷺ), and in that is a testimony for the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) that Allah has entrusted it with the method of Allah. If it is deprived in any soul of its individual filters, its social filters will remain, and it must be that this exists within the nation of Muhammad, because the absence of that would necessitate the existence of a new prophet.

Indeed, Allah has entrusted the nation of Muhammad with His method, and therefore no prophet came after our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Truth has entrusted the nation of Muhammad, so that the individual or social filters were never withheld from it, and therefore the true word comes: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and believing in Allah﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 110].

This is a directive to us from the Truth, so that we know that the social filters will continue to exist within the nation of our master Muhammad (ﷺ). So, after the heedlessness that occurred after Noah (peace be upon him), Allah brought other choosings as a mercy from Him to the worlds, and the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds﴾. We say of Abraham (peace be upon him): "the father of the prophets," and the Truth mentioned the news of some of the descendants of the family of Abraham, namely the family of Imran, and gave them a distinction.

When this word "Imran" occurs in Islam, we should know that there are two who share the same name: there is "Imran," the father of Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them both), and there is another "Imran." The father of Moses and Aaron had a father named "Yasahar" (Yuṣhar), and his grandfather was named "Fahath" (Qahath), and after him "Lawi" (Levi), and after him "Ya'qub" (Jacob), after him "Ishaq" (Isaac), and after him "Ibrahim" (Abraham). As for the other Imran, he is the father of Mary (peace be upon her).

A problem arose for a number of scholars: "Which of the two Imrans does Allah mean here?" What increased the perplexity of these scholars was the existence of a sister of Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them) named Mary, who was the daughter of Imran, the father of Moses and Aaron, so both of them were named Mary bint Imran. In that era they took omen from the name "Mary," because its meaning is "the worshipper," and when they disputed, they did not perceive that the Qur'an had clarified and made the meaning manifest, and they should have understood that the intended one here is not the Imran father of Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them), but the Imran father of Mary, from whom came Jesus (peace be upon him). The Imran father of Mary is the son of Mathan, who was of the lineage of Solomon, Solomon was of David, David of Awshi, Awshi of Judah, Judah of Jacob, and Jacob of Isaac.

In the past, during the days of seeking knowledge, we used to set a vocalisation for it letter by letter, saying "'Amm'am Sadi'ayy" and its meaning: Jesus son of Mary, Mary daughter of Imran, Imran son of Mathan, Mathan of Solomon, of David, of Awshi, and Awshi of Judah, Judah of Jacob, Jacob of Isaac. The matter became confused for many, and they said: "Which of the two Imrans is the one about whom Allah makes this noble statement?" To these we say: the mention of the name of Mary (peace be upon her) after that means that he is the father of Mary, and we should also be alert to the fact that the Truth said about Mary:

﴿So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance and caused her to grow in a goodly growth, and entrusted her to Zechariah. Whenever Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision. He said: "O Mary, from where is this for you?" She said: "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 37].

Zechariah (peace be upon him) is the son of Adhan (Iddo), and Adhan was a contemporary of Mathan. The intended one here is the father of Mary. Thus we have determined which of the two Imrans the Truth means by His saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds﴾. When you say, "I have preferred so-and-so over so-and-so," it means that it was possible for you to choose one from a group over the others, and therefore we understand that the meaning of "over the worlds" is over the worlds of their time. They are people who existed, and from them He chose one; as for the one who would be born after that, there is no choosing over him, so there is no choosing over Muhammad (ﷺ).

Then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿Offspring, one of them from another; and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾.

When He says ﴿offspring, one of them from another﴾, we may ask: does this refer to lineage (al-ansab) or to religion and values? We should also note that the Truth has taught us, in the matter of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that lineage by blood and flesh carries no weight with the prophets, and that the lineage acknowledged in relation to the prophets is the lineage of values and religion. We have already presented what the Truth said:

﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed, I will make you an imam (leader) for the people. He said: And of my offspring?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124].

Allah answered him, saying: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124].

Why? Because the imam is the one who is followed in guidance. So the matter is not inheritance by blood. Thus Sayyidna Ibrahim knew that lineage for the prophets is not inheritance of blood. Accordingly, we understand the Truth's words ﴿offspring, one of them from another﴾ as offspring in their inheritance of values. And we hear in the Qur'an:

﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are one of another; they enjoin what is evil, forbid what is good, and withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67].

This hypocrisy is not a matter related to lineage but to values; these are all matters of values. And when it is said ﴿and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, it means that Allah knows the statements, as well as the actions and the hidden things.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 35:

Then, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿When the wife of Imran said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated (to Your service), so accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."...﴾

When you read "idh" (when), know that it is an adverb of time (zarf), and in the language one supposes for it the verb "udhkur" (remember). One says "idh ji'tuka" (when I came to you), meaning "remember that I came to you." When the Truth says ﴿idh qalati imra'atu Imran﴾ ("when the wife of Imran said"), some people among the people of insight and understanding see that God, glorified is He, is All-Hearing and All-Knowing at the time the wife of Imran said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb," and they try to connect this verse with what came before it, that God is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. We stop at the words of the wife of Imran: ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated (to Your service)﴾.

When we hear the word "muharraran" (dedicated, freed), its meaning is that it is not owned by anyone. So when we say "harrartu al-'abd" (I freed the slave), it means he goes off without any restriction upon him. Or "harrartu al-kitab" (I corrected the book) means I corrected what is in it. The liberation (tahrir) of any matter is the correction of what is in it of corruption, or releasing it from any tie or restriction. As for her words ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated﴾, it is a supplication (munajah) to God. So what is the motive for this supplication to God?

The wife of Imran lives in an environment where people take pride in their children, and children, as we know, govern the movement of people, and people govern the movement of their children. People toil so that children may be a support and a comfort to the eye, and society advances by that material connection. The wife of Imran was not pleased with that. She wanted what is in her womb to be freed from all of that. She wants it free from her, and she is free from it. This means that she desires that what is in her womb be unconnected to anything, to any love, or to any care.

Why? Because a person, however far he reaches the rank of certainty, the matters that relate to people and to Him pass over him and preoccupy him. Therefore the wife of Imran wanted what is in her womb to be freed from all of that. It may be said: the wife of Imran was binding by this vow a human being like herself. We answer this with the following:

In former times, when they vowed a son to the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis), this vow continued as long as they held guardianship over him, and he remained as they wished until he reached the age of maturity (rushd). Upon reaching the age of maturity, the son has the choice between remaining as his parents wished or living his life as he wants.

Reaching the age of maturity is an acknowledgment of the human being's selfhood in making the decision appropriate to his life. The wife of Imran did not want from what is in her womb that it be a comfort to the eye, or that it be with her. She wanted it freed for the service of the Holy House, and in human conception that required the newborn to be a male, because those who served the House were males.

We know that the word "walad" (child) is also applied to a girl, but the common usage is for people to apply the word "walad" to a male.

But the linguistic meaning of "walad" is the one born, whether male or female. When we hear the word "nadhr" (vow), let us understand that it is a matter intended as obedience beyond the obligation of the one obligated, of the same kind as what God has imposed on him.

God has enjoined upon us five prayers. If a person vows to pray a number of additional units (rak'at) beyond that, then the person has bound himself to something more than what God bound him to, and it is of the same kind as what God imposed, namely prayer. God has prescribed the fasting of the month of Ramadan. If a person vows to fast Monday and Thursday, or two months, the person is free, but he chooses a vow of the same kind as what God has imposed as obligations, namely fasting. God has prescribed zakat at a rate of two and a half percent, but a person may vow beyond that, such as ten percent or even fifty percent.

The person is free, but he chooses a vow of the same kind as what God has imposed as obligations. The vow is an increase over what the obligated one was charged with, of the same kind as what He, glorified is He, charged. Among the meanings of her words "I have vowed" is that the wife of Imran was a pious and scrupulous lady, and she was not compelled to vow, but she did it, and it is an additional matter for the service of God's House.

The vow, as we know, expresses the servant's love (ishq) for God's obligations, so he binds himself with much of some of them. After that, the wife of Imran called upon God to accept that vow, saying: "So accept it from me" (fa-taqabbal minni). "Taqabbul" is taking a thing with consent and pleasure, because you may take something unwillingly or grudgingly, but "to accept" (tataqabbal) means taking it with acceptance and pleasure. In response to this supplication came the word of the Truth:

﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37].

We note that the wife of Imran said at the start: ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated, so accept it from me, indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, and she did not say "O Allah." This is so that we know that the Lord (Rabb) is the one who undertakes nurture, so when one calls "my Lord," the meaning in it is nurture. And when one calls upon "Allah," the meaning in it is obligation.

"Allah" is the address to the worshipped one who is obeyed in what He imposes, while "Rabb" is the one who undertakes nurture.

The wife of Imran said: ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated, so accept it from me, indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This is the supplication, and thus was the response: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance﴾. After that, the Truth spoke of the things that come from the side of nurture: ﴿And He made her grow a good growth... and Zakariya took charge of her﴾. All of that is connected with nurture and lordship (rububiyyah). So when the wife of Imran called, she knew how to call, and she vowed what was in her womb. After that the answer came of the same kind as what she called for, at the summit of acceptance, which is taking with pleasure.

﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance.﴾

So "good" (hasan) here is an increase in pleasure, because the word "qabul" gives us the meaning of taking with pleasure, and the word "hasan" clarifies that there is an increase in pleasure. That indicates that God accepted what the wife of Imran offered with pleasure and with something good, and this is evidence that people will notice in her upbringing something above pleasure; it is not an ordinary acceptance, it is a good acceptance. ﴿And He made her grow a good growth﴾. This indicates that the wife of Imran, when she vowed what was in her womb, intended not to raise what was in her womb until the age at which the newborn could serve in God's House. Rather, she vowed what was in her womb from the very first moment of birth. She would not enjoy the child, and therefore the Truth said: ﴿And Zakariya took charge of her﴾, and Zakariya was the husband of the maternal aunt of Lady Mary.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 36:

After the supplication of the wife of ʿImran, there comes the wise utterance: ﴿So when she gave birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female..."﴾

This statement came from her because she had said that she had vowed what is in her womb to be dedicated (muharraran) to serving the House. Her saying "dedicated" means that she wanted a male for the service of the House, but the child came out a female. It is as though she said: since I was not enabled to fulfil the vow, then Your decree preceded, and the child has come out a female. But then the Truth says: ﴿And Allah knew best what she had given birth to.﴾ This means that she did not intend to inform God, but she wanted to show regret, because the purpose of her vow had not been achieved. Then the Truth says: ﴿And the male is not like the female.﴾ So is this from her speech, or from the speech of God?

She said: ﴿I have given birth to a female.﴾ And God said: ﴿And the male is not like the female.﴾

The Truth says to her: Do not think that the male you were wishing for would reach the rank of this female; this female has a great status. Or the statement is a continuation of her speech: ﴿I have given birth to a female,﴾ and the saying of the Truth, ﴿And Allah knew best what she had given birth to,﴾ is a parenthetical clause (jumla iʿtiraḍiyya), and the completion of her speech is ﴿And the male is not like the female.﴾ That is, she said: O Lord, the male is not like the female; she is not fit for serving the House.

Let the believer take the meaning he loves. We will find that the first meaning carries more radiance. It is as if the Truth had said: You want a male by your understanding of fulfilling the vow, to serve the House; I have granted you a female child, but I will give her a sign greater than serving the House. By the sign I will give this female, I intend to support beliefs, not merely the service of a place where rites are performed.

I will make of this sign a continuation of the course of beliefs in the world until the Hour comes. And because I am the Creator, I will bring into being in this female a sign that exists in no other, and it is a sign that establishes the absoluteness of the power of the Truth. I have said before that the absolute power differs from ordinary power: ordinary power creates through causes, but from where are the causes? The Truth is also the Creator of causes.

So, since the Creator of causes wills creation through causes, this is His will. Therefore the Truth has given us the ability to see the absoluteness of His power, because these are beliefs of faith, which must remain at the focus of the feeling of faith and always in the mind of the believer. God created some creatures through causes, as He created us, and the multitude of creation through reproduction between a father and a mother; but the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, was by the Truth without causes. We know that a thing that is between two has a rational and logical division: as long as there is a father and a mother, male and female, there will come from them multiplication. The Truth says:

﴿And of everything We created two mates, that you may remember.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49].

When the two spouses come together, this is the complete picture, and this is the first in the logical division and rational conception. Or the two spouses are absent, and this is the second in the logical division and rational conception.

Or the first spouse is absent and the second party remains, and this is the third in the logical division and rational conception; or the second spouse is absent and the first party remains, and this is the fourth in the logical division and rational conception.

These, then, are four conceptions of the rational division. All of us came from the union of the two elements, the man and the woman. As for Adam, God created him by the absoluteness of His power to be the cause. Likewise Eve was created from Adam. And the Truth brought forth from the meeting of Adam and Eve offspring. And there is a female, Mary, from whom comes the Messiah ʿIsa son of Mary, without a male. This is the sign among the worlds, and it establishes a summit of belief. So let no one say: a male or a female, because the intention of the wife of ʿImran in obedience was that the child be a male, but the decree of your Lord willed that it be loftier than the decree of the wife of ʿImran in obedience; therefore He said: ﴿And the male is not like the female.﴾ That is, the male will never reach the rank of this female.

And the wife of ʿImran said: ﴿And I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her with You and for her offspring from Satan the accursed.﴾ The wife of ʿImran said what shows her feeling: when the female child was deprived by her femininity of being in the service of God's House, the wife of ʿImran wished that the daughter be obedient and worshipful, so she named her "Maryam," because Maryam in their language, as we have said, means "the worshipper."

The first thing that obstructs worship is Satan. He is the one who makes man rebel against servitude. Man wants to become a worshipper, and Satan comes to make sin attractive to him. The wife of ʿImran wanted to protect her daughter from the incitement of Satan, because she knew from her experience that all sins come from Satan's incitement; she named her "Maryam" so that she would become "a worshipper of God," and because the wife of ʿImran possessed a present faithful mind and bore the whole methodology of worship, therefore she said: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You and for her offspring from Satan the accursed.﴾ The one sought refuge in is God, and the one from whom refuge is sought is Satan. When Satan enters into the adornment of sins with a creature of God, he enters into a struggle with the creature; but Satan cannot enter into a struggle with his Lord. Therefore it is said of Satan that when he hears the remembrance of God he withdraws (yakhnus), that is, he draws back, and the Noble Qur'an described him as "al-Khannas" (the one who withdraws). Satan only isolates a person when the person is far from God, and therefore the Truth teaches man:

﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ [al-A'raf: 200].

Satan trembles and quivers from seeking refuge in God. When the trembling of Satan is repeated by this word, he knows that this worshipping man will not swerve from obedience to God into sins. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us how a man should approach his wife, and approaching the family is the likely occasion for a child to be conceived, so the servant says: "O Allah, keep Satan away from me and keep Satan away from what You provide me" (from the supplication of the Messenger).

Whoever says this before conception occurs, Satan will have no authority or power over the child who comes by the permission of God. Therefore the wife of ʿImran said: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You and for her offspring from Satan the accursed.﴾ People may understand "dhurriyya" (offspring) as multiplied progeny, but the word "dhurriyya" is applied to one, to two, and to three or more. The offspring here, with respect to Maryam, peace be upon her, is ʿIsa, peace be upon him, and the matter ends there.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 37:

After the supplication of Maryam's mother (﴿And I seek refuge for her in You and her offspring from Satan, the accursed﴾), the true Word comes: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance, and caused her to grow in a good growth, and entrusted her care to Zakariyya...﴾

We have already understood the good acceptance and the good growth. As for His true Word ﴿and entrusted her care to Zakariyya﴾, it means that the matter came from above. It is the Lord who accepted her with a good acceptance and who caused her to grow with a good growth. Therefore, Zakariyya's care for her came by the command of God. The evidence for what happened at the time of Maryam's guardianship is that the notables of the people gathered, each desiring to take charge of her, and they conducted a lottery (qur'ah) among themselves for that purpose. Whenever you find a lottery or a drawing of lots, the people have come out of their various desires into the desire of God. When we disagree about something, we conduct a lottery, a share is assigned to each participant, and then we see whose share comes out. People resort to this matter so as to prevent human whims from interfering in the choice, and the matter becomes outside the desire of humans and within the desire of God, glorified and exalted be He. This is what happened at Zakariyya's taking charge of Maryam. Therefore, the Truth says to our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ):

﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens [to see] which of them would be charged with Maryam, and you were not with them when they disputed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44].

So the guardianship of Maryam caused an uproar, and this is evidence that they agreed to conduct a lottery concerning her guardianship. They would not have resorted to this lottery unless a dispute had arisen among them over which of them would take charge of Maryam. By God's grace, Zakariyya, peace be upon him, was married to Ishae, the sister of Hanna, who was the mother of Maryam; thus he was the husband of her maternal aunt.

Regarding the word "aqlamahum" (their pens), the commentators said: they are the arrows (qidah) that they used to make in ancient times, or the pens with which they wrote the Torah, which they threw into the sea. Whoever's pen floated did not take up the care of Maryam, and whoever's pen sank in the sea is the one who won the guardianship of Maryam. Thus they had come out of their own desires into the desire of God.

Coming out of desires, and coming out of whims by means of an object that has no choice, like the arrows of the lottery, causes no resentment in the soul. But if someone were to take charge of Maryam by force and anger, he would certainly find the hearts of others filled with bitterness or resentment. Therefore, in that era it was customary to conduct the drawing of arrows whenever they feared that injustice might befall someone or that someone might be suspected unjustly. There is also the story of our master Yunus, when the ship neared sinking, and it was necessary for one of them to go down into the sea to save it, and the wise Word came:

﴿And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers. When he fled to the laden ship, and he cast lots and was among the losers, and the whale swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [As-Saffat: 139-144].

It was necessary that one of the people of that ship go down, so a lottery with arrows was conducted, so that no fight would break out among those aboard the ship, and so that victory would not belong to the strong, but the lottery protected people from one another's injustice.

They said: let us draw lots with arrows; whoever's arrow comes out is the one to be thrown. Yunus, peace be upon him, had to go down into the sea, and the whale swallowed him. Because he was among those who glorify God, God rescued him. Yunus, peace be upon him, accepted God's choice and did not forget to glorify God, so that was his deliverance. Thus we read God's words to understand that Zakariyya's guardianship was by God's choice: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance, and caused her to grow in a good growth, and entrusted her care to Zakariyya﴾.

The word "kaffalaha" means he undertook every task of her upbringing; this is kafala (guardianship). We know that the kafil in our usage is the guarantor, and the guarantor is one who settles a debt when the person is unable to pay. His true Word ﴿and entrusted her care to Zakariyya﴾ gives us the clear meaning that Zakariyya, peace be upon him, was the one who undertook the affairs of Maryam's care.

The Generous Truth continues: ﴿Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary (mihrab), he found provision with her﴾. He did not enter only once; he entered upon her in the sanctuary many times. And every time Zakariyya, peace be upon him, entered upon Maryam, he found provision with her, so he had to ask about the source of this provision, and his question necessarily expressed astonishment. Therefore the true Word comes on the tongue of Zakariyya: ﴿Where does this come to you from?﴾

When you hear ﴿Where does this come to you from?﴾ this indicates that he had placed locks on the place where Maryam was; otherwise he would have suspected that someone had entered upon Maryam and brought her those various kinds of provision. As they say, Zakariyya would lock the doors upon Maryam. And if the doors were not locked, he would have suspected that someone had entered and brought her those varied provisions.

"Rizq" is that which one benefits from (the word is in the passive sense), and when Zakariyya, peace be upon him, says ﴿Where does this come to you from?﴾, we may recall what we said earlier: that any person whom God has placed in charge of a group, and who sees among them what exceeds their capacity or the limits of their income, must ask each of them: "Where did you get this?" For the corruption of homes and societies comes only from neglecting to ask and from the necessity of obtaining an answer to the specific question: "Where did you get this?"

A father who enters his home and finds his daughter wearing an expensive dress beyond the family's means, or finds his son has bought something the family cannot afford, must here stop and ask: "Where did you get this?" In that there is protection of the family's morals from collapse or dissolution. If each person were to be alert to ask his family and those under his guardianship, "Where did you get this?", he would know every detail of their movements; but if the reins are left loose, the matter will be corrupted.

Zakariyya's question, "Where does this come to you from?", is a specific question about the source of this provision. Let us look at her answer: ﴿She said: it is from God﴾. Then the faith-inspired intuition does not leave Zakariyya without reminding him of a clear truth lodged at the core of every believer's consciousness: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾. This matter stirred various impulses in Zakariyya's soul; it is an unusual matter. Maryam had informed him that the provision she had was from God, who provides for whom He wills without reckoning, the God who is able to say "Be" and it is.

Here Zakariyya remembered himself, as if his own soul spoke to him: "If power is unrestricted to act without causes and to give without reckoning, then I desire a child to succeed me, although I am old and have reached an advanced age, and my wife is barren." The matter of the provision Zakariyya found every time he entered upon Maryam is what alerted Zakariyya to what he longed for and desired.

We know that the thoughts that pass through the human mind are many, but not all of them settle at the core of consciousness; some information lies at the margins of consciousness and is recalled when needed. So when Zakariyya found the provision in Maryam's possession and she told him about its source: ﴿It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾.

Here Zakariyya asked himself: how did this matter escape me? That is why the Truth says of Zakariyya: ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord...﴾

At the moment she told him that provision comes from Allah, and that He is the Truth who gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning, the faith matter was awakened in him, and his longing came to the forefront of his consciousness. Zakariyya said to himself: let us ask our Lord to grant us what we hope for ourselves. Since she has said this, he must have believed Maryam in her case, that this provision that comes to her is from Allah. Another proof of his belief is that he must have seen that the many kinds of provision found with Maryam were not common in his environment, or not in their season; and all of this was in the mihrab.

We know that the mihrab is a word meaning a place of worship. The Truth says:

﴿They made for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries (maḥārīb), statues, basins like reservoirs, and heavy cooking pots. Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude; and few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba': 13].

Or "al-mihrab" is the place of the imam in the mosque, or it is a chamber reached by a stairway, like the raised prayer-niches found in some mosques. Since Maryam had informed Zakariyya, while she was in the mihrab, that provision comes from Allah, and thereby awakened that faith matter in the core of his consciousness, what would his response be? Here Zakariyya called upon his Lord while he was in the mihrab: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication﴾. Here he is asking for a child. But we must note the following:

- Was his request for a child like what ordinary people ask for, to be an adornment of life, a "support," or a male heir? No. He asks for a good offspring, and Zakariyya's mention of a "good offspring" indicates his knowledge that there are offspring who are not good. In Zakariyya's saying which the Truth relates:

﴿who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾ [Maryam: 6].

That is, the supplication is for the inheritance of prophethood, the inheritance of methods, and the inheritance of values. This is how Zakariyya asked for a child. He asked for him for great tasks. Zakariyya's words "My Lord, grant" (rabbi hab) mean that he is requesting a gift without any return. He acknowledges: I do not have the qualifications that would make me have a child, because I am old and my wife is barren. So Your giving to me, O Lord, is a gift and not a right; and even one who possesses the capacity does not have this matter as a right for himself. He must know that Allah's giving to him remains a gift. So beware of thinking that the completion of causes and youth are what give offspring. The Truth, glory be to Him, alerts us not to fall into the deception and self-deceit of causes.

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He renders barren whom He wills. Indeed He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾ [al-Shura: 49-50].

In that is a clear lesson and a specific warning not to be seduced by causes. Thus every gift from Allah is a gift, and causes do not give anyone what he wants.

Zakariyya says: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself﴾, and when you say "from Yourself" (min ladunka), he means "grant me from beyond Your causes." Why? Because everything is from Allah.

However, there is a difference between Allah's giving through a cause, such as when a person goes to learn knowledge and remains for twenty years studying, and a person upon whom Allah pours some talent, which is why the people of illumination (ahl al-ishraqat) say: this is "knowledge of ladunni" (ʿilm ladunnī), that is, without toil. When we hear "min ladun," it means the causes are set aside. Zakariyya's supplication was ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself﴾, and the word "hab" clarifies what came in Surah Maryam from Zakariyya's saying: ﴿He said: My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?﴾ [Maryam: 8].

It is "hab" that clarifies these meanings for us. This was Zakariyya's supplication: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication.﴾ Does he mean that Allah hears the supplication, or that Allah answers the supplication? He places all his hope in Allah, as if saying: O Lord, the moment You hear me, You will answer my request with the ease of Your power. Why? Because You, O Lord, know the sincerity of my intention, that I want a boy not for things like comfort of the eye, male heirship, honor, or others, but I want a child to be an heir to me in carrying Your method on earth.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 39:

After that the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary...﴾

Did all the angels gather together, or did they call out to Zakariyya? No, because it was Jibril (peace be upon him) who called to him. And why did the Truth state here that the angels were the ones who called to him? This statement came so that we would notice something: that sound in an event, like a human being, has a direction from which it comes, whereas the sound that comes from the Higher Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la) does not let a person know from where it comes.
