A person hears it as though it comes from every direction, as though there were an angel in every place.

The modern age we live in has advanced in acoustics and has reached the point where a person is able to make the sound effect surround a person from multiple directions. So His saying, the Truth: ﴿then the angels called to him﴾ means that the sound came to Zakariyya from all directions.

﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: that Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah, and a noble leader, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 39]

The angels called to him at his most scrupulous meeting with his Lord. Or, when he made supplication, he took what Allah had taught the prophets: whenever a matter distressed them, they stood up to prayer. Was it not his request to Allah? So let him stand before Allah. Let each of us try this whenever anything becomes difficult for you, matters become critical, and means are blocked: let him stand, perform a fresh ablution (wudu'), and begin it with intention even if he is already in a state of ablution. Let him stand before Allah and say: "O Lord, this matter has become hard for me, so attend to my means," and let him pray with humility. I am certain that a person, as soon as he finishes this prayer, will find relief has come. Did we not receive from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) this wonderful conduct? That whenever a matter distressed him, he stood up to prayer?

The meaning of "a matter distressed him" is that his means had become constricted; therefore he goes to prayer to the Creator of means. It is going to the Causer (al-Musabbib). Instead of turning and circling around yourself, go to Allah by the shortest route, which is prayer. Why do you tire yourself, O servant, when you have a wise Lord? It has been said of old: he who has a father does not carry a worry, so is the one who has a Lord not more worthy of tranquility?

Zakariyya called upon Allah concerning the matter that distressed him, and as soon as he supplicated concerning the matter that distressed him, he stood to prayer, so the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer. The angels did not wait until he had finished his prayer: ﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: that Allah gives you glad tidings﴾.

Glad tidings (al-bushra) is the announcement of a good whose time has not yet come. If glad tidings are of a good whose time has not come, then let us see who is announcing the glad tidings: is it one who is able to bring it into existence, or one who is not able? If Allah is the one who gives the glad tidings, then He is the One who is able, and therefore the thing promised is certainly coming: ﴿that Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya﴾. He has said to him: I will give you. Beyond giving, Allah named him ﴿Yahya﴾, and above all that: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾.

Consider the precision of the Truth when He says: ﴿of Yahya, confirming﴾. This is evidence that he would live by the method of Allah, and what he knows of acts of obedience he would walk in this path while confirming; and he would come confirming a word from Allah, or he comes to confirm a word from Allah, because our master Yahya was the first to believe in the message of 'Isa (peace be upon him). He is described by the Truth's words: ﴿and a noble leader, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous﴾. That is, one restrained from everything forbidden to him, or restrained from the peak of desires, which is lust; and he is a prophet, that is, an exemplar in following the Messenger who comes in his age.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 40:

Zakariyya (peace be upon him) had made supplication and stood to pray, and he received the glad tidings of Yahya. Here the matters became confused for Zakariyya's human nature, and the Truth depicts him with His words: ﴿He said, "My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?"﴾

Zakariyya, who was the one seeking, was struck with wonder at the answering of his prayer, so he questioned: how could that be? The Truth relates this to teach us that the human soul is always in the states of alternation (al-talwin), not in the states of establishment (al-tamkin). This is so that Allah gives to His creatures who are not guided to the Straight Path the example that, if a trial befalls them, they should return to Allah. So Zakariyya says: ﴿How can I have a son when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?﴾

Reaching old age is not evidence that a man is incapable of fathering children, since he may be advanced in years and still able to make a woman conceive. For some men, fertility is not difficult however far they have advanced in age, provided they are not sterile. But the woman is the important element: if she is barren, that is the utmost inability in the means. Had Zakariyya said only ﴿and my wife is barren﴾, it would have been an unbecoming statement regarding his wife, and it would have meant that he attributed to himself a capacity while he was the one unable.

This is the courtesy of prophethood, and it is a lofty courtesy; therefore he mentioned it from its beginning: ﴿and old age has already reached me and my wife is barren.﴾ Let us observe the precision of the expression in ﴿old age has already reached me﴾. He did not say, "I have reached old age," but rather he says that old age is what came to me and I did not come to old age, because the arrival (bulugh) of a thing implies that there is a feeling and a desire in you to go towards it. Zakariyya's mention of ﴿and my wife is barren﴾ is an amplification of the freedom of power in the mind of the one listening to the story. He has set out all the human anxieties, and after that comes the decisive word: ﴿He said, "Thus does Allah do what He wills."﴾ It is the absolute freedom of power that is above causes, because it is the Creator of causes.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 3, verse 41:

Zechariah says: ﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign..."﴾

Zechariah is asking for a sign that the word has passed into deed.

﴿He said, "My Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?" He said, "Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾ [Maryam: 8–9].

This statement was an undoubted affirmation, for once the Lord has spoken, the matter is settled. So what does Zechariah want after that? He is asking for a sign (āyah), that is, a mark that Yahya has been brought into being in his mother's womb. Since the woman has grown old, her menstruation has ceased for her, and he must have known the sign, because he already knew she was barren. But Zechariah did not wish to let slip from himself a single moment of God's gifts, and since the pregnancy had occurred, here was Zechariah's plea: "Do not leave me, O Lord, until I understand through the apparent, perceptible signs, for I want to live, from the very first of Your blessing upon me, within the frame of gratitude to You for the blessing. Once fertilization occurs, I must live within the scope of gratitude, for a blessing may come while I am not grateful."

He asks for a sign in order to live within the scope of gratitude. He did not ask for a sign because he doubts — God forbid — God's power, but because he does not want to let a moment of the blessing pass from its very beginning without gratitude accompanying it. What gives us this meaning is the true word: ﴿He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning."﴾ It must be that its meaning is that he desired to speak and was unable.

There is a difference between being able to speak and not speaking, and being unable to speak. Since the sign is a gift from God, the Truth is the One who said to him: "I will prevent you from speaking." So when you find yourself unable to speak, know that this is the sign, and you will know that you are to speak with people by gesture, that is, by signs. So that you know the sign comes from God, and that God knew about His servant that he did not want a moment to pass with God's blessing without thanking God for it, we know that God will make him speak..

﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning.﴾

Zechariah wanted to live from the very first moment of the Benefactor's blessing in gratitude, and to make all his time remembrance. He did not occupy himself with people or with people's speech. Remembering the Lord much is what God taught him — exalted is He — about Zechariah when he asked for the sign, so that he would always accompany it with thanks to God for it. His words ﴿remember your Lord much﴾ indicate that Zechariah was able to remember [God] but unable to speak with people; therefore God does not want to occupy him with people's speech. It is as if God were saying to him: since you wished to live in gratitude for the blessing, I will make you unable to speak with people, but you will be able to remember [Me].

Remembrance in general is the remembrance of God through His favors, greatness, power, and attributes of perfection. Glorification (tasbīḥ) is declaring God far above imperfection, because what God has done cannot happen from anyone other than Him. So "Glory be to God" (subḥān Allāh) means the declaring of God transcendent, because He is the One who is able to do what causes do not do and no one can make. He wants to thank the Truth who gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning. That is the subtle allusion... which came earlier from Maryam to Zechariah.

Zechariah, as we know, was her guardian (kafīl). Her saying this phrase is an indication that God had prepared provision for her, coming to her from other than Zechariah, by her bringing forth something without causes. It is as if God wanted the test to be from herself, for herself; because she would be exposed to something touching on a woman's honor, so she had to know in advance that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning and without causes. If she bore a child without a cause of fatherhood, let her know that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning.

When Zechariah heard that from her, he said: since God gives provision without reckoning and brings things about without causes, and I have reached extreme old age and my wife is barren, why should I not ask my Lord to grant me a boy? So Maryam's saying ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ caught Zechariah's attention and alerted a faith present in the depths of his being and at the margin of his feeling. We do not say it created a new faith in Zechariah that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning; rather, it brought the matter of faith from the margin of feeling to the center of feeling. So Zechariah said: since the matter is so, I ask God to grant me a boy... Zechariah's saying ﴿Grant me from Yourself a good offspring﴾ shows that he and his wife do not possess the ability to acquire fatherhood and motherhood, and therefore he asked for it as a gift from God. A gift is something without return.

When he asked God for that, God answered him, and said to him — exalted is He: I will grant you a boy without causes, from your fertility in impregnation or the wife's fertility in gestation. Since the matter will be without causes, and I — the Creator — will take charge of the bringing into being with "Be," and for a lofty, noble meaning I will give you something else which you, as fathers and mothers, usually do: it is naming the newborn. So the Truth bestowed upon them another blessing, which is naming the child after He had given him to them. Here is a pause at the gift of the name.

﴿Then the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, God gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, and a leader, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 39].

When people have a child, they name him, for naming is a common custom among people. But those concerned with the newborn, when they set about naming him, try to be optimistic; so they name him a name they hope will come true in the one named. They name him "Saʿīd" (happy), hoping he will be happy, or they name him "Faḍl" or "Karīm."

They bring the name they wish to find their newborn to be, and that is their hope. But do destinies come according to hopes?

They may name him Saʿīd, and he is not happy. They name him Faḍl, and he is not generous. They name him ʿIzz, and he is not honored. But what happens when God, glory be to Him and exalted, names? The situation must be entirely different. When He says His name ﴿Yahya﴾, this indicates that he will live. Long ago a poet, when he was optimistic in naming his son Yahya, said: "So I named him Yahyā, that he might live, but there was no way to avert God's decree concerning him."

The poet had named his son Yahya hoping he would live, but God did not will that, and the son died. Why? Because the one who names among humans is not the one who gives life; the one named is a human whose power is weak, but the "Giver of Life" (al-Muḥyī) has absolute power. When He names one who has absolute power over willing that he live, he must live a distinguished life. And lest you understand that the life God indicated by His saying "his name is Yahya" is the life known to humans ordinarily — because a man, when he names his son "Yahya," hopes the son will live an average lifespan, as people live sixty years, or seventy, or any number of years written for him from eternity.

But when God names "Yahya," He does not take "Yahya" according to what people take; rather, He must give him a life longer than the limits of people's lifespans, and the Truth will prepare for him from his opponents and enemies one who will kill him, so that he becomes a martyr, and through martyrdom he becomes alive; it is as if he lives forever, for the martyrs are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.

Thus God willed for Yahya, peace be upon him, to live a life like people's lives, and to live longer than people's lives until the Hour is established. Also, we note that when Zechariah was given good news that God would grant him a boy and name him Yahya, we find he received it with wonder. How does Zechariah receive the matter of provision of a child with astonishment, when he had seen it in the provision he found with Maryam? ﴿He provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾

Could you wish that such a matter, extraordinary beyond custom and beyond the normal order, should pass over our master Zechariah as an ordinary matter he would not be amazed or astonished by? No; he must be amazed and astonished, so he said: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son?﴾ It is as if the amazement drew his attention to the fact that a wondrous sign would come; and had there been no such amazement, the matter would have been dull, as if it were an ordinary affair. Thus he draws our attention to the wondrous matter with which God singled him out. Also, the matter came contrary to the normal law of procreation, reproduction, and offspring: ﴿Old age has reached me, and my wife is barren.﴾

The whole matter is grace and a gift from God.

When the good news came to him, God did not say to him: "I will grant you the boy, whose name is Yahya, from this wife of yours," or "while you are in this state," so that he might doubt, hesitate, and say: "Will the boy named Yahya come from me while I am in this condition, my wife barren and I having reached this age? Or perhaps God will restore us to youth so that we can beget, or another woman will come and I will marry her and beget."

So the wonder lies in the form in which the begetting would take place. His saying ﴿How can I have a son, when old age has reached me and my wife is barren?﴾ — this question from Zechariah aims to learn the form or state in which the begetting would come, because begetting comes in multiple states. When God affirmed that, He said: "Thus" (kadhālika). What does "thus" mean? It means that the begetting will come from you and your wife while you are in your state: you have reached extreme old age, and your wife is barren. For the wonder is realized thereby. Was it reasonable that God would restore you both to youth so that they could help him grant them the child? No. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Thus God does what He wills.﴾ That is, as you both are, in your condition.

God made the sign that Zechariah would not speak to people for three days except by gesture. It might seem to people that not speaking is an illness; no, it is not so, for the Truth says to him: ﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning.﴾ The Truth makes Zechariah able to glorify, yet unable to speak. This is another capacity of God's absolute power: it is one tongue, unable to speak, and if he tried to speak he would not be able to; yet this same tongue becomes able only to glorify and remember God in the evening and the morning. He remembers God with the tongue, and people will hear it, and that is a demonstration of absolute power.

After that, the Truth moves us to another matter related to Maryam, for Maryam is the origin of the speech; the provision that came to her from God without reckoning is what alerted our master Zechariah to ask for a child, and the Truth brought us the story of Zechariah and the child.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 42:

Then he returned to the story of Maryam: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you..."﴾

﴿And when the angels said﴾: what is meant is Jibril (peace be upon him). The reason the Truth (al-Haqq) expresses it as ﴿the angels said﴾ is that the speech of a speaker, that is, a human being, has, as we have said, a direction of origin from which the voice comes. You can confirm this when a voice reaches you: you find your ear inclining toward the direction of the source of the sound. If the voice comes from the side of your right ear, you turn and incline to your right; and if the voice comes to you from your left, you turn to the left. But the speaker here is Jibril (peace be upon him), and his voice comes from every direction, until the matter becomes wondrous; for this reason the speech was attributed to the angels.

So what did Jibril say? Jibril said, conveying from the Lord of Might: ﴿O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds.﴾ And what is istifa' (choosing)? Indeed, istifa' is selection and election, and it is derived from safw or ṣāfī, meaning the thing that is pure, free of turbidity. Meanings are usually taken from sensible things; when you say "pure water," meaning water without turbidity, or as the Truth says:

﴿And rivers of clarified honey﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

When the Truth says: ﴿Indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾, we are here before two instances of choosing. The first istifa' came without being preceded by the word "ʿalā" (above), and the second istifa' is preceded by the word "ʿalā." The purpose of the first istifa' is to inform Maryam that Allah distinguished her with faith, righteousness and good character; but this first istifa' came unqualified by "ʿalā," meaning that this first istifa' does not prevent others from sharing with her in this istifa', as is evident from the Truth's saying:

﴿Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Ibrahim and the family of ʿImran above the worlds﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 33].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, mentioned that He purified her, and after that came the second istifa', preceded by "ʿalā," saying ﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. Thus this is an exclusion of men from the scope of this istifa'; the field of istifa' will not be a matter related to manhood, for she is chosen above the women of the worlds, as though there is no female in the worlds who shares this istifa' with her. Why? Because she is the only one who will give birth without a male, and no one will share this with her.

As for the Truth's saying ﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾, this statement must awaken in her mind a question: what is it in which she is distinguished above the women of the worlds? The mind occupies itself with this matter, and preoccupies itself with a matter of the female's function. Let us add this to the Truth's saying on her tongue: ﴿Indeed Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾, and we find that all of these are consolations (īnāsāt) for the event that will come after it, which is an event related to her honour and chastity, so Allah must prepare for it a fitting preparation so that you may be certain that there is nothing in this matter that wounds dignity.

﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. And we may ask: what is the result of the istifa'?

We have known that istifa' is ijtiba' (selection) and ikhtiyar (choice), and it entails "muṣtafī" with a fatḥa on the fa', and it entails "muṣṭafā" with a kasra on the fa'. The one chosen (al-muṣṭafā) is Allah, but what is the cause of the istifa'? The one whom Allah chooses, He chooses for a task, and it is a difficult task. So He chooses him so that his choosing spreads among people. It is as if Allah has singled him out for istifa' for the sake of people and their benefit, whether this istifa' is for a place, a person, or a time, so that its purity may spread over everything upon which it was chosen. Why did Allah choose the Ka'ba? So that every person may turn toward the Ka'ba. Thus He chose it for the sake of mankind, and so that its choosing would spread to every other place; for this reason the Truth said of the Ka'ba:

﴿Indeed the first house established for mankind is that at Bakka, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 96].

And if the Truth, glory be to Him, chooses a time, like His choosing Ramadan, then why did He choose it? So that its purity spreads, and the purity of what was sent down in it spreads in every age. Thus the Truth's choosing of a person, a place or a time is for the benefit of the rest of people, places or times. Why? Because none of creation is a son of Allah, and no place is more deserving than another place with Allah. Rather, Allah chooses one time over another time, one place over another place, and one person over another person, so that the choosing of the chosen one spreads over everything upon which he was chosen. So must people rejoice in the chosen one, or not rejoice in him? They must rejoice in him, because he came for their benefit.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 43:

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord...﴾

So it is as though the grounds for the first selection and the second selection deserve from her qunut, that is, pure worship, submissive and humble. Someone may say: And why does God select one person so that his selection becomes widely known among people? Because selection by the Truth must absolve him of everything that could befall his equivalent among the unsatisfactory choices, and the Truth, glorified is He, wants him to be a model who commits only goodness. The perfect example of this is the Truth's selection of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) from the very beginning, and making him commit only good conduct from the very beginning, so that he might give us the model of faith throughout twenty-three years, which is the duration of the Muhammadan mission.

The Truth says to Mary through the tongue of the angels: ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾. He commands her to constant, humble worship of her Lord. The word ﴿لِرَبِّكِ﴾ (to your Lord) means "nurturing" (tarbiyah), so it is as though the selections are among the blessings of God upon you, O Mary, and deserve from you qunut. ﴿وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ﴾ (And prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow). And ﴿وَاسْجُدِي﴾ (prostrate yourself) means: exert yourself in humility and submission, by placing the forehead, which is the noblest thing in man, upon the earth, because prostration is the highest degree of submission.

But does this kind of submission exempt her from bowing to God along with the people? No. It is a true command that comes to Mary: ﴿وَارْكَعِي مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ﴾ (and bow with those who bow). Your having done the higher act of submission, which is prostration, does not exempt you from bowing. Rather, you must bow with those who bow. It is not right for you, O Mary, to say: "God has commanded me with a higher command and I did not carry out the lower command."

Indeed, the Truth commands her to be also in the company of those who bow, just as we read His words concerning the disbelievers:

﴿مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ * قَالُواْ لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 42-43].

They are disbelievers, so how would they pray? It is their acknowledgement that they were disbelievers, that they had not been counted among those who pray, and an acknowledgement that they had not been Muslims or believers in God. Here a noble questioner asks: Why did He, glorified and exalted is He, say in His address to Mary: ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow﴾, and the Truth did not say: "with those who bow (feminine)"? This is the question.

In answer to this question, we wish to offer a brief introduction to the philosophy of names in their assignment to what they designate. Names are words of language that specify their referent. Referents are varied: some are inanimate, some are plants, some are animals, and some are names that indicate the unseen world, such as jinn, angels, and everything God has made unseen. These names indicate their meanings.

God guided mankind to them through what He taught Adam of the names. How was Adam able to express the data of names by their referents? Therefore there must exist for everything a name, so that when we agree upon a thing or a being we can mention a single concise word that refers to it.

Were this not so, how could one person speak with another about the mountain, for example? Would the speaker have to take the listener to the mountain and point at it? Or is it enough to say to him the word "mountain," so that the listener summons in his mind an image of this referent?

Thus, the philosophy of the Truth's teaching us names has relieved us of a great burden of difficulty in understanding one another. Were it not for this, we could not understand one another about anything unless we confronted the thing and pointed to it. The word "mountain," the word "rock," and other words are names for referents. When I speak, for example, about America, I will not take the listener there and point to him saying, "This is America," but one word, "America," gives the listener a meaning of the referent, so that rulings attach to their referents. Since the matter is thus, there must be names for referents; these names God taught to man so that he may understand one another by them, and man's origin is from Adam.

The word "Adam," when you speak it, you find in grammar that it is masculine, and the masculine is opposed by the feminine. The Supreme Truth created masculinity and femininity, because from their pairing offspring will come forth. Therefore it was necessary to distinguish between the two sexes of a single species. The male and the female are the children of Adam, and from them proliferation arises. But the wonder is that when God named Adam and we pronounce it as a masculine noun, and named "Eve" and we pronounce it as a feminine noun, God made the original name from which creation was made to be "nafs" (soul/self). The Truth said:

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, God is ever Watchful over you﴾ [al-Nisa: 1].

The Truth named Adam with the word nafs, which is feminine. So the feminine does not mean that it is less than the masculine; rather, "masculine" is only a sign to place things in their true referents, and likewise the feminine. The Truth, glorified is He, applies to each of us the word "nafs," which is a feminine word, and when the Truth, glorified is He, spoke another word about creation, He said:

﴿O mankind, We created you from male and female and made you nations and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13].

The word "nas" (people) means the collective of mankind. Thus we know that the word "insan" (human being) is applied at one time to the masculine and at another time to the feminine. So the Truth has at one time given a masculine term and at another time applied a feminine term, so that we do not say that the masculine is better and superior to the feminine, but that is merely a means of understanding, and therefore the Truth, glorified is He, affirms for us that He has assigned names to their referents so that we may know one another by them.

﴿And We made you nations and tribes that you may know one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13].

The meaning of "that you may know one another" is that each of us should have a name by which he is known to others.

In our ordinary life, and to God belongs the highest likeness, we find a man who has many children, so each son is given a name so that society may know him by it. The wonder in this noble verse, ﴿And We made you nations and tribes that you may know one another﴾, is that we find the word "nations" (shu'ub) is masculine and the word "tribes" (qaba'il) is feminine. So there is no differentiation by excellence; rather the words here are referents for mutual recognition. The Supreme Truth says:

﴿By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 1-3].

So what is the status of the women who believed? They are included within ﴿those who have believed﴾. And why did God include the feminine within the masculine? Because the masculine is the root, and the feminine came from it as a branch. So the feminine is the one who enters with the masculine in matters shared by the species.

﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21].

This means that the "feminine" must enter under the obligation of servitude to God.

The general meaning establishes that the one required to worship is mankind as a species, both in the male and female type. And in the matter specific to women, God specifies woman by her own particularity. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36].

Why? The matter here includes both sexes of the one species: man and woman, husband and wife. For example, we find a husband who wants to divorce his wife, so the Truth brings a detailed explanation clarifying that. And if there is a matter specific to women, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, specifies the command; behold His wise words:

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear God, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate words. And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God intends only to remove from you the impurity, People of the House, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32-33].

Everything that came in the preceding verse specifies the duties concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). The address precisely specifies the command: "lastunna" (you are not), "ittaqaytunna" (if you fear), "la takhda'na" (do not be soft), "qarna" (remain), "la tabarrajna" (do not display). The discourse in this noble verse concerns women, so it brings their pronouns in the feminine.

But when a command concerning humanity in general comes, the Truth brings the command inclusive of man and woman and in the masculine form. Therefore, when the women said, "Why is the man better than the woman?", the word of the Truth came:

﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember God often and the women who do so — God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

Thus the Truth settled the matter.

He, glorified is He, said in confirmation of this:

﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer — those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged a [speck] an iota﴾ [al-Nisa: 124].

Here the male and female enter under one description, which is ﴿and he is a believer﴾. So when the command comes in the general sense addressed to man and woman, it includes the woman within the man, because she is built upon covering and veiling, buried within him, inside him along with him. So when the Truth, glorified is He, says to Mary: ﴿and bow with those who bow﴾, bowing is not specific to women, so that it would say "with those who bow (feminine)"; rather it is a general command that includes man and woman, and therefore the command came to Mary to bow with those who bow.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 44:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿That is of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you...﴾

We have said before that the word "naba'" (news) is only used for a great piece of news. The unseen (al-ghayb) is that which is hidden from the senses. There is a "hiddenness from the senses" that someone like you can perceive, and there is a hiddenness from the senses that someone like you cannot perceive. We said before that the veils of the unseen are three: sometimes the veil is in time, past; sometimes it is future; and a third time the veil is in place. Why? Because the circumstances of events are time and place. If a informer tells me of a matter whose time has passed, this is a breaking through the veil of past time, for the event occurred years ago and has become past. If he tells me of it now, this means he has broken through the veil of past time. If he tells me of a matter that will happen two years from now, this is a breaking through the veil of future time. Suppose he informs you of a piece of news contemporary with your present time; we say: here there is the veil of place, for when I am with you now I do not know what is happening in another city other than the one we are in, even though the time is one.

Therefore we must know that sometimes the veil is time, i.e., the time may be past, or the time may be future, and it may be a veil of place. So if God informs His Messenger of this news, the means of knowledge of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) are three, because the means of knowing a piece of news is one of three things: observation, or hearing, or reading.

The first means, which is observing the news, requires that one be present at the time of this news. The news that God informed His Messenger of happened before the Messenger was sent by no less than six centuries. So observation as a means of knowledge of this news is not valid, because the news occurred in the past. Someone may say: perhaps the Messenger (ﷺ) read it, or heard it; but by the admission of the opponents of Muhammad (ﷺ) he was not a reader, so this means was also ruled out; and by the admission of his opponents (ﷺ) he did not sit with a teacher, so he did not hear from a teacher. Therefore there was no way for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to know of this news except through revelation. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿That is of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be the guardian of Mary; nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]

We said long ago that revelation is an informing in concealment, because ordinary informing is that a person tells another person some news, or a person reads the news; but informing in concealment is called "wahy" (revelation). Revelation requires a "mu'hi" (the one who reveals), who is God; a "muha ilayhi" (the one to whom it is revealed), who is the Messenger of God (ﷺ); and a "muha bihi" (that which is revealed), which is the Noble Qur'an.

If we look at informing in concealment, we find that it has many means.

God reveals, but the one to whom He reveals differs. God, glory be to Him, reveals to the earth:

﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking, and the earth brings forth its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it.﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1-5]

It is informing in concealment, because none of us heard God revealing to the earth. The Truth, glory be to Him, reveals to the bee, reveals to the angels, reveals to the prophets, and there is revelation from other than God, like the revelation of the devils:

﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you; and if you obey them, you are indeed polytheists.﴾ [al-An'am: 121]

And there is revelation from humans to humans:

﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech as deception. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.﴾ [al-An'am: 112]

But when "wahy" is used without qualification, it refers to revelation from God to whomever He has chosen for a message. Whatever other kinds of revelation there are, they call "linguistic revelation" (wahy lughawi); the technical revelation (al-wahy al-istilahi) is only revelation from God to a Messenger. Therefore God's revelation to the earth is not technical revelation, God's revelation to the bee is not technical revelation, God's revelation to the mother of Moses is not technical revelation, God's revelation to the disciples is not technical revelation. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And when I inspired the disciples: "Believe in Me and My Messenger." They said, "We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 111]

This is a kind of revelation that is not technical; rather it is linguistic revelation, i.e., He informed them in concealment. But true revelation is that God informs the one He has chosen for a message, and this is the revelation that came to the Messenger (ﷺ). The Truth says: ﴿That is of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be the guardian of Mary; nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾

Thus the Truth informs us that the Messenger received this news by revelation, so he did not read it, nor did he observe it, and we know that the opponents of the Messenger of God testified that he did not read and did not hear from a teacher. Thus the Truth informs us that the Messenger (ﷺ) was not present with the people of Mary when they cast their pens.

"Pens" (aqlam) refers to the pen with which one writes, or it refers to the arrows (qidah) with which they drew lots when they disagreed about something. When they disagreed, they would bring arrows, so that whoever won would take the disputed thing; we call it lottery (qur'ah). They carried out the lottery to remove desire from a shared division among individuals, so that desire would not incline toward this or that, favoring it over the others. Therefore we too carry out the lottery, placing for each one a slip of paper.

So no one has a desire in carrying out a division by lottery, and thereby we have left the matter to the decree of God, because the slip has no desire. When the people of Mary disagreed over her guardianship and disputed about who had the right to be her guardian, they wanted to remove desire from this matter, and wanted it to be decided by fate, with the verdict given by an arrow that has no desire.

This drawing of arrows would proceed according to what was decreed. As for "their pens," they may be the arrows by which they drew lots, or the pens with which they had written the Torah for blessing.

Some have asked what is meant by the Truth's words "when they cast their pens" and where these pens were cast. It is said that they were cast into the river (or sea). And if the pens are cast into the water, who is distinguished in that? It is said: whichever pen rises upward with its tip, its owner is the winner; or if all the pens sink and one pen floats, its owner is the winner. They must have agreed on a sign or mark by which the pen belonging to the one who had the honor of guardianship of Mary would be distinguished. ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be the guardian of Mary; nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾

The phrase ﴿when they disputed﴾ indicates the intensity of the rivalry among the people, out of longing for the guardianship of Mary, to the degree that the matter of her guardianship entered into a dispute; and so that the dispute might end, they resorted to casting lots with the pens.

Now we move on to another stage.

The first stage in preparing Maryam was her own utterance of the Truth on her tongue: ﴿Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾. Through it she came to know the absoluteness of Allah's power. The second stage was her hearing the story of Zakariyya and Yahya, and the Truth's affirmation to her that He had chosen her above the women of the worlds. This concerns women, and it was a comfort from the Truth to her. Maryam now enters a new stage.

﴿When the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you glad tidings of a word from Him﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 45].

Glad tidings are only of a great and joyful matter. Some may ask: what does the Truth mean by His words ﴿a word from Him﴾? The answer is that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, exercises His dominion over His kingdom by the word, not by treatment. Almighty Allah taught us this by His saying:

﴿Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 47].

This statement is merely an explanation and a bringing-near to us, for there is nothing among us shorter in command than the word "Kun" (Be). His power, in its absoluteness, could precede our pronunciation of the kaf, which is the first letter of "kun". But the Truth clarifies for us, by the shortest command in the manner of humans, that when Almighty Allah wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is. This clarifies that the mere divine will for a thing makes it come into being immediately, and "Kun" is merely the manifestation of the matter to creation. Thus we understand the meaning of the Truth's glad tidings to Maryam with ﴿a word from Him﴾. And the Truth says: ﴿His name is the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam﴾. These are three names: "al-Masih," "'Isa," and "Ibn Maryam."

What is the meaning of al-Masih? It may be the one forgiven of sins; or that among his signs he wiped over the sick and they were healed; or al-Masih al-Mubarak (the blessed Messiah). As for 'Isa, this is the name; al-Masih is the title (laqab); and Ibn Maryam is the kunya (patronymic). We know that the ʿalam (proper noun) in the Arabic language comes in three types: ism (name), laqab (epithet), or kunya (patronymic). Ibn Malik says: "Ismun atā wa kunyatun wa laqabā" (A name came, and a kunya, and a laqab). A proper noun for a person has three states. Either it is an ism, which is what is applied to the named first. The second name that we apply to him: if it indicates the elevation or the lowliness of its bearer, we call it a laqab. As for that which contains "father" or "mother," it is called a "kunya." All three came for 'Isa: ﴿His name is the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam﴾.

"al-Masih" is the laqab, "'Isa" is the ism, and "Ibn Maryam" is the kunya. The coming of 'Isa with the laqab, the ism and the kunya will have a wisdom that will become apparent to us later. And the Truth says about him: ﴿Honoured in this world and the Hereafter﴾.

In our lives we use the expression "so-and-so is wajih (of standing) among the people." The wajih is the one whom an official does not refuse a request made to his face, as we hear in our daily lives: "So-and-so should not be made to feel shame by our refusing any request of his." And as the common folk say: "He is a face that no one would embarrass." So the wajih is one who takes on distinction and prominence, such that people are ashamed to refuse him if he asks. There is another person who may ask you or ask people, and no one cares about him; he spills the water of his face, and the matter ends.

So the Truth's words describing 'Isa son of Maryam: ﴿Honoured in this world and the Hereafter﴾ mean that no one refuses him if he asks, because of the honour of his face. A person is ashamed to refuse one who holds such dignity. Therefore you find that the one asking may say: "Give me for the sake of God's Face." That is, he says to you: do not look at my face, but look at the Face of God; for it is Allah who brought me into this world and created me, and since the Creator has brought me into the world, He is the One who guarantees my provision. So when you assist in the provision of one whom Allah has summoned into existence, you have given for the sake of God's Face. He is the Creator who provides for every creature, even the disbeliever.

Thus a person's giving to the beggar is not giving for the beggar's face, but giving for the Face of Allah. And the Truth says of 'Isa son of Maryam: ﴿Honoured in this world and the Hereafter﴾. We have understood how a person is honoured in this world. So why did the Truth specify 'Isa's honour in the Hereafter, especially since the faces of all believers will be radiant? The Truth specified 'Isa's honour in the Hereafter because he will be asked a question related to the summit of faith:

﴿And when Allah says: O 'Isa son of Maryam, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" He will say: Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You, You are the Knower of the unseen﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 116].

Beware of thinking that this question is a rebuke from Allah to 'Isa son of Maryam. No, the Truth wants to rebuke those who said these words. For this reason the Truth says of him:

﴿And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾ [Maryam: 33].

Because his birth was a commotion, and some of the Children of Israel accused, God forbid, his mother Maryam the virgin. As for "the day of death," we all know the story of the crucifixion, and it caused a commotion. He was not crucified, but the one who betrayed him and informed on him was crucified; Allah cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him, and they killed him. And the day of resurrection, alive, is the day Allah asks him:

﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" He will say: Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 116].

He is 'Isa son of Maryam, upon whom Allah bestowed peace in these three situations. The Truth continues describing 'Isa son of Maryam, saying: ﴿Honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near﴾. The phrase "of those brought near" indicates the exaltedness of the Truth in His greatness. When some people go astray regarding one of them, some may become angry at the person about whom others have gone astray, even though he bears no fault in that.

The Truth, glorified is He, teaches us that the exaggerator has his own recompense, but the one exaggerated about is saved by the mercy of the Forgiving.

The Truth teaches us that the misguidance of some people concerning 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, does not affect the station of 'Isa, peace be upon him, with the Truth. He is brought near to Allah, and the misguidance of others does not affect his station with Allah.

Allah says: ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle...﴾

Speech (kalam) means the utterance that conveys the thought of the speaker to the listener. The saying of the Truth: ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾ means that the ones addressed by Jesus, peace be upon him, in the cradle are the people. And the "cradle" (al-mahd) is that which is prepared as a bed for the infant. The Truth has mentioned ﴿in the cradle and in maturity﴾ as a symbol of something: that Jesus, son of Mary, is among the contingent things (al-aghyar, things subject to change). A state may come upon him once of being in the cradle, and another state may come upon him of being a mature man, and as long as he is within the realm of contingent things, it is not valid for anyone to be enamoured of him so as to say that he is "a god" or "a son of God."

We also understand from ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾ the secret of the existence of the sign of the miracle which Allah granted him while he was an infant in the cradle. For the matter was connected with the honour of his mother, her dignity and her chastity, so it was necessary that a sign should come to erase the wonder of the people when they saw her give birth to this infant without a father or a marriage for her. Yet this matter we have not found to exist, although it is a matter that ought to have been mentioned, because they glorify their prophet, and it was necessary that they not overlook this marvel. Indeed, the speech of an infant in the cradle, since it was a wondrous matter, must have been something preserved and transmitted among the people, and the people would not be content with narrating the event of his speaking in the cradle only, but would preserve what he said and repeat his words.

The word that Jesus, peace be upon him, spoke in the cradle does not support those who describe Jesus, peace be upon him, with a description that contradicts his humanity; for the first word that he uttered was: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah." They concealed all of this matter, because this word refutes the proposition in which they wish to place Jesus, peace be upon him. The Truth says: ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾.

We know that speaking in the cradle means while he is an infant, and "in maturity" (kahlan) means after the age of thirty, that is, in the fourth decade. Some have said that maturity begins after forty years of age. In their narration, the account of the crucifixion occurred before he became mature. So if he spoke in the cradle, it remains that he would speak when he is mature. They said that the incident of the crucifixion or non-crucifixion, or his disappearance from human perception, occurred before he became mature. Therefore there must come a time when Jesus son of Mary speaks when he has become mature. Also, the Truth's saying ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾ means that he spoke as an infant in the cradle and will speak as a mature man, that is, of fully developed form. Thereby we know that Jesus son of Mary has contingent attributes and has states. So if you say he is a god, is divinity in the cradle the same as divinity in maturity?

If divinity were only in the cradle, it would be deficient, because he did not remain in the cradle, and changes occurred to him; and since changes occurred to him, he is originated, and since he is originated, he cannot be a god. After that, the Truth says about Jesus son of Mary: ﴿And of the righteous﴾. What is the account of this?

The wonder about which Allah said, "He speaks to the people in the cradle," was not by his choice, and his speech when mature will be by revelation, meaning he has no choice in it either. ﴿And of the righteous﴾ is intended to refer to his deeds, that is, the behavioural movement.

Why? Because it is not enough for him to be a messenger, nor enough to be a bearer of a sign; rather, he must render the conduct of faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 47:

The Truth speaks on the tongue of Maryam al-Batul (the Virgin Maryam):﴿She said: "My Lord, how can I have a son when no man has touched me...?"﴾

We want to pause for a reflective, contemplative moment at her words: ﴿She said: "My Lord, how can I have a son when no man has touched me?"﴾ Had she stopped at her saying ﴿how can I have a son?﴾, her question would have been a reasonable one. But her addition ﴿when no man has touched me﴾ raises a question: from where did she derive this statement, ﴿when no man has touched me﴾? Did anyone tell her that you will bear a son without a father? The angels did not inform her of that, so her mind turned to the matter of touching. This is the innate nature and acute intelligence of one prepared and readied to receive from God, when He said to her: "The Messiah, Isa son of Maryam."

She said to herself: his attribution to me is by God's command, so he has no father. The Truth has said that he is "the son of Maryam," and therefore her words came: ﴿when no man has touched me﴾, because it is impossible for a child to be attributed to the mother while a father exists. Thus we see the acuteness of receiving from God in Maryam al-Batul. Fear came over her when she learned that Isa was attributed to her, and she said to herself: the conception of Isa will not be through a father, so how can a pregnancy happen without a man touching me? The Most Generous Creator said: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning no man will touch you. He did not say to her: We attributed him to you because you are dedicated to serving the House; rather the Truth said: ﴿Thus﴾, as confirmation of what she had understood about Isa's birth without a man touching her. The absoluteness of power is manifest in His glorified saying: ﴿God creates what He wills﴾.

It is the absoluteness of power, and the absoluteness of power in procreation, begetting, or in the absence of multiplication with respect to man. The absoluteness of power is not confined to bringing into existence maleness and femaleness. Were the absoluteness of power in creation not confined to bringing into existence maleness and femaleness, then He is the Supreme Truth, capable of creating without maleness or femaleness, as in His creation of Adam, peace be upon him, and the Truth, glorified is He, creates through one of the two, as in His creation of Hawwa' and the creation of Isa, peace be upon him. And the Supreme Creator, through maleness and femaleness, can accomplish creation; maleness and femaleness may exist without procreation. Behold the Truth's word:

﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed He is Knowing, Competent.﴾ [al-Shura: 49-50].

This is the will of the Truth. So do not say that the completion of the two elements, maleness and femaleness, is what brings about creation, for creation occurs by the will of the Truth: ﴿Thus God creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ You, O modern people, act through causes. But He who created you and created the causes for you is the One in whose hand it is to bring into existence without causes, for He originated the world, when He first originated it, without causes.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 48:

The Truthful One (al-Haqq) subhanahu says about ʿIsa (peace be upon him): ﴿And He will teach him the Book and wisdom...﴾

When we hear ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾, we understand that what is meant is the Book that was revealed. But since the Truthful One follows that with His words ﴿the Torah and the Gospel﴾, we must ask: what then is meant by "the Book"? Was the intended meaning the earlier scriptures, such as the Psalms (al-Zabur) and the earlier pages (al-suhuf al-ula), like the pages of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)? This may well be correct, and the meaning of ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾ is that Allah taught him what had been revealed before him: the Psalms of Dawud, the pages of Ibrahim, and then the Torah of Musa, to which ʿIsa came as a completion.

Some scholars have said: it is related from ʿIsa (peace be upon him) that nine-tenths of the beauty of handwriting was in his hand. On this basis, ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾ can be understood as the ability to write. As for the statement that ʿIsa (peace be upon him) received from Allah, in addition to ﴿and He will teach him the Book﴾, that he was also taught ﴿wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel﴾: the word "wisdom" (al-hikmah) usually comes after a revealed Book. An example is the words of the Truthful One:

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and the wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34].

The Book of Allah meant here is the noble Qur'an, and the wisdom is the speech of the Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). The Messenger has speech which he receives and conveys, and the Truthful One also grants him the right to say wisdom. As for the Torah which Allah taught to ʿIsa (peace be upon him), Allah taught it to him, because, as we know, the mission of ʿIsa (peace be upon him) came to complete the Torah and to complete what the Jews had diminished from the Torah. The Torah is a foundation of legislation for his era and for the people to whom he was sent. He is, by the Qur'anic text: ﴿and a Messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying] "Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord..."﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 49:

﴿And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel: "Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I will design for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by the permission of Allah. And I will heal the one born blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers."﴾

The word "rasul" (messenger) needs a sign. No one may say, "I am a messenger from God," without presenting before his claim a miracle (mu'jiza) that establishes that he is a messenger from God. The sign (aya), as we know, is the wondrous matter that departs from the laws and norms (nawamis) in order to confirm the messenger's truthfulness in conveying the message. Since the miracle lies outside the norms of human beings, we say to the opponent: when you deny that the bearer of the miracle is a messenger, how do you account for his coming with a miracle that departed from the norm? Thus the miracle binds the denier who challenges, and silences him, because he cannot produce its like. For this reason we say: part of the nature of the challenge is that God, when He gives a messenger a miracle, gives him only something in which the people to whom that messenger is sent excel, because if the truth came to them with something they had not studied or known, their response to the messenger would be to say: "This is a matter we have not trained ourselves in or accustomed ourselves to; had we trained ourselves in it, we would have been able to do the like of it, and you have come to us with something we have not accustomed ourselves to." Therefore God sends any messenger with a miracle of the kind in which the people to whom he is sent excel. For example, Musa (peace be upon him) was sent by God to a people who were masters of magic, so his miracle was close to magic.

Beware of saying that Musa's miracle was magic, for Musa (peace be upon him) did not come with magic but with a miracle. They used to make people imagine things that were not real. Therefore the Qur'an gives you the difference between what God brings through the hand of a messenger, a miracle, and the magic of the people. The Qur'an says:

﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa? He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep, and I have in it other uses." He said, "Throw it down, O Musa." So he threw it down, and suddenly it was a snake, moving swiftly.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 17–20].

It is as if the Truth were saying to Musa (peace be upon him): your knowledge of what is in your hand is that it is a staff you lean on and beat down leaves with for your sheep, but My knowledge is another knowledge. Therefore He commands him to throw the staff, and when he threw it, he found it a snake moving swiftly, so he felt fear within himself. The phrase "he felt fear within himself" is what distinguished between the magic of the people and the miracle of Musa (peace be upon him).

Why? Because the magician throws the staff and people see it as a snake, while he himself sees it as a staff, for if the magician saw it as a snake he would be frightened like the people. Musa (peace be upon him) was frightened because it had truly changed and become a real snake. For this reason God said to him:

﴿He said, "Take it and do not fear; We will return it to its original form."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 21].

Had it been of the kind of magic, he would not have felt fear within himself, because he would have seen it as a staff even though others saw it as a snake. This is the difference.

The people of Isa were also renowned for wisdom and medicine, so the signs were to come from the kind of wisdom and medicine, and then the miracle rose above that, because one who treats and heals a body cannot restore the dead to life, since once a person dies the dead person has left the sphere of the physician's treatment. Therefore God elevated the sign of Isa: he heals the sick and also brings the dead to life, and this is an elevation in miraculousness. Isa said: ﴿that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I will design for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by the permission of Allah.﴾ The word "akhluqu" (I design/create) requires a pause, and likewise "al-tin" (clay), "al-hay'a" (form) and "al-tayr" (bird).

"Akhluqu" is derived from khalq, and khalq is bringing a thing into existence according to a measure; you imagine it and measure it in your mind first, then bring it into being in this state. If it comes out other than your measure, it is not khalq but something haphazard that came without knowledge or measure. Whoever takes a piece of clay and makes something from it is not creating. True creation is what is brought about according to a measure. For example, the crystal cup or glass from which we drink: was there a tree that produced cups, or did the craftsman take sand, melt it, add chemical materials to purify it from impurities, and then shape it into the form of a cup?

So the cup did not exist, and it came into existence according to a measure to be the shape of a cup; it is a creation brought into being according to a measure. What then of God's creation? He creates according to a measure, and there is a difference between the work of humans when they create and the work of God when He creates. When humans create, they create from something existing; when God creates, He creates from non-existence. This is the first difference: He, glory be to Him, creates from nothing, whereas man arranges things in a system that produces reactions which God willed, so they come into being. No one, for example, can make a cup from material other than what God created.

This is the first difference between God's creation and human creation: God's creation is from nothing, human creation is from something existing, though both are according to a measure. Also, God gives His creation a secret that humans cannot give to their handiwork: He gives it the secret of life, and life involves growth and reproduction, whereas humans make a cup, for example, and it remains a cup, and there is no reproduction between a male cup and a female cup.

Man brings his handiwork into existence and it remains in its state; he cannot make it small and then have it grow. But God's work is the work of the Capable who bestows life, so His creatures grow, develop, pass through stages, and produce their like. So creation is bringing into existence according to a measure; this bringing into existence produces what did not exist, and for what did not exist its material is already present; this is in human creation. As for God's creation, God creates from non-existence for which there is no material.

God creates from the thing male and female and gives them the capacity to reproduce. Here is the word of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of semen] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed be Allah, the best of creators.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–14].

The Truth has not prevented His creatures from making things, but God's creation is better. Why? Because He creates from nothing, while humans create from something existing. He, the Truth, creates and brings into His creatures life and reproduction, whereas humans create without growth or life. He is the Truth, the best of creators. So the saying of Isa (peace be upon him), ﴿I design for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by the permission of Allah.﴾

That is, every person can make a statue in the form of a bird. But God made Isa's miracle: he forms from clay the likeness of a bird and breathes into it. You may ask: into what does he breathe? Into the bird, or into the clay, or into the form? If we say the breathing is into the clay after it has become a bird, then the breathing is into the clay as into the bird. In another verse it is stated that the breathing is into the form:

﴿When Allah said, "O Isa, son of Maryam, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [something] like the form of a bird by My permission, and you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission.﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 110].

"Fihi" (into it) may refer to the clay or the bird, and "fiha" (into her/it, feminine) refers to the form. There is also a verse concerning Maryam the virgin:

﴿And Maryam, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her [the garment] of Our Spirit, and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was of the devoutly obedient.﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12].

Here the breathing is into the "farj" (the placket/ chastity), and another verse concerning Maryam the virgin:

﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91].

Once he says "nafakhna fihi," meaning into the farj, and once "nafakhna fiha," meaning into her; both statements are equivalent. And here in this verse we find that the miracle is not that Isa made from clay the likeness of a bird, since any person can do that. It is as though, when he said ﴿that I will design for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by the permission of Allah﴾, he had become a bird from the breath. As for making a bird from clay, any person can do that, but Isa (peace be upon him) does it by the permission of Allah, and the matter must come out different; "by the permission of Allah" here covers both the making of the bird and the breathing into it.

Isa would not have dared to do all that except by the permission of Allah, and the phrase "by the permission of Allah" came from Isa's own tongue as an acknowledgement that this was not of his own craft, as if he were saying to his people: if you were tempted by this...

Then you should have been tempted by Ibrahim all the more, when he cut up the birds and placed a part of them on every hill, then called them.

﴿And when Ibrahim said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." He said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] that my heart may be at rest." He said, "Take four of the birds and incline them toward yourself, then put on every hill a portion of them; then call them, and they will come to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise."﴾ [al-Baqara: 260].

So it was more fitting that people be tempted by what Allah gave Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a miracle. If the temptation were regarding the bringing to life, what Ibrahim did would have been more deserving of it; and if the temptation were regarding his coming into the world without a father, the temptation would have been greater in the case of Adam, because Allah created him without a father or mother. So the temptation has no basis and no logic to justify it. The Truth, glory be to Him, continues on the tongue of Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him):

﴿and I heal the one born blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah.﴾

Why did Isa son of Maryam address these two ailments? Because they were the intractable diseases of that age. The "akmah" is one born blind, that is, blindness did not befall him after his birth. And "baras" (leprosy/vitiligo) is the whitening of a patch on the skin, even if its owner is white or black. Afterwards white patches spread scattered over the whole body, which indicates that the colour of the skin depends on chemicals in the body that nourish this colour; if the chemicals are prevented in the body, the person becomes a leper.

The truth of this is shown by the fact that contemporary science has discovered that the pigments of the skin are special glands found in the body, called the pigment glands; if the pigment glands cease to give colour, leprosy comes, God forbid. It is a difficult disease that they could not treat. When Isa son of Maryam came, God gave him a sign of the kind in which they excelled, which is medicine, and he brought them a sign that is the healing of what they were powerless to heal.

And some of the people who try to bring the miracle close to people's minds say that...

And the Truth (Allah) continues, on the tongue of Jesus son of Mary:

﴿And confirming what was before me of the Torah...ﴩ

We have said that "musaddiqan" (confirming) means that what Jesus son of Mary brought agrees with what came in the Torah. And we have said that "what is before my hands" (ma bayna yadayy) refers to what came before a person, i.e. what preceded him and came before him. Since Jesus son of Mary came confirming what was before him of the Torah in his time, and the Torah was in existence, why, then, did his message come?

But the true statement includes this meaning: Jesus would bring new rulings, and this is made clear in the words of the Truth, glorified is He, on the tongue of His servant Jesus son of Mary:

﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾. So confirmation alone is not the point, for Jesus came to make lawful some of what the Torah had forbidden.

Someone may say: if the heavenly books come confirming one another, what is the benefit of the successive revelation of heavenly books? The answer is: the benefit of later heavenly books is that they remind those who forgot the earlier books, this being the first; and second, heavenly books bring things and rulings suited to the time periods in which these books are revealed. These are the benefits of the heavenly books which came successively from the Truth to His messengers: they remind whoever has forgotten, and they modify some of the rulings.

It is natural that we all understand that beliefs do not change, nor do the news reports and stories, but change extends to some of the rulings. For this reason the true statement came on the tongue of His servant Jesus son of Mary: ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾. We know that the people to whom Allah sent Jesus son of Mary were the Children of Israel, and prohibition and permission come with wisdom from Allah.

Allah has wisdom in what He makes lawful and wisdom in what He forbids. But beware of understanding that everything Allah forbids is harmful: Allah may forbid things to discipline creation, commanding prohibition, and it is not proper to ask about harm in them. A believer may live his worldly life without any harm from some of what Allah forbade being established for him. If someone asks: why did Allah forbid that? You say to him: who told you that when Allah forbids, He forbids only the harmful thing? He, glorified is He, forbids what is harmful, and forbids some of what is not harmful. Therefore the Truth said:

﴿So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which had been made lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 160].

And the detail of this is in another verse:

﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs or entrails carry, or what is mixed with bone. That We recompensed them for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾ [Al-An'am: 146].

So prohibition is not necessarily for what contains harm. Therefore the word of the Truth came on the tongue of His servant and messenger to the Children of Israel, Jesus son of Mary: ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾. Jesus son of Mary came to make lawful for them, by a command from Allah, what Allah had previously forbidden them.

After that the Truth says on the tongue of His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary: ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me﴾. The collection of these commands that preceded is a sign of something astonishing, which reached the people to whom Allah sent Jesus. He, as a messenger and a human being, cannot bring the miraculous sign by himself; rather he must be sent by Allah. They must turn their attention to the fact that Allah, who sent him and who has absolute power to break the laws of nature, is the One who, glorified is He, performed these matters through the hands of Jesus. Jesus son of Mary therefore commands them to fear Allah as a result, and calls the people to obey Him in applying the method of Allah.

Then, after that, the Truth says on the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾

So the messenger and those to whom he was sent are united in that they are all under the nurture (rubūbiyyah) of one God, who takes charge of their upbringing. Upbringing requires bringing into existence from non-existence, requires provision from non-existence, and requires sustaining care (qayyūmiyyah). Jesus, son of Mary, acknowledges his servitude to God, as if he were saying: "I did not do this to be a master over you, but rather, I and you share in servitude to God." ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾

The meaning of ﴿This is a straight path﴾ is that it is a path not twisted, for when a road twists, it deviates from the goal. And so that you know that everyone travels on one straight path, consider, for example, a circle: you will find that it has a circumference and a center. Into the center of the circle we place the point of the compass (sinn al-farajār) in order to draw the circle; then from the center you reach the circumference with radii, and the further we move from the center, the greater the difference becomes, and the closer we come to the center, the more the differences vanish.

If all creation meets at one center, this means agreement; but disagreement arises among people as they move away from the center. Therefore you do not find people with divergent desires, nor do you find people split into sects, except when they distance themselves from the unifying center. The unifying center for them is worship of the One God, and as long as their servitude is to one God, there is in this a gathering of people without desire or division.

Even in the sensible matter, which is the drawn circle, you find that the radii taken from the circumference and passing through the center of the circle overlap at some distance before the center, until at the point of the center they become one thing with no separation between them at all. Likewise, people, when they all meet at the center of their servitude to the One God, and when they differ, they have distanced themselves from servitude to the One God by the measure of that difference.

For this reason, the Messiah Jesus, son of Mary, called people to worship God: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ That is the logic of Jesus. His first logic was when he was in the cradle:

﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."﴾ [Maryam: 30].

The matter of his servitude to God was settled from the beginning; it is the summit of the matter. He is the servant of Allah. The second matter is the matter of the message and the conveying of God's intent and obligation to the creatures of God, so that they may build the movement of their lives upon what God has sent down to them. It is natural that any messenger who comes with a method from God aims to bring people together to follow this method, and to define the movement of their lives by "do this" and "do not do that." When a person hears the command "do," he may find the obligation burdensome, why? Because it binds him to an action that may weigh on him; and "do not do that" carries hardship, because it keeps him away from an action he loved.

A person, in his affairs, is between two things: an action that is hard on him, so he wishes to avoid it, and an action that attracts him, so he wishes to draw near to it. The method came from heaven to say to the human "do" and "do not." So there is hardship in a person forcing himself to perform some act of obligation, and another hardship in keeping away from an act the obligation has forbidden.
