Most people do not turn to the original purpose, nor do they understand it as it should be understood, so the partisans of evil come, and they do not like forcing their souls to the desires of their Creator. The ideas of evil press upon their holder, so he rebels against the obligation of faith, and the ideas of evil try to bring their holder close to doing the things the obligation has forbidden. For this reason people divide, because they have not defined their goal in existence.

Every movement in existence can be known as either a faith-based movement that serves the harmony of the human with the cosmos, or a non-faith movement that spoils the harmony of the human with his nature and with the cosmos. If the movement reaches the human to his faith-based goal, it will be a good and virtuous movement for the believer; and if it distances him from his goal, it is an evil and false movement. Thus we see that the goal is what determines the movement.

A student who goes to school has a goal of graduating in some profession, and as long as that is his goal, we measure the movement of his behavior: is it a movement that brings him closer to the goal or distances him from it? If he is diligent, his diligence is a movement that brings the goal nearer; if he is lazy and sluggish, he distances himself from the goal. Therefore we must define the goal so that we know whether this action is sound or not sound.

The bane of people is that when they define their goals, they fall into considering as a goal what is not a goal. And as long as there are those who consider what is not the goal to be the goal, disorder and misguidance must occur. The one who considers life to be the goal wants to achieve for himself the greatest amount of pleasure in it. But the one who knows that the goal is not life, that life is only a stage, we ask him: "What then is the goal?" He says: "It is meeting Allah and the Hereafter."

This believer's work will be for this goal. But the misguided one who sees this world alone as his goal and does not believe in Paradise or Hell is immersed in his error and turns to what his soul desires, and turns away from what tires him, even if his happiness lies in it.

But the believer knows that the goal is not this world, and that the goal lies in another realm; therefore he strives to apply the obligations of faith to reach the goal, which is Paradise. So what corrupts people's conduct is their ignorance of the goal, and when the goal is present, the human tries to know the action that brings him closer to the goal, and does it; this is goodness. But the one who distances himself from the goal and does the opposite of what leads to it, this is evil.

If this is the case, and the matter lies in defining the goal, you must know that people encounter many events in a way that contradicts knowledge of the goal. And as long as the goal is that you go to the Hereafter to meet Allah, why would a person sink into grief because a beloved of his has passed to the mercy of Allah?

We can ask this person: "Why do you grieve, when Allah has shortened for him his steps to the goal?" Surely you grieve for yourself, because you feel lonely without him, and because you used to find comfort in him; but as for your grief on his behalf, there is no grief, because he has drawn near to the goal and reached it.

In our daily life, when a group's goal is to reach Alexandria from Cairo, we find one person going to Alexandria on foot, because he has no money or means to carry him; another goes riding a donkey, a third riding a horse, a fourth arrives by bus, a fifth arrives by flying in an airplane, and a sixth arrives by rocket. All that has happened is that each one in this group has drawn near to the goal by the means available to him. Thus we find a person who goes to Allah on foot over seventy years, and another whom Allah summons immediately; so why would you grieve for him?

We have the right to grieve for the person who was not successful in serving the goal, but for the one who succeeded in serving the goal, we have the right to rejoice for him, and say: Allah has shortened the distance for him. Most of us, if he has a child who is dear to his heart and young, and he loses him, he sinks into grief saying "he never saw the world." To this person we say: "Man, Allah made your son leap over sins and pass beyond them, and took him to the destination; so what is grieving you?" We must receive well what God decrees for His creation, and know that He is wise, that He is merciful, and that everything from Him must not be understood as outside of wisdom.

Following the verses of Maryam and 'Isa (upon him peace), the Truth (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says:

﴿So when 'Isa perceived disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?" The disciples said, "We are the helpers of Allah. We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾

'Isa, son of Maryam, first mentioned the comprehensive and decisive principle when he said:

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 51].

'Isa, son of Maryam, made clear, beyond any dispute: "I am with you in equal standing as creatures under one God, and I have not come to teach you because I am distinguished from you in anything. Regarding worship, we are equal. Allah is the Lord of me and the Lord of you, and the straight path is the worship of the true God."

When we hear "the straight path" (al-sirat al-mustaqim), we immediately imagine the roads that lead to a destination, and we all know that no road in life is made for its own sake; rather, a road is made to lead to a goal. And when you hear "path" (sirat), we immediately understand the goal we want to reach. The Truth says:

﴿And this is My path, straight, so follow it. And do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. That is what He has instructed you, that you may become righteous.﴾ [Al-An'am: 153].

Since there is a road to a certain goal, the goal must first be determined, and determining the goal aims to clarify the way before a person so that he may take the road that leads to that goal. Thus the Truth says, on the tongue of 'Isa, son of Maryam: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.﴾

Worship ('ibadah) is the worshipper's obedience to the command of the one worshipped. And so we must realize that worship is not confined to the establishment of the ritual pillars of religion: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, the fasting of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it. These are the pillars of Islam, and it is not right for the Muslim to separate himself from his Lord outside the times of the ritual pillars. The ritual pillars are necessary, because they charge the soul with faith-energy so that it can devote itself to the work of building up the world. And we must realize that worship in this world is every movement that leads to the happiness of people and the building up of the universe.

We must also know that the ritual pillars are a technical division made by the scholars of jurisprudence (fiqh), such as the chapter of acts of worship ('ibadat) and the chapter of transactions (mu'amalat). But we must know that everything Allah commands is called "worship." So worship includes what connects the servant with the One worshipped, so that he takes the spiritual charge from his Creator, the Creator of the universe, and what relates to building up the universe. Therefore we have said: when you receive from Allah a command to some act of worship, you receive it while you are connected to Allah's means, in search of provision and other matters of life. The clearest example of this is the Truth's saying:

﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah: 9].

This command to attend the congregational prayer on Friday removes a person from the matter of trade, and this command to pray did not take the person from emptiness; it took the person from an activity, which is trade.

If we look at the precision of the wording regarding trade, we find it is the height of direct taking of provision. The speech of Allah reaches in its precision what no human speech reaches. Allah did not say, for example, "Leave off the craft" or "Leave off the farming," but the Truth mentioned trade here because it is the height of immediate benefit.

The one who plows and plants waits a period that may be long until the fruits ripen, but the one who sells something gains the benefit immediately. The command to leave off this immediate fruit for the Friday prayer was given, and this command includes leaving off all matters whose fruits might come afterward in favor of the prayer.

The word "trade" (bay') is the precise expression, because the speaker is Allah. The Truth did not speak here, for example, of buying (shira'), because the buyer may buy while unwilling, but the seller is filled with joy while selling. A man may go to buy things for his home, then hear the call to prayer and hasten to the prayer, and say to his family afterward: "I went to buy, but the muezzin has called to the Friday prayer." That is because a person must not pay money, whereas the seller benefits to the utmost. Therefore the Truth takes us from the height of "all works and the end of all works, which is the exchange of goods for their prices." But what after the prayer is concluded?

﴿Then when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much, that you may be successful.﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah: 10].

He has brought us out of prayer into life, seeking Allah's bounty. Therefore dispersing in the land and seeking provision is worship.

Let us look at the precision in His saying: ﴿disperse in the land﴾. Dispersal means that people spread out to take their places in all the movements of life, and by this every movement in it is built up. Every movement in life is worship. Thus we comprehend the Truth's saying on the tongue of 'Isa, son of Maryam: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ Then the Truth says: ﴿So when 'Isa perceived disbelief from them﴾. 'Isa, son of Maryam, settled the matter of belief when he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord.﴾ In that is a warning that the followers of 'Isa should not say anything else about 'Isa except that he is a servant of Allah, submissive to Allah, commanded to obey and worship Allah. He set the method before them, saying: ﴿This is a straight path.﴾

The Truth's saying ﴿So when 'Isa perceived disbelief from them﴾ indicates that every bearer of an idea, every bearer of a mission, and every bearer of an aim must be alert in his perceptions, because the bearer of an idea, especially a religious one, brings people out of darkness into light.

Someone may say: why do people live in darkness and not turn toward light from the very beginning? The answer is: there are people who benefit from the masses being in darkness. Therefore among them are oppressors and oppressed. The oppressor who takes by force the good of others and runs riot in the universe fears the man of the call who forbids him from oppression and invites him to guidance toward the logic of reason. Such an oppressor, when he hears the word of reason and the call to faith, does not want this word to be spoken; he hates the word and the one who says it.

The caller is commanded by Allah to be alert, because if some people are guided by his words and become happy by them, he will anger other people, since corrupt society contains those who profit from corruption. So the caller must have alertness of perception. Alertness of perception means attention to the hidden perceptions present in every person. We call the outward ones among them the five senses: touch, sight, hearing, taste, and smell.

The man of the call is commanded to have all his senses at work, so that he knows who cowers and trembles at the moment the call to goodness arrives, and who is at ease and comfortable with the call to goodness. The man of the call is commanded to precise alertness and perception, so that he distinguishes between the one whose complexion changes at the moment of the call to goodness, and the one who rejoices and is glad.

When 'Isa, son of Maryam, announced the method of the Truth, he found that the supporters of injustice, the supporters of transgression, and the supporters of darkness were not pleased with the clear method of belief in Allah. Therefore he perceived disbelief from them, for he was full of alertness and attentiveness. He knew that he had come with a message from Allah to bring people out of corruption into benefit. And when he perceived disbelief from them, he wished to appoint a group to help him in the matter of the call. ﴿He said, "Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?"﴾

The call needs a battle, the battle needs sacrifice, and sacrifice is with the self and with what is precious. Therefore one who finds in himself the ability to bear this matter must be stirred and moved. He did not call out particular individuals; rather, he put forward the call so that the helpers would come, those who see in themselves the capacity to carry the banner of the call, and so that the sacrifice would be by the willing soul, not by response to a summons. ﴿So when 'Isa perceived disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?"﴾ The word "helpers" (ansar) is the plural of "helper" (nasir). A nasir is one who gives you strong support toward your aim.

When 'Isa asked: ﴿Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?﴾, the particle "ila" in the question indicates the goal, which is Allah; that is, who will help me with a help whose goal reaches Allah alone, not these human beings? He does not ask about people who enter the banner of the call for the sake of spoils, or who enter for the sake of status, or for other things. He asks about people of resolve, so that each of them directs his energy toward supporting Allah alone.

An example of this is what passed between our Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), and men of Madinah during their pledge to him at al-'Aqabah. The Messenger of Allah said to them: "I pledge to you that you will protect me in what you protect your women and children from." Al-Da' ibn Ma'rur took his hand and said: "Yes, by the One who sent you with the truth, we will protect you from what we protect our loincloths from." So they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah on that. Then Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, between us and the Jews there are ties, and we are about to cut them. Would you perhaps, if we do that and then Allah makes you victorious, return to your people and leave us?" The Messenger of Allah smiled and said: "Rather, blood for blood and destruction for destruction. I am of you and you are of me. I fight whom you fight, and I make peace with whom you make peace." That is, my protection is your protection, and my sanctity is your sanctity.

Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to them: "You will possess the earth and rule the world, or you will triumph over your enemies"? No. Rather he (ﷺ) said: "I am of you and you are of me." Why? Because if he had told them, "You will triumph over your enemies," they might enter the battle and one of them might die without seeing victory. But the matter that every believer will see is that the Messenger of Allah is of them and they are of the Messenger of Allah, and as long as they remain so, they will enter Paradise with him, which is the ultimate goal.

When 'Isa, son of Maryam, asked ﴿Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?﴾, it was as if he were asking: who will help me with a help whose goal is Allah? Why do we take this meaning? The answer: I take the meaning according to the measure of my understanding, because the intended meanings of Allah in His words are not limited in perfection, and another may come and take from them a different meaning. The meaning of "nasir" is: one who helps with effort and strength. Let us look at how victory in faith comes. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, spoke of victory in faith, He said:

﴿O you who believe, if you help Allah, He will help you and make your feet firm.﴾ [Muhammad: 7].

So victory from us to Allah is by implementing His religion, and this is the intent of Allah. Therefore victory comes sometimes from the believer to his Lord, and sometimes from the Lord to His servant. Perhaps the intent of 'Isa, upon him peace, in "Who are my helpers" was: who will help me so as to join Allah in victory?

We are here before two camps: the camp of faith and the camp of disbelief. 'Isa asked ﴿Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?﴾, meaning that he asks about those who are able to join a goal which is Allah. We understand this meaning in light of what the Truth said:

﴿O you who believe, if you help Allah, He will help you and make your feet firm.﴾ [Muhammad: 7].

We also know that there is victory from the believer to Allah and victory from Allah to the believer. Thus the question of 'Isa, son of Maryam, {Who are my helpers

Would their proclamation of faith mean their belief in the legislation of a previous message? No. Here, faith is intended to refer to what Jesus brought from God, because every messenger came with something from God. Behind the coming of a new messenger there is a matter that God wants conveyed to people. We know that creed does not change, and likewise reports and narratives do not change; but rulings (ahkam) are what change. So the proclamation of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) is a proclamation of faith in what came before Jesus son of Mary of creeds, and in what Jesus son of Mary brought of rulings and legislation.

As for their saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down﴾, the word ﴿what You have sent down﴾ indicates a method (manhaj) sent down from above to below, and when we take legislation we take it from above. That is why we said earlier: when God calls those who have believed in Him to follow the methods of faith, He says: "Come" (ta'alaw), meaning rise up to the level of receiving from the Divinity and take the method from Him, and do not remain in the lowland of the earth; that is, do not follow the desires of some of you, the opinions of some of you, or the legislation of some of you. And since the believer wants to rise in faith, let him direct his conduct on earth toward the method of heaven.

As for their saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and we have followed the Messenger﴾. The one who follows usually is convinced of the one he follows first, so that following proceeds from the values of the soul and not from compulsion by force or coercion. We may find a person forcing another person to walk with him, and in that case the one who is forced is not said to have "followed"; rather, the one who follows, that is, the one who walks on the same path as his companion, does so by his own will and free choice. If a person walks on another's path by force or coercion, that following is merely in the mold, not in the heart. Thus a tyrant may hold a whip and compel a weak person to walk with him, and in that there is subjugation of the weak person's outward form, but he has not subdued his heart. Coercion subdues the outward form, but it does not subdue the heart.

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3-4].

The Truth informs His Messenger that none of the servants can resist their Creator, and that He, glorified be He, is able to give life and cause death. Had God willed to send down a sign that would subdue the necks of all the servants, He would have done so; but the Truth does not desire people's necks, rather He seeks hearts that come willingly and by choice, and that the servant come to faith while being able not to come. This is the greatness of faith. After proclaiming their faith in what Jesus brought, the disciples said: ﴿So write us among the witnesses﴾. This is a lofty, conscious and understanding faith-based request. They bear the trust of conveying from the Messenger, and they bear witness as the messengers bear witness for their peoples, and they ask that God write them among those who witness that the messengers convey the messages of God and that they carry them after them. That is why we said of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ): it is the community to which God entrusted the task of conveying the message of Muhammad until the Hour comes.

Why? Here is the Truth's saying:

﴿And strive for God with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion, the creed of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before and in this [Qur'an], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over mankind. So establish prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to God; He is your protector, and what an excellent protector and what an excellent helper﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

Therefore, no prophets or messengers will come after the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). God has entrusted the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) after Muhammad (ﷺ), and so there is no prophethood after the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

The Sha'rawi commentary on Surah 3, verse 54:

Then, after that, the Truth informs us: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers...﴾

Things that the intellect perceives are designated things (musammayat) and have names, and they come first through the senses (al-hiss), because the senses are the first companion of a human being in perceiving things. After that, meanings come when we grow up and come to know realities. The beginning is always with perceptible matters. For this reason, Allah says about the faith-based method that it is a straight path (tariq mustaqim), meaning that we know the goal and the road that leads to it. The phrase "the straight path" is one of the perceptible matters, which people recognize through applying the rules of the method.

The word "makr" (scheming, plotting) is derived from trees. When you see a tree whose branches are not intertwined with one another, a person can tell that a certain leaf belongs to a certain branch. But there is a type of tree whose branches are wrapped around one another, such that a person cannot know which leaf belongs to which branch. From this meaning we took the word "makr." The man who twists and turns is the one who schemes. The one who winds around a person in order to extract a truth from him, and the one who maneuvers in order to bring out a truth, is doing so. If it is done without intent to harm, we call it a stratagem (hila); if it is done with intent to harm, this is evil scheming (al-makr al-sayyi'). For this reason, the Truth says:

﴿And evil scheming; but evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people. Then do they await anything but the precedent of the former peoples? But you will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 43].

This means that there is a scheming that is not evil, that is, scheming not intended to inflict harm on anyone; we call this "good scheming" (makr khayr). As for scheming intended to inflict harm, it is "evil scheming." And we may ask: what drives a person to scheme? The one who schemes conceals his intentions. He may show you love while he harbors hatred, and he wants to make an action appealing to you in order to scheme against you. For example, he tries to take you to a remote place without people and wants to inflict the greatest harm upon you, and it may be killing.

So, among the foundations of scheming is premeditation (tabyit), and premeditation requires shrewdness and experience, because the one who attempts premeditation may find in front of him someone who detects the hidden aspects of the plot through intuition and conjecture. And since scheming requires premeditation, that is a sign of weakness in human beings, because the strong does not scheme or plot, but confronts.

When the strong man grips a weak opponent, he may release him, because the strong is confident that his strength can harm this weak one. But the weak, when he holds a strong one, regards the matter as an opportunity that will not recur. For this reason the poet says:

"The weak, when he hits an opportunity, kills; likewise is the power of the weak."

The weak is the one who schemes and plots. And the one who schemes may take into account that his opponent is stronger than him in cunning and sounder in intellect, and may be harshly punished by him, so the schemer conceals the matter of his scheme or premeditation.

If the opponents of the faith-based method want to scheme, against whom will they scheme? The Messenger is not in the battle alone, but with him is Allah.

﴿They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none but themselves, and they do not perceive.﴾ [al-Baqara: 9].

Allah knows what any person premeditates. For this reason, when Allah wills to bring something forth and bring it into existence, no one can confront the will and command of Allah. Thus, the scheming of Allah has no counter for anyone to confront.

﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

Whenever you find an attribute that seems improper to be ascribed to Allah, know that it came only by way of mushakala (reciprocal wording) and is not among Allah's Most Beautiful Names. The believers can say to the disbelievers: if you wish to plot against us, Allah is able to turn the scheme back upon you. As for the names and attributes of Allah, they are tawqifi (determined only by revelation), brought down by Gabriel to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But if there is an act of Allah from which we may not derive an attribute and make it a name of Allah, as in ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers﴾, then "the Deceiver" (makhadi') or "the Schemer" (makir) is not among Allah's names. Beware of saying that, because the names and attributes of Allah are tawqifi. The mention here of Allah's scheming is given as a counterpart to an action of humans, to show them that they cannot deceive Allah, nor can they scheme against Allah, because if Allah wishes to scheme against them, they cannot withstand it. The Truth says: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers.﴾

So there is "good scheming," which is evidence that there are those who engineer scheming to lead to good. Why does this verse come here? Because there is a battle that Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) will enter. Jesus (peace be upon him) did not come to fight with the sword to protect the creed; he came as a preacher to guide people to the creed. Victory does not come by the sword alone, but by proof. We know that heaven did not require any messenger to fight for the creed, because heaven itself took charge of chastisement.

﴿So each We seized for his sin; of them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and of them were those seized by the Blast, and of them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and of them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40].

Fighting came only when the Children of Israel asked:

﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: "Send to us a king that we may fight in the cause of Allah." He said: "Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting is prescribed for you?" They said: "And what is [wrong] with us that we should not fight in the cause of Allah, while we have been expelled from our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Baqara: 246].

But the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) is the one to which Allah permitted bearing the sword, to discipline with it those who stand between people and reaching the correct creed.

The sword did not come to impose the creed; it came to protect choice within the faithful soul. Instead of leaving people subdued into adopting a mistaken creed, the Muslims raise the sword against the oppressor who subjugates the servants of Allah. And the servants of Allah have the right to choose their creed.

Therefore, when the enemies of Islam say: "Islam spread by the sword," we respond: Allah began Islam in weakness so that this accusation would fall away. The first Muslims were weak and could not defend themselves, so some of them turned toward Abyssinia, emigrating seeking protection. Had Islam spread by the sword, we may ask: who bore the first sword to coerce the first believer? The believers accepted Islam as a religion while in the utmost weakness and its extreme. Islam began, continued, and still lives by the power of faith.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to an unlettered nation, from a tribe with its own might, and Allah willed that He not support His religion through the conversion of the mighty of Quraysh first; rather, the weak believed in the Messenger (ﷺ), and the Messenger (ﷺ) undertook the journey of the faith-based call for thirteen years, a call to belief in Allah. Then the Messenger migrated to Medina, until all the Muslims became a strong unit of faith, and the sword was raised not to impose the creed but to protect people's freedom to choose the correct creed. And had Islam spread by the sword, how would we explain the presence of adherents of other religions in Muslim lands? Islam granted every person the opportunity to choose his creed.

Thus every Muslim represents an independent unit of faith, and it is the duty of every Muslim to know that Islam spread by the good example, and that as a believer in Allah and in the religion of Allah, he has been chosen by Allah to embody the faithful conduct; Allah has established Islam on earth through conduct and exemplary behavior.

Every Muslim has a duty not to leave in his conduct a breach through which the enemies of Islam can enter to Islam, for the imbalance of a Muslim's conduct relative to the method of Allah is a breach through which the enemies of Islam enter. Therefore, thinkers in other religions, when they turn to Islam and are convinced by it, are convinced because it is a true method. They scrutinize it with reason and are guided to it by the faith-based nature. As for those who want to attack Islam, they look at the conduct of some Muslims and find in it breaches with which they accuse Islam.

Fair-minded thinkers always distinguish between the creed and the follower of the creed, and therefore most thinkers who follow this direction turn to Islam and believe in it. But those who approach Islam through its adherents, if they encounter a committed Muslim, that leads them to believe in Islam. Thus, the great multitude in contemporary Muslim lands, in lands that were not entered by Islamic conquest, were entered by the Islamic example embodied in committed individuals. People were impressed by the pious life these Muslims led, their upright and beautiful conduct, and their gentle, trustworthy, honest, clean manner of dealing. All of that drew the multitude of people to Islam and made them ask: "What made you adopt this good conduct?" They said: "Because we are Muslims."

And the people in those societies asked: "And what is the meaning of Islam?" and the Muslims began explaining Islam to them.

So what drew people to Islam was the committed, methodical conduct. Thus, when the Glorified and Exalted Truth presents the method of successful calling, He says:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."﴾ [Fussilat: 33].

Calling to Allah is done by tongue and righteous action, so that the believer shows that what he calls others to, he himself has found beneficial and adopted. Righteous action is a testimony to the call by tongue. The believer does not stop at that; rather he declares: ﴿Indeed, I am of the Muslims.﴾ He says this to whom? He says it to those who see him in tolerant, pleasing, and good conduct. It is a turning from his own self to his religion.

This explains to us how Islam spread through a group of merchants who traveled to many lands and dealt with people with Islamic manners, with Islamic dignity, and with Islamic piety, so their committed conduct became conspicuous. When the people asked them about the secret of their committed conduct, one of them would say: "I did not bring this from myself, but from my following the religion of Allah, Islam."

An example of exemplary conduct is the first Muslims, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His companions, may Allah be pleased with them, feared for him from his adversaries, so they took turns guarding him. The meaning of taking turns as guards is that they wanted to be the shield against dangers, taking turns among themselves. The Truth, Glorified is He, willed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrate from Mecca to Medina secretly, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, slept in the Messenger's place (ﷺ). 'Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, wanted to be the shield; if a danger came, he was the one who would repel it.

There is no doubt that he did this because he was certain that the Messenger's (ﷺ) survival was better for Islam, even if he ransomed him with his soul. This is the lofty self-sacrifice of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Each one of them loved the Messenger...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 55:

﴿Remember when God said: "O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Myself, and purify you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me will be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ."﴾

After the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, mentioned the matter of the plotting (al-makr) with this wise statement, which is evidence that Jesus, peace be upon him, sensed from the Children of Israel disbelief, scheming, and a plot to kill him. So God reassured Jesus about the outcome of the battle. ﴿Indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself, and purify you from those who disbelieve, and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾. These are four stations which God intended for Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him.

We want to stop now at the word of the Truth: ﴿mutawaffika﴾ (I will take you in full / cause you to die). We often take the meaning of some words from the common and widespread usage, and then the other meanings of the word die out, the common meaning prevails, and we understand the purpose of the word through it. We understand the word "tawaffi" as death, but here we must return to the original usage of the word, for a word may come to be dominated by one meaning, while the word is set for several meanings, and one takes it to make it specific to one of these. The word "tawaffi" may be taken by someone to mean "wafat," which is death. But, did not your Lord, who said ﴿Indeed I will take you (mutawaffika)﴾? He is the One who says in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿It is He who takes you back (yatawaffakum) at night, and knows what you have committed by day. Then He resurrects you therein, that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ [al-An'am: 60].

So ﴿yatawaffakum﴾ here in what sense? It means: He puts you to sleep (yunimukum). Sleep is thus one of the meanings of tawaffi. Did not the Truth also say in His Book, the one in which He said ﴿Indeed I will take you (mutawaffika)﴾?

﴿God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He retains those for which He has decreed death, and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [al-Zumar: 42].

The Truth has indeed called sleep death as well. This is from the standpoint of the logic of the Qur'an. The logic of the Noble Qur'an makes clear to us that the word "tawaffi" does not mean only death, but has other meanings too; however, its usage among the speakers of the language has made one meaning dominant, so the word has come to stand alone with this meaning among them. Whenever the word is used by these people it refers only to this meaning. To these we say: No, we must examine the word carefully and ask why it came.

Someone may say: And why does God choose the word in this way? The answer is: because matters at which the intellect may stop do not affect the required rulings, and God brings them in a style that admits this and admits that, so that no one stops at a matter that does not deserve a pause. Whoever believes that Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised by God to heaven, what has been added to his religion's rulings? And whoever does not believe that Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised, what has been lacking from his religion's rulings? This question does not affect the required rulings of the religion, but the intellect may stop at it. One says: How could he ascend to heaven? Another says: God has taken him in death.

Let anyone believe it as he wishes, for it does not affect the required rulings of the religion.

So, matters which do not affect the ruling required of creation God brings with speech that admits understanding in more than one way, so that the intellect is not left in perplexity before a matter that neither harms nor benefits. We now know that "tawaffa" comes from wafah in the sense of sleep, from His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿It is He who takes you back (yatawaffakum) at night, and knows what you have committed by day. Then He resurrects you therein, that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ [al-An'am: 60].

And from His saying, glory and exalted be He:

﴿God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He retains those for which He has decreed death, and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [al-Zumar: 42].

The Truth, glory be to Him, has called sleep death, because sleep is the absence of the sense of life. The Arabic language makes this clear: you say, for example, to someone to whom you lent a sum of money, who asks you to waive part of it: "No, I must receive (astawfi) my money." And when he gives you all your money, you say to him: "I have received (istawfaytu) my money in full," so he has fully paid (tawaffa) it, meaning you took it in its entirety.

So the meaning of ﴿mutawaffika﴾ may be your taking the thing in full. I say this so that we know the difference between death and killing. Both meet in being a deprivation of life, but the phrase "deprivation of life" may at times be by breaking the structure, like one striking another on the skull so that he dies; this is a kind of deprivation of life, but by breaking the structure. Death, however, does not come by breaking the structure; rather, God takes the soul and the structure remains as it is. For this reason God, in His wise Qur'an, distinguished between "death" and "killing," even though they unite in the extinguishing of life.

﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all; and God will reward the grateful.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 144].

Death and killing each lead to the end of life, but killing ends life by breaking the structure, which is why some humans are able to act upon humans, killing one another. But no one can say: "I want so-and-so to die." Death is what God brings upon His servants as a deprivation of life by removing the soul. Humans are able to affect the body (al-bayna, the structure) by killing, but the structure is not what removes the soul; rather the soul dwells in matter and so lives, and when God removes it from matter it dies and becomes a corpse (ramma), that is, it becomes a rimmah.

So killing is nothing but a disruption of the particular specifications which God intended for the soul's presence in matter, such as the soundness of the brain or the heart. If any of these essential particular specifications is disrupted, the soul says: "I do not dwell here."

When the soul is removed, it is because it does not want to be removed, for some reason, but the structure is no longer fit to house it. We strike the example, and to God belongs the highest example.

Electricity in the house is installed, and one knows the existence of electricity by the lamp from which light is emitted. The lamp did not bring the light, for light does not appear except in a structure with these specifications, as evidence that when the lamp breaks the electricity remains, but the light goes. Likewise the soul in relation to the body. The soul exists only in a body with particular specifications. Most important among these particular specifications is that the cells of the structure be suitable; if the heart stops, it may be massaged before seven seconds pass from the stopping, but if the brain cells are destroyed, everything ends, because the specifications have been disrupted.

So the soul dwells only in a structure with particular specifications, and killing is a basic means of demolishing the structure and removing life, but death is the extinguishing of life without demolishing the structure, and none can do that except God, glory be to Him. But God's creatures are able to affect the structure, because it is matter, and so they can destroy it.

So "mutawaffika" means, on one hand, the completion of a thing, "like the receiving of money," and on the other hand, "sleep." When the Truth says ﴿Indeed I will take you (mutawaffika)﴾, what does that mean? He, glory be to Him, means to say: I want you in full; that is, My creatures cannot destroy your structure. I am taking you to Me complete, for you on earth are exposed to the changes of humans from humans, but I will bring you to a place where you will be purely Mine alone. I have taken you from the humans complete, and the meaning of "complete" is that the soul is in your body with all its specifications, and those who are able to demolish matter have not been able to reach it.

So the Truth's saying ﴿and raise you to Myself﴾ is a wise statement that comes in harmony with the Truth's saying ﴿mutawaffika﴾. Someone may say: Why do we take tawaffi in this meaning? We say: The Truth, in the majesty of His power, was able to say: "I will raise you to Me and then cause you to die afterward." We also say: Who said that the "waw" requires sequence in the event? Did not the Truth, glory be to Him, say:

﴿Then how was My punishment and warning?﴾ [al-Qamar: 16].

Did the punishment come before the warnings or after them? Punishment comes only after warnings. The "waw" indicates only the joining of the two events. Did not God also say in His Book:

﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary, and We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7].

The "waw" does not require the sequence of events. So, supposing you take ﴿mutawaffika﴾ to mean "causing you to die," who said that the "waw" requires sequence in the event? That is, God causes Jesus to die and then raises him. If someone says: Why did ﴿mutawaffika﴾ come first? We reply: Because some may think that the raising is an exoneration from death.

But Jesus will certainly die, for death is an inescapable decree (ḍarbatun lāzib), a matter every human passes through. This is the statement from the standpoint of the Qur'anic text. If we go to the hadith, we find that God entrusted His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to explain and clarify. Did not the Truth say:

﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them, and that they may reflect.﴾ [al-Nahl: 44].

The hadith, as narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim: "How will you be when the son of Mary descends among you, and your imam is from among you?"

That is, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear to us that the son of Mary will descend again. Let us now pause an intellectual pause to confront the rationalists who try to spread doubt in the world, and we say: O rationalists, did you accept at the beginning of Jesus that he came into existence without a father, in a way other than the usual manner of creation and birth? They will say: Yes. Here we say: If you accepted his beginning of birth as something wondrous that breaks the laws, how do you stop at the end of his life if it too breaks the laws? The one who made you accept the first wonder paves the way for you to accept the second wonder. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to Myself, and purify you from those who disbelieve, and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55].

He, glory be to Him, conveys to Jesus: I will take you complete, not subject to being overpowered by humans, and purify you from the filth and impurity of these disbelievers, and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. The word "ittaba'a" (to follow) indicates that there is a "follower" who comes after a "followed." That is, the follower is the one who comes later. So who came after Jesus with a method from heaven? It is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. But on which method are those who follow you? Is it the method they brought, or the method you, O Jesus, conveyed? The one who follows you on a method other than the one you taught will not be a follower of you; rather, the one who comes to correct the situation according to the correct method is the one who has followed you. And Muhammad, Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 56:

God will judge between them concerning that about which they differed. What, then, is the fruit of this judgment? Is there any obligation (taklif) after it? No. Rather, the fruit of the judgment is recompense (jaza'). In the Hereafter there is no action; judgment there is for recompense. And, as we have said: as long as there are followers and disbelievers, and one group above another, and their return is to God, we must see what the judgment will be. Here is the wise word:

﴿As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.﴾

Why did God not state the judgment regarding the believers first? Because the believers fully affirm this; through their faith they know it and are conscious of it. Let us note here that the judgment does not include only the punishment in the Hereafter, but also includes punishment in this world. The punishment of this world will come before the judgment. It is as if the Truth were saying to us: Do not think that My punishing them in this world exempts them from My punishing them in the Hereafter, because punishment in this world alone may befall one who believed in Me.

As for one who disbelieved in Me, I punish him in this world and I punish him in the Hereafter. I do not postpone punishment for the disbelievers to the Hereafter only, but I will add the punishment of this world to the punishment of the Hereafter.

The outcome, after all, is that the disbeliever is punished in this world and in the Hereafter. The Truth says about this punishment that it is a severe punishment, because when an event occurs, the strength proportionate to the one who caused it must be taken into account. Let us strike this example, and to God belongs the highest likeness:

A child may break something within the limits of his strength as a child, and a young man may break something proportionate to his strength. So the matter must be measured relative to its doer. If the doer is God, then can anyone have the capacity to withstand God's punishment? No one can imagine that. And none of these people has any helper, because whomever God defeats and punishes has no helper.

Afterwards, the Truth comes with its counterpart: ﴿But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full...﴾ That is, since those who disbelieved will receive a severe punishment from God, those who believed will receive everlasting bliss by the permission of God.

﴿That is what We recite to you of the signs and the wise Reminder.﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿That﴾ refers to the events mentioned earlier concerning the wife of Imran, Maryam, Zakariya, Yahya and 'Isa (peace be upon him). Each of these people had a wondrous matter in which the law of the cosmos was broken, and all of them are signs, that is, wonders. These wonders have been transmitted to us from what those who lived through those events witnessed. The certain report of these wonders came in the Qur'an, "falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it" (﴿Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or behind it﴾), and it is the true Book which Allah described as "the wise Reminder" (﴿the wise Reminder﴾). So, O believers, be assured that what has reached you through the Qur'an is a report of a reality that falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it. What it has brought of reports about those signs matches the reality that the people of those times witnessed and related.

Then Allah, glorified is He, presents to us the matter of our master 'Isa (peace be upon him). It is a matter that we must pay fresh attention to. We set out the view of those who place him in a position other than the one Allah intended, and we set out the view of those who place him in the position Allah intends. The matter is not a victory for us in this world over a group that says such-and-such, because it is a matter with a consequence in the Hereafter, for which Allah, exalted is He, will hold us to account. Therefore it is extremely important that we clarify it, so that the truth becomes evident and no one wrongs himself.

'Isa (peace be upon him) came upon the religion of Judaism, meaning that he came after Judaism had appeared. We know that the religion of Judaism was distorted by the Jews in a way that made it incline towards purely material matters, with no regard at all for spiritual matters and belief in the unseen. They are materialists, and their materialism is shown in what they said to Musa (peace be upon him), as the Qur'an relates:

﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly," so the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55].

They did not realise that part of the perfection and majesty of Allah is unseen, because if He were perceptible to the senses, He would be delimited (ḥuddida, with the ḥāʾ vowelled with a ḍamma and the dāl with a kasra) and confined to a space (ḥuyyiza). Since in their conception He has been delimited and confined, this means that He might exist in one place and not in another. Allah, glorified is He, is far above such a thing, because He exists in all existence. We do not see Him with the eye, but we see the traces of His works and the beauty of His making throughout the cosmos.

So the fact that Allah is unseen is part of His perfect majesty.

But the Jews portrayed everything as sensory, even the matters by which their lives are sustained, which is food. Allah intended it for them to be unseen, so that it would comfort them in the wandering (al-tīh), and so He sent down to them the manna and the quails as a provision from the unseen which comes to them. They did not cultivate it, did not import it, did not know its essence, and did not strive to extract it. It is a provision from the unseen. Yet they rebelled against this provision coming to them from the unseen and said, as Allah reported about them:

﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils and its onions." He said, "Would you exchange what is lower for what is better? Go down to a city, for indeed you will have what you ask." And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they returned with anger from Allah. That was because they had been disbelieving in the signs of Allah and killing the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61].

They want their food to be as they are accustomed to, and they want to see this food as a material matter of life. Therefore they doubted the provision of the unseen, namely the manna and the quails, and said, "Who can assure us that the manna may not come, or that the quails may not descend upon us?" They had no confidence in a provision bestowed upon them from the unseen, because they handled all their affairs in a purely material way. And since all their affairs were material, they needed a violent shock that would shake the joints of this materialism, in order to bring them out to a meaning in which they believe in the unseen.

We know that materialistic thought sees life only as causes and effects. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, willed to strip them of that materialistic thinking. Therefore He brought 'Isa (peace be upon him) not by way of the ordinary law through which humans come, but made him from a woman without a father, in order to shake the foundations of materialism among the Jews. But the trial came among his people, who said that he was the son of God. Allah, glorified is He, is far above having a son.

We may ask: what was the confusion that led them to say this sonship?

They said: motherhood exists, but fatherhood is impossible, and the confusion arose from the fact that Allah breathed the spirit into him, so Allah is the Father.

We say to them: if the matter were so, you ought to have been tried over Adam more than over 'Isa, because 'Isa (peace be upon him) had a mother in his creation, whereas Adam had neither mother nor father, so the trial over Adam would be greater. And if you say, "Allah said that He breathed into him of His spirit," then you should know what Allah says about Adam (peace be upon him):

﴿When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am creating a human from clay, from black mud altered in form. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him in prostration."﴾ [al-Hijr: 28-29].

So the breathing here into Adam exists. Why then did you stay silent about this story from Adam until the coming of 'Isa (peace be upon him)? Thus that argument is refuted and ended. After that we come to another matter, which is His taking him in death (tawaffī) or his death (wafāt). We will address both matters together, so that we may set out both opinions. Here we ask: why did you fall into trial over this? They say: 'Isa brought the dead to life. We reply to them: Have you not considered the history of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when Allah said to him:

﴿And when Ibrahim said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." He said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but for my heart to be assured." He said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then put on each mountain a portion of them; then call them, and they will come to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 260].

So the scope of trial over Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is great. Likewise, did Musa (peace be upon him) not come with a sign, the staff? He did not come with a dead man who had life in him; rather Allah carried out through his hands the creation of life in something which had no life, so the staff, which is inanimate, became a living thing that moves. Then why did you not fall into trial over the staff of Musa (peace be upon him)?

Thus we know that it is not right for anyone to be tried over the miracle that came with 'Isa (peace be upon him), or over his raising of the dead by Allah's permission. The followers of 'Isa (peace be upon him) agree with us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is unseen, but they differ with us, saying that Allah wanted to make humans familiar with Him by appearing to them in a form, as a human, and so He sent 'Isa (peace be upon him) so that this familiarity might be realised for them.

We say to them: we will examine this matter without sensitivity and without partisanship, but by reason. We ask: "Did Allah create 'Isa in order to give an image of God? 'Isa was a child, then he grew up after that. So which of the images of his stages represented God?"

If it was the image of a child, is that the image of God? And if it was the image of an adult man, is that the image of God? God has one image which we do not see and whose essence we do not know; He, glorified is He, is "not like unto Him is anything" (﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾). So which of the images you say is the image of God?

And if God is in all these images, this means that God has changes, and He, glorified is He, is far above that. Had He been in one image, we would have said that He is constancy and that is how it is: He, glorified is He, is the Truth which does not change. They say that Allah wanted to put His image in a human so as to make people familiar with God, and so He appeared in 'Isa.

We may ask: how long did 'Isa's existence on earth last? The answer: thirty years or a little more. Thus, according to your conception, the period in which people knew the divine image would be limited to these thirty years. We must also ask: "What is the age of the whole human creation?" The age of humankind is millions of years. Did Allah leave His earliest creatures without showing them His image, then leave His later creatures who came into life after the death of 'Isa, that is after he completed his mission and was raised up, without giving them an image of Himself? This is a conception of an unjust god, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is far above association and injustice. It is not reasonable that He would withhold His image so that it remains for only thirty years. This statement is not accepted by a reason that trusts in the absolute justice of Allah.

Furthermore, they say that 'Isa (peace be upon him) was crucified. They are excused in this, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has excused them in this, so He provided the true and just history when He says:

﴿And for their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah." But they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain.﴾ [al-Nisa: 157].

Allah has given them an excuse for saying that he was killed or crucified, because it appeared so to them. It would have been reasonable for them to seek a solution to this problem from Islam, because Islam came to say: "No, it was made to appear so to you; they did not kill him nor crucify him." For this act, killing or crucifixion, undermines their idea that he is a god or the son of a god. For if the crucified one were a god or the son of a god, he would have the power to overcome the crucifier. How can it be reasonable that a god, or the son of a god, be subject to the power of a creature? When Islam says that 'Isa, son of Maryam, was not crucified, it has honoured him. Thus you see that Islam came to purify all beliefs from the defects of distortion committed by the followers of those religions.

After that, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, comes to set before us a disputed matter which occurred in the days of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that people, Muslims, Christians and Jews, may come out of this confusion, and so that this may happen in affection, because they all believe in the worship of one worshipped Lord. A delegation of the Christians of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah. They met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and these people had disputes with the Jews and disputes with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), just as the Jews and Christians together had disputes with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The dispute between the Jews and the Christians arose because the Jews and the Christians hold contradictory views about one another, which Allah relates to us:

﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything," while they recite the Scripture. Likewise said those who do not know, the like of what they say. So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 113].

So the Jews say, "Ibrahim was a Jew," and the Christians say no, "Ibrahim was a Christian."

As for the dispute between the Christians and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), its cause is that they wanted to speak about the matter of 'Isa, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wanted to clarify the matter conclusively, so that it would not remain hanging, tossed about by tongues and becoming a source of trials. When the Christians of Najran gathered under the banner of their leaders, among whom were one called al-Sayyid, and another called al-'Aqib, the man of counsel, and with them a priest, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "What do you say about 'Isa?" They said: "He is the son of Allah." The Messenger said to them: "'Isa (peace be upon him) said, 'I am the servant of Allah,' and he is His servant and His Messenger and His word which He cast to the virgin Maryam." They became angry and said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Have you ever seen a human without a father? If you have seen the like of that, then tell us about it."

Here the noble verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, the likeness of 'Isa to Allah is like the likeness of Adam...﴾

Ahmed Mahmoud (Editor's note: the passage above repeats the preceding paragraph verbatim in the source; it has been translated as it appears.)

The disputation between the Christians and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arose because they wanted to speak about the matter of Jesus. Almighty and Exalted God willed to settle the question with a final settlement, so that it would not remain suspended, passed around on tongues and becoming a source of strife. When the Christians of Najran gathered under the banner of their leaders, among whom was one called al-Sayyid, and another called al-'Aqib, the man of counsel, and with them a priest (qissis), the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "What do you say about Jesus?" They said: "He is the son of God." The Messenger said: "Jesus, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed I am a servant of God,' and he is His servant, His messenger, and His word which He cast to the virgin, the pure (al-Batul)." They became angry and said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Have you ever seen a human being without a father? If you have seen the like of that, then tell us about it."

Here the noble verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, the example of Jesus before God is like the example of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾

The decisive word came with the strongest proof. If Jesus, peace be upon him, came into being without a father, then Adam, peace be upon him, came into being without a father and without a mother. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "Do you know that I am the Messenger of God and that I am the prophet of this community?" They said: "Give us time until tomorrow, and we will discuss these matters." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) called them to faith, but they said: "No."

When Almighty God presents a conflict between a matter of truth and a matter of falsehood, He says:

﴿And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance, or in clear error.﴾ [Saba': 24]

That is, one party is upon guidance and the other party is in manifest error. Why? Because the two matters contradict each other and cannot be combined. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) invited them to meet with him in a open place, where both parties would summon their sons and women, and all would beseech the true God (mubahala, mutual invocation in which each side calls down God's curse upon the liars). And in this the noble statement came:

﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters...﴾

The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt.

The clear truth and the decisive word had come from God to His Messenger (ﷺ), so there is no room for doubt or dispute. Whoever wishes to have a matter judged by someone should accept judgment by the just God, who never judges by falsehood. He, glory be to Him, is the Truth. And this statement comes: ﴿Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly and lay the curse of God upon the liars.﴾ Both parties are called to bring their sons and women. The Messenger (ﷺ) is called to bring his sons and women, and those who have authority over them, in his presence (ﷺ). They too are called to bring their sons, women and themselves for mubahala (mutual imprecation, invoking God's curse on the liar).

A questioner may ask: why is the call made to sons and women? The answer is that sons and women are the closest kin who concern every person, even if he is not a messenger. They are a part of a man's own self and his household. So the Messenger (ﷺ) was commanded to say to them: "Bring your beloved ones from among your sons and women, for they are the dearest of family and the closest to the hearts, and enter with us into mubahala." "Mubahala" means earnest supplication for the descent of God's curse upon the liar. The word "bahla" (with a damma on the ba') means curse. When both parties say, "O Lord, let Your curse fall upon the liar among us," this supplication carries absolute justice, for the God who can send down the curse is the true God. He will send the curse upon those who associate partners with Him. Even if curses could descend from many gods, the curse would fall upon the followers of the One God.

Therefore the call to mubahala, and the bahla as we have said, is a supplication to the overpowering Power that disposes of the matter to end the dispute. Then the meaning of mubahala here became general supplication, so we say, "We invoke God (nabtahil ila Allah)," meaning we call upon God.

Thus the Messenger (ﷺ) brought them the command revealed from the true God, to call the sons, women and selves. But they said to the Messenger (ﷺ): "Give us respite until tomorrow, and we will come to you."

Then in the morning they sent one of them to see what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had done, and whether he was truly ready for this matter, or whether it was merely a threat from him. Their envoy found that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had come with al-Husayn, al-Hasan, Fatimah and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Therefore they said: "No, we will not be able to do mubahala." By God, no people have ever invoked curses against a prophet without being seized. They sought to appease the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "Let us remain upon our religion, and let Muhammad and his followers remain upon his religion." They had thought that the call to mubahala was merely a threat that the Messenger would not carry out. But the man of true certainty came with his family, ready for mubahala. Only one who has deep faith and certainty will approach such a situation; as for one who lacks certainty, he will not approach mubahala and must certainly withdraw from it.

They withdrew from mubahala and said to the Messenger (ﷺ): "Let us agree together that you will not attack us or frighten us, on condition that we send you tribute (jizyah) in Rajab and in Safar, consisting of horses and other things!" They fled from mubahala because they knew they were in doubt about their matter. As for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he was certain of what God had revealed to him. It was the custom of the Arabs, when they went out to war, to take their women with them, so that a man would be ashamed to flee, and so that he would not leave his children and women to be humiliated after his death; if he was killed, they would be killed with him too.

So, if we now wish to end the dispute concerning Jesus, peace be upon him, let us listen to the word of the True One, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with God is like the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt.﴾ This is the truth coming from the Lordship; so do not be, O listener, among those who doubt in this matter.

If someone wants to produce an argument opposing the argument that came from God, we can settle it by saying: ﴿Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars.﴾

None of them would dare to do that. Why? Because those before them have already fled from mubahala (mutual invocation of curse).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 62:

And because God, glorified be He, wishes to increase the believers in faith and in assurance that what He sends down to His Messenger is the truth, He - majestic is His glory - said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative...﴾

His saying, the Truth: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ draws our attention to the fact that what the Truth relates to us is absolute truth, and not merely an account or a story, or a mixture of imagination with reality, as happens in modern times, when the word "qissa" (story) was taken in modern literary usage, which came from Western civilization. In its well-known modern form, the story is one in which imagination plays a great role. But if we knew that the word "qissa" is derived from qassa al-athar (to trace the traces), the people of literature would have searched, regarding what they write of narratives and imaginings, for a word other than "qissa". Al-qasas is the tracing of what has actually happened, with no alteration in it and no fancies.

And here is the Truth, glorified and exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative, and there is no god except Allah﴾. So when the narrative comes from the One God, let us be assured that there is no other god who will bring other narratives. And because the One God is ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning the one who prevails over His affair, and although He prevails over His affair, He is wise in His dealings.

Yet did those people who argued take heed? No. The Truth (Allah) says: ﴿But if they turn away, then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.﴾ His saying ﴿But if they turn away﴾ indicates that Allah had known from eternity that they would not accept the mubahala (mutual invocation of curse). Thus they passed judgment on themselves that they were the corrupters, and the Truth, glory be to Him, was true in His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.﴾ Nevertheless, Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to invite them to the complete religion, because they believe in God, in the heavens, and in the Book. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you..."﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 64:

﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah. And if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'"﴾

It is a call to a word that is straight, with no crookedness in it. ﴿That we will not worship except Allah﴾ — this is a matter about which there is no dispute. Then ﴿and not associate anything with Him﴾, meaning we do not bring into worship anyone who cannot rise to the majesty of His perfection. Sound minds reject the notion of "shirk" (associating partners with God), for shirk — on what would it be? Is shirk regarding the creation of the universe? Every created being that they made a partner in divinity came only after Allah had created the universe. Or is shirk regarding the management of this universe?

If that is the cause of shirk, it is too trivial to be a cause, because the Truth, glorified is He, is capable of managing this universe, and He sent down a method which, when man follows it, the universe becomes harmonious. Therefore, any shirk is unnecessary. And if — God forbid — He had a partner, and some god possessed special powers, then these powers would diminish the powers of the second god. This is a deficiency in the power of these gods, and for this reason the Truth settles this matter with His noble words:

﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any god; for then each god would have taken away that which he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Glory be to Allah above what they describe.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91].

So this matter of partners is not acceptable. After that, the Truth says: ﴿and not take one another as lords instead of Allah﴾. That is, that we do not take from among ourselves a priesthood and priests, one of whom lays down what is lawful for us or unlawful upon us. Permitting and forbidding come only from Allah, and no created being has the right to make lawful or unlawful. Then the Truth says: ﴿And if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾ That is, whoever does not accept the worship of the One God, who has no partner and no lords who make lawful or unlawful, but wants lords and partners, this means that his heart is not prepared to accept the matter of faith; for the matter of faith is distinguished by one single source which has absolute power, and which is the source of command in motion, the One, the Unique. Thus the movements in the universe do not conflict.

All our movements, which are subject to the method of Allah, are governed by "do" and "do not do." If there were one god who said "do" and another god who said "do not do," that would mean, God forbid, that these gods are changeable and have desires. The Truth, glorified is He, settles this with His words:

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but from their reminder they turn away.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 71].

Thus was the call of Allah upon the tongue of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah. And if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'"﴾ It is a verse carrying a call that is straight, without protrusions: there is no worship except for Allah, we take "do" and "do not do" only from Allah, we do not associate anything with Him, and none of us takes another as a priesthood or a source of permitting or forbidding. If they reject and turn away, let the believers say: ﴿Bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾ That is, there is only one God, with no partners, and none of us takes another as lord; and this is a testimony that Islam came with a straight matter, free of crookedness or protrusion, and we follow what it brought.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham...﴾

He, the Truth, asks them: why is your dispute about Abraham, the Friend of God (Khalil Allah)? The Jews among you attribute themselves to Moses, and the Christians among you attribute themselves to Jesus, peace be upon him. Yet Abraham, peace be upon him, cannot have been a Jew as the Jews claim, for Judaism came after Abraham. Nor can the Christians claim that Abraham was a Christian, for Christianity also came after Abraham, peace be upon him. So why the argument? The Torah and the Gospel were sent down after Abraham, so how could he have been a follower of the Torah and the Gospel?

Afterwards, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Here you are! You argued about what you have knowledge of...﴾

That is: you have disputed concerning what remains with you of the Torah, and you want to take disputation as an open door, arguing about everything, while you do not know what the Creator, the Most Merciful, the Knower of the unseen (ʿAllām al-Ghuyūb), knows.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary tells us that the Truth clarifies this matter, saying: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a upright monotheist (ḥanīf), a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.﴿

Thus it is confirmed that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was not a Jew, because Judaism came after him. Nor was Ibrahim a Christian, because Christianity came after him. Rather, being the Friend of the Most Merciful (Khalīl al-Raḥmān), ﴿he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾ We understand that the word ﴿ḥanīf﴾ means the pure religion that comes from God. The word is derived from sensory images: al-ḥanf is an inclination in the legs from below, meaning a crookedness in the feet, and then ḥanf was transferred to every matter that is not straight.

Here a person asks: was Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in crookedness or in straightness? And how can he be a ḥanīf when ḥanf is crookedness? We say: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was upon straightness, but he came into a world of idolatry and overpowering crookedness, for the world was crooked. Ibrahim came to depart from this crookedness, and since he was turning away from crookedness, he was straight. Why? Because the messengers come only into a situation of overpowering corruption in belief and legislation. When the Truth, glory be to Him, sends down His method, He places in every soul a faithful cell (khaliyya īmāniyya). The faithful cell awakens once and so adheres, and becomes heedless once and so deviates; then awakening comes after deviation, and there is attentiveness. Thus there exists the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwāma), that soul which whispers to a person at the moment of a wrong act: God has not commanded this.

The person returns to God's method repentant and seeking forgiveness. If the self-reproaching soul does not exist, the soul becomes the one that commands evil (al-nafs al-ammāra bi'l-sū'), which always inclines toward deviation. Around the single soul there exist many souls that try to resist and correct the crooked; these are souls from the environment and society. Sometimes moderation and the turning toward right after error come from the person's own self, that is, from the self-reproaching soul; and sometimes the self-reproaching soul is absent and only the commanding soul exists.
