But the society around this person is not free of containing a cell of goodness that guides him to what is right. If, however, all the cells in society have become commanding to evil, then who will straighten and correct it?

Here God must send a new messenger, because the human being lacks restraint from the self's own inner cells of faith, and lacks restraint from the existing society, which is likewise devoid of those good cells. Thus darkness engulfs and spreads, and God sends a messenger to rekindle the flame of faith in souls. God, glory be to Him, has guaranteed to the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that no prophet will come after the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. Therefore it is necessary that goodness remain within them: goodness persists in the Muslim self, so if heedlessness occurs, the self-reproaching soul corrects it, and if there is a commanding soul, there are many at peace who guide the commanding soul to what is right.

Thus the nation of Muhammad will never be without goodness in any age. As for the earlier nations, their matter is different: God sends them messengers when all the lamps of goodness in souls are extinguished and the darkness of corruption spreads, so heaven intervenes; and when heaven intervenes, it is said that heaven has intervened upon crookedness to straighten and correct it.

So Ibrahim, peace be upon him, came as a ḥanīf, that is, inclining away from what inclines, and since he was inclining away from the inclined, he was straight. The tolerant ḥanīfiyya is straightness. Thus we understand the Truth's saying: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾

Ibrahim is the father of the prophets. Judaism had not yet been distorted and altered, and likewise Christianity; it would have been acceptable for the Jews and Christians to be upon the creed of Ibrahim, because religions do not differ in their foundations, though they may differ in some legislation suited to eras. Therefore, our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, cannot be a Jew given the distortion that occurred among them, meaning he would not agree with them in their belief; and likewise he cannot be a Christian for the same reasons. Rather, he ﴿was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, and not of the polytheists,﴾ that is, he was inclining away from the path of crookedness.

Someone may say: why did God not say "Ibrahim was upright" and why did He use the word "ḥanīf," which indicates crookedness? We say: had He said "upright," some people would have thought that he followed the way of the people of his time, who were in crookedness and error. For this reason the Truth describes Ibrahim as ﴿a ḥanīf, a Muslim.﴾ The word ﴿Muslim﴾ requires "muslam ilayh" (one to whom one surrenders), which is God, meaning he surrendered his reins to God, and "muslam fīh" (that in which one surrenders), which is belief in the method.

When Ibrahim surrendered his reins to God, he submitted in everything stated with "do" and "do not." If we apply this derivation to the procession of prophets and messengers, we find that Adam, peace be upon him, was a Muslim, Noah, peace be upon him, was a Muslim, and all the prophets who preceded the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, were Muslims.

Every prophet and messenger in the procession of messengers surrendered his reins in everything to the one to whom he surrendered (God), and applied the method that was sent down to him. Thus Islam was a description of all the prophets and of the believers of earlier scriptures, until the complete method was sent down, with which the message of heaven was concluded, upon Muhammad, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, with "do" and "do not." No new command comes after it, and no one will legislate a Islam for God other than what was sent down upon the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.

The purpose of Islam has been completed, and the method has come down in its entirety from God. Islam settled as a purified creed, and Islam became the name of the Muslim nation, the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, which cannot be superseded, because it is a nation that has surrendered to God in everything stated and sent down upon Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Ibrahim are those who followed him...﴾

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 68:

﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believed. And Allah is the Ally of the believers.﴾

It should be noted that every messenger before our master, the Messenger of Allah, was sent to a specific nation. Moses (peace be upon him) was sent by Allah to the Children of Israel, and likewise Jesus (peace be upon him). He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾, meaning a messenger who submitted within the limits of applying the method he brought, which was revealed to these messengers. Then some of the legislation was altered, and the faith-based method was purified through the final message, which is the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), and which is universal for all mankind. Some people from those nations believed in his message (peace and blessings be upon him), just as those among whom the Messenger of Allah was sent believed in it. The procession of faith in the final religion continued until it reached us. Thus the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) became the final of the Islamic nations, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers.

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My likeness and the likeness of the prophets before me is that of a man who built a house and perfected and beautified it, except for the place of one brick in a corner of it. People began to circle around it and admire it, and they said: 'Why was this brick not placed?' So I am the brick, and I am the Seal of the Prophets."

As for their saying that Abraham (peace be upon him) was a Jew or a Christian, they only brought this up because Abraham (peace be upon him) is the father of the prophets. They wished to invoke the origin of the faith-community in an attempt to attribute it to themselves, as if faith were inherited by lineage. The matter of faith is not by race, homeland, or blood, or any other affiliation other than affiliation to the method of the One God. Therefore, the people most worthy of Abraham are not those who descended from his offspring; rather, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him. Our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) followed Abraham (peace be upon him), so Abraham has no connection to those who came from his lineage but distorted the method and did not persist in faith. Allah settled this matter with Abraham when He, glorified be He, said:

﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said: "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." He said: "And from my descendants?" He said: "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124].

The Truth tested Abraham with words, which are the commands and prohibitions, and Abraham (peace be upon him) fulfilled them completely, to the utmost degree of commitment; it was not a mere fulfilment that merely made a show of formality, but a fulfilment in both form and substance together.

An example of fulfilling the commands and prohibitions in form only is our observation of someone who receives the command from Allah to pray five obligatory prayers, and so prays these five obligatory prayers as a formal procedure. But there is another person who prays these five obligatory prayers in their full right, in both substance and form; he fulfils the divine commands in a way that pleases Allah.

Abraham (peace be upon him) performed the trials that came in the words of obligation from Allah in the most perfect manner.

Did Allah not command Abraham (peace be upon him) to raise the foundations of the House? Would it not have sufficed Abraham (peace be upon him) to carry out the command of raising the building of the Kaaba as high as his hands could reach? Had he done that, he would have fulfilled the command; but Abraham (peace be upon him) wished to discharge the command of establishing the foundations of the House in complete fulfilment, so he built the Kaaba as high as his hands could reach, and as high as his ingenuity could also reach. He brought a stone to stand on, to increase the height of the wall of the Kaaba by the height of the stone. He wished to complete the building with his capacity in his hands and with his inventive cunning too, for "scaffolds" and other tools that help a person rise from the ground to the utmost of his ability were not known in that era.

Had Abraham (peace be upon him) raised the foundations of the building only as high as his hands could reach, he would have discharged Allah's obligation; but he wished to perform it with his real personal capacities, and he added to that a stratagem of his own invention, so he brought the stone on which he stood to increase the wall of the Kaaba. This is what we know when we visit the Sacred House as the "Station of Abraham." When Abraham completed the words in this manner, the Truth, glorified be He, said to Abraham:

﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124].

That is: you, O Abraham, are trusted to be a leader for the people in their religion, because you discharged "do and do not" perfectly and with mastery. Consider Abraham's zeal for the method of his Lord: he did not wish the method to continue only during his own life, but he asked Allah that the method and the leadership should remain in his descendants. So the Truth, glorified be He, said, on Abraham's tongue, seeking the continuation of this trust among his descendants:

﴿And from my descendants﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124].

Our master Abraham was filled with zeal for the method and feared for it even after his death; but the Truth, glorified be He, teaches all creation through Abraham, so He says:

﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124].

That is, the matter is not inheritance, for there will come from your descendants someone who is a wrongdoer to himself and who alters the method to suit his desires, and such a person does not possess the qualities of leadership. The Truth teaches us the rules of the inheritance of prophethood: these rules require that the inheritors of the prophets be those capable of applying the method in its entirety without distortion. An example of this is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us when he said to Salman al-Farisi: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House."

The master of creation, Muhammad (ﷺ), did not say to Salman al-Farisi, "You are an Arab," no; rather, he attributed him to the People of the House, that is, he attributed him to the inheritance of prophethood with what this inheritance requires of applying the method in its entirety. The Messenger (ﷺ) knew what the Truth, glorified be He, taught our master Abraham (peace be upon him) about the inheritance of prophethood. This inheritance is not by blood, but by applying the method in letter and spirit, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) learned from what the Truth taught him about Noah (peace be upon him). The Truth promised Noah that He would save him and his family from the flood.

Noah (peace be upon him) saw his son overwhelmed by the drowning, and asked: "Did not Allah promise me that He would save my family?" Then Noah (peace be upon him) called out to his Lord, as the Noble Qur'an reports when it says:

﴿And Noah called to his Lord and said: "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."﴾ [Hud: 45]. The Truth responded to Noah's request for the salvation of his son:

﴿He said: "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose work is other than righteous. So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I admonish you, lest you be among the ignorant."﴾ [Hud: 46].

Let us consider the Qur'anic reason for the denial of family membership to the son of Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family﴾? Why? ﴿Indeed, he is one whose work is other than righteous﴾. The Truth did not say "Indeed, he is a doer of unrighteous work" — self-attribution is excluded — because it is the deed for which Allah calls to account; faith is not lineage, nor affiliation to a particular land or a particular people; it is deeds. Whoever acts according to the law of any messenger is of that messenger's family; affiliation to the prophets does not come to the person who descends from the prophet's lineage, but affiliation to the prophets comes through the deeds that the person performs.

In another passage the Truth teaches us about our master Abraham a situation that depicts the mercy of the Creator toward all His creation, both those who believe and those who disbelieve. Abraham (peace be upon him) asked for abundant provision for the people of his household whom he had settled in Makkah, as the Noble Book reports:

﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 126].

Did the Truth answer Abraham's prayer by providing only for those of the people of Makkah who believed? No; rather, He provided for the believer and the disbeliever. And He taught Abraham this when He said to him:

﴿He said: "And as for him who disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 126].

Material provision is guaranteed by the Truth to all creation, believer and disbeliever alike, and material sustenance is guaranteed by Allah because it is He who brought the believer and the disbeliever into this world. But the provision of the method is a different matter: following the method requires submission to what was brought without distortion. Few have followed this method after Abraham (peace be upon him): only a small number believed in the message of Moses (peace be upon him) without distortion.

Then Jesus (peace be upon him) came with a message that turned the Children of Israel away from pure materialism toward belief in the unseen, but the message of Jesus (peace be upon him) was also distorted. Accordingly, the people most worthy of Abraham (peace be upon him) are those who followed the correct and purified final method, which is pure of all earlier messages, and these are the ones who believed in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). And Allah is the Ally of all the believers, of those among them who believed in the message of Abraham, Khalil al-Rahman, with correct and complete faith, and of those who believed in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ)..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 69:

After that, the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray...﴾

The meaning of "wadda" (wished) is "tamannat" (desired) and "ahabbat" (loved). Why did they love to lead the believers astray? Because the deviant, when he sees the upright person, knows that he is like a deviant who has not succeeded in governing his conduct according to the requirement of the faithful obligation of "do" and "do not do." As for the committed believer, he has been able to govern himself. When the non-committed person sees another person who is committed, he despises himself, and says to himself, out of envy of the believer: why and how was this committed person able to master himself?

The deviant tries to draw the committed person to the side of deviation, and when he cannot draw the committed person into deviation, he mocks him, ridicules him, and tries to trick him so as to take him to the side of deviation. Did not Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, say:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their own people, they would return jesting. And when they saw them, they would say, "Indeed, these are the astray." But they had not been sent as guardians over them.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-33].

This is what happens now when the people of deviation see a believing person of uprightness, so they mock him with words like the ones you hear, "Take us under your wing," or they try to damage his faith. And when the people of deviation return to their families, they relate with amusement how they mocked the believers, as though they are bringing happiness to those families with stories of mockery of the believing person. The Truthful One reassures the believers that they will have a day on which they laugh at these disbelievers:

﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34-35].

The Truthful One asks the people of faith:

﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 36].

That is, you have already known how I repay the people of disbelief with punishment.

Therefore, the people most worthy of Abraham are the believers in the message of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Some of the people of disbelief do not cease trying to draw the believers into error. They love that and desire it, but not everything a person wishes for happens. Desire (tamanni) is for a person to seek something impossible or hard to attain. They love that, but they will not reach what they want. This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted:

﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray, but they do not lead astray except themselves, and they do not perceive.﴾

They wish to lead the believers astray, but can they reach that? No. An example of this is what some of the Jews among the People of the Book did when they went to Mu'adh ibn Jabal and to Hudhayfah, the two great Companions, and they also went to 'Ammar, the great Companion, and tried to tempt Mu'adh, Hudhayfah and 'Ammar, but they were not able to.

We must know that "dalal" (going astray) comes with multiple meanings. Sometimes it comes in the sense of going away and being lost in a thing, such as the saying of the Truthful One:

﴿And they say, "When we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?" Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.﴾ [as-Sajdah: 10].

The polytheists asked, "After we dissolve into the earth and our primary elements disintegrate, will we return again and be raised anew?" And sometimes going astray comes in the sense of a person not being guided to the face of the truth, as the Truthful One described His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when he rejected the worship of idols and kept searching for the true way:

﴿And He found you lost and guided you.﴾ [ad-Duha: 7].

That is, O Muhammad, the approach of Quraysh in worshipping idols did not please you, and you kept searching for the true way until Allah guided you and sent down to you this straight method. You were astray seeking guidance, and then complete blessing came to you from Allah.

There is another kind of going astray: that a person recognizes the true way, but deviates from it and turns away from this method, such as the saying of the Truthful One: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray, but they do not lead astray except themselves.﴾

We ask: how does self-misguidance happen? The answer is: the one who is astray, who knows the method and denies it, is committing a sin, and this sin grows more grievous by the astray person's attempt to lead others astray. He is not content with his own going astray, but increases in error by his attempt to lead others astray. This noble statement has resolved for us a difficulty in understanding the saying of the Exalted:

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative.﴾ [Fatir: 18].

And in understanding His saying, majestic is His affair:

﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and [also] some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.﴾ [an-Nahl: 25].

Thus we know that the "wizr" (burden) in the verse of Fatir is the burden of going astray in oneself, and the "awzar" (burdens) in Surah an-Nahl are for leading others astray. These misguided people are not content with going astray themselves, but increase their own error with burdens from leading others astray; by that they grow in error, in addition to bearing their burdens in full. ﴿And they do not lead astray except themselves, and they do not perceive.﴾

They do not perceive the catastrophe that will come from this compounded error, for which they will receive punishment. If they had reflected a little in understanding, they would have stopped leading others astray, and if they had sought the true certainty, they would have stopped going astray themselves.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 70:

After that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the Signs of God...﴾

The Truth questions them, through the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ: Why do you disbelieve in the wondrous Signs of God while you are witnesses to them? Here someone may ask: did the People of the Scripture witness the wondrous Signs in the time of the Messenger of God?

The answer is: did the Jews not seek victory (yastaftihun) over those who fought them by the coming of a prophet who was about to be sent? They used to call upon God, saying: "We ask You by the right of the Unlettered Prophet whom You promised to send to us at the end of time, that You would not help us against them," and they were helped over their enemies. But when he (ﷺ) was sent, they disbelieved in him out of insolence and envy. God the Exalted says:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from God, confirming what was with them, and though they had previously sought victory over those who disbelieved, when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 89].

They disbelieved for the sake of temporal authority, for they wanted kingship and rule. And this is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, who was a Jew and then embraced Islam, who said of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "I recognized him when I saw him just as I recognize my own son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger."

Thus their knowledge of the Messenger of God's attributes and description is present in the verses of the Torah. They witnessed the clear Signs, but they denied the Signs out of greed for temporal authority, even if that required that some of them distort the method (manhaj) of God, the Glorified and Exalted, and convert this distortion into corrupt temporal authority, like those who sold indulgences (sukuk al-ghufran). Therefore the Truth said about those who distort the method of God:

﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, "This is from God," that they may exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 79].

Indeed, punishment is the destiny of those who distort the words of God and His method.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 71:

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you clothe the truth with falsehood...﴾

The meaning of "talbis" (clothing, mixing, disguising) is to insert one thing into another. When we dress ourselves in our garments, we are putting our bodies into the clothes, and by this the appearance of the one who wears the garment and of the garment itself becomes different.

In the field of calling to God, we always find the truth confronting falsehood. They mix the truth with falsehood. This verse speaks of an attempt by some of the People of the Scripture to dress the truth in falsehood. This occurred when they distorted the Torah and the Gospel and inserted into them what Moses, peace be upon him, or Jesus, peace be upon him, had not brought. This was one attempt among other attempts to dress the truth in falsehood. Then came the greatest of these attempts to dress the truth in falsehood, which is their denial of the good news of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, despite its being recorded in their heavenly books.

They declared their faith in Moses or Jesus, but they did not believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They denied the good news of Moses and Jesus concerning the message of Muhammad, the final seal of the prophets, and this was the peak of clothing the truth with falsehood, because they professed belief in two messengers and then denied belief in the final Prophet. That was because they knew that Islam, which Muhammad, the Messenger of God, brought, is the true religion, and when they were alone with themselves they recognised this, but they denied it.

﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

Nevertheless, they were trying to find a stratagem by which people might be turned away from that final message, out of their persistence in disbelief. And the Word of the Truth was revealed: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end; perhaps they will return."﴾

Some of the People of the Book wanted to cast doubt upon the Muslims regarding the matter of the method (al-manhaj). Therefore they devised that stratagem. The believers among the Arabs and the Quraysh at that time were unlettered (ummiyyun), and they knew that the People of the Book had knowledge of the methods of the heavens, and the whole Qur'an had not yet been revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So if some of them believed in the Messenger of Allah's message at the beginning of the day, and then disbelieved in him at the end of the day, this is a mixing of truth with falsehood, and in it is deception of the believers.

We should understand that ﴿the beginning of the day﴾ is meant to refer to the hours of morning and midday, for the "face" (wajh) is the first thing that meets one in any matter. We take this in examples from our daily lives, when we say of the fruit seller: "He has made a face for the fruit," meaning that he has placed the ripest fruit at the front of the cart and hidden behind the good, ripe fruit other spoiled fruit. When a merchant does such a thing, his intention is cheating and deception, because whoever buys any quantity of this fruit will find that only a quarter of what he bought is from the front of the fruit, and the rest is spoiled fruit.

Likewise, some of the People of the Book tried to deceive the believers by declaring faith at the beginning of the day and then declaring disbelief at the end of the day. The aim, naturally, is to spread doubt and sow confusion in the souls of the believers concerning this religion. Some of the unlettered may say: "The People of the Book tested this new religion, and they have knowledge of the methods of the heavens, and they did not find it to be in accordance with the methods of the heavens."

Or the verse was revealed concerning the matter of the change of the qibla to the Ka'bah. When the Almighty commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to change the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah, the disbelieving People of the Book wanted to undo that, and they said: "Let us listen to Muhammad's words at the beginning of the day and turn in prayer toward the Ka'bah, then pray at the end of the day and make our qibla Bayt al-Maqdis."

It is as if the Truth wanted by this to reveal to us that all the methods of disbelief stem from complete lack of discernment and inability to reflect well. They wanted to ignite psychological warfare against the Muslims, perhaps some of the Muslims would doubt the matter of the new religion. But without noticing, they exposed themselves, and acknowledged, without intending to, that those who believed in the Qur'an are the truly believers, while they had taken for themselves the position of disbelief, which is the opposite of faith. He, glorified is He, said, relating about them: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end﴾. So they had accepted disbelief for themselves.

These doubters announced their affirmation of Islam, so that people would know this about them, and since they were People of the Book, they were able to judge it. Then, if they turned back from Islam after knowing it, they would say: "Our return was not due to ignorance or fanaticism, but due to our testing of this religion, and we did not find it suitable or in harmony with what was revealed to our Prophet." And this is one of the methods of psychological warfare.

The Exalted Truth (Allah) unveils that scheme and deception to those who tried to conceal their deceit and their cunning game, by which they intended to sow doubt and deception. So He sends down to His Messenger this true statement: ﴿And do not believe except to one who follows your religion. Say, "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah..."﴾

Indeed, the Exalted Truth reveals to the Messenger ﷺ and to the believers among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) the game of some of the People of the Book: belief in Islam at the beginning of the day and disbelief in it at the end of the day. The plotters urged one another to keep the matter secret, so that the scheme would not lose its aim, which is to confuse the unlettered Muslims. For this reason these plotters said to one another: ﴿And do not believe except to one who follows your religion﴾, meaning: do not disclose the secret of this trick except to someone who is of your kind. But the Truth exposes this entire matter by the revelation of this verse to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his conveying it to the believers. By this, the plan of confusion was undone, and the psychological warfare recoiled upon the breasts of those who had ignited it. The noble statement continues exposing the deception of this group of the People of the Book, so the Exalted says: ﴿Say, "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah, that anyone should be given like what you were given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord."﴾

Indeed, the Exalted Truth exposes the act of the deceitful People of the Book who wanted to announce belief at the start of the day as a form of "guidance of the self", but it is from the very core of misguidance and leading others astray, and a means to it. It was not guidance from Allah, because the guidance of Allah only brings a person to the goal that Allah wills. These people of the Book, by their deception, wanted to leave our master, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, without followers who believe in Islam. These people of the Book had agreed among themselves to conceal their arrangement to feign belief at the start of the day and disbelief at its end, and not to announce this except to the people of their own religion, so that the scheme would not lose its aim, which is to confuse the Muslims.

Fear overtook them, because if people embraced the religion of Muhammad ﷺ, they would be given the like of what the People of the Book were given of knowledge of the method; indeed, the method brought by Muhammad ﷺ is the final method. The people of deception among the People of the Book only wanted to deprive people of faith, or they feared that the Muslims would enter into argument with them concerning matters of faith. All of this stemmed from a lack of discernment reaching the level of stupidity.

Why? Because they imagined that Allah does not know the inner part of what they concealed and the outer part of what they did. They forgot that the Truth knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. This agrees with their earlier conduct when they left Egypt and went into the wilderness during the crossing of the desert, and claimed that Allah said to Moses, peace be upon him: "Mark your houses, O Israelites, for I am going to descend and strike the whole land." As if, had they not placed marks on the houses, Allah would not recognize them. It is an utterly failed statement, indeed the very height of failure and misguidance. And the Truth conveys to His noble Messenger: ﴿Say, "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing."﴾

And since bounty is in the hand of Allah, you, O people of deception against the Muslims, will not be able to take people as you wish and then want to deceive them; for when Allah gives bounty to one who believes in Him, none can remove it except Allah.

So trickery will not strip away the bounty of faith in Allah, since Allah has granted it. "All-Encompassing" means that He is able to give bounty to all creation, and that will not diminish His bounty in the least; and the Exalted Truth is All-Knowing of who deserves this bounty, because his heart is occupied with his Lord.

Then after that the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He specifies for His mercy whom He wills...﴾

No one has any right over Allah; every moment of life is a bounty from Allah, and He, glory be to Him, gives His mercy, through faith in His method, to whomever He wills, and He is the Possessor of absolute bounty.

And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you...

It is the absolute justice of God. If the Truth has revealed to the Messenger some of the deceit of the People of the Book, that does not mean there is a campaign against the People of the Book, as though they were all people of evil. No; rather, among them are those who are distinguished by trustworthiness, and this statement only confirms the fairness of the just and equitable God.

Indeed, the Truth, glorified is He, addresses the souls whom He knows. He knows that the call of Muhammad (ﷺ) has been sent down as a mercy to all the worlds, and He addresses the whole world with it, including the People of the Book, who know the signs and indications that point to the coming of the message of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them are people who have placed the call of Muhammad (ﷺ) at the core of their feelings, so that they might study it and believe in it. Had God made the attack upon all the People of the Book, those who disbelieved in believing in the Messenger of Allah would have said: "We were thinking of believing, and we wanted to carry out the teachings of God for us, but Muhammad is launching an attack on all the People of the Book, and we are among them."

So when God says that some of the People of the Book are distinguished by trustworthiness, those whose thoughts turn toward Islam say: "Muhammad (ﷺ) speaks only of a light from his Lord." But if the Qur'an had generalized the ruling to all of them, those who are occupied with the desire to believe in what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought would ask: "Why does the ruling encompass everyone while we are walking the path toward belief?"

Therefore the Truth places the decisive word that among them are people who are inclining toward belief:

﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is a community standing [in obedience], reciting the verses of God during the night hours while they prostrate﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 113].

In this there is reassurance for those who have occupied themselves with the study of this religion and with the thought of believing in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Had the Qur'an been revealed cursing all of them, those among them who are contemplating belief would say: "We are not like that, and we do not deserve the curse, so why does Muhammad bring a curse upon us?"

Hence we see the statement that ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ is absolute justice in fairness:

Some exegetes have said: the Qur'an here means by "the People of the Book" the Christians, because among them are people with a living conscience; and we know that the intended meaning of the People of the Book is the Jews and the Christians. In this interpretation there is fairness to the Christians, for the Lord does not deny them the quality of goodness; rather He spreads it in His Qur'an that is recited until the Day of Religion. This is so that the People of the Book may also believe the truth of whatever evil matter is revealed about them in verses of the Qur'an, because the Qur'an is absolutely fair. Since it has stated the quality of goodness in them, it must be truthful when it states the evil matters with which they were characterized.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says: "And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you," the qintar here is for emphasis on a great amount of wealth. And the word amanah (trust), when we survey it in the Book of God, we find that once it is transitive with bi' (ب), as in this verse ﴿one who, if you entrust him with a qintar﴾, and once it is transitive with 'ala (على):

﴿They said: "O our father, why do you not trust us with Yusuf, while we are indeed his sincere advisers?"﴾ [Yusuf: 11], and His saying, the Truth:

﴿He said: "Shall I entrust you with him except as I entrusted you with his brother before? But God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾ [Yusuf: 64].

The root amanah comes transitive once with bi' and once with 'ala.

Each of these two particles has a wisdom, and the Speaker is God.

Amanah is a thing in which one party entrusts another, and the owner of the entrusted thing has no proof except the good faith of the trustee. If the relationship between them is governed by a receipt, a contract, or witnesses, then this is not amanah; amanah is what a person gives to another between them. After that, the trustee either returns it or does not return it.

We said earlier: the true believer must be cautious with the trust, because there is a time when the trust is taken on, and there is another time when the trust is discharged if its owner requests it.

An example of taking on a trust: a person offers you a sum of money and says, "Keep this sum as a trust with you," and you say, "Yes, I will do so," and you take the money. This act is called "taking on" (al-tahammul). When the owner of the money comes to ask for it, this is called "discharging" (al-ada'). Everyone guarantees themselves at the time of taking on, and the intention may indeed be so; but the true believer does not feel secure against the vicissitudes of circumstances. For the one who takes on the trust, when the owner of the money comes to demand it from the trustee, finds himself occupied with changing circumstances; life's conditions may have overtaken him, pushing him to dispose of the trust, or his soul may have stirred and said to him: "What would happen if you disposed of the trust?" The true believer does not guarantee himself at the time of discharge, even if he guaranteed himself at the time of taking on.

Thus we must note two considerations regarding the trust: "discharge" and "taking on." Those who take the trust with the intention of discharging it have guaranteed themselves at the time of taking on, but they do not guarantee themselves at the time of discharge. Therefore the cautious believer says to himself: "Why should I expose myself to this? A time of discharge may come and I may not be able to return it to its owner."

Therefore he says to the owner of the trust: "Please keep away from me, for I will not bear this trust."

He fears the time of discharge, and that is what happened in the trust of responsibility and choice, of which the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was ever unjust and ignorant.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

The heavens, the earth and the mountains asked that they not have choice and that they remain subdued, because they could not guarantee the moment of discharge. As for man, because he is unjust and ignorant, he said: "No, I am rational and I will arrange affairs." So man is unjust to himself, and ignorant because he did not know what to do at the time of discharge.

Therefore here we see the true statement: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar﴾, and we find the trust transitive with bi'. The meaning of bi' in the language is attachment: the qintar has become joined to his trust, so there is connection and blending. And beware, at the moment of discharge, of separating the trust from the qintar. When the gold qintar dazzles you with its glitter, you must join the trust to the qintar. And beware lest a qintar tempt you so that you abandon your trust, for if you look at the qintar without looking at the trust, this is the loss.

As for the use of 'ala with the trust: 'ala in the language comes for elevation and dominance, that is, make the trust elevated above the qintar, and thus your trust will be above the qintar. When your soul suggests to you that you take the qintar because it sets your life's movement in motion, and because it brings you out into a wide and tempting world, then remember the dignity of the trust. For this reason we find the jurists have said the hand of a thief is cut for a quarter of a dinar, and they made the blood-money for cutting off the hand of a person who did not steal five hundred dinars. Someone objected, saying:

"A hand, its price is five hundred camels' worth of gold, and its blood-money is paid; why is it cut for a quarter of a dinar?"

So a jurist replied to that objector:

"The dignity of trust is precious, and its cheapness is the humiliation of betrayal; so understand the wisdom of the Creator."

Therefore the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar﴾ came with bi' to join the trust to what it is entrusted with, and never to separate them, for if the trust and its dignity were separated from the qintar, the soul might prompt him to take the qintar and abandon the trust.

Likewise, when the trust is transitive with 'ala, the trust is above the thing entrusted, so the trust must be elevated over the thing, however great its value. The Truth says afterward: ﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you remain standing over him﴾, that is, that you must constantly ask about your dinar that you entrusted to that person, and persistently demand your dinar.

Then the Truth says: ﴿That is because they said, "There is no blame upon us regarding the common people."﴾ Some of the Children of Israel, in the time of the Messenger of Allah, deceived the Arab common people who were believers and denied their rights. The "common people" (al-ummiyyin) here means the believers who were not of the People of the Book, or those attributed to the mother, as the Truth said:

﴿And God brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts that you may be grateful.﴾ [al-Nahl: 78].

Or the intended meaning of "the common people" is the people of Makkah, for they were called that because they are attributed to Umm al-Qura, "Makkah the Honored."

From where, then, did the People of the Book get this two-faced method of dealing with people? And who established this method that requires deceiving the believing common people? Do virtues and degrees of character differ in dealing from one person to another? Does upright character require that a person take a trust and deny it if it belongs to an unlettered man, and return it and acknowledge it if it belongs to a Jew? Is it proper for a person to lend his money at usury to non-Jews while lending to Jews without usury? Then these dealings would be unjust: here is a virtue, and there is no virtue. No, the matter must be equal and complete in every time, every age, and for every person, and it must not be varied.

From where, then, did they come with this saying, while they are People of the Book? This is against the method of the Book that God revealed to them; rather it is from distortion and alteration. They deceived themselves and attached to the legislation what is not in it. The heavenly Book that was revealed to them does not contain a classification of humanity into two kinds: a kind who are People of the Book and have a special treatment, and a kind who are the common people and have a different treatment. They should have learned from the justice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his dealings with them.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them the true and just account through the text revealed to him from God. In this noble saying, which we treat with these reflections, is recorded the history of Judaism's relationship with Islam. God did not issue one single ruling encompassing all of them in this history; rather He was fair to those among them who had the right, even though they were upon the religion of Judaism. Thus it became fixed in the minds of the fair-minded among them that Islam had come with all the truth. For if Islam had issued one general ruling against all the Jews, whether those who stood against the call of the Messenger or the fair-minded among them whose thoughts turned toward believing in Islam, had such a general, comprehensive ruling been issued, the fair-minded Jews would have said: "We are thinking of believing in Islam, so how does Islam attack us with this attack?" But Islam came to be fair, giving each owner of a right his right.

These are the ones for whom God gives the account with the saying: ﴿Among them is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾, and that is a testimony to the truthfulness of certainty among these people. As for those whom material things overwhelmed, these are the ones of whom the wise saying came: ﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you remain standing over him﴾, and this is the true account of those whom material things overwhelmed, for such a person does not return what he owes unless pursued and hounded. Thus the Qur'an conveys history to us truthfully.

The reason that one who is entrusted with a qintar and discharges it is a person committed before a God described by the name the Truth...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 3, verse 76:

﴿Yes, whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God—indeed God loves those who are mindful of Him.﴾

The word of the Truth at the beginning of this verse, ﴿Yes (balā)﴾, has come to negate the earlier claim advanced by the People of the Book, as if the Truth were saying: "There is no blame upon you regarding the unlettered (al-ummiyyīn)," because the Lawgiver is God, and people are equal in relation to Him, glory be to Him.

After that comes the word of the Truth with a general principle:

﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God—indeed God loves those who are mindful of Him.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 76]

What is the covenant here? And which covenant is it?

It is the covenant of faith (al-ʿahd al-īmānī) that we have accepted for ourselves, that we believe in God. At the moment you believe in God, the meaning of your faith in Him is the basis of your acceptance of every ruling that proceeds from Him, glory be to Him, and that you commit yourself to what He requires of you. If you do not commit yourself to what He requires of you, your faith is without value, because the benefit of faith is commitment. For this reason we have said: when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wishes to legislate a ruling for those who believe in Him, He first calls out, "O you who believe, it is prescribed for you…" The Truth, glory be to Him, does not address all people in matters of obligation; rather He addresses those who have believed, as if He, glory be to Him, were saying: "O you who have believed in Me as God, listen from Me to the ruling that I want from you. I do not demand a ruling from those who have not believed in Me; I demand it from those who have believed."

And here the Truth says: ﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God—indeed God loves those who are mindful of Him.﴾ Some may understand this statement to mean that whoever fulfils his covenant of faith and is mindful of God, making all his movements conform to "do" and "do not do," then God loves him. This is the meaning that may be understood at first glance, but God did not say that. "Love" does not return to the essence (al-dhāt) but returns to the deed. The Truth said: ﴿indeed God loves those who are mindful of Him.﴾

A person may err and say: "God has loved me, so I will afterwards do whatever I please." We remind the speaker of this saying that God loves the righteous deed which the servant performs with a sincere intention for God, and the essence has no value in itself. Therefore He said: ﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God—indeed God loves those who are mindful of Him.﴾

Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God, God will love in him the quality of God-consciousness (al-taqwā). Beware lest you understand that God's love for the servant becomes love of the essence; rather it is love because the quality is present in him. So be keen that the quality remains yours always, so that you remain within God's love.

Therefore we say: the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has clarified for us that essences proceed from essences, and essences with God are descended from one origin. Lineage (al-jins) has no value in itself; the value lies only in righteous deeds.

We have given this example previously: when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, promised Noah, peace be upon him, that He would save him and his family from drowning, then Noah was surprised that his son was among the drowned. God, glory be to Him, said, relating what happened:

﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." He said, "There is no protector today from the decree of God, except for whom He has mercy." And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾ [Hūd: 43]

What did Noah, peace be upon him, do? He called upon his Lord, seeking the salvation of his son:

﴿And Noah called to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."﴾ [Hūd: 45] Through His response to Noah, God teaches us that the family of the prophets are not those who descend from their lineage; rather the family of the prophets are those who follow their way. Therefore the Truth said to Noah concerning his son:

﴿"Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose conduct is not righteous."﴾ [Hūd: 46]

Why is Noah's son not of Noah's family? Because the family of prophethood are those who follow the method of prophethood. For this reason the Truth did not say to Noah about his son, "He is an unrighteous doer," but the Truth, glory be to Him, said of Noah's son: ﴿he is one whose conduct is not righteous﴾. God attributed the matter to the deed.

Thus the wisdom is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, in His Qur'anic style, makes clear to us that God does not love a person for his essence, but for his deed and qualities. So He did not say, "Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of God, indeed God loves him," because the pronoun "him" here would return to the essence. In this there is complete clarity that God loves the servant's deed, not the servant's essence. So if the servant is keen to be beloved of God, that requires of the servant that he remain following the way of God.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, those have no share in the Hereafter...﴾

Whenever we hear the word "buying and selling" (shira' wa bay'), we must pause at it to understand its meaning precisely. In the countryside we see barter (muqayadah) or exchange of livelihood that has direct benefit, such as one party exchanging wheat for cloth. This is a commodity exchanged for another commodity, and so there is no buyer and seller, because each of the two parties has both bought and sold. Here we ask: when does it then become buying and selling?

Buying and selling occurs when we exchange a direct livelihood for an indirect livelihood. An example of this is when a person buys a loaf of bread for five piasters. This is buying and selling, because the five piasters are an indirect livelihood in terms of benefit, since money does not satisfy you, nor quench your thirst, nor cover you. The loaf is a direct livelihood in terms of benefit, because it satisfies you and repels hunger from you. When a person wishes to buy something, what he pays in the purchase is called the price (thaman).

So how is the price bought?

Allah makes clear to us that prices are never bought; they are that by which something is bought. Therefore the first loss in the transaction of those who buy the covenant of Allah for a small price is that they have bought the price, whereas the price is not bought; rather, what is bought is the commodity. Would that the price they bought had been a valuable price, but it is a small price. From here came the prohibition of usury (riba), because the usurer gives a person one hundred and wants to recover one hundred and ten. In this matter the usurer has made money a commodity, and thus the transaction is lost from its very beginning.

So the first loss lies in the souls of those people who exchange guidance and take error in its place; they are the losers.

﴿Those are the ones who bought error in exchange for guidance, so their trade has not profited, nor were they guided﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 16].

And the Almighty says here: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾. We know that the particle "bi" (ب) always enters upon what is abandoned; that is, they abandoned the covenant of Allah and the oaths they swore to affirm the Messenger and to support him when he came to them, and they bought that for a small price. How does this happen? For this matter there is an actual event, and although the intended meaning is the generality of the subject and not the specificity of the cause, no one should say: "This verse was revealed about such-and-such matter, so it has nothing to do with me." No. Everyone who buys the signs of Allah for a small price is covered by this verse.

The actual event in which the verse was revealed is that a group, in a time of drought and famine, entered upon Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf the Jew, asking him for food supplies (mirah), that is, food and clothing. He said to them: "Do you know that this man is the Messenger of Allah?" They said: "Yes." He said: "I was determined to feed you and clothe you, but Allah has deprived you of much good." They asked among themselves: "Why has Allah deprived us of much good?" And the answer came to them: "You have declared faith in Muhammad." When they found themselves in this position, they said to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf: "Leave us for a period, for perhaps a doubt has overcome us, so let us reconsider it among ourselves."

When the period passed, they preferred food and clothing over faith, and said to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf: "We have read in our books which we possess an error, and Muhammad is not a messenger." So Ka'b gave them provision and clothing. These are the ones who bought the signs of Allah for a small price, which was food and clothing. And everyone who buys the signs of Allah for a small price obliterates one of the rulings of Allah in order to appear before people as modern, or as one who keeps pace with the spirit of the age, or to adorn for those in authority an act with which Allah is not pleased.

So whoever does such a thing is buying the signs of Allah for a small price, and everyone who makes a sign of Allah subject to sale in order to take a small price for it, and everyone who makes a sign of Allah subject to sale in order to take a price for it, is considered included in this text: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾.

The covenant of Allah intended here is either the covenant of the natural disposition (fitrah), or the covenant that Allah took from the People of the Book, that if they encountered the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they must declare faith in him. This is the covenant brought by the true Word: 

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom, then there will come to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My burden upon that?" They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 81].

So when there came the description of their denial of the faith they had earlier declared, in exchange for food and clothing, and that was a great loss, they had bought the price, and the price is nonetheless small. Therefore the true Word says of them:

﴿Those have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran: 77].

The word ﴿those﴾ (ulaika) indicates that the connection, which is ﴿they sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾, attaches to them every person who has these attributes and gives him the same destiny. Thus this verse, though it was revealed concerning these individuals who engaged in the incident of buying food and clothing in exchange for retreating from faith in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), includes everyone who bears this attribute and everyone who is of this character in any age and in any religion. The Almighty describes them as ﴿those have no share (khalaq)﴾.

The word ﴿khalaq﴾, and the word "khuluq" (character), and the word "khaliqah" (disposition), and the word "khalq" (creation), all revolve around a meaning that is nearly similar. Thus al-khalq, with the kha' and lam vowelled, is that a quality comes to exist in a person that dominates him until it becomes a faculty (malakah). One says: "So-and-so has the character of truthfulness," or "So-and-so's character is generosity," meaning that the first one has made truthfulness a faculty for him, and he does not tire himself in order to be truthful, but truthfulness becomes a natural matter in him; and likewise the second is described as generous, meaning generosity has become a faculty and an innate disposition (sajiyyah) for him.

This faculty in abstract matters is equivalent to the automatism (aliyyah) in sensory matters, because we know that every action requires practice so that a person becomes distinguished in its performance. For example, a worker who weaves on a loom needs to train himself to move the shuttle of the thread, and to learn how to move the shuttle between the threads of the fabric, and after that the two threads are alternated together so that the second movement of the shuttle, in its return, holds them, and thus the weaving is completed. When a person trains in this work, he needs a long time to reach proficiency in the movement.

At the beginning of training the matter is difficult, and after mastering the training, the weaver can sit in front of the loom with his hands moving the shuttle automatically. The matter has become, for the trained weaver, automatic.

I have already given the example of the person learning to drive a car: the instructor teaches him how to turn the key, how to wait for the engine to warm up, how to release the car's brake, then how to move the control stick for the car's acceleration, and how to balance between pressing the fuel pedal and pressing the separating control pedal, and how to balance the car's movement by reducing speed with light touches on the brake pedal.

A person may err at the beginning of learning and become confused, but after completing training he works automatically and without thinking. It is an automatic act that needs no thought. I also previously gave the example of the boy who learns sewing of garments: he takes time to put the thread through the eye of the needle, and he makes mistakes in measuring the different distances between the stitches, but afterwards he trains himself to perform these actions that were difficult, and performs them automatically. The automatic act in sensory matters corresponds to the faculty in abstract matters, so one says: "Truthfulness is a faculty in so-and-so," meaning he is a person for whom being truthful does not burden him.

When we teach our children grammar, for example, we say to them: "The case of the subject is nominative (raf') and the object is accusative (nasb)." When the child pronounces a phrase, he tries to apply the rule during reading, and he may forget it or stammer, but when he recalls it he pronounces the words in their correct phonetic form, and after the rule has been practised and the child reads, his errors disappear, and thus grammar becomes a faculty for him.

Likewise is character (khuluq): character is a quality that becomes firmly rooted in the soul, so that actions proceed from it with ease and facility. One says: "Truthfulness has a character," and "generosity has a character," and "courage has a character." These are the qualities that become firmly rooted in the soul, so that actions proceed from them with ease and facility. The Almighty says: ﴿Those have no share in the Hereafter﴾. Some have interpreted the deprivation of those people from character as meaning that this category of people has no portion of character, since character is a firmly established quality in a person. And the Truth specifies the time as ﴿in the Hereafter﴾.

The Hereafter is the time in which correction is impossible, for the Hereafter is the day of true and final evaluation.

A person may not have a portion of right conduct, so he corrects his conduct until he acquires this right conduct in this world. But in the Hereafter a person cannot find room for making amends, and this is the decisive loss.

A person in this world may do an action and have no portion of its reward, or we may not see the recompense and portion that Allah gives him; yet Allah compensates him in the Hereafter for this action of which he had no portion in this world. But for the one who has no share in the Hereafter, how can compensation take place? That is an impossible matter.

The Truth adds: ﴿Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾. Someone may say: Did not the Noble Qur'an say in another place that Allah says to the disbelievers:

﴿He said: "Be driven away therein, and do not speak to Me."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 108].

So why does the Truth say to them once: ﴿Be driven away therein and do not speak to Me﴾, and once again the Truth says: ﴿Allah will not speak to them﴾? We answer such a question: the Truth does not speak to them with speech that benefits them, or He speaks to them through His angels. But how is it that Allah does not look at them?

When we find a matter that exists among people and has a counterpart attributed to Allah, the Exalted, and He says it about Himself, we must take this matter within the framework of: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾.

In our human domain we say: "So-and-so does not look at so-and-so," meaning he does not direct his eyes toward him, and turns his pupils away from him. But this cannot be measured on Allah, because Allah is exalted above resemblance. In the human situation we find a person who loves a friend and turns toward him with his face and gaze, and it is said: "A youth who is 'qayyid al-ain'" (one whom the eye is bound to), meaning that he is a young man whom, when the eye looks at him, it is bound to him and does not go away to another place; in this young man there are attractions that keep the eye from going far from him. Thus we take the eye's attention with looking as a sign of concern for the thing looked at or seen, and this is correct in the human situation.

But when this applies to Allah, here we take the matter within the framework of: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. Thus we understand Allah's not looking at ﴿those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾ as meaning that Allah neglects them and has no concern for them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 78:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And indeed, among them is a party who distort their tongues with the Book, that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book...﴾

That is, they twist their tongues with the speech that comes from Allah, in order to distort it from its meanings. Or they twist their tongues when they wish to express meanings. "Layy" (twisting) means to twist fibres. When we twist a rope, we braid together two strands of threads and then twist them together to make a rope. The purpose of twisting is to gain strength: the individual hair-like fibres of the threads have limited strength, but when we twist these threads, we increase their strength by braiding them together.

Thus the twisting is intended to reach strength. So we see that they twist their tongues with words that they claim are from the revealed method sent down by Allah, while these words are not from the method and were not sent down by Allah. They do this to strengthen their position, to diminish the standing of Islam, and to slander the Messenger, as they said previously: "Ra'ina" (Do not say "Ra'ina"). Therefore the Truthful addressed the believers:

﴿O you who believe, do not say "Ra'ina" but say "Unzurna" and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 104].

Allah clarifies for us that we should not give them an opportunity to distort the words of Allah. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their places and say, "We hear and disobey," and "Hear without being heard," and "Ra'ina," twisting with their tongues and slandering the religion. And if they had said, "We hear and obey," and "Listen and look at us," it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few.﴾ [an-Nisa': 46].

Allah, glorified is He, has exposed them to us, for they distort speech from its place. The Truthful has said this statement to mean: what you hear will not harm you. Allah has recorded against them that they said "We hear and disobey," and they also distorted a word and said, "Hear without being heard," meaning "may you never hear," exactly as they had earlier taken Allah's saying:

﴿And say, "Hittah" (remission)﴾ [al-A'raf: 161].

And they distorted this saying into "Hintah" (wheat). They did this so that we would think this distortion is from the Book, when it is not from the Book. That is, they twist some of the meanings derived from the words so that they deceive the believers into thinking that these meanings that are not intended and not correct are meanings intended by Allah and correct in meaning. They attribute to the revealed method sent down from heaven what is not in it. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿so that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book﴾. When they twist their tongues with the Book, they distort it, desiring deception and fraud upon you, so that you will think it is from the Book sent down from Allah to their messenger. If they had only done this, it would have been possible for them to repent, return to their Lord, and feel remorse for what they did.

As for their later saying: ﴿It is from Allah﴾, it is evidence that they introduced something into the Book and persisted in it, so they said ﴿It is from Allah﴾ to clear themselves of the suspicion that they would be accused of distorting the Book. Had they not distorted the Book, would this thought have occurred to them? Their affair came under the principle of (the suspect almost says, "Take me"). By this statement they are trying to conceal a matter that happened from them.

The Truthful, glorified is He, affirms that treachery pursues them, so He says: (And it is not from Allah), and this noble verse exposes them and reveals their distortion of the Book of Allah. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they speak falsehood against Allah while they know﴾. They know that what they say is falsehood. Falsehood, as we have known, is that the verbal attribution does not correspond to reality. Attributions of events come in three states:

An attribution that is actual.

An attribution that is thought about, which is a mental attribution.

An attribution that is uttered.

When we know a person named Muhammad who is in fact diligent, this is an actual attribution. If it crosses your mind to inform a friend of Muhammad's diligence, this thought is a mental attribution.

When you speak this news to your friend, the attribution becomes verbal. Truthfulness is that the verbal attribution has a reality that agrees with it, such as saying "Muhammad is diligent" when there is indeed someone named Muhammad who is diligent. In this way you, the one uttering the news of Muhammad's diligence, are a truthful person. But if there is no one named Muhammad who is diligent, the verbal attribution does not agree with the actual attribution, so the news becomes false. The scholars distinguish between truth and falsehood by this criterion. Truth is the correspondence of speech to reality, and falsehood is the non-correspondence of speech to reality.

Some who love to cast doubt have stopped at the surah of the Hypocrites, in which the Truthful says:

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].

The hypocrites said: "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah," and our master Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is indeed a messenger from Allah. The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And Allah knows that you are His Messenger﴾. Is their knowledge like Allah's knowledge? No, because Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars﴾. How, then, does the Truthful describe them as liars when they testified to what He Himself testified?

The Truthful does not call them liars regarding the proposition that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, for that is a true proposition. Rather, He has called them liars regarding a claim they made, which is: ﴿We testify﴾. Their saying ﴿We testify﴾ means that the spoken words agree with what they believe in their hearts, and their saying ﴿We testify﴾ is a statement that does not agree with what is in their hearts. Therefore they became liars, for each one's tongue does not agree with what is in his heart.

So the Truthful's saying ﴿And they speak falsehood against Allah while they know﴾ means that they utter speech for which there is no external attribution corresponding to it, and they know it is false. Lest we say that they spoke this out of heedlessness, they deliberately lied, knowing that they were saying falsehood. Precision requires that we distinguish between the truth of the report and the truth of the reporter. The truth of the report is that it corresponds to reality, but sometimes the reporter is truthful while the report itself is false, such as when someone says, "So-and-so studies all night," because he saw the room of so-and-so lit and him opening a book, while that so-and-so was in fact absorbed in reading some novel. In this case the reporter is truthful, but the report is false.

In the context of the verse, however, we find that they are liars deliberately. The tongue is the means of expressing what is in the soul:

"Indeed, speech lies within the heart, and the tongue was placed as a guide upon the heart."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 3, verse 79:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and the prophethood﴾

We know that when the Truthful One, glory be to Him and exalted, sends down His method (manhaj), He sends it down in a Book, and that requires Him, glory be to Him, to choose a human being for the message. That is, the Messenger (rasul) comes with a method, applies it to himself, and conveys it to the people. The Messenger is chosen by Allah and differs in his mission from the Prophet (nabi). The Prophet too is chosen, to apply the method, and so on, so that people do not hear the method merely as speech but see it also as practice. So the Messenger is a conveying intermediary and a behavioural model, while the Prophet is not a conveying intermediary but only a behavioural model.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him and exalted, sends the Prophet and sends the Messenger, and for this reason the verse comes:

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or desired], Satan threw into his wish. But Allah abolishes what Satan throws in; then Allah makes His verses precise. And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Hajj: 52].

Thus we know that both the Messenger and the Prophet are sent from Allah. The Messenger is sent for conveying and as an example, and the Prophet is sent only as an example, because there are times when the method exists, but bringing the self to the method is what is lacking. An example is our present age: the method exists and we all know what is lawful and what is unlawful, but the failure of this time comes from not bringing ourselves to the method. Therefore we need a behavioural exemplar. Thus we have understood the Book and the prophethood; so what is the wisdom (hukm) then?

The Truthful One used the word "al-hukm" (wisdom/judgement) here to show us that it is not necessary that faith-wisdom be found only in the Messenger or the Prophet; rather wisdom may fall to a person from among the faithful common folk, and the matter of faith is mature in his mind, so he speaks it, because wisdom requires this. Did not Allah mention to us the counsel of Luqman to his son? The counsel of Luqman to his son is the religious method, and on that basis it is possible for a person to come without a message or prophethood, yet the faithful method is kindled in his mind, so he admonishes with it and applies it. This is a sign from Allah that the method can, for any mind that receives it, lead it to be convinced, so it acts by it and conveys it.

We must affirm that whoever Allah grants wisdom in calling to the method of Allah and applying this method will add nothing to the method, and by virtue of his truthfulness with Allah he will not claim that he is sent by Allah to the people. He is content to call to Allah and to be a good example.

But why did this verse come? This verse came after the disputation of the Christians of Najran with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina. During the disputation a group of Jews joined them, and they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

- "What do you believe in and command?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed them of the commands and prohibitions of the method, and the fundamentals of worship. Because that group were People of the Book, some from the Christians of Najran and others from the Jews of Medina, and they were distorting worship commands that were not from Allah and wanted people to obey these commands, they did not perceive the difference between the method of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and his commands, and what they had falsified of commands. Muhammad (ﷺ) asks people to worship Allah in the light of the method Allah the Truthful sent down to him, whereas they demand people's obedience to commands of their own falsification.

Obedience, as we know, belongs to Allah alone in the fundamentals of all religions. So when a person brings a command that is not from Allah and asks people to obey him in it, this means that person asks that people worship him, God forbid, for obedience to humans in matters other than the commands of Allah is shirk with Allah. For this reason the situations became similar for some of the People of the Book, and they thought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) demanded their obedience to his own commands, just as they had demanded of people, after their distortion of the method, and they said: "Do you want us to worship you and take you as a god?"

They did not perceive the difference between the trustworthy Messenger over the method of Allah and their leaders who opposed the rulings and replaced them with others. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not demand obedience to himself for his own sake, but he demanded obedience to the method he brought as messenger and exemplar, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) denounced what they said.

Allah, glory be to Him, sent down His true word:

﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and the prophethood and then he should say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 79]

Their heedlessness and shirk reached the point that they thought Allah had not chosen a trustworthy messenger over the method, and they thought an evil opinion of Allah, or they thought the Messenger would distort the method as they had distorted it, so they turned from worshipping Allah to worshipping one whom Allah had sent as messenger. Hence came the decisive word: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and the prophethood and then he should say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah"﴾.

The meaning may also extend to the fact that some companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to exalt him (ﷺ), and every believer is required to revere and magnify the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Out of excessive love of some companions for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said to him: "Shall we greet you as some of us greet one another? Shall we not prostrate to you?"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never demanded prostration to himself from anyone. The Truthful One, glory be to Him, is the One who charged His faithful servants with honouring His Messenger, saying:

﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of some of you to others. Allah already knows those of you who slip away, concealing themselves. So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment strike them﴾ [al-Nur: 63].

What is required is veneration of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), not that we give him things that belong only to Allah.

Our honouring the Messenger of Allah and our glorifying him consists in making his call distinct from our calling one another.
