And the Truthful One, in this verse about which we are offering these reflections, says: ﴿But be rabbaniyyin (people of the Lord) by what you have been teaching of the Book and by what you have been studying﴾.

Here "lakin" (but) is for correction (istidrak). As we said before, "bala" (rather/yes) annuls the proposition before it and establishes after it a proposition contrary to it. The Truthful One corrects here so that we understand that it is not for any human to say, "Be servants to me," after Allah has given him the Book, wisdom and prophethood. The proposition for which the correction is made and established is: ﴿be rabbaniyyin﴾. The word "rabbani", the word "rabb", the word "rabbiyyun", the word "rabban", and the whole root composed of the letters "ra" and "ba" indicate upbringing, guardianship, and the care of the one who nurtures, and revolve around this meaning. Is not the "rabban" of the ship the one who steers the ship?

The word "rabb" designates the one who holds charge of upbringing. So what is the meaning of "rabbani"? If you want to ascribe to "rabb" you say "rabbi". If we want to intensify the ascription we add to it an alif and a nun and say "rabbani", and so in contemporary expressions we find those who want to ascribe a matter to knowledge saying "ilmani" (secularist), and in that there is an intensification of ascription to knowledge. The difference between "ilmi" and "ilmani" is that the secularist claims for himself that all his affairs proceed on material knowledge, and we find that in "ilmani" there are two added letters, alif and nun, to emphasise the ascription to knowledge.

Someone may say: why do we emphasise the attribution to Allah with the word "rabbani"?

We say: because the word is derived from the word "rabb", and it yields meanings. Among them: whatever he has of the yield of the conveying must be issuing from and ascribed to the Lord, because he has brought nothing of his own; that is, he takes from Allah and never takes from anyone else; he is rabbani in what he takes.

The word also yields another meaning: when he says and speaks, he is characterised by a disposition sent down by a Lord who nurtures the people so that they reach the intended goal from them. So when he conveys what he has to the people he is a nurturer, and he manages the affair for success and righteousness.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿by what you have been teaching of the Book and by what you have been studying﴾. Knowledge is the receiving of the methodical text, and study is the intellectual examination of the methodical text.

Therefore we in the countryside say: "we thresh (nadrus) the wheat", meaning we thresh the wheat with a sharp tool such as the threshing sledge until the grains of wheat separate from the chaff, and the result of threshing is the extraction of what is beneficial.

So there is a difference between "you teach" (ta'lamun), meaning you teach others the method issuing from Allah, which is subject to receiving the text, and ﴿what you have been studying﴾, meaning you work your thoughts in understanding the text.

Understanding the text needs mutual study (mudarasa), and the meaning of mudarasa is giving and taking. It is said "darasahu", meaning one has exchanged teaching with another; and it is also said "tadarasna", meaning I have said what I have and you have said what you have, until we can extract and deduce the ruling that is in the text.

The text may come definitive (muhkam), and the text may come admitting more than one meaning.

Since you have learned, you must have come to know the definitive texts of the method. And since you have studied, you must have understood from the ambiguous texts, through your study with the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr), a good reception of the method; therefore you must be rabbani in both matters together.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 80:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Nor would He command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords...﴾

That is, it is not for any human to whom Allah has given the Book, the judgment (hukm) and prophethood to tell people to take angels and prophets as lords. Whoever Allah has singled out with knowledge, a Book and prophethood cannot possibly say: "Worship me," or "Worship the angels," or "Worship the prophets."

Why? The Truth, glorified is He, answers: ﴿Would He command you to disbelieve after you have submitted (to Allah)?﴾

His words, the Truth: ﴿after you have submitted (muslimun)﴾ indicate that the occurrence of this matter and what accompanied it took place with Muslims. It seems that when they came, they wanted to exalt the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We want to give you a status of veneration greater than any created being, and we want to prostrate to you." The Prophet (ﷺ) clarified to them that prostration is due only to Allah.

So those who spoke were Muslims, and they intended by that to venerate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Had the Messenger of Allah agreed with them, that would have meant he was taking them out of Islam, and it is inconceivable that this would issue from our master and beloved, the Chosen One (ﷺ), or from any other of the prophets (peace be upon them).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 81:

The Most High says: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom..."﴾

This verse makes us aware of the reasons why the Truth sent the procession of the messengers (rusul). We all know that the first method (manhaj) was sent down by Allah to Adam (peace be upon him), comprising everything that brings life into harmony. Adam conveyed this method to his children, just as he taught them the affairs of their lives, exactly as a father teaches his children what serves their affairs of life. Likewise, he conveys the essentials of religion to his children, and the children convey it to their own children, and the conveyance continues from generation to generation so that the method fully reaches the offspring. But with the passing of time and its succession, we find that some of the requirements of religion come to be forgotten.

This is evidence that people have become heedless of the method, and thus we see that heedlessness of the method occurs in stages. After the method has been conveyed, we find a person who neglects a single part of this method, and his own self (nafs) awakens him and blames him for leaving that part. We call the bearer of this stance the one with the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah). He commits a bad deed, but his self returns to alertness toward the method of Allah, because he possesses the "cell of faith immunity" (khaliyat al-manaah al-iimaaniyyah) within him. And there is another person who gets accustomed to opposing the method, and his self insists on opposition; he is the one with the soul that commands to evil (al-nafs al-ammarah bi'l-su'). Occasions for committing evil deeds follow one upon another for him, and such a person needs someone outside his self to draw his attention to good.

And what happens to society when all its members become those with the soul that commands to evil?

This means that corruption has spread, and there must be the coming of a messenger, because the purpose of the Most High is the guidance of people. He, glory be to Him, created us, and He possesses all the attributes of perfection, and our creation added nothing to Him. Here is the sacred hadith (hadith qudsi) which Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, relating from Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, that He said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself, and I have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, you err by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me, nor will you reach My benefit so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all upon the most God-fearing heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one plain and asked Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not diminish what I have except as a needle diminishes when it is dipped into the sea. O My servants, these are only your deeds which I count for you, then I shall repay you for them. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame none but himself."

Indeed, Allah, the Most High, created us, and He is from eternity to eternity in perfect attributes of perfection, and this creation added nothing to Him. And He is the One who said:

﴿I do not desire any provision from them, nor do I desire that they should feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 57–58].

So when the Truth legislates for us a command, He legislates it for our benefit. He, glory be to Him, loves that His creation should attain the happiness of the method; therefore He sent down the method as "do" and "do not." When the method says "do" and "do not," it does not wish to restrict freedom of movement for creation except by that which protects them; it restricts freedom here in order to protect freedom there. So when Allah forbade theft, for example, the command applies to all human beings, so that no one steals from anyone.

When the Most High forbids the hand of one person from theft, that is a prohibition upon millions of hands from stealing from this person, and in this there is protection for all humanity from one person stealing from another, and in that there is gain for every person. So when you take up a legislation, do not take it as something required only of you, but take it as something required of you and also required for you.

Another example: the method has forbidden the believing servant to extend his eyes toward the forbidden things (mahārim) of others, and this prohibition was not for one servant alone but for every believer. Thus no eye extends toward the forbidden things of this servant. The command came to you to lower your gaze from the forbidden things of others, though you are one person, and We restrained, for your sake, millions of eyes lest they extend toward your forbidden things.

Thus every believing servant gains a tranquil life from the existence of the legislation, and all legislations came for our benefit together. Therefore the Truth is merciful to us, because the procession of the messengers has continued and persisted in the universe from Adam until Muhammad (ﷺ). The method brought by all these messengers contains no contradiction whatsoever, because in this method there is benefit for creation. Therefore it is impossible that the procession of one messenger should come in order to contradict the procession of another messenger.

But what brings about contradiction between the religions when the Legislator is one, and all people are His dependents?

We absolve the messengers of contradiction. And if some attempt to depict the matter as such, let us know that it is the followers of the messengers who want for themselves a temporal authority by which they control in this world. Those who held temporal authority in a religion such as Judaism or Christianity did this.

When Christianity came after Judaism, the rabbis of the Jews said: "We do not want Christianity." Why? Because temporal authority was in their hands. Had these rabbis remained upon the method that Allah had sent down to them, they would have kissed the hands of any messenger who came, thanking him for his coming and saying to him: "Help us to deepen our understanding of the method of Allah."

Thus disagreement occurs only where there are desires that possess temporal authorities. The procession of the messages from the day Allah created man is a method that supports one another, not one that opposes one another.

When a messenger comes to find people who do not believe in a God, the problem is easy, because he will draw their attention to one God and to the method that Allah wants. But the problem is great with the community that has a messenger and that is attributed to heaven. When a messenger comes from Allah, he comes while these followers have taken, from their claim of belonging to the message of a previous messenger, a temporal authority, as happened with the Jews and Christians. So they become zealous for the religion they were upon, forgetting that their elders had distorted the method for the sake of temporal authority.

The procession of the messengers continued among creation so that Allah would protect creation from the dominance of deviation, and Allah chose the community of Muhammad (ﷺ); for Allah has guaranteed the continuance of good in this community. So if you see people who have gone to extremes in disbelief, be assured that there are people whom Allah has increased in support until balance is achieved, for the Truth is the One who says:

﴿And let there be among you a community calling to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And those are the successful.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 104].

And in another place in the Noble Qur'an the Most High says:

﴿You are the best community produced for mankind; you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah. And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110].

So if the inner restraint of the self-reproaching soul fails in an individual of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), then Muslims will come who will alert him to the method. The Most High does not protect people from erring, for He says:

﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ [al-'Asr: 1–3].

The Truth said "watawasaw" (advised each other), and did not say "wasaw" (advised), so that we understand that advising is a mutual matter among all. When a person is in a moment of weakness before the method, there is a moment of strength in another who advises him.

This matter also returns to the one advised: a moment of weakness may come upon him before the method, and he finds one who advises him. Thus we see that there are no particular people designated to advise and others whose task is to receive advice; rather the matter is reciprocal among them, and this is the mutual support of faith (al-takaful al-iimani). A person may weaken in some matter, and a believing brother comes and says to him: "Stay away from this weakness." This matter occurs by alternation, to resist the moments of change in the human self, because moments of change do not let a person remain in one state. So when we see a person who has weakened before some commitment, it is incumbent upon us to advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience; and you too, when you weaken, you will find among your brothers in faith one who advises you.

This is the situation in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). As for the nations before it, they did not forbid one another from an evil they committed, and therefore it was necessary for heaven to intervene and bring a new messenger with a new miracle that would compel minds to attention, showing that there are things the miracle brings, namely breaking the law of the cosmos, and in that there is a compelling call from God to people toward the realms of power.

And Allah took the covenant from the Prophets that each prophet should convey this message to his people: await that heaven will send you messengers, and when the messenger who conveys Allah's method comes, be with him and support him.

The messengers, peace be upon them all, were commanded to place in the method, and its core is that when heaven intervenes and brings a new messenger, his people must follow him, and must not be zealous against the coming messenger, but rather submit with him and welcome him, because the messenger comes only to help people toward the correct method. But the followers who love temporal authority deliberately distorted it. And in order that the Truth protect His creation from this disease, He sent down the covenant that He took from the Prophets, saying:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must support him."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 81]

Someone may say: this statement fits when a messenger is contemporary with another messenger, as Shu'ayb was contemporary with Moses (peace be upon him), and as Lot was contemporary with Abraham (peace be upon him). We say: this also happens even when messengers are not contemporaries. The Most High willed for each messenger to give his people clear conveyance, and even if two messengers are not contemporaries, the messenger must give immunity against zealotry. Since they have believed in the messenger and followed him, it is incumbent upon them to receive well the messenger who comes after their messenger. And each messenger had to tell his people: "Be awaiting that heaven may intervene at any time. When heaven intervenes at any time and brings a messenger confirming what is with you, beware of taking a stance of harm toward him, and beware of taking a stance of enmity toward him; rather you must 'support him'." This is a clear and manifest statement with no ambiguity.

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you"﴾

We say in explanation of the meaning of: ﴿a messenger confirming what is with you﴾.

Religion brings matters on which there is agreement, because the creeds are one, the reports are one, and the narratives are one; but what differs is the legislative ruling, which may suit one era and not suit another. So if a messenger comes with a Book confirming what is with you in matters running within the method of creeds or the method of narratives, then you must believe him.

But the Jews did not do so;

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 82:

﴿Then whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun).﴾

The meaning of "tawalla" (turned away) is the opposite of "aqbala" (came toward). "Aqbala" means that he came facing you. "Tawalla" means he turned away, as we say in our common expression: "he turned his back on me." The meaning of this is that he did not care for me and did not turn toward me. So the purpose of taking the covenant is that people should turn toward that religion. The one who turns away from and gives his back to the new faith, God threatens him and describes him with His words: ﴿Then whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ After what? After the taking of the covenant and pledge from the prophets, the testimony of nations against one another, and God's testimony over all of them. Therefore no one has an excuse. So whoever turns his back on the new Prophet, what is God's threat against him?

Indeed, the Truth describes them with His words: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾, meaning that the threat is that God will reckon with him the reckoning of the defiantly disobedient. And fisq (defiant disobedience), as we know, is going out of the path of obedience. Meanings, as you know, took their form from perceptible things, because the origin of human awareness is the perceptible thing first, and then non-physical meanings come to take from the wording of perceptible things. The word fisq in its original linguistic sense is the moist date leaving its skin: when the unripe date (balah) ripens and softens, the size of each fruit has shrunk away from its skin, and when the natural size shrinks from the skin, the skin becomes loose on it, and any movement becomes an opportunity for the moist date to slip out of its skin.

It is said: "fasaqat al-rutabah" (the moist date went out of its skin), meaning it came out of its skin. Religion took this expression and made it a description of one who goes outside God's path, as if God's path surrounds the human being in all his conduct; so when the human being goes outside God's path, he is like the moist date that has come out of its skin.

We are faced with a greater kind of fisq: there is small fisq and there is great fisq. Here we ask: could the fisq here be merely a departure from obedience to the Messenger? But this departure is attributed to every sinner; that is, its bearer is a believer in the path but has deviated partially. We say of every sinner: "he is fasiq," meaning he believes in the path but has departed from a part of this path. As for the fisq that the Truth speaks of here, it is the fisq of the summit, because it is a departure from the whole caravan of faith. If God has taken the covenant, and the prophets have testified over their peoples, and the peoples have testified over one another, and God has testified over all, is there then still room for a person to turn away and refuse?

Then why does he turn away and refuse? He does so because he wants a path other than this path that God has sent down. Had he been convinced by God's path, he would have turned toward it. But whoever is not convinced turns away from the path and seeks a path other than it. So which path do you want, O you who do not accept this testimony or this confirmation? Especially since you know that there is no true path except this path, for there is no other god who sends other paths.

Thus we know that no path comes other than God's path, except a path from humans for other humans. To whoever follows a path other than God's path we may say: who made one human more worthy of being followed by another human? The follower must seek someone to follow, and the one he follows must be higher than him. But for one human to follow another human in a path of the latter's own devising is not fitting, and it is fisq against God's path. The equal does not follow his equal at all. Among God's bounties, He, glorified be He, made the path from Himself for all people, so that no human follows another human. Why? So that one person's desire does not dominate the destinies of another person, and the Truth, glorified be He, has no desire. Every human being must have his desire subject to God, who created all humans.

And since there is no other god, what path does a human choose for himself?

The path a human chooses for himself, if he does not follow God's path, is a path devised by humans, and the path devised by humans always springs from desire. And since desires exist, every human lawgiver has a desire, and this leads to the corruption of the universe. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿And if the Truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 71].

If they do not accept God's path, then what defiant disobedience are they in? It is a great defiant disobedience, because God has taken the covenant from them and from their prophets and confirmed this covenant. Do they seek other than God's religion? Yes, they seek other than God, and who is that other? Is it another god? No, there is no god with God. Rather, they have set creation in place of the Creator. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of God, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 83:

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned?﴾

Since they do not believe in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom Allah sent as a prophet and messenger, this reveals their desire: they want a method other than the method of Allah. Before them then there remain only the methods of men, which spring from desires and which inevitably lead to misguidance. Allah, glorified and exalted, wants His creation to be consistent with themselves. He, the Truth, has explained in His method, and said to us through this method: you are vicegerents in the universe, and you, O vicegerents on earth, are the masters of this universe, masters whom the whole universe serves. Look at the kinds of existence and you will find them in your service. The animal is less than you in thought. The plant is less than the animal in sensation. The inanimate is less than the plant.

So the kinds of the universe, of animal, plant and inanimate, submit to your will, O human. The plant serves the animal, the animal serves you, O human, and the inanimate serves all. The elements we humans take from the inanimate are also benefited from by plants and animals. So every kind in existence that you see with your eyes serves the kinds that are above it.

The inanimate serves the plant.

The inanimate and the plant serve the animal.

The inanimate, the plant and the animal are in the service of the human. And you, O human, whom do you serve? It was incumbent upon your intellect, O human, to reflect on whom you are bound to in a relation that befits your mastery over the other kinds. You had to seek the one who gave you mastery over the other kinds.

Did you, O human, subjugate these kinds by your own power and strength?

No. You do not possess an innate power that enables you to do that. Was it not incumbent upon you to think: what is the power that subjected to you what you cannot control? Your service came when you had no power, and your service came while you were asleep, sunk in deep sleep. Should you not have thought this thought? You, O human, must be consistent with yourself, and seek for yourself a master who befits your mastery over others. The universe has no master over you, because the universe is sensed. If someone comes to you and tells you that an unseen being is God and asks you to be in His service, you should say: "This speech is logical with respect to my position in the universe." After that, look at the universe. You are not alone in the universe; rather there are other kinds, and each kind has its law and its mission. The animal has a mission, the plant has a mission, and the inanimate has a mission. Have you found a kind that rebelled against its mission? No.

The horse, for example, you use as a mount, with a saddle of silk and leather and a bridle of silver, so that you may ride it. Then on another day you find this mount carrying the earth's fertilizer, animal dung, and it does not refuse. It has rendered you service as a rider, and rendered you service as a carrier, and it has never rebelled against you. All kinds, then, perform their mission as they should, so the affair is set right in them. And since the affair is set right in them, by what is it set right? It is Allah who created them and made them subservient. He said to them: "Be in the service of man, whether he is a believer or a disbeliever." In this is the justice of lordship, so none of them delays or deviates from its movement in serving man.

Has one of you seen the sun say once: "The creation no longer pleases me, I will not shine upon them, and I will veil myself today?" Did the air rebel and say: "No, the creation no longer deserves to breathe air, so I will not enable them to benefit from me"?

Have we seen the rain refuse? Has man cultivated fertile land which resisted him? No. Everything in existence performs its mission by subjugation and submission.

Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them are their mounts and some of them they eat. And for them in them are benefits and drinks; will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72-73].

The Truth, glorified and exalted, lets some animals loose so they are not tamed and not domesticated. This is so that you, O human, know that you did not tame the camel by your power. If you had absolute power over the universe, then tame some of the serpents of this world, or tame the lion. You, O human, see in this universe some wild creatures, such as serpents and savage animals, untamed, so that the Truth shows us that this which serves you, if Allah had not made it subservient for you, you could not have subjected it by your own power. It is subjugation, subservience and submission of these creatures which Allah, exalted be He, granted you, O human, as a favour from Him, glorified be He, despite your helplessness and weakness.

We have not found any beneficial thing that has disobeyed man in the universe, because all creation is subjected by Allah to serve man, whether he is a disbeliever or a believer. This is the gift of lordship, for the gift of lordship encompasses all creation. The Most Generous Creator is the Lord of all people and takes charge of raising them all. Therefore the kinds other than man respond to man whether he is a believer or a disbeliever. If the disbeliever uses the means well, the means give to him, and they do not give to the believer who does not use the means, or does not use them well. This is the gift of lordship, and lordship is for all. As for the gift of divinity, it is "do and do not do," and it is a gift for the believers only.

If this is the picture of the universe, performing its mission without any deviation in it, and harmonious in its essence with a wondrous harmony, then we may ask: "From where did the defect in the universe come?" The defect has come from you, O human. Therefore we do not find corruption in the universe except that man has a share in it; as for what man has no share in, there is no corruption in it at all.

Have you seen anyone complain that the air has become scarce? No.

Why? Because no one has any part in this matter of the air at all. It is true that we interfere with the air by polluting it with exhaust and waste, and it is also true that the Truth honours creation with discoveries that may then remedy this corruption. So when man interferes, the thing may become corrupted.

But does that mean we should not interfere? Should we stand toward the universe with folded hands? No, rather we must interfere in the universe, but by the method of Allah.

If you interfere in the universe by the method of Allah, then everything proceeds, for the universe, which has no method except submission and subjugation. Just as the sun performed its mission, and the inanimate its mission, and the animal its mission, you, O human, are required to perform your mission, which is to obey Allah. That obedience is summarized in what He requires of you: "do such-and-such and do not do such-and-such." If you align with the method through "do" and "do not do," you will have harmonized with the universe.

Allah, glorified be He, concludes this matter with a question at which the hearts of the believers are severed and split:

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 83].

Everything in the heavens and the earth has submitted to Allah, willingly or by compulsion. If we ask, and what is the meaning of "willingly"? The answer is obedience of subjugation, as the heavens and the earth said in the wise Qur'anic text:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

Whatever has no obligation came obediently and subjugated. And what is the meaning of "by compulsion"? Some scholars have said that "willingly" includes the kinds of angels, the inanimate, the plant and the animal, for each of them performs its mission in submission, none of them objects, and none of them has the power to disobey. As for "by compulsion," some scholars understood them to be people who serve people by force, such as slaves for example. To these we say: it is not correct or proper that we give the enemies of Islam an opportunity to say that Islam compelled a human being to serve another human being by compulsion, because the Truth, glorified be He, said:

﴿There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become distinct from error. So whoever disbelieves in the Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold, with no breaking of it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 256].

Since Allah has not compelled anyone to believe in Him, how would He compel a person to serve another person? Therefore we must understand "by compulsion" in its true sense. The Truth, glorified be He, has informed us that this entire universe is subjected to Him, because He is the one who created it and there is no god other than Him, and this is an established matter. The whole universe belongs to Allah, and He is its administrator and its subduer. The Truth said:

﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any god; otherwise each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Glory be to Allah above what they describe.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 91].

Since He is the One and He is the Creator, no one will rebel against His will. It was necessary for man to understand his mission as being that he is the only one whom Allah has charged, because the rest of the kinds have no choice and are not charged as Allah has charged man with "do" and "do not do." Thus obligation is a branch of choice. The method says to you: "do such-and-such and do not do such-and-such," because the One who set it knows that He created you fit to do what He commands you, and fit to do what He does not command you.

The hand, for example, is created to move according to the will of its owner. This is evident because if the will is paralysed and the thread connecting the commanding will to the acting limb is severed, then the person afflicted with that, God forbid, tries to raise his hand and cannot. So the hand is subjected to the will of the human. When your will, O human, follows the light of Allah's method, you direct it in the light of "do" and "do not do."

When it is said to you, for example: "Do not strike anyone with it," that means the hand is fit to strike. When it is said to you: "Take the hand of the one who stumbles," your hand is able to take the hand of the one who stumbles. You are created with your limbs in a disposition of obedience to your will. Then the method comes to say to you: "Execute the will in such-and-such, and do not execute the will in such-and-such."

Thus when a human follows the method, he agrees completely with the subjugated things and performs everything in the best performance. But when does a human deviate from harmony? When he does not apply the method, and he strays from the ranks in the whole universe. Read His saying, glorified and exalted:

﴿Do you not see that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures, and many among mankind? But many have deserved punishment. And whoever Allah humiliates, there is for him no honorer. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.﴾ [Al-Hajj: 18].

Behold, all kinds are prostrating: the sun prostrates, the moon prostrates, and the stars, and the mountains; all these inanimate things prostrate. Likewise the trees and plants prostrate to Allah, and the animals and beasts prostrate to Allah, and many of mankind prostrate. But in contrast to this numerous prostrating multitude of humans, there is a numerous multitude that does not prostrate, so punishment has become due upon them. Had the human taken the method of Allah and implemented it, he would have become like the rest of the kinds. But the human differed and said: "I will take the choice of bearing the trust, because I am knowing and rational," as the true word says:

﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 72].

So if man took Allah's method of "do" and "do not do," he would harmonize with all existence, and when man harmonizes with all existence, no disobedience will come from him at all, just as no disobedience comes in existence from other than man. And at that point

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 3, verse 84

The Truth (Allah), glorified is He, says after that: ﴿Say: "We believe in God, and in what has been sent down to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submissive."﴾

When we look at this verse with our reflections, we find that the Truth blends the Messenger, the believers in him, and those to whom he was sent in faith in Him. He addresses the Messenger and the believers as one faith-unit. The Truth's words "Say" ("qul") are an address to a single person, the Prophet ﷺ, and the speech that follows, ﴿We believe﴾, is evidence of the Messenger's harmony with the believing community. It is as if the Muslim community has been fused into "Say," and as if the Messenger is present within ﴿We believe﴾. Through this, the blending and harmony between the Messenger and those who believe in him are achieved, and the Truth's address to them becomes an address to one faith-unity with no severance in it.

The Truth has come with this style to make clear to us that the Messenger did not come to lord it over his community, but came to bear the burdens of this community. For this reason we said earlier that the Messenger ﷺ has two faiths: he believed in God, and he gave security (amana) to the believers. He ﷺ will intercede for us, because he has discharged a duty that encompasses his entire community. He completed the message and submitted to the obligation in a way that encompasses his whole community. For this reason the Truth says ﴿Say: "We believe"﴾. The expected form would have been "Say: 'I believe'," or ﴿Say, "We believe"﴾ in the plural imperative ("qūlū"). But the Truth, in His noble Qur'an, places every word in its proper place, so the word attracts its meaning, and every meaning is enamoured of its word. Here the Truth said ﴿Say: "We believe"﴾ so that it becomes clear to us that Muhammad is a messenger fused with his community, and the community of Islam is obedient to its Messenger. The command comes to the Messenger of God from the Truth, glorified is He, and its execution is by all. In this there is an indication to the adversaries that the Messenger ﷺ will have a strong faith-based solidarity. Had he said "Say: 'I believe'," it would have meant that the Messenger would possess only his own faith. But the Messenger ﷺ was believed in by his people and by many others, and through him the conquest of Mecca came about, as the Truth says:

﴿When the help of God comes and victory, and you see the people entering the religion of God in multitudes﴾ [al-Nasr: 1-2].

When we read His words ﴿Say: "We believe in God and in what has been sent down to us"﴾, we may note that the scholars have a pause over the matter of "inzal" (sending down). Sometimes the Truth says:

﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and in the Hereafter they are certain﴾ [al-Baqara: 4].

And at other times the Truth says:

﴿And We have not sent down the Book to you except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ, and as a guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-Nahl: 64].

Thus we find that "inzal" comes sometimes transitive with "ila" (to), and at other times transitive with "'ala" (upon). Some scholars have said: when the speech is directed to the Messenger of God ﷺ, the Truth says "anzala 'alayka" (He sent down upon you). It is as if these scholars, without intending it, separate God's delivery to the Messenger from the delivery to the Messenger's community, and they did not notice that the purpose of sending down the method upon the Messenger is the guidance of the community.

We say: we must not take the matter superficially from a style that appears to us, for there is a hidden style here: "ila" and "'ala" both indicate that the method was sent down to the community and to the Messenger ﷺ. Sometimes the Truth uses "inzal" transitive with "ila," and the address is directed to the Messenger ﷺ, as in His words:

﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say: "Our Lord, we believe, so write us down among the witnesses"﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 83].

And at other times the Truth uses "inzal" transitive with "'ala," and the address is directed to the Messenger ﷺ, as in His words:

﴿And We have not sent down the Book to you except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ, and as a guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-Nahl: 64].

And a third time the Truth uses "inzal" in an address to the believers:

﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they enter into a conversation other than that. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together﴾ [al-Nisa': 140].

It is a Book sent down from heaven, in which elevation is observed, and the purpose of the sending down is the benefit of the community. So the use of "'ala" indicates elevation, and for the benefit of the community. The "'illiyya" (exalted status) here increases the standing of the method in the eyes of the believers, for it has been sent down for their benefit. Thus "inzal" implies "'illiyya" (exaltedness): in terms of height it comes with "'ala," and in terms of purpose it comes with "ila." It is a method that came down from the Highest Truth, and came down to the Messenger and upon the Messenger, so that he might convey it to the believers for their benefit. For this reason we said: if we see a ruling that restricts the freedom of the individual, we must not understand that God intended this individual to restrict his freedom. Rather, such a restriction comes to restrict millions for the sake of the freedom of the individual. An example of this: when the method forbids theft to a human being, it is a command for every one of the millions, and it is for the benefit of every human being. So the Qur'an has been sent down for your benefit and for the benefit of all the believers.

When we read His words ﴿Say: "We believe in God and in what has been sent down to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submissive"﴾, this statement makes clear that the Messenger ﷺ came with a method that includes sound beliefs, narratives and reports, and it agrees with what came in the procession of messages from the day God created the earth and sent the messengers. God took a covenant from the nations and the prophets before, that when a messenger comes confirming what they have, they must believe in him. Likewise God took from our Messenger ﷺ a covenant that he would believe in the earlier messengers. He ﷺ did not come to demolish religions, but to complete them. Thus we see the noble Qur'anic text:

﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 3].

It is as if the earlier religions, with all that came in them of sound beliefs, narratives and reports, are present in Islam. And above all that, Islam came with laws suited to every time and place. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ said in his noble hadith: "The example of me and the prophets before me is like a man who built a building and made it beautiful and perfect, except for the place of one brick. The people went around it and said, 'We have not seen anything more beautiful than this, were it not for the place of this brick.' So I was the brick."

Thus the reins of the whole matter have ended with the Messenger of God ﷺ. God took a covenant from others that they would confirm him when he came. He ﷺ believed in and confirmed those who preceded him among the messengers, and nothing has come after him that asks the Messenger of God or his community to confirm it. The Truth said, as an appendix to this noble verse: ﴿and to Him we are submissive﴾.

That is to say, the followers of none of the earlier messengers have any temporal authority that gives them power. Rather, the whole matter begins with God and ends with God. That is the final issue in the procession of messages. Since Islam is that submission which a human being chooses for himself, so that he may be in harmony with himself in Islam, submitting to God, and in harmony with the rest of existence, with its animals, plants, inanimate things and others, in that they have all submitted in obedience to God, the universe, with the believing Muslim human being in it, becomes entirely subjugated to God, glorified and exalted is He. And since the universe with the human being has become subjugated to God, there is no contradiction in one movement that opposes another movement, because the One who holds this dominion is the One who set for every human being, in the field of his movement in life, a law that protects him from colliding with others. If human beings have been able to set for themselves standards that prevent collision in movement, that collision which leads to disasters and calamities.

An example: consider the railways. Is there not an employee called the "mahawlaji" (switchman)? The meaning of this job is that the one who performs it diverts an incoming locomotive from a certain track onto a specific line, so that another locomotive coming from the same track does not crash into it. That is from the action of human beings in what they have made of trains and transport. They have also made means that prevent their collision. So what about the Truth, to whom belongs the highest likeness, who created the human being? He, glorified is He, has set the method so that no movement in existence collides with another movement.

Let us look at things that come under the law of subjugation and things that fall under the realm of choice. Have we heard that two camels walked on two opposing roads and one camel collided with another? That never happened. The camel protects itself and what it carries from the other camel and what it carries. But we hear of a car colliding with a car, because the car does not move by itself; it moves under the guidance of a chosen human being, and he is the one who collides, and it is he who, in his heedlessness, may bring about the calamities.

So the collision of one movement with another arises only in matters of choice, or from a person's heedlessness of his duty, like the heedlessness of the "mahawlaji" in his work of regulating the movement of trains. But the collision of one movement in existence with another movement in existence is impossible and never happens, because the matter is still in the hand of the Supreme Guardian, the Guardian of earth and heaven, who is God, who runs the universe in harmony, and who makes us know His attributes when He says: ﴿God—there is no god but Him, the Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾.

Its meaning is: I am the One who sustains your affairs and manages your matters, and I do not sleep, nor does drowsiness or heedlessness overtake Me. So sleep, you, for I have subjugated the whole of existence for your sake.

Since the matter in Islam is thus, and existence is in harmony with itself, why do you, O human being, deviate from existence? And why do you deviate from the faculties of your own soul?

Why do you not be in harmony with the universe? If you are in harmony with yourself and with the universe, you become the happy human being.

In our modern age we see the world's material advancement at a high level, such that an event occurs in America, for example, and we see it on the television screen immediately, and a human being boards a rocket vehicle into space. But has the world found rest? No. The world has increased in toil, as if it is wearing out its mind and exhausting its scientists in their laboratories to invent things that give the world more anxiety and turmoil, that collide and conflict. Thus the universe is never free of a cold or hot war.

All of this arises from the management of the world's affairs by human desires. We are not all referred to one method that commands us so that we obey, and forbids us so that we desist. Rather, every person follows his own desire in his work. For this reason we see anxiety and turmoil, and we see cries filling the world from horrors and calamities. Among them, for example, drugs. The person is discontent with the reality of his life, so he does not want to face his life; he tries to escape from it through addiction. We say to such a person: this is not a solution to the problem, because when a human being encounters a problem he needs a mind over his mind to confront this problem, and by this addiction you are only wasting your mind, even though you are required

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 3, verse 85:

﴿Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.﴾

The goal that makes the whole world happy is the religion of Islam, and whoever desires a religion other than it, God will not accept it from him. If there is someone who does not like the legislation of heaven and says in astonishment: "There is cruelty in this legislation; you cut off a person's hand and disfigure him," we answer such a speaker: a car that strikes another car disfigures dozens of people inside the two cars, or a train suffers a catastrophe and disfigures hundreds of people.

When we search for the number of hands that were cut off in the whole history of Islam, we will find them to be far fewer than the number of those disfigured by accidents. Any claim of preserving human beauty is a matter that provokes ridicule, because the legislation of cutting off the hand of the thief has kept life in order, whereas wars arising from desire have disfigured and annihilated hundreds and thousands. Such a statement is sophistry. Does the purpose of legislating a punishment mean that the sin occurs? No. The legislation of a punishment means warning the human being against committing the sin.

When we say to a person: "If you kill a soul, the guardian of the affair will take your life," is there not in that a preservation of his life and the lives of others? When the legislation preserves the life of one individual, it at the same time preserves the life of every human being. God Most High says:

﴿And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding, that you may be mindful of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 179].

Thus this legislation becomes perfectly sound. So the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ indicate to us that the one who legislates a law that contradicts what God has legislated is, as it were, finding fault with God in what He legislated, as if he were saying to God: "I am more compassionate toward creation than You, O God, because this matter escaped You."

In this statement there is deviation (fisq) from the law of God, and it is incumbent upon the human being to observe proper conduct (adab) with his Creator. Let everything be referred back to God, the Nurturer. When you, O human, refer everything to your Lord, you find rest and give rest. Unless you have an interest in deviation; if you have an interest in deviation, then you want other than what God wants. But if you want the interest of people, then the Truth has legislated what contains the interest of all people. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾.

Someone may say, regarding His words ﴿it will never be accepted from him﴾, that this phrase is not sufficient to give assurance about the reward for the deed by which I draw near to God, since God may accept or may not accept. He, glorified is He, is not compelled by anyone to do anything. We say to him: you will come to your Lord, whether you are pleased or refuse, so what need do you have for this statement? If you could, then be sensible and do not rebel against the command of your Lord. The Truth says: ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾. The "loser" (al-khasir) is derived from "al-khusr," and "al-khusr" is the loss and destruction of capital, and the Hereafter is a life after which there is no life. It is foolish for someone to say: "I will be punished a little and then the matter will end." No, the matter does not end, because the Hereafter is an everlasting life and there is no life after it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 86:

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified that the Messenger was true...﴾

Here we see the wondrous style. Allah, glorified is He, calls us to marvel at a people who disbelieved after faith. Had they not declared their faith beforehand, we would have said: they never tasted the sweetness of faith. But the one who believed and tasted the sweetness of faith, how does he accept for himself to go over to disbelief? It is a compounded rebellion.

Someone might ask: since Allah did not guide them, what is their fault? We say to him: you must keep in mind what we repeat always, so that the matter becomes clear in the mind, for it is a common matter, especially among those who are not committed, where one of them says: "Allah did not want my guidance, so what can I do?" That is an argument used to justify deviation, and such a saying comes only from one who is wasteful toward himself, and it never comes from one who obeys Allah. The one who says: "Disobedience is what Allah willed for me, so what is my fault?" must know that obedience is also from Allah. So why did he not say: "Obedience is from Allah, so why does He reward us for it?" Why, O disobedient one, do you neglect mention of the reward of obedience, and stop at disobedience, saying: "Allah has decreed disobedience for me, so why does He punish me?" It would also be right to say: "Since He has decreed obedience for me, why does He give me a reward for it?"

We say to the one who justifies deviation to himself: you want to take the reward of obedience, and you want to flee from the punishment of disobedience. You need to understand the matter as it truly is. I have said before that "guidance" (hidayah) comes in two meanings. "Hada" means to point out the road that leads to the desired goal, and does nothing more than that. The example is the deaf traffic signals: each signal indicates a particular road and guides to it, and another signal indicates another road and guides to it. Nobody at this signal takes a person by the hand and says: "I will take your hand and repair the vehicle when it stops with you, or ride with you to bring you to your goal."

This signal is guidance only, that is, an indication of the road that leads to the desired goal. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has guided all people, believer and disbeliever alike, that is, He has pointed them to the road that leads to the goal. After that, people divided into two groups: a group accepted this method, approved it, and proceeded as Allah wills. And when this believer went to the presence of Allah and believed in Him, it is as if the Truth says to him: "You have believed in Me and My method, so there will be another reward for you, which is that I will help you and make matters easy for you." This is the second guidance that Allah gives as a reward to whoever believes in Him and approves His method, and it means "assistance" (ma'unah). Allah gives His believing servant the sweetness of obedience and makes him eager for it with energy.

So guidance is sometimes "indication" (dalalah) and sometimes a second time "assistance" (ma'unah). I repeat this so that the matter becomes clear in all our minds, and so that we remember it always, and say: who helps a person? The one who helps him is the one who believed in Him. As for the one who disbelieves in Allah, Allah does not help him.

I had earlier given an example, and I still give it: a person walking along a road when the route to the desired destination becomes confused for him, like a traveler heading to Alexandria, for example. Then he finds a policeman standing, and asks him: "Where is the road to Alexandria?"

The policeman points to the road leading to Alexandria, saying to the questioner: "This is the correct road to Alexandria."

Here the policeman has indicated the way to this person. But when the questioner says to the policeman: "Praise be to God that I found you here, for you have made the way easy for me," this saying captures the policeman's heart, so he increases his directions to the questioner and explains to him in precise detail how to reach the road, and alerts him to any obstacle that may confront him. If the questioner increases his thanks to the policeman, that captures the policeman's conscience even more, and he volunteers to ride with the questioner to bring him to the road, explaining to him what obstacles he must avoid. In this way the policeman has offered all assistance to the one who thanked him.

But suppose another man asked the policeman about the road, and he lied to the policeman. In such a situation the policeman ignores such a man. I have given this example for approximation, not for comparison. The Truth first guides by the guidance of indication: Allah has guided all people, that is, He pointed them to the method. Whoever goes to its precincts and believes in it, Allah gives him a second guidance, the guidance of assistance and facilitation.

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

The Truth gives them the sweetness of guidance, which is piety, as if the Truth says to the believing servant: since you have turned to Me in faith, you have the sweetness of faith. As for the one who disbelieves, and who wrongs himself by associating partners with Allah, the Truth withholds from him the guidance of assistance, because he has seen the guidance of indication and did not believe in it. So the interrogative in His saying, ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾, is a question meant as denial and remote improbability, not about the first guidance, which is the guidance of indication, but about the guidance of assistance; that is: how shall I assist one who disbelieved in Me?

The one meant by this saying is a group of the People of the Book, to whom the description of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had come in their books, to the extent that Abdullah ibn Salam, who was one of them, said: "I knew Muhammad when I saw him as I know my own son, and my knowledge of Muhammad is stronger." The confirmation of this is what the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor him, support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him — it is those who will be the successful﴾ [al-A'raf: 157].

The precise Qur'anic expression does not say: "whose description they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel," but the Truth says:

﴿whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-A'raf: 157].

As if one who reads the Torah and the Gospel could see the image of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, from the precision of the description. The Torah knew him and the Gospel knew him with detailed and comprehensive knowledge, together with speech and utterance confirming that. There is a difference between "knowing" and "saying," for a person may know and conceal what he knows. But they knew the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and acknowledged it, for they had previously sought victory through him against those who disbelieved. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, though before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89].

They took the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, before his coming as a support against the disbelievers, saying: a prophet will come, and we will follow him and kill you with him, the killing of 'Ad and Iram. So what did they do? The Truth answers:

﴿So when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89].

Thus they believed in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, before his coming, and when he came they disbelieved in him. Look at the justice of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, when He wants to show them the stance of truthfulness, the Truth, and the dignity of faith.

﴿Say: Allah suffices as witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43].

Those who have knowledge of the Book are the Jews and the Christians. These testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that the Qur'an, in its justice, does justice to the Torah and the Gospel, which are the books in their hands. ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified that the Messenger was true﴾. They believed in him as a messenger from the content of their books, then they declared it when they said: "A prophet will come whom we will follow, and we will kill you with him, the killing of 'Ad and Iram."

If they did that, how would Allah guide them? They have no readiness for guidance, and they did not turn to Allah with any love, therefore He, glorified is He, does not assist them in guidance, and if they had turned to Allah, He would have helped them. Allah said:

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

These did not get guided, so Allah left them without the guidance of assistance. This clarifies for us the meaning of the true saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾ [al-Nisa': 88].

Those who were not guided by the guidance of indication and did not believe, Allah leaves them astray, that is, He leaves them in their error and disbelief. That is, as long as there is one who does not believe in Allah, would Allah take his hand to guide him with the guidance of assistance? No; because if he does not believe in the origin, which is the guidance of indication, how would Allah grant him the guidance of assistance? And as long as he does not believe in Allah, would he accept the facilitations Allah grants him? No. He does not accept them. You must know that the guidance of indication is a general guidance for every person addressed by the address of obligation, that is, the human being absolutely, while the guidance of assistance is for one who believingly turns to Allah. It is as if the Truth says to him: "You have believed in My indication, so take My assistance," or "You are worthy of My assistance," or "You will find facilitation in all matters." As for the one who disbelieved, Allah does not guide him.

Allah, glorified is He, does not assist the disbeliever, because assistance presupposes an initial action from the one assisted, and the disbeliever has not done what could earn this assistance, for he has not believed. Therefore the decisive statement is: ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, and the true statement is ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, and the true statement is ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. These are the wrongdoers who committed the fundamental wrong, which is associating partners with Allah, as the Truth said:

﴿And when Luqman said to his son while he was admonishing him: "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association is a great wrong"﴾ [Luqman: 13].

When the Truth leaves them, He increases them in misguidance, and seals their hearts, so they do not know a path to faith:

﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified that the Messenger was true, and the clear proofs had come to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 86].

The Messenger came to them with the signs indicating the truth of his message, but they wronged themselves with the great and immense wrong, which is associating partners with Allah. But is this verse revealed concerning the People of the Book who had the description of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and its signs and glad tidings? Or was it revealed for something else, namely that some people believed in the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and then disbelieved in him?

The true saying encompasses both groups and applies to them, whether they were from the People of the Book who believed in the earlier messengers and did not believe in the message of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or from those who believed in the message of the Messenger of Allah and then disbelieved in it, as happened with some of them in the time of the Messenger, such as Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, Ibn al-Ash'alt and al-Harith ibn Suwayd. These declared faith and headed to Mecca and remained there. One of them repented, and his brother took a pledge for him before the Messenger of Allah, while the rest did not repent.

The true saying encompasses both groups.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 3, verse 87:

The Wise Almighty (Al-Haqq subhanahu) details the recompense of these people in His words:
﴿Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾

Al-La'nah (the curse) is expulsion from mercy. Allah knows every one of them who is cursed. And since they have been expelled from the mercy of Allah, the angels, who are the believers in Allah with the faith of witnessing, repeat the curse; the believers among the creatures of Allah repeat the curse; and likewise all people curse them. How can all people curse them, whether they are believers or disbelievers? How can the disbelievers curse them? When the disbeliever sees a person committing some sin, he lowers him in his eyes and despises him, even if he is not a believer.

Suppose a disbeliever finds a person who goes out of the method and commits a sin and perpetrates a crime: does the disbeliever not curse such a person? He curses him, because the innate nature (al-fitrah al-markuzah) with which Allah created people rejects that and does not approve of it.

Thus Allah willed to make them, as disbelievers, curse one another, and we find that all people curse them likewise, because they have departed from the method of Allah by disbelief after faith, and that led them to commit sins; and thus cursing them becomes universal.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 88:

They will remain eternally in the curse. The Exalted said: ﴿Abiding therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾

As for ﴿the punishment will not be lightened for them﴾, its meaning is that the punishment will continue constantly, forever. Some people may think that since the disbeliever is going to enter the Fire and burn, his matter will come to an end. No, he overlooks one matter and mentions another. He forgets the words of the Truth:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses, We will drive them to a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa': 56].

They will taste the punishment by the command of the Truth, constantly and forever. Some may say: science has determined that a person's sensitivity to the pain caused by lashing with a whip decreases after the first twenty lashes. In saying this, he forgets that the punishment in the Hereafter follows a different pattern. Indeed, Allah creates for the one being punished a new sensation so that he continually perceives the punishment. The Truth said: ﴿The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾, meaning that their punishment is certain, and the Truth does not leave them to rest from their punishment.

Then, after that, the Exalted says:

﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾

The Truth, glory be to Him, is the Creator of all creation. He loves that they should be upon what He wills and loves, because they are His handiwork. So He, glory be to Him, loves those who repent (al-tawwabin) and loves those who purify themselves (al-mutatahhirin).

He has commanded His servants to turn to Him in sincere repentance (tawbah nasuha), that is, a true and pure repentance from which there is no turning back. This repentance is marked by giving up the sin, regret for what has passed, the firm resolve not to return to the sin again, and restoring wrongs to their owners if there are any wrongs. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah stretches out His hand by night to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by day, and He stretches out His hand by day to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by night, until the sun rises from its place of setting."

Thus the Truth has legislated repentance with the aim of reforming the universe, for if Allah had not legislated repentance for the one who sins, then whoever neglects the way of Allah even once might come to see himself as lost, corrupt, committing every folly. So by legislating repentance, Allah has guaranteed that the one who has been extravagant against himself in sin may return to Allah, just as society is protected from the evils of a corrupt person. Therefore the legislation of repentance came for the benefit of the universe and for the benefit of the human being, so that he may enjoy the love of Allah. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al 'Imran: 89].

Despite their earlier disbelief, Allah in His mercy does not include them in the threat, because they are required to repent and make amends. The meaning of the word "aslaha" (to make amends) is that he adds something good to his goodness. The universe contains nothing corrupt, except what arises from a voluntary act of a human being, and the penitent must increase goodness in the universe. Thus we ensure that the penitent does not come to a thing and corrupt it, for whoever wishes to increase what is good in goodness will not corrupt the good thing.

Perhaps those who were extravagant against themselves, in a moment when their faith-consciousness lapsed, when they recall the sin or the offence they committed in regard to their religion, try to strive and hasten in a good matter, so that Allah may mend the breach of their earlier disobedience with their later obedience.

For this reason you find many people who are zealous for reform and for good are people in whom there may be a corner of self-extravagance in some matter, and afterwards they turn to doing good deeds in very many fields, as if Allah says to each of them: "You have stolen something from My sacred things, and I will take you to My beloved ones." Truly, the Truth makes the earlier sin of the individual into lashes that continually goad his conscience, so he turns to goodness, gives charity to the poor, and perhaps those who live in steady obedience do not have such lashes in their lives.

But those who were extravagant against themselves are the ones whom those lashes goad. So whenever one of you sees a person who has been extravagant against himself, let him pray to Allah for his guidance, and know with complete certainty that Allah will make him a means of doing good, for no one will ever steal the universe from its Creator. This applies to those of whom Allah said: ﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends﴾ ("and make amends," i.e., they performed many good deeds), because the heat of their self-extravagance constantly scorches their backs, so they always want to do subsequent things that cover over and erase their earlier deviations.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 90:

And after that the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief - their repentance will never be accepted...﴾

This verse speaks of those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief. Such people, their repentance will not be accepted, and they are the misguided. It has come in contrast to the previous verse: there are people who repented and people who did not repent. But how does disbelief increase? It is that a person disbelieves in himself, and then becomes an obstacle for others from believing. He is not content with his own loss, but tries to spread his loss onto others, and in that there is an increase in disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah. This statement was revealed concerning some of the Jews who believed in the good tidings that foretold the coming of Jesus, peace be upon him. When Jesus came, they disbelieved in him, and when Muhammad came, they increased in disbelief.

They disbelieved in Jesus first, then they increased in disbelief by rejecting Muhammad, and they claimed that they are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones. These are not among those who repented. Or they declared repentance with their tongues, but did not repent a sincere repentance, and "the one who returns to his repentance is like one who mocks his Lord." May Allah protect us and you from this overturning.

Then, after that, the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any one of them the earth filled with gold, even if he should ransom himself with it...﴾

They disbelieved, and God had already decreed for them the opportunity to repent, but they died in disbelief. God wants to give us a ruling specific to their deeds in this world, and a ruling specific to the punishment they receive in the Hereafter. The ruling specific to their deeds in this world is due to the fact that they have choice (ikhtiyar, free will), whereas the ruling specific to the punishment they receive in the Hereafter, which is punishment, is because they no longer have any choice. Here the scholars pause. Is the "earth filled with gold" referring to what they spent during their lives, filling the earth with gold? We say to him: this spending will not benefit you in acts of goodness, because your deeds are nullified.

Suppose a disbeliever died in disbelief, having spent in charity the earth filled with gold. We say to him: this spending does not benefit, along with the supreme betrayal, which is disbelief. As long as he does not believe in God, he spent this wealth for the sake of people, and became one who spends on those who cannot reward him with good in the Hereafter. Therefore he has nothing with God. One who performs a deed should seek a reward from the one for whom he performed it. Was God in the mind of that disbeliever? No, because he died in disbelief. Therefore, even if he spent the earth filled with gold, it will not be accepted from him. He did that good while people were in his mind, and people give him his due of praise, whether he was an inventor, a benefactor, or otherwise. He receives his reward from humanity, and the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) applies to him: "You did it so that it would be said, and it has been said."

It is as if God says to him: I was not in your mind, so why do you seek a reward from Me in the Hereafter? God was not in your mind; the kingship is Mine. He, glorified is He, said:

﴿The Day they will come forth, nothing of them will be hidden from God. "Whose is the dominion today?" "God's, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

Some people say: how would those who filled the world with discoveries and inventions, and eased the pains of humanity through them, not receive the reward of the Hereafter? We say: humanity has given them and preserved their memory, erected statues, books, festivals and prizes for them. They worked for people, and people gave them. So there is no diminishing of their rights. But they did not act with God in mind. The Truth has depicted their situation in a marvelous depiction, saying, exalted is His majesty:

﴿As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him in full his account. And God is swift in reckoning.﴾ [An-Nur: 39].

It is a mirage resulting from the imagining of water in the desert, which the thirsty traveler imagines due to reflections of light, so the traveler continues heading toward the illusion of water. He creates hope for himself; when he reaches it he finds nothing, and he is confronted with the presence of God, so he regrets and receives the punishment.

Likewise, the earth filled with gold will not be accepted from him if he spent it on any good in this world. Then, in the Hereafter, God will not accept from him the earth filled with gold, even if he ransoms himself with it. If he were to find the earth filled with gold, and supposing he had found it, would he find anyone to accept it from him? No. In reality he will not find the gold, because in the Hereafter he no longer owns anything. The Truth says:
