﴿Whose is the dominion today? God's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

And He says:

﴿Even if those who did wrong possessed all that is on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from God what they had not reckoned.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 47].

﴿Those will have a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers﴾ — meaning: these have a painful punishment, because every event takes its strength from the strength of its doer. When the punitive event is attributed to God, who has absolute power and capability, the punishment cannot be endured. The wrongdoer will not find anyone to ward off this punishment from him, because he will find no helper for himself, and no intercessor. No one will come and say: so-and-so is being punished, come, let us help him; no one will come to help him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 92:

After that, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love...﴾

Every root consisting of the letters bāʾ, rāʾ, and a doubled rāʾ leads to the meaning of "expanse" (saʿa). Thus "al-barr" (the vast) means the wide one, and "al-barr" (the open land) means the expansive earth, whose opposite is "al-baḥr" (the sea). If someone says: "The sea is wider than the land, because the size of the continents is not the size of the seas and oceans that separate them," we say to such a speaker: "No. Your movement on the barr, the land, is expansive, while your movement on the baḥr is constricted, because you do not move in the sea except in a particular form: either by a ship or even on a plank of wood. But your movement on the barr, the land, is that you walk or ride, go or come, so your field of movement on the land is wider than your field of movement at sea."

And "al-birr" (righteousness) is piety and obedience, or it is "the Garden" (al-Janna). All these meanings converge, because they lead to expansiveness: obedience leads to expansiveness, and so does piety, and so does the Garden. All of them converge, because all of them are expansiveness. One of the commentators took the meaning of the word from its first stage, that is, by the cause, which is obedience; and some of them took it from its last stage, that is, by the effect, which is the Garden.

Someone may ask: why did God wish to bring a discussion of spending after the discussion of the punishment of the disbelievers? We say: when the Truth speaks of those who suffer painful punishment because they disbelieved and died as disbelievers, and "they will have no helpers," the opposite comes to mind, namely the one who believed and did righteous deeds and died upon his faith; for him is the opposite of painful punishment, which is bliss, and he will find someone to take him by the hand, whereas the disbeliever will find no helpers. The believer will find God's recompense for obedience, which is righteousness, because righteousness is every good; and when it is mentioned without qualification, it refers to the recompense from God, whose summit is the Garden.

Thus we see that the counterpart of the Truth's treatment of the disbelievers is the Truth's treatment of the believers. This speech has come in the Qur'an, which is the miraculous word of God, and when He, glorified is He, addresses those charged with the methodology, He addresses through His speech human faculties that He Himself created. Therefore this speech must nourish all the faculties created by God. Had the Creator of the faculties been other than the Speaker, it would have been possible for the speech not to harmonize with the faculties; but the speech here is that of God, who created, so the faculties must necessarily harmonize with the word of God.

In the human soul there are many faculties, and these many faculties are intricately interlinked, so that when addressing one auditory faculty you can stir emotional sensations, and if the one who knows the faculties were not knowledgeable about them, it would not be possible for the reasoning to agree with an auditory faculty and with emotional faculties that may be brought about by the nature of the association of meanings (tadāʿī al-maʿānī).

"Tadāʿī al-maʿānī" (association of meanings) is a property present in human beings. Its meaning is that a person receives a certain meaning, and that meaning points to hidden meanings which it summons to be present in the mind. For example, when you see a person you know, association of meanings gives you your history with him and his history with you; it also brings to your mind images of his family, his friends and his acquaintances, and association of meanings brings you the events that took place between you and him, or that you both witnessed. This is what we call "tadāʿī al-maʿānī," meaning that one meaning calls another meaning.

When God, glorified and exalted is He, addresses a human being, He addresses every faculty within him at one and the same time, so that no faculty takes its nourishment while another faculty finds no nourishment for itself. The word of God comes complete and sufficient for all the faculties. An example of this is when the Truth, glorified is He, wished to prevent the polytheists from circumambulating the House. Before God forbade their circumambulation, the polytheists used to circumambulate the House and would come from far-distant places to circumambulate during the season of the pilgrimage, and they would bring their wealth to spend on the people of Makkah and buy everything they needed from them, for the pilgrimage season was an economic season. When God wished to prevent the polytheists from performing the pilgrimage, He addressed the Muslims residing in Makkah so that they would prevent the polytheists from circumambulating. He, glorified is He, knowing—and He is the All-Knowing—what faculties He had created, knew that another faculty would intervene at this time, so He said:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Ḥarām after this, their year.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28].

When this ruling was revealed, faculties necessarily stirred in the human soul, and the Truth had known from eternity that the faculty of economic utility among the people of Makkah would be stirred upon hearing this ruling. That is to say, some of the Muslims residing in Makkah at the time this ruling was revealed might say: "If we prevent the polytheists, who come to us with wealth to buy our goods, and whose economic season is what sustains us throughout the year, then what shall we do?" God knew that when a ruling forbidding the polytheists from approaching the House was revealed, the faculty of utility in the human soul would necessarily be stirred, so He, glorified is He, said immediately after that:

﴿And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28].

"Al-ʿaylah" means fear of poverty, and this is the greatness of divine speech, for when a human being speaks, many meanings may escape him, and afterwards there may be uproar, confusion and upheaval among people; but when the Most High Truth says: ﴿Indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Ḥarām after this, their year﴾ and follows it immediately with His reassuring words: ﴿And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty﴾—and He did so, and the Truth gathered and brought to the Sacred House the fruits of everything—it is as if He is saying to us: do not think that these fruits come by way of voluntary giving, but they are a provision from Us, as He says, the Truth:

﴿And they say: "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be swept away from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 57].

That is, there is no freedom for anyone to give or not to give to the people of the Sacred House; it is a levy (jibāyah), to reassure the utilitarian faculty in the soul, and He, glorified is He, gives economic security upon which the sustenance of life depends. When we reflect upon the verses of the Qur'an, we find that there is a verse that comes forward, a verse that comes later, and a verse that comes in the middle; and we find that the middle verse is linked by association of meanings to the verse before it and linked by association of meanings to the verse after it. Therefore, so that all of a human being's faculties may be satisfied and nourished, no command comes that suggests there is something lacking in the human soul. Let us consider an example of this, the Truth's saying:

﴿And they say within themselves: "Why does God not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 8].

The polytheists did not say it to anyone; they said it to themselves, and the Truth, glorified is He, the All-Knowing, exposes them in their most hidden concealments, and reveals what is in their souls; He is the All-Knowing of all the hidden things of His servants and the Revealer of all the psychological faculties in His creation. When the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love, and whatever you spend, indeed God is Knowing of it.﴾ The verse is an exhortation to spending, and it came after a verse indicating that there is a kind of spending which God does not accept, in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers—never will be accepted from one of them the earth filled with gold even if he were to ransom himself by it. Those will have a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 91].

Thus there is a kind of spending which God rejects, and association of meanings in the human soul may lead a person to ask: "What then is the accepted spending?" Therefore it was necessary that His saying, the Exalted, should come: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love﴾. If there is a rejected spending, there is also an accepted spending, and thus we see that the verse that urges spending is harmonious with what precedes it. ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love.﴾ One may ask: and why does a person not attain righteousness until he spends of what he loves? He should know that the nature of the human soul is "shuḥḥ" (miserliness), and for this reason the Noble Qur'an says:

﴿So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul—those are the successful.﴾ [al-Taghābun: 16].

The miserliness of the soul comes because a person never feels safe that incapacity may come upon him after capability, so if he owns something he tries to secure against the imagined incapacity, and he preserves what he has of needs. From here came possession and ownership; these things did not arise from the beginning of creation, but arose from the day when the places that give were no longer sufficient for needs. When the places that give are sufficient for needs, there is no reason for this imagined incapacity.

Let us suppose that a man bought a crate of oranges and entered his home, and when this man's son needs an orange or two, he takes what he wants; but if the man brought only a few oranges, his wife would be keen to divide the oranges among the children, so as not to leave each child to his own disposition, which might deprive the others.

Thus it was at the beginning of God's appointment of the human being on the earth: whoever wanted the land took it, and whoever wanted to eat the fruits, they were before him. When the supplies of needs decreased, because the giving places became narrow, the desire for ownership and the distinguishing of things began to appear. The Truth, glorified is He, draws our attention to this matter, as if He were saying to us: if you look at spending with a realistic and true view, you would find that you, O servant, are a mudārib (a partner in a profit-sharing venture) of God in God's wealth. "Mudārib" means that you work for God with the intellect He created for you, and you plan with it, and you work for God with the energy God created, and the material God created for you responds to you—so what is yours?

Everything belongs to God, and you are merely a mudārib who owns nothing. And as long as you are a mudārib, O servant, give God His due; and God's due is not taken by Him, for He is the Richest of the rich. God's due is taken by your brother who is unable and cannot interact with the material. Do not think, O servant, that when God asked you to spend of what you love, He, exalted is He, considered what He asked you to spend too much for you. Rather, when He takes from you for your brother while you are able, He is assuring you that if you become incapable, He will take for you from the capable; that is the insurance in the hand of God.

The Truth wants to make us love spending, but a human being tries to spend of what he does not love: he gives away a garment that is no longer fit for use to a poor person, or gives a worn-out shoe to someone in need. But God commands us to spend of what we love. Therefore the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were moved when they heard this text: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love.﴾ Abū Ṭalḥah, when he heard it, said: "O Messenger of God, the most beloved of my property to me is Bayruḥāʾ, so I give it in the way of God." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Place it among your relatives," so he placed it among his relatives. Likewise Zayd ibn Ḥārithah heard the noble verse and was moved by it as well; he had a mare named "Sabal," which he loved, and he said: "O Messenger of God, you know my love for my mare, and I make her in the way of God," so he took her from him...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 93:

﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel had made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."﴾

When the Prophet of God, Ya'qub (Israel), made some food unlawful, he was free to do so: he might make a food unlawful for himself as a vow (nadhr), or as a means of treatment, or out of asceticism (zuhd). But God did not make anything unlawful for him. What you Jews rely on, O Jews, is a particularity of our master Ya'qub: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel had made unlawful for himself﴾. So why do you say that camels and their milk were unlawful?

They did this because they wished to conceal a deficiency about themselves that they did not want exposed, and that is the deficiency the Qur'an revealed through the noble statement:

﴿And to those who were Jews We made unlawful every animal with claws; and of cattle and sheep We made unlawful to them their fat, except what their backs carry, or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That is how We recompensed them for their rebellion; and indeed We are truthful.﴾ [al-An'am: 146]

So there are things that were made unlawful for the Jews because they did wrong, and this noble verse is what clarified that the Truth made these foods unlawful for them because of their wrongdoing. The meaning of ﴿every animal with claws﴾ is the animal whose toes are joined and connected, so that the toes are not separate. We find this in the camel, the ostrich, the goose, and the duck, and all of these are called "those with claws" (dhawat al-zufur). ﴿Except what their backs carry﴾ means the fat that is on the back. As for "al-hawaya", these are the fats in the large intestines. ﴿Or what is mixed with bone﴾: that is, the fat that is mixed with the bone. The prohibition here was not because these things are harmful; rather, the prohibition was a punishment for them for their wronging of themselves and their transgression against others.

I say this so that no one who wishes to escape the judgment of God will say, "What is the harm in forbidding such-and-such a thing?" Seeking harm in what God has forbidden is a desire to escape the judgment of God. Prohibition may come as discipline and as correction. Among us human beings, and to God belongs the highest likeness, a father may withhold the allowance from his son as a correction, or withhold sweets from him, because the son has disobeyed his mother. So the prohibition was a recompense and a punishment for them. God, Exalted, says:

﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful to them good things that had been lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of God, and their taking of usury though they had been forbidden it, and their consuming people's wealth falsely. We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nisa': 160–161]

That is the recompense that God intended for them.

When the divine legislation addresses a wrongdoer who departs from the method of God, it is as if it says to him: what is the purpose of your departure from the method of God? Why do you wrong? Why do you take usury? Why do you bar from the way of God? Why do you consume people's wealth falsely? The wrongdoer does this so that he may enjoy something beyond his right, so the divine legislation comes to frustrate for him the portion of enjoyment, which would have been a right and lawful for him, but the legislation forbids it to him.

An example of this: the killer is deprived of the inheritance of the one he kills. Why? Because the killer hastened what God had delayed for him, and wanted to secure for himself the enjoyment of the inheritance, so he committed the crime of killing. Therefore the legislation comes to deprive him of the inheritance.

It is as if the legislation says to him: "As long as your intention is such, you are deprived of the inheritance." And when the legislation established this, it protected every testator; otherwise every testator would be exposed to his heirs' aggression by killing him so that what he owns would pass to them. So it said: No, we deprive him of the inheritance. Likewise here we find wrongdoing in its various kinds: wrongdoing by denying the truth, barring from the way of God, taking usury, and consuming people's wealth falsely. And since the Jews had imposed upon themselves things that were not theirs, the legislation strips from them things that were truly their right.

The Jews in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished that this matter not be spread about them, so they said: "This food is unlawful for the Children of Israel." Afterwards the Messenger of God (ﷺ) found that this kind of food is lawful in the Torah, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) exposed this matter that disgraced them.

Why does this verse come after His statement of truth in the previous verse: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾? We know that the verse ﴿You will not attain righteousness﴾ came after a verse clarifying the expenditure that is not accepted by God. Let us recall what we said at first about the association of meanings in human faculties: in the human soul there is a faculty that receives, and then another faculty moves. When the Truth says ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾, those who hear this will be moved by different emotions. The one who is sated among people will not turn to this matter with intense attention, and the one who has some food may have his soul move toward other kinds of food. But the one who has no food will turn with intense attention to learn which food is lawful and which is forbidden.

So before God brings the ruling that makes lawful and forbids, a ruling that stirs in the hungry the anguish of need and the anguish of remembering food whose saliva flows for him, indeed the Truth, before it stirs the destitute over what he does not have, stirs the giver over what he has. Therefore, before the Lord, Glorified, mentions food, and before the matter is turned upon the human soul that finds no food, the Messenger had already uttered, before it, what God had sent down to him: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾. Thus, by the association of meanings in the human soul, He, Glorified, has moved the faculty of plenty and possession before moving the faculty of want. And thus is the balance that God willed in His created universe.

He is a Lord who governs His dominion, so He forgets nothing and mentions nothing [by chance]. ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾. Everything is in His knowledge as He has decreed it, and He is the Creator, the Powerful, the All-Knowing; He does not remember some of creation and forget others. He has decreed poverty for a wisdom, and given bounty for a wisdom.

He has made the poor a lesson, yet He has not abandoned him, so that every person may see that the capacity to earn is only a passing accident. It is possible that the one who is able now becomes unable within minutes or hours, and it is possible that the strong becomes weak. When the strong or the capable knows this, he moves to give to others, so as to secure for himself the divine protection should he become weak, and so the strong give to him. Thus when God commands the strong to give and to spend, they must respond, because each of them, if he becomes weak, will take.

So the saying of the Truth, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ served a matter that preceded it, namely that not even the filling of the earth with gold would be accepted from one of them, even if he ransomed himself with it, so long as he is a disbeliever. That expenditure is rejected and has no worth; it is wasted. Then He comes after that to specify the expenditure that is not wasted, and then He exposes the Jews with a matter that exists among them in the Torah but which they denied, a matter concerning food. And since the matter concerns food, there are many faculties that can be moved, for the faculties of the one who has are moved in a manner different from the manner in which the faculties of the destitute are moved. Before stirring the destitute man's feeling that he is destitute, lest he receive that with anguish, He, Glorified, has laid up a store for this destitute man, and softens the heart of the one who has first: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love, and whatever you spend, God is knowing of it﴾. After that comes His statement, Glorified:

﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel had made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93]

The meaning of the word "hill" (ḥill) is "lawful" (ḥalal), and its opposite is "forbidden" (ḥaram). Ḥill is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and since it is a maṣdar we do not say "these two are lawful" (ḥalālān) but rather we say "these are ḥill," and we say "these (feminine) are ḥill." If you wish, read His statement, the Exalted:

﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them; God knows best their faith. If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful (ḥill) for them, nor are they lawful for them (yaḥillūna lahunna).﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 10]

"Lā hunna" here refers to the group of women, and ḥill is singular in form. When the Truth, Glorified, says: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel had made unlawful for himself﴾, this means that he had made some of the food unlawful for himself, so he is free to take or leave it; or that he made it unlawful for himself and God agreed with him, because the one who vows, when he vows something that God did not impose on him, has bound himself by the vow before God.

The time when Israel made some foods unlawful for himself was ﴿before the Torah was revealed﴾, meaning that this prohibition was not decreed by God. Then comes the command to His noble Messenger to address the Children of Israel: ﴿Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."﴾ He has exposed their concealment; they knew that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) knew that the text that confirms his truthfulness is present in the Torah. For this reason the Jews did not bring the Torah, because they knew that in it there is an explicit text confirming what the Messenger of God brought, one that admits no obstinacy or disputation. And since they did not bring the Torah, this means that they are not truthful.

The Truth (Allah) says: ﴿Then whoever fabricates a lie against Allah...﴾

Indeed, in this statement there is a clear warning that no one should invent anything about Allah that neither a messenger nor a scripture has brought down. Whoever fabricates lies against Allah wrongs no one but himself.

Almighty God then says: "Say: God has spoken the truth; so follow the religion (millah) of Abraham, a man of pure faith (hanif). He was not of the idolaters" (Q. 3:95).

God commands His Messenger, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, to say: "Say: God has spoken the truth; so follow the religion (millah) of Abraham, a man of pure faith (hanif)."

We know that the religion (millah) of Abraham is that which named all believers in God "Muslims." The call to adhere to the religion of Abraham serves to make clear that the essence of faith admits of no disagreement. The mount of faith, the Messengers and the Prophets are one caravan. The word "follow" (ittaba'u) implies that there is a leader and there is a follower. The "millah" (religion, community of belief) encompasses the general beliefs and legislation, just as the "shari'ah" (sacred law) encompasses the rulings, while "din" (religion) is used to denote the articles of belief.

We have already learned that the word "hanif" means one who walks on a straight line and follows a upright and balanced method. We call our religion "the tolerant, pure hanifiyyah." Yet "hanaf" in the legs means an inclination in the shins, the right one curving to the right and the left one curving to the left. How, then, do we say of the true religion, which guides to God's method and law, that it is hanif?

We have said that heaven does not intervene by sending Messengers except when corruption has become widespread. As long as corruption has spread, the one who inclines away from corruption, deviating from it, is the one who has been guided to the straight path. So "hanif" means one who turns away from corruption; one who turns away from the crooked is upright. "...So follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith (hanif), and he was not of the idolaters."

"God has spoken the truth" — yes, because truth is that the statement corresponds to what actually occurs. When the Real, who is All-Knowing from eternity, speaks, what happens? It must be that what occurs in reality conforms to what He, glorified and exalted, says. It is not reasonable that God would speak words that come upon the tongue of a Messenger, or upon the tongue of the Messenger's followers, and afterwards life's reality would come and nullify and contradict the word of the Real. The Real, All-Knowing from eternity, sends down words that serve the call to His method.

Thus, when God issues a matter of faith, He, glorified be He, is All-Knowing from eternity that it will happen in accordance with what He said, provided the circumstance in which it is stated does not encourage its acceptance and understanding. The believers were at the outset persecuted and oppressed, and if one of them had no clan to protect him, he would emigrate from the land; and if he could not emigrate, he would be tortured and persecuted. In this severe and harsh period, at the height of the persecution of the believers, the true word descended:

"The host will be routed and they will turn their backs" (Q. 54:45).

When Sayyidina Umar, may God be pleased with him, heard this word he asked: "What host is this? Reality does not support this." Then Badr came, and the believers routed the host and turned the enemy's backs, and this is evidence that God had issued a matter and guaranteed that it would happen as He said and as He informed, and this is absolute truth. A person could doubt truthfulness if the one who spoke were other than the one who created; but the one who said it is the one who creates, creates anew and knows. From where, then, would contradiction come? This is the meaning of the noble verse:

"Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy" (Q. 4:82).

It is a true word that came from the All-Knowing from eternity. Strangely, the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, cling to Sayyidina Abraham: some of them said Abraham, peace be upon him, was a Jew, and some said Abraham was a Christian. They should have understood that Judaism and Christianity came only after Abraham. How could he be a Jew or a Christian when these religions came after him? Therefore the noble Qur'an says:

"People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not sent down until after him? Will you not reason?" (Q. 3:65).

Then the Real explained the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him:

"Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a man of pure faith, a Muslim, and he was not of the idolaters" (Q. 3:67).

How could they fabricate against Abraham that he was a Jew or a Christian? It is a statement that comes only from little discernment and extreme heedlessness. When the Real says of Abraham, "and he was not of the idolaters," are the People of the Book idolaters? Yes, because when they believe in the sonship of Uzair and believe in the prophethood of Jesus in a way that amounts to associating partners with God, this is shirk. Likewise, the Arab idol-worshippers used to say that they were upon the religion of Abraham, because the rites of the pilgrimage were brought by Abraham, peace be upon him. For this reason the Real, glorified be He, declares Sayyidina Abraham free of that, and says: "Say: God has spoken the truth; so follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the idolaters." This shows that the religion of Abraham and what he brought agree with the religion of Muhammad, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, and what he brought, and that it is a response to the call of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 96:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾

We have already known how the association of meanings was the cause of the Truth's satisfying all the faculties of humanity. Before this verse, which speaks of the building of the Sacred House in Makkah the Honoured, there was a discussion of our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when the Truth said:

﴿Say: "God has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Ibrahim, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 95]

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is the first of the prophets connected to the Sacred House, and the raising of the foundations of the Sacred House was at his hands, after it had been buried and covered by the flood in the time of Nuh (peace be upon him). So when the discussion concerns the mission of our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the greatest event in the history of our master Ibrahim must come, and that is the event of the building of the Sacred House. Likewise, when the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of the disputation between the Muslims, headed by the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), with the Qur'an in his hand, and the People of the Book, who held the distorted Torah and the distorted Gospel, He, glory be to Him, wished to return us to one thing, namely the religion of Ibrahim, who named us "Muslims". This means that God wants the values of heaven to govern the movement of the people of the earth, because if the movement of the people of the earth follows desires, the movements collide, and once the movements have collided, what results from them is the loss of human effort, and this effort becomes squandered.

But the person who carries the values that are rooted as belief in his heart, after examining them with his reason, this person has a form (qalib) through which the legislation of God is carried out. Were it not for the existence of this form, a person could not implement God's legislation, could not perform these legislative duties, and could not obey God with his limbs. A person without a form cannot perform the required movement.

Thus the human form, the body, in legislation requires another process, which is that the form is set up and has an action when it turns towards one House of God. Thereby the form also acquires a share in worship.

For this reason, there must also be a direction (mutajah) for the form, and this direction governs the form itself. So the believing Muslim is governed in heart and in form. When we come to prayer, to be in the presence of God, we take care that our form is turned toward the place which God has commanded us to face. Why?

Because the Truth, glory be to Him, when He bestows His mercy, blessing, descents and illuminations, wants the body to be in a state qualified to receive these manifestations. For this reason there had to be a House of God toward which everyone turns, so as to give religiosity unity. Just as the Truth gave the procession of the messages unity, He also gives unity in the human form and the direction. Every place where God is worshipped, in relation to Islam, is considered a mosque. God has made the matter easy for the community of our master Muhammad, and he (peace be upon him) said:

"The earth has been made for me a mosque and a means of purification."

In previous religions, meeting God and worshipping Him required a specific place, but He has extended His mercy to the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him).

The dust of the earth is a means of purification. When we lack purifying water, the dust, which at first glance may seem a cause of uncleanliness, has been made by God a means of purification for us.

A person may perform tayammum and purify himself with dust, as if God wished that each individual of the community of Muhammad's meeting with Him be made very easy. Every place where we worship God and the Muslim prostrates to God becomes a mosque.

However, there is a difference between any place where we worship God and the mosque. We see the worker worship God in the factory, the pupil worship God in the classroom, and the farmer worship God and perform the obligatory prayers in the field. A passer-by in the street may perform his prayer anywhere and then pursue his work, but when a person sets aside a place to be a House of God, it is forbidden to engage in any other activity of life there; it is a restricted space (mukhayyaz).

All worship is accepted, but there is a difference between a place where you work and a place you designate to become a mosque. The mosque is a place in which nothing is practised except meeting God. Therefore the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) wished that we not exploit this space for any matter concerning our worldly life. He (may God bless him and grant him peace) clarified for us that whoever concludes a transaction in the mosque, God does not bless it, and whoever seeks a lost item there will not find it. The Messenger prayed that God not return his lost item to him.

The affairs of this world are content to take from a person twenty-three hours every day. So let the believing person set aside one hour for God alone, and let him take off all the concerns of worldly life as one takes off sandals at the door of the mosque. It is not good manners or propriety for a person to be occupied with anything other than meeting God at the time set for meeting God and in the place set for this meeting.

So when you enter the mosque, you should restrain yourself from anyone speaking to you with idle and frivolous talk, and intend i'tikaf (retreat) so that you benefit from your presence in the mosque. And when we set aside a certain space to be a mosque, how is the direction inside the mosque determined? Should the matter be left to each individual to choose his own direction?

No. The believer is committed to facing one single place. This single place is a House of God by God's choosing, whereas the other mosques are Houses of God by the choosing of God's creatures. So the direction of all the Houses of God by the choosing of God's creatures is the Sacred House of God.

When you look at it this way, you will find the world facing one another, because every worshipper's direction will be towards the House of God together with the rest of the worshippers of God. So all believers gather around the House of God and face one another. Our faces all face one another. But what is the necessity of facing the Ka'bah? The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿To God belong the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 115]

We say: this verse confirms what we are saying. Since to God belong the east and the west, this is the general meaning. People, when they first came to know the cosmos, became acquainted with east and west, then north and south as well. After knowledge reached the determination of the secondary directions alongside the four principal well-known directions, we came to know "north-east", "north-west", "south-east" and "south-west". So all directions belong to God, and facing the Ka'bah realises this noble saying.

When a person turns towards the Ka'bah, the east may be behind him and the west in front of him; another person turns towards the Ka'bah and his face meets the face of the one facing the Ka'bah; a third turns towards the Ka'bah and, in another corner, is looking at it. Thus humankind gathers from the east, the west, the north, the south and all the secondary directions around the Ka'bah.

So the saying of the Truth, ﴿To God belong the east and the west﴾, means that all creation faces the Ka'bah, and thereby no direction is more proper to God than another. I do not want to enter into the maze of whether the Ka'bah is the centre of the earth and that the earth was created from it, because if a thing is spherical, any point in it can be the centre for all; so let us leave such talk. But is it not enough to prefer it that God has chosen it? That suffices and more, and with that the matter ends: it is so, because it is the House of God by God's choosing, and that is enough.

The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) taught us that matters which reason stops at and which are not part of the core of belief or religion should not be made subjects of disagreement or dispute. Our master Ali (may God ennoble his face) reports concerning the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace): a man asked, "Is that the first House of God?" The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) clarified that before it there were houses, but it is the first House established for mankind. This is a clarification that God made the Ka'bah His first House in which the human species worships, according to the saying of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾ But if there were earlier species before the human species, it is certain that there were Houses of God which we do not know. Adam, in the logic of reason, is one, but on analogy there are Adams.

Therefore the existence of the Sacred House as a House of God does not clash with the logic of people who possess only a shallow religious culture. When one of them hears that fossils have been discovered from so many million years ago, he asks: "How, when millions of years have not passed over Adam?" Let us suppose there were five generations for Idris (peace be upon him), three generations for Nuh (peace be upon him), eleven generations for Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and thirty generations for Muhammad (peace be upon him); thus human existence is measured in thousands of years, not millions.

To this person we say: Did anyone tell you that Adam was the first to inhabit the earth? Religion did not say that. Religion said that Adam is the first of this human species, but he is not the first to have dwelt on the earth. So let the scholars say that the age of this earth is millions of years. Let us all listen to the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿Have you not seen that God created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation.﴾ [Ibrahim: 19]

So there is no room for this inquiry. Therefore the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No, rather there were houses before it."

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, also says something that clarifies that the jinn inhabited the earth before us:

﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of scorching wind.﴾ [Al-Hijr: 27]

Did not the Truth, glory be to Him, say that the human being is a khalifah (successor), and the angels responded:

﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we confess Your praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 30]

Those who said that are not of mankind. So the word of God confirms that the Ka'bah is the first House established for mankind, that is, for the human species. Therefore there is no need to speak about matters at which reason stops, lest we enter a maze. Had God wished to teach us that the Ka'bah is the first house on earth, He would have said to us, "Indeed, the first house established on earth," and would not have specified the species for whom the house was established. But the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah, blessed﴾, and therefore the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) clarified that before it there were houses, but it is the first house established for mankind. It is an answer that accommodates whatever science may bring.

And when we look at the saying of the Truth: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah, blessed﴾, what is the meaning of "first"? It is the beginning. Does every beginning have an end? No. There are things that have a "first" but no "last", and an example of this is the number "one", for what follows the number one has no last. The "last" after the number one is what a person may count as an incapacity in the estimates of the decillion, but beyond the decillion there are other numbers. Formerly a person would stop at the thousand and then say of the million "a thousand thousands". Likewise Paradise has a beginning and no end.

Thus the first house God established for mankind is the Ka'bah. When we see the word "established" (wudi'a), we find it is a verb, and we see that it was established for mankind. Since this House was established for mankind, it is necessary that whenever the word "mankind" comes, there be a "house", and Adam is among mankind, the father of all mankind, and a house was established for him.

And when it is said that the House was built before Adam, we say:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿In it are clear signs: the standing-place of Abraham; and whoever enters it is safe...﴾

We find that the plural form is present in His words ﴿In it are signs﴾ and ﴿clear﴾, which is a description of the plural. Then Allah says ﴿the standing-place of Abraham﴾. He, glory be to Him, mentions after the signs only the standing-place of Abraham, and the standing-place is one sign. This indicates that in the standing-place of Abraham are the clear signs. We read ﴿maqāmu Ibrāhīm﴾ with a fatḥah on the first mīm in the word "maqām," and we do not pronounce it "muqām" with a ḍammah on the first mīm, because muqām with a ḍammah means the place of Abraham's residence, whereas maqām with a fatḥah means the place of standing. Why was Abraham, peace be upon him, standing?

Abraham was standing to raise the foundations of the Sacred House, and Abraham was standing upon a "stone." When we look at the standing-place of Abraham, you find in it all the clear signs; because Allah asked Abraham, peace be upon him, to raise the foundations of the House, and it would have been enough for him, when raising the foundations of the House, to give it the height that the length of his arms achieves. Thus Abraham, peace be upon him, would have fulfilled what Allah required — as we said before — but Abraham, peace be upon him, had become accustomed with Allah to perform all of Allah's obligations with passion, love, completion and perfection. So Abraham said to himself: "Why do I not raise the House more than what my arms can reach?" In that ancient time there was no notion of "scaffolding," and with Abraham, peace be upon him, there was none but his son Ishmael. Abraham, peace be upon him, brought a stone and stood upon it, so that he could raise the foundations by the height of the stone.

Thus Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, wanted to carry out Allah's command to raise the foundations not merely by the measure of bodily stretching, but by the measure of devising a way to raise the foundations above what Allah had required. This is the meaning of Allah's words about Abraham, peace be upon him:

﴿And when his Lord tested Abraham with words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed I will make you a leader for the people. He said: And of my descendants? He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]

That is, he fulfilled Allah's requirement in complete fulfilment, and there is no stronger proof of this complete fulfilment than that he brought a stone to stand upon, to increase the height of the House by the height of this stone. We know that the one who helped him and shared with him in raising the foundations was his son Ishmael. And whoever Allah has honoured with seeing the standing-place of Abraham finds that the stone is wide enough for one person to stand upon; thus we understand that Ishmael was assisting and handing his father the stones. As for the places of the feet present in this stone, this means that when Abraham stood and carried a stone that ought to be carried by two people, this required the two feet to be firmly fixed in a secure place so that he would not fall.

Now, does Allah, glory be to Him, when He saw Abraham devise this stratagem, say to His friend: "I will spare you the burden of that"? And Allah made the feet sink into the stone, sinking in a way that supports them so that they do not fall.

As for one whose mind cannot encompass that Allah softened the stone for Abraham, we say to him: Abraham devised a means, and feared that his foot might slip, so he carved a place in the stone to the measure of his foot so that his foot would be firm when he lifted and carried the stone; and these are clear signs. Take what your mind and understanding can contain. Indeed Allah helped Abraham because he thought to build the foundations and raise them more than his arms could reach, and Allah enabled him in that and aided him in it. We know that guidance is of two kinds: the guidance of indication and the guidance of assistance.

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety.﴾ [Muhammad: 17]

﴿In it are clear signs: the standing-place of Abraham; and whoever enters it is safe﴾. Signs are wondrous matters, and when you see them you cannot deny them. Entering the House means safety for the person who enters it, and we know that the House was built in this place. This place is where the tribes gather, and between some of these tribes there are vendettas, blood and wars; therefore Allah makes clear the condition by which blood is protected: ﴿and whoever enters it is safe﴾. Why? Because it is the House of the Lord, and it is not proper for someone who enters the House of the Lord to be punished, even if he has committed a crime that obliges Allah's prescribed penalty in it. For this reason, our master ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If I found in it the killer of al-Khaṭṭāb — his father — I would not touch him."

But the noose is tightened on the criminal until he leaves. This safety is specified with respect to whatever offence he committed in his worldly life; as for whoever enters it being safe on the Day of Resurrection, the judgement concerning that is something else. It is a high degree of Allah's bounty. The clear signs in the Sacred House are seen by whoever visits the Sacred House, and so that Allah fulfils the hope of everyone who desires to visit the Sacred House, and to repeat the visit for whoever has gone and wishes to return to visit again. When you enter the Sacred House, you turn toward a place in the House, and the one opposite you on the earth turns toward the opposite place, until the directions come to include the whole Kaʿbah. When we are in the Kaʿbah, we turn our faces toward the structure because we see it, and we turn faces toward the structure which is definitely part of it. The Ḥaṭīm, which is the curved wall built around the stone of Ishmael, is also part of the Kaʿbah, but the expense fell short, so they made it to mark the place of the Kaʿbah, and it remained so. So if a person is absent from the Kaʿbah and turns toward it, it suffices that he turn toward its direction.

For this reason, we find the rows in prayer around the Kaʿbah take the shape of a circle, because those who pray inside the Ḥaram see it; but those who pray outside it need only face its direction, even if the row extends to a thousand metres. Therefore the rows for worshippers outside the Ḥaram are straight, whereas inside the Ḥaram the rows take the shape of a circle, because the greatest dimension of the Kaʿbah is twelve and a quarter metres. We find, among the wondrous signs, that when you look at the Black Stone you find people crowding to kiss it, and the stone represents the lowest of the kinds of existence. We all know that man is vicegerent as master in the universe, and after him the animal is lower in intellect and subjugated; after the animal comes the kind of plants, and after that comes the kind of inanimate matter, of which the stone is part.

We see this man, master of the universe, whose worship Allah does not accept in its complete and goodly acceptance unless he kisses the stone or greets it. Thus the Truth transfers the highest kinds to the lowest. People crowd around the stone, and whoever does not kiss it feels that he has missed something great. Thus you see a passage and conduct from creation to the door of Allah. The arrogant human who imagines he is master over others is given a rite of worship to kiss the Black Stone or greet it with peace; and this person, although the Truth — glory be to Him — accepts from him that he greet the Black Stone with peace and did not oblige him to kiss it, nevertheless tries to kiss the stone, which is the lowest of kinds, because Allah has exalted it; and this is the first breaking of the nose of human pride. And lest anyone suppose that it is stone-worship or idolatry, a command comes from the Truth to stone another stone.

So stone-worship has no basis here: we find a stone that is sanctified, and another stone that is stoned. We find a stone that a person kisses and venerates, and another stone that he scorns and despises. This shows our submission to the will of the Commander, glory be to Him alone. When He commands us to venerate a stone, the believer fulfils the due of veneration by hearing and obeying; and when He commands us to stone another stone, the believer stones that stone also by hearing and obeying Allah. Thus the essence of the stone has no bearing whatsoever. Some of those with evil suspicion have said: "Islam has retained some idolatry."

To these we say: Why do you mention the veneration of the Black Stone, but do not mention the stoning of Iblis, which is three stones? The believer performing the rite venerated one stone and stoned three stones. The believer obeys only the command of Allah; there is no intrinsic quality of the stone in the rite or the worship. Truth has raised us from the abyss of idol-worship, which is the very essence of disbelief, but He said to us: "Kiss the Black Stone," and we kissed the stone out of respect for the command of the Commander; and that is the utmost of certainty. The Truth has transferred us from one equal to another equal, from worship of a stone to veneration and sanctification of a similar stone; but idols were the utmost of polytheism, and kissing the Black Stone is the utmost of certainty. Are these not clear signs?

And Zamzam, which is in the bosom of the Kaʿbah — are these not clear signs? Hagar left the Kaʿbah and went to al-Ṣafā and climbed to al-Marwah, after placing Ishmael beside the Kaʿbah, and she searched about for water. Hagar walked seven rounds, perhaps she would see a bird or find a person who knew the way to water, because her son needed to drink. Had she found water on al-Ṣafā or al-Marwah at the beginning of her effort, would she have found confirmation of her words to Abraham when he brought her to settle in this place: "Indeed Allah will not abandon us"? She made the effort.

It is as if Allah says to her and to every person: Be diligent in effort, but I will not give you from the effort; rather I give you the water beneath the foot of Ishmael. Thus she spoke truly in her words: "Allah will not abandon us." The Truth made her walk seven rounds, and a woman of her age could not manage more than that; and this teaches us that a person must engage the causes, but the heart must be attached to the Causer of causes, who is Allah, glory be to Him; and in this is what rectifies the conduct of all people. When a person sees that the well is at the place of Ishmael's foot, with al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah at a distance, and he walks between them, and afterwards finds Zamzam at the place of the strike of Ishmael's foot — is there not in this clear signs guiding a person to engage the causes and take them, and the heart to be attached to the Causer of causes?

This gives the believer the faith of reliance (tawakkul), which differs from laziness and "the dullness of dependence." The faith of tawakkul is that the limbs work and the hearts rely; but laziness in taking the causes while claiming reliance is dullness. Such a lazy, dependent person, when food is placed before him, eats greedily and voraciously; had he been sincere, he would let the morsel leap into his mouth. Why then does he chew it? Why does he choose dependence, idleness and non-action, and then stretch out his hand to eat? These are the "characteristics of dependence."

We take from Hagar's effort and the gushing of the water a lesson: taking the causes of Allah. Then we find every person in the Sacred House preoccupied with himself and his Lord, and from the excess of his preoccupation he is heedless of whoever is with him; even if he were the dearest person to him, he would not notice him. When you enter and look at the Kaʿbah, every thought about anything at all is shaken out of your mind; you do not remember your children or your wealth. But after you finish the rites, you return to thinking about your children and your work; for otherwise, if your love, longing, attachment and spiritual ecstasies remained in this spot, the place would be too narrow for all people. After that the Truth — glory be to Him — says about the Sacred House: ﴿and whoever enters it is safe﴾. Here we must understand that there is a difference between an "informative statement" being a record of an actual event, and an "informative statement" being a statement of a legal obligation. Had ﴿and whoever enters it is safe﴾ been a record of an actual event, that would have been refuted by many things, for people have entered it and were not safe.

We know the recent assault that Juhayman attempted some years ago. People said: when Juhayman attacked the people, the pilgrims of the House of the Merciful could not be secure in the House, and some asked: how then did the Truth say ﴿and whoever enters it is safe﴾? Indeed some people of deviance said: then the matter of Juhayman's entry into the Sacred House makes ﴿and whoever enters it is safe﴾ not truthful! To these we say:

There is a difference between the Truth informing of a reality that has occurred, and informing of an obligation.

The informing of reality would mean that no one enters the Sacred House and

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 98:

After that, the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah...﴾

When you hear "Say" (qul), it is a command from Allah to His Messenger, as we said before. If you assign a person to say a sentence to someone you send him to, does that person come with the command "Say," or does he convey the sentence? He conveys the sentence. An example: when you tell your son, for instance, "Say to your uncle: My father will come to you tomorrow," your son goes to his uncle saying, "My father will come to you tomorrow."

Someone may say: Would it not have been sufficient for Allah to tell the Messenger, "Say, O Muhammad," and then the Messenger of Allah would convey to us, "O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve?" That would have been sufficient. But the Messenger is conveying the same command from Allah; it is as if he said what he received from Allah, and what the Messenger received from Allah is: ﴿Say: O People of the Book﴾. This shows that the Messenger conveys literally what he heard from Allah. There are many verses in the Qur'an that begin with the saying of the Truthful One: ﴿O People of the Book﴾, and in which the words "Say" from the Truthful One do not occur. And there are verses that come preceded by "Say." What is the difference between the two?

We find that the Truthful One at times shows gentleness toward His creation, making them worthy of His address, so He says: ﴿O People of the Book﴾. This is an address from Allah to them directly. At other times He tells His Messenger: "Say to them, O Muhammad," because they have not risen to the level of being addressed by Allah directly. So when we find an address from the Truthful One to the creation, sometimes preceded by "Say" and sometimes not, know that the Truthful One, when He addresses His creatures whom He created, is gentle with them at times, making them worthy of being addressed by Him, and at other times, when He finds obstinacy from them, He conveys to His Messenger, ﷺ: "Say to them."

The example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, in our own lives: we find one of us saying to the person beside him: "Tell the loud-voiced one to be quiet." This speaker has risen above addressing this loud person directly, so he asks the one sitting next to him to order the loud-voiced one to be silent. When the address comes to the People of the Book, we know that they are the Jews, possessors of the Torah, and the Christians, possessors of the Gospel, and these are the ones of whom the Truthful One says: ﴿O People of the Book﴾.

No one has said to us, "O people of the Qur'an." Why? Because when the Truthful One says to them: ﴿O People of the Book﴾, we know that "Book" (kitab) applies to everything written, and their disbelief contradicts what Allah knew to be present in the Book that was revealed to them; for it is He who sent down the Book, and He knows that what is in the Book calls to faith and does not call to disbelief. Since He is the Truth who sent down the Book, and He is the Witness, it becomes folly on the part of the People of the Book to throw themselves into the trap of disbelief, for by that they lie against Allah; and Allah - glorified is He - records against them that they have contradicted what is written and sent down to them in their Book.

They - the People of the Book - if they are able to mislead the people of the earth, they will not be able to do so with regard to the Creator of earth and heavens.

And when the Truthful One says: ﴿Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, do we understand from this that their disbelief in the signs of Allah is their concealing the signs of Allah at the outset, or that they believed in them and then disbelieved in them? Let us see what happened from them. The glad tidings of him, ﷺ, were written in the Torah and written in the Gospel, and they had believed in them before the Master of us, the Messenger of Allah, came. Then when the Messenger of Allah actually came, they disbelieved in them. Concerning this the wise saying came:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89]

Why did they disbelieve in him, ﷺ? Because he removed from them temporal authority, so that they no longer had the temporal authority through which they used to sell Paradise, sell the good pleasure of Allah, and do what achieves their interests without regard for the commands of Allah. I have said before that Quraysh refrained from saying "There is no god but Allah," and this refraining is evidence that they understood the meaning of "There is no god but Allah." Had it been merely a word to be spoken, they would have said it. But they knew and understood that there is no one worshipped, no one obeyed, no one legislating, and no one obligating except Allah.

Indeed, the Truth says to the People of the Book: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked..."﴾

Suppose you have perished within yourselves and bear the burden of your own misguidance. Then why do you also bear the burden of misguiding the people? It would have been enough for you to bear the burden of your own misguidance, not to bear also the burden of your misguiding others.

Indeed, the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.﴾ [An-Nahl: 25]

He, glory be to Him, said this although He had also said:

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.﴾ [Fatir: 18]

The one who does not bear another's burden along with his own is the one who went astray and did not lead others astray; he bears only his own sin. But the one who bears the burden of his own self and the burden of others is the one who went astray and led others astray. Here the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addresses them through His Messenger: ﴿Why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe?﴾

It is as if He is saying to them: what do you want from the religion that binds the servant to his Lord? You do not want it to be an upright religion; you want it to be a crooked religion. And that which is crooked from uprightness is crooked only for a purpose, because the crooked path lengthens the distance. The one who walks on a straight path, what calls him to deviate from the straight path to lengthen his own way? If he wants the goal directly, he prefers the straight path. As for the one who deviates from the straight path, he does not attain the sought-after goal; rather, he lengthens the distance for himself, and he may never reach the goal.

The Truth says: ﴿Why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ When you hear "ʿiwajan" (crooked), you may hear it sometimes as "ʿawaj" with a fatha on the ʿayn, and sometimes as "ʿiwaj" with a kasra on the ʿayn. When we hear "ʿawaj" with a fatha on the ʿayn, it refers to something that has upright standing, like a wall or a spear. But "ʿiwaj" with a kasra on the ʿayn refers to meanings and values. Therefore, the Truth says to them, concerning their deviation in meanings and values: ﴿seeking to make it crooked while you are witnesses.﴾

The Truth informs them: you seek to make the religion crooked despite the fact that you are witnesses that what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought is the truth. He came conveying with truthfulness, and you used to give glad tidings of the message of Muhammad, and you used to seek victory over the polytheists of Makkah, saying: "A prophet will come whom we will follow, and then we will kill you with him, the killing of ʿAd and Iram." And you, O People of the Book, are witnesses to the truthfulness of this Messenger.

They committed a series of sins: they went astray and strove to lead others astray. Would that this were done out of ignorance, but it was a matter done deliberately and with knowledge. The matter reached such a point with them that they became witnesses to the truth, and despite that they persisted in misguidance and misleading. The meaning of "witnesses" is that they knew what they were saying and saw it with their own eyes; witnessing is seeing something that you observe, not something you have merely heard. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, reminds them with His words: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

The message brought by Muhammad, as a conveyor, is clear, and this is mentioned in your heavenly books. So what makes you, O People of the Book, not adhere to the path of truth while you are witnesses? There must be some doubt that has touched you, that Allah is unaware of that. So He tells them, No: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 100:

After that comes the saying of the Truthful, glory be to Him: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelievers.﴾

The meaning of this is that Allah alerts the believing group that those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will not be at ease for as long as you, O believers, are on the right path and as long as you remain upright. The disbelievers in the signs of Allah will have no peace of mind except by casting doubt upon the believers in their religion, seeking to make it crooked, and declaring them disbelievers after their Islam.

This is a matter to which those who believe must pay attention, because those who seek to make the affair crooked have gone astray and led others astray. They themselves bear witness to this, and they know that Allah is not unaware of what they do. So what should be the stance of the believing group? The Truthful, glory be to Him, clarifies it with His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾.

The People of the Scripture try to turn the believers away from the way of Allah. By "turning away" is not meant that there are those who prevent the believers from believing; no. Rather, it is an attempt by the People of the Scripture to persuade the believers to return and to apostatize from the faith they have embraced. The believers are the group that adheres to the obligations from Allah, and therefore the Truthful, glory be to Him, warns them with His saying:

﴿If you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelievers.﴾ The Truth specifies a portion of those who were given the Scripture, and this is history recorded with integrity, truthfulness, and right, without bias. As if the Truthful, glory be to Him, is informing us that there is a faction of the People of the Scripture who will take the straight path and will come to the Muslims in groups, companies, and individuals, with Islam; so the Truth does not speak of all those who were given the Scripture. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾. Indeed the Truth records history while protecting the reality,

And after that He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿How can you disbelieve while the Signs of God are recited to you and His Messenger is among you?﴾

This is a matter of great astonishment and wonder: that disbelief should come back upon the believers, when they are in the bliss of knowing God. The Signs of God are recited to them, and the Messenger of God is true and with them and among them.

The True One, glory be to Him, then says to the believers: ﴿If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture...﴾. There is a story behind this. The Jews in Medina controlled the economic power, because they were skilled in dealing in wealth, and anyone who wanted money went to them to borrow at usury (ribā). The Jews also had scholarly superiority and distinction, because they studied the Book, while most of the people of Mecca and Medina were unlettered (ummiyyūn, those who could not read a heavenly Book). There was also another distinction for the Jews, which was their experience in war, for they had fortresses and strongholds. Thus the Jews had three sources of distinction:

Wealth, which brought them economic leadership; knowledge of the Book, which was their scholarly superiority; and then their mastery of the arts of war. Over and above this, they tried to create discord among the people and deepen it, such as their attempt to stir up enmity between the Aws and the Khazraj, and their trading in that conflict so that wars would continue. In this way they ensured the market for weapons, which they manufactured and supplied to every side of the warring parties.

When Islam came, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) united the Aws and the Khazraj, and thereby they lost their economic superiority. Islam came with a religion and a Book that was dominant over the earlier scriptures, so the Jews lost their scholarly standing. And they also lost their military standing, for they saw a small number of believers defeat the disbelievers and inflict a crushing defeat upon them at Badr. Thus every authority the Jews had in Medina was lost, so they wanted to restore the situation to what it had been before Islam came. They said: let us ignite and kindle the enmities between the Aws and the Khazraj and stir them up.

A man named Shas ibn Qays, who saw the light of faith shining on the faces of the Aws and the Khazraj, and the harmony of faith encompassing them, and affection and smiles of purity among them, was stirred by this, and said: "By God, we must bring it back fresh and return them to the rancour and enmity they had before. We will have no stability as long as they are united."

So he sent a young Jewish man, who sat among the Aws and the Khazraj. Then he brought the conversation round to a day called the Day of Bu'ath, which was the name of a day of the Arabs before Islam, when there had been fighting between the Aws and the Khazraj, and victory in it had gone to the Aws over the Khazraj. The young Jew sat reciting and bringing forth the poetry that had been composed on that day, and he stirred up the zeal of the Aws and the Khazraj, and the dispute broke out. Boasting took place, and hatred awoke, and they said: "The weapons! The weapons!" Thus the scheme succeeded. The news reached our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so he rose, (ﷺ), with his companions, until they arrived at the gathering of the Aws and the Khazraj, and they found the situation at the highest pitch of agitation: dispute, hatred, and weapons carried. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Are you calling upon the claims of the Jahiliyya (the age of ignorance) while I am among you?!"

That is, you should have been ashamed of yourselves, because the Messenger of God is among you. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) added: "God has honoured you with Islam, and has cut off by it from you the affair of the Jahiliyya, and has joined your hearts together." What effect did the words of the Messenger have on the hearts of the people? His words (ﷺ) moved them to lay down their weapons, and they wept, and some embraced one another, and they departed with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). There had never been a day more shameful at its beginning and better at its end than that day.

When we reflect on what those Jews did to kindle strife between the Aws and the Khazraj, we find that they understood the nature of the old conflict between the Aws and the Khazraj, so they wanted to stir up those old enmities and grudges. We also find that the stirring of feelings between the Aws and the Khazraj opened a door for loss of control, so that fighting nearly broke out. But when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke to them, the agitations subsided, they laid down their weapons, and they regretted what they had done.

If we want to see the matter with deep perception of what happened, we find that the perception of enmity between the Aws and the Khazraj by the Jews is what led the Jews to set in motion this mistaken perception and revive the old vendettas. Then the agitation of the Aws and the Khazraj over those old vendettas opened the way to bearing arms for fighting.

Thus we find that perception of a thing passes through three stages: first, sensation of the thing; second, the soul's being affected by it; third, behavioural inclination. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke, the Aws and the Khazraj perceived the matter in the reverse manner: they laid down their weapons, the agitations of hatred subsided, and they abandoned the mistaken perceptions.

The Prophet (ﷺ) reminded them of three things: "Are you calling upon the claims of the Jahiliyya while I am among you? God has honoured you with Islam, and has cut off by it from you the affair of the Jahiliyya, and has joined your hearts together." They responded to this first by laying down their weapons, second by weeping, and third, which is a matter moved by the agitations within them, by embracing one another, that is, correcting their perceptions. Thus the inclination occurred in reverse. When this happened, the Jews were struck by rage, frustration and vexation. The chronicler of this story said: "There had never been a day in Islam more evil at its beginning and better at its end than that day."

That day began with frowning and ended with the dawning of tranquillity. After that there came into being the cell that forms immunity in the souls of the believers, after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said that saying: "Are you calling upon the claims of the Jahiliyya while I am among you, after God has honoured you with Islam, and has cut off by it from you the affair of the Jahiliyya, and joined you together?"

This noble saying has become present in the mind at every incitement of Satan or scheme of an enemy. The True One has made immunity against the act of deception and the prodding of Satan among the believers of the Aws and the Khazraj. Thus we see that God makes even the disbeliever serve the exaltation of the rank of faith. Had this matter not occurred, and had the Messenger of God (ﷺ), with his effective speech, not come upon the people while he was among them to say that saying, the believers would not have acquired this immunity from hatred among themselves. And if one of the followers of the Messenger had said such a word, it would have been possible for this effect to occur, but when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said it, it created immunity for other events that might come when the Messenger is no longer present.

Therefore, O believer, if you look at the disbelievers, you will find their minds barren. They spread Islam without intending to, through their foolish stances. For example, when they said: "A prophet will come whom we will follow, and we will kill you along with him, as the people of 'Ad and Iram were killed." What happened?

When the Ansar (the Helpers) heard of the new religion, some of them said to others: "Listen, O people, this is the religion the Jews gave you good news of. Before they get ahead of us to it, come, let us get ahead of the Jews to it."

The haughtiness and boasting of the Jews over the Aws and the Khazraj was a motive for the Aws and the Khazraj to enter Islam. Thus the True One, glory be to Him and exalted, makes the disbelief of the disbeliever effective in strengthening the faith of the believer.

When the True One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿How can you disbelieve while the Signs of God are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds fast to God has already been guided to a straight path﴾, we understand that it is a matter of great astonishment and wonder coming from the Truth. When you hear ﴿How can you disbelieve?﴾, that is a wondrous matter, because it is unlikely that believers would disbelieve while the Book of God is recited to them and the Messenger of God is among them.

Then comes the call to hold fast to God. The meaning of iʿtiṣām (holding fast) is clinging firmly, and it is not possible except from a height, as one says: "I held fast to the rope of faith", because a person has his own weight; if nothing else lifts him, it drags him down. This only arises when a person is suspended in the air and grips a rope, and no one pushes him down, but rather he descends to the earth by his own weight. Whoever holds fast to God and grips the rope of faith prevents himself from falling and plunging.

Here we feel that holding fast to God is to follow what is recited to us of the Signs, and what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) has laid down for us. So the gateway to holding fast is the Book of God and the Sunna of His Messenger. Likewise the presence of the Messenger among them was a necessity, because they were immersed in the mire of the Jahiliyya, so the radiance of the Messenger had to be among them to shine on them, so that they would see that God had brought them out from darkness into light. And the True One did not take His Messenger until He had perfected the religion for us, completed His favour upon us, and approved Islam as a religion for us. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I have left among you two things, you will never go astray after them: the Book of God and my Sunna."

Thus we see that the presence of the Signs of God and the Sunna of the Messenger of God is the safeguard that guides to the straight path. Guidance, as we know, is that which leads to the desired goal. Suppose your goal is to go to a certain place: what brings you to that place is guidance, and everything that shows a person the means to reach the goal is called guidance.

The True One, glory be to Him and exalted, created all creation, and made some of creation subjugated and some of creation free to choose.

The subjugated part of God's creation is all created beings in the universe except humans, and even humans are subjugated in some of their affairs. That is why we said: everything other than humans in God's creation performs its task as it was required.
