Nevertheless he asked the Messenger of Allah to go to the battle, and said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, my sons want to keep me from this direction and from going out with you in it. By Allah, I hope to set my lame foot in Paradise with this limp of mine."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "As for you, Allah has excused you, so there is no jihad obligation on you." And he said to his sons: "What harm is there in your not preventing him? Perhaps Allah will grant him martyrdom." So he went out with him and was killed.

Another believer said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, my son who was martyred at Badr, I saw him in a dream saying to me: 'O father, come to us.' I hope that you will permit me to fight at Uhud, for indeed he..." fa-an lahu fa-qatil fa-q

Quran 3:123 — "And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak..."

He transferred them from a battle in which there was something like defeat or lack of victory to victory. It is as if He wants to say: the matter, as far as you are concerned, is the matter of your God, who watches over you, helps you, supplies you and cares for you. Beware lest you rely on numbers and equipment; rather, rely on the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and on what the Truth wills as guidance for you, because Allah's support comes only to one who is receptive to Allah's support, and support does not come to one who is not receptive to Allah's support.

We know that there is a difference between the agent (al-fa'il) and the receiver (al-qabil), for the agent is one thing, while the one receptive to the effect of the action is another thing. To make this clear, we give an example: the agent may be one, but the effect differs. To bring the matter closer, we say: you pick up a cup of tea to drink from it, find it hot, and blow on it so that it cools; and in winter you wake up to find your hand cold, so you blow on it to warm it. You blow once to cool the cup of tea and once to warm your hand. So the agent is one, namely the one who blows, but the receiver of the effect is something else. There is an agent and there is a receiver. Another example: the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and had it been sent down upon the mountains, they would have crumbled in humility; yet some people hear it, and Allah does not veil them, but rather exposes them to us and disgraces them by the greatness of His divinity:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and they follow their desires.﴾ [Muhammad: 16]

They were not affected by the Qur'an, and their saying "What did he just say?" means mockery of what was said. And we find the Truth responding to that with His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and they follow their desires.﴾ [Muhammad: 16]

The agent is one, while the receiver differs. The Truth continues His wise message in His saying: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak, so fear Allah that you may be grateful.﴾

Thus, Allah's support for you comes only to a receptive faithful state; if the receptive one (al-mustaqbil, with the ba' kasra) does not exist, then the support does not exist. If you cannot receive what the heavens send of support, we say to you: repair your receiving apparatus, for the receiver is like a faulty radio. The broadcast from the stations is continuous, but it is only the faulty radio that does not receive. So if you want to receive from Allah, your receiving apparatus must be sound. Thus Allah's support for you comes only to a receptive faithful state; if the receptive one (al-mustaqbil, with the ba' kasra) does not exist, then the support does not exist. If you cannot receive what the heavens send of support, we say to you: repair your receiving apparatus, for the receiver is like a faulty radio. The broadcast from the stations is continuous, but it is only the faulty radio that does not receive. So if you want to receive from Allah, your receiving apparatus must be sound.

Therefore, God's support for you comes only to a receptive believing recipient. If the receiver (with a kasra on the ba') does not exist, then the support does not exist. So if you cannot receive what the heavens send down of support, we say to you: repair your receiving apparatus, for the receiving apparatus is like a faulty radio. The transmission from the broadcasting stations is continuous, but it is the faulty radio that does not receive. Therefore, if you want to receive from God, your receiving apparatus must be sound.

The Truth (al-Haqq) clarifies this with His saying, majestic is His majesty:

﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾

Al-Sha'rawi explains how the receiving apparatus is set right so that one may receive God's reinforcement. He says: ﴿Yes! If you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you suddenly this very moment...﴾

God, glorified and exalted, set forth the example of patience and God-consciousness (taqwa) at Badr, with few in number, and victory came. Here at Uhud you did not show patience: the moment you saw the spoils, your mouths watered, and you did not hold back from them, nor did you keep to God's command, conveyed through His Messenger, to remain in your positions. So how could you be worthy of reinforcement?

Then who determines the reinforcement? It is God who gives the reinforcement. But who receives it so as to benefit from it? It is the one capable of patience and God-consciousness.

Thus patience and God-consciousness are the equipment (ʿuddah) in war. Do not rely on numbers or equipment alone. That is why our Lord said to us: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of strength﴾. He did not say: prepare what you think will overpower them. No. You prepare what is within your capacity, and when you have prepared what is within your capacity and your means have run out, then God is the One who completes your victory.

Human beings do this among themselves too. For example, and to God belongs the highest example, before and after: suppose you are a large merchant, and enormous lorries arrive loaded with goods, big crates and parcels, while you sit as the workers unload the goods. A worker comes to lower a parcel, and the parcel overpowers his strength, and you find yourself, without any conscious decision, rising up to support and help him the moment you see him about to fall. This worker has exhausted his means and could not manage it, so the one concerned with the matter extends his hand to him. How much more so is God, glorified and exalted. It is as if He says: exert yourself and offer your means. When you see your means have run out and the situation is greater than you, know that it is greater than you, but it is not greater than your Lord. He, glorified, says: ﴿And God made it only as good news for you, and that your hearts might be reassured by it...﴾

Then beware lest you think that the reinforcement with three thousand or five thousand, whom God sent down and reinforced you with, or with the angels trained for fighting... Beware lest you think that this reinforcement is a condition for God's victory for you, whether by yourself or by the angels. He is able to grant you victory without angels, but it is good tidings, to comfort the human material. So when the believers see large numbers of reinforcements, while the disbelievers were superior to them in number, the causes of the believers are reassured and trust in victory. Thus the angels are merely good tidings, but victory is from God, the Mighty who cannot be overcome. And all matters proceed by His wisdom, which nothing surpasses ever.

The Truth (Allah) says after that: ﴿That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or disgrace them so that they turn back frustrated﴾.

The meaning of "cutting off a part" is determined by knowing what the "part" is. If the "part" is a large number, then cutting it off means that some of them are killed. If the "part" is a wide land, then cutting it off means taking from their land. For this reason, the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment, and He is swift in account﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].

The land of disbelief was losing a portion of itself every day, and this portion was joining the land of faith. This is in regard to the extent of the land. Suppose the "part" is wealth; then cutting off the part here means that we take some of their wealth as spoils. Then there is the standing that the whole Peninsula held in awe. The whole Peninsula stood in awe of Quraysh, and no tribe could attack their trade caravans going to the north and south, because all the tribes knew that they would go to the House during the pilgrimage season, so no tribe would attack them, since tomorrow they would be going to Quraysh. Therefore, sovereignty and greatness belonged to Quraysh. When the tribes learn that the men of Quraysh have been broken and defeated, and that their journey to Syria has become threatened, they will search for another party to go to.

Cutting off the part took many forms. If the part is a number, some of them are killed. If the part is land, some of it is taken and goes to a land of faith. If it is greatness and dominance, defeat comes to them. If it is influence in the Peninsula, it is shaken: ﴿That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve﴾.

Let us notice that the Truth said ﴿that He might cut off a part﴾ and did not say "that He might uproot," because Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, spared some of the disbelievers, since they have a role in faith to play. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was full of tenderness, mercy and compassion towards his community, and he had good expectations of Allah that He would guide them. For this reason, the verses of the Qur'an that speak on this matter are many. Behold, the Truth says:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this discourse, in sorrow﴾ [al-Kahf: 6].

And in another place in the noble Qur'an, the Truth says:

﴿Perhaps you will kill yourself [with grief] that they will not be believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3-4].

Allah says to the Messenger (ﷺ): "Your duty is only to convey the message," and the Messenger loves that every individual in his community be guided to faith. So the Truth said: ﴿You have no say in the matter; He either accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾.

That is, you have no say in the matter, Muhammad. It is only for God to accept their repentance, and you rejoice at their repentance, or He punishes them, and that should not grieve you, because they are wrongdoers. That is, Muhammad, your duty is only to convey the message. As for them, they have wronged themselves by disbelief. Injustice, as we know, is taking what is due to its rightful owner and giving it to someone else. The greatest injustice is ascribing divinity to other than God, which is *shirk* (associating partners with God). For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Indeed, associating partners with God is a tremendous wrong.﴾ [Luqman: 13]

The Truth says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace:

﴿You have no say in the matter, whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 128]

This is a matter that does not fall outside God's dominion. Why? Because the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them belong to God:

It was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the polytheists had stained his face with blood while he was calling them to their Lord, wanted, peace and blessings be upon him, to invoke a curse against them. God forbade him, knowing, glorified is He, that among them were those who would believe. And God revealed His words:

﴿To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

It was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the polytheists had stained his face with blood while he was calling them to their Lord, wanted, peace and blessings be upon him, to invoke a curse against them. God forbade him, knowing, glorified is He, that among them were those who would believe. And God revealed His words:

﴿To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 129:

It is said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), after the polytheists had stained his face with blood while he was calling them to their Lord, wished to invoke curses upon them. Allah forbade him, because He knew that among them were those who would believe. Then He revealed His words:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Since we are speaking of aspects of the Battle of Uhud, I want to say: "Mount Uhud, may Allah be pleased with it." We heard some of those who know Allah, whenever the word "Uhud" is mentioned, say: "Uhud, may Allah be pleased with it." The people were surprised at the words of Sheikh Abdullah al-Zaidan, who said this. When he saw their surprise, he said to them: "Did the Messenger of Allah not address it by saying: 'Be steady, Uhud, for upon you are a Prophet, a truthful one, and two martyrs'? Did the Messenger of Allah not say of it: 'Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it'? Do you want a better companionship than that? Say: Uhud, may Allah be pleased with it."

We have said before that when your intellect stops at a matter, do not measure it by your own standards, but by higher standards. We say these words because science is now running and striving swiftly and eagerly to discover some of Allah's secrets in the universe. It has shown us that animals have languages through which they communicate, and they are now trying to compile a dictionary for the language of fish. Allah, the Exalted, has also related to us the story of the ant with Solomon (peace be upon him), when He said:

﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive.﴾ [An-Naml: 18]

This statement indicates that an ant came out and performed a "shift" (wardiyya) of work in order to protect those with her, then returned to speak with the members of her kind. Our master Solomon heard her and smiled at her words. So science is competing, striving and hastening now to establish that every species in existence has a language through which it communicates, that every species has responsiveness, and that every species has reproduction. For this reason the Truth said, on the tongue of Solomon:

﴿O people, we have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given of all things. Indeed, this is manifest bounty.﴾ [An-Naml: 16]

This was a distinction specific to Solomon (peace be upon him). Thus birds have a speech. When we rise to inanimate things, we hear the words of the Truth, the Exalted, concerning the people of Pharaoh and the fact that inanimate things did not weep over them:

﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and noble dwellings, and comfort in which they had been delighting. Thus [it was], and We caused other people to inherit them. The heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved.﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 25-29]

Do the heaven and the earth weep? It is a wondrous matter. Inanimate things, such as heaven and earth, do not only communicate, but also have emotions, because weeping arises only from an emotional, sentimental reaction. This means that inanimate things not only speak, but also feel. The earth brings forth its burdens and reports its news. How? 

﴿Because your Lord has inspired it.﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 5]

The heaven and the earth came to Allah in complete obedience and humility:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ [Fussilat: 11]

So there is more than communication. They have emotions just like you. Just as a matter saddens you, the earth also weeps. Since it weeps, it must also have a counterpart, which is rejoicing. Allah the Exalted says about the land of Pharaoh: ﴿The heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾. Had it not wept for some people, this statement would have no distinction.

Therefore Imam Ali (may Allah honour his face) said: "When the believer dies, two places weep for him: the place of his prayer, because he will be deprived of the blessing of faith, and the ascent of his deeds. There is a place on earth and a place in heaven." So we must understand that everything has feeling. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believer dies, the places of the earth rejoice for him, for there is no spot except that it wishes that he be buried in it."

Why do we say this now? We say it so that, when it is established by knowledge that everything has a language and that everything in the kinds of the universe communicates, it may be said that there are people upon whom the breezes of faith have blown, who perceived and felt them from the Qur'an. No one claims that he invented it from himself, for it is in the Qur'an, although we do not know how it comes.

This battle, the Battle of Uhud, which occupied sixty verses, is discussed here by the Truth in the words: ﴿And [recall] when you set out from your family﴾ and ﴿when two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾, and His words: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were few and weak﴾. After that, He leaves the campaign in its heat and brings us matters which He places here, then comes back to complete the campaign. If this were a single scene of the campaign which ends and then another topic begins, it would not have occupied us. But the campaign will continue with sixty verses. How then does He end the discussion of the campaign, giving us only its opening, and after that the Qur'an turns to meanings far from the campaign? What makes Him, glory be to Him, leave the matter of the campaign to say:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, and fear Allah that you may be successful. And fear the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy. And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous, who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people; and Allah loves the doers of good. And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who can forgive sins except Allah? — and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know. Those — their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; and excellent is the reward of the workers. Precedents have passed before you, so proceed throughout the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers. This is a clear statement for mankind and guidance and instruction for the righteous.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 130-138]

Why did the Truth give us only the opening of the campaign and then focus on matters, the first of which is the matter of usury? What is the connection between these matters and that campaign? I say: may Allah have mercy on the author of "In the Shade of the Qur'an" (Fi Zilal al-Qur'an), Sheikh Sayyid Qutb, for he was able to draw from this transition principles of faith and creed which, if the Muslims in every part of the earth had placed before their eyes, no state of disbelief would have overcome us.

We want to understand these scenes and why they began with the matter of usury. Because what was the cause of the defeat, or of the failure to achieve victory, at the Battle of Uhud, was that they coveted the spoils. The spoils are surplus wealth, and usury involves greed for surplus wealth.

When the Qur'an addresses here an event-specific matter, and events are changes that pass and end, He, glory be to Him, wants to preserve the benefit of the event so that it spreads beyond the time of the event; otherwise the event may pass with its admonitions and lessons and end without any benefit. When the soul passes through events, its faculties are open, because the event, as the forgiven Sheikh Sayyid Qutb said, is hot. So when the Qur'an exploits the event before it cools, the matter that the admonition addresses takes firm hold on the human soul. He, glory be to Him, did not want the events of Uhud to pass, with their lessons and admonitions, without the Holy Qur'an exploiting them to establish matters of faith that spread in times other than the time of the event, of wars and others, so that they also become ordered in the time of peace. Thus the verse on usury here seems to have fallen in the midst of the texts that deal with the Battle of Uhud.

The superficial ones may say: What made the Qur'an move from speaking of Uhud to speaking of usury a second time, after having spoken of it first?

We say: The Qur'an does not chronicle events, but wants to exploit events in order to unfold and clarify the meanings within them that give the event breadth, length and depth. Every event in the universe takes from time an amount equal to the event, and the event has a length, which is an amount of time: it may be an hour, two hours, or a night, for example. This is the length of the event.

The events that Allah brings about have a length determined by the chronological duration of the event, and they have a breadth that gives them expansion. After being a straight line, they become an area, and the Truth makes them comprehensive of many things. He does not want the event to proceed as a straight line, but wants it to be a wide road with area and breadth. This breadth gives it a planar extent that takes in many things, and this too may end with the event. Therefore Allah wants to give the event a third dimension, which is depth in history, so that it gives its benefit, just as we now benefit from the benefit of an event, which is the Battle of Uhud.

Thus the event also has volume, and this is what makes people stop and say: kinship ties prolong life. Life has a specific temporal limit, which is its straight line. There is one who increases the breadth of his life: instead of benefiting people in a small field, he works and benefits in a wider field. Thus he gives his life an area.

There is another person who wants to be stronger in life. What does he do? He gives his life depth. Instead of working merely for his own existence, after which his life ends however wide its extent, he increases his righteous work and leaves a trace of knowledge or goodness that continues after his life, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is derived, or a righteous child who prays for him."

For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, its root firm and its branch in the sky, giving its produce every time by the permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that they may remember.﴾ [Ibrahim: 24-25]

It is a good word that was spoken, but it is like the good tree, because it takes root in the ear of the one who hears it, and it becomes a movement subject to the word. Whenever the hearer acts as a result of the influence of this word, some of the reward returns to the one who spoke it, even if he has died.

It is as if the speaker of this word is still living, and as if his life has been prolonged by his good word. Thus the good deeds a person performs do not mean that they prolong his life, because life is limited by a term. But there is a person who gives his life breadth, and another who gives it depth, and his giving continues to be connected until the Hour comes, so it is as if he has given himself an everlasting life. They say: remembrance is a second life for a person.

The Truth, the Exalted, explains the lessons to be drawn from the Battle of Uhud. The first violation was the cause not of the defeat, but — let us say — "of the failure to complete the victory." They had begun victorious, and the victory was not completed because a violation occurred. The motive for this violation was that, when they saw the spoils, they rushed toward them. So its motive was seeking wealth by an unlawful means, because the Prophet had said to them: "Protect our flank with horses, and let them not come at us from behind. Stay in your places whether the day goes in our favour or against us, and if you see us being snatched by the birds, do not leave your place." Thus leaving the place became an unlawful act, so the soul's aspiration toward something other than what the Messenger of Allah had commanded is considered an unlawful act. The aspiration here was for wealth, and so is usury.

The Truth wanted the heat of the event to be present, and the effect that arose from the event: that the Muslims did not complete their victory, and they grew weary. The source of the weariness was that a few

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 130:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury (riba), doubled and redoubled, and fear Allah that you may be successful.﴾

Riba is an increase in wealth. So is it to be eaten? Yes, because all financial matters are for the sake of the morsel you eat; this is the principle. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you wakes up secure in his dwelling, healthy in his body, and has his food for the day, it is as if the whole world has been gathered for him."

We know that when one of us is in a place where there is no loaf of bread, the ownership of a mountain of gold will not benefit him. ﴿Do not consume riba, doubled and redoubled.﴾ His saying, glorified is He, ﴿adh'afan﴾ (multiplied) and ﴿mudda'afah﴾ (doubled) is an economic statement of the most modern system. The "ad'af" (multiples) is the increase such that, when you compare it with the principal, the principal becomes weak. So when the capital of money is one hundred, for example, and twenty percent is taken on it as interest, the total becomes one hundred and twenty. Thus the one hundred and twenty make the one hundred weak; this is the meaning of "multiples."

As for the meaning of "doubled" (mudā'afah)? We will find that the one hundred and twenty become new capital, and when a year passes you will take interest on the one hundred and on the twenty as well. Thus the multiples have also been doubled, and this is what is called compound profit. Does this mean that we may consume it without being "multiplied and doubled"?! No, because the reality in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was like this.

Someone may say to you: "I understand the Qur'an, and what is forbidden is multiplied and doubled usury. So if it is not multiplied and doubled, is it permissible to take a simple profit represented by a percentage of interest on the principal only?" But we refer such a speaker to the word of Allah:

﴿And if you repent, you will have your principal; you will not wrong and you will not be wronged.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 279]

This wise statement makes clear that repentance requires that a person return to the limits of his principal, and that no simple or compound profit be mixed into that. When we find the phrase ﴿adh'afan mudda'afah﴾, it came only to describe the reality that prevailed in its time.

After that, the Truth says, as a conclusion to the verse: ﴿and fear Allah that you may be successful.﴾ We always say, whenever we see the word "fear" (ittaqu), it means: place between yourselves and Allah a protection (wiqayah). Is the protection between you and Allah from all of His attributes of beauty and majesty? No. Protection is from what tires, what pains, and what harms. So "fear Allah" means: place between yourselves and His attributes of majesty—of might, subjugation, and retribution—a protection. When the Truth says ﴿fear Allah﴾, it is like His saying ﴿and fear the Fire﴾, because the Fire is among the soldiers of the attributes of majesty.

When the Truth says ﴿that you may be successful (la'allakum tufliḥūn)﴾, we know that this word "al-falāḥ" (success) comes to encourage the believer toward the way of Allah. The Truth has brought it from a tangible thing that we see at all times, and we see it because it is tied to the survival of our lives: it is cultivation and farming. You plough, you sow, you water, and after that you harvest.

So He wants to make clear to you that the hardships of ploughing, the hardships of sowing, and the hardships of watering all—when do you see their result? You see the result at the time of harvest. The farmer takes two measures of wheat from his storehouse in order to sow a quarter of a feddan, and we do not say to him: "You have diminished your storehouse," because he diminished the storehouse for the sake of increase. Therefore the one who does not diminish his storehouse and does not sow will come on the day of harvest, placing his hand on his cheek in regret, and regret will not benefit him then!

The Truth wants to tell us: the way, even if it tires you and takes much of your movement, will nevertheless return good to you according to your intention and your eagerness in work. Allah has struck for us the parable in His saying:

﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes; in each spike a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 261]

This is a clear matter: a grain that we take from you diminishes what you have, but it gives you seven hundred. So when a grain is taken from you, do not say that you have lost; rather, estimate that you will gain such-and-such. Allah gives us this parable in one of His creations, which is the earth—the barren earth. You give it one grain, and it gives you seven hundred. If one of Allah's creations, the earth, gives you multiples upon multiples of what you gave, will not the Lord of this earth give you multiplied multiples? He is capable of the most generous bounty. This is success in its reality.

After that, when He speaks of success, He tells you: you will not only obtain success, but you will also guard against the Fire. So the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿and guard against the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.﴾

After that, when He speaks of success, He tells you: you will not only obtain success, but you will also guard against the Fire. So the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿and guard against the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.﴾

And after that, whenever he speaks of success (al-falah), he says to you: you will not only attain success, but you will also guard yourself against the Fire. So the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And guard yourselves against the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾

﴿And guard yourselves against the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾

So there are two matters in it: the negation of a harm, and the affirmation of a benefit. It affirms for you the benefit of success, and it negates from you the harm of the Fire. Therefore, He, exalted is He, says:

﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has certainly triumphed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 185]

For when one is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, this is the great triumph. And this is the reason that our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, when we walk on the Sirat (al-Sirat, the bridge over Hell), will show us the Fire and we will pass over it. Why? So that we may know how faith saved us from it.

What is the means (wasila) by which we may prosper and guard ourselves against the Fire? The means is to follow the method of God which He brought through His Messenger: ﴿And obey God and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾

And "mercy" is manifested in that it does not bring you into hardship; as for healing, it is that you fall into hardship and then it departs from you. Therefore, if we take the method from the beginning, we will take mercy.

﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy﴾ [al-Isra: 82]

Healing is the removal of the sin into which we have fallen, and the Qur'an serves as a remedy; mercy is manifested when we take the method at the outset, so that no hardships come upon us.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾

Speed (al-sur'ah), as we have known, has as its opposite haste (al-'ajalah). Speed is advancing in what is appropriate, and the meaning of advancing in what is appropriate is that you make an event take less time. An example of this is when a person drives his car from Cairo to Alexandria: he tries to cover the two hundred and ten kilometres in less time, so that, instead of the journey taking him three hours by car, he speeds so that it takes him two hours. Thus speed is advancing in what is appropriate, and it is praiseworthy, and its opposite, slowness, is blameworthy. So speed is praiseworthy, and slowness is blameworthy.

But "haste" (al-'ajalah) is advancing in what is not appropriate, and it is blameworthy; its opposite is "deliberation" (al-ta'anni), and deliberation is commendable. So speed is praiseworthy and its opposite, slowness, is blameworthy; haste is blameworthy and its opposite, deliberation, is commendable. The popular proverb says: "In deliberation is safety, and in haste is regret."

Allah says: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾, meaning: take the forgiveness and take the Garden quickly, because you do not know how long you will remain in this world. Beware of postponing any act of religion or any act of goodness, because you do not know whether you will remain to do it or not. So seize the opportunity of your life, take the forgiveness and take the Garden. This is the meaning in which the widely known saying comes: "Work for your worldly life as if you will live forever, and work for your Hereafter as if you will die tomorrow."

People understand it in a way that serves their psychological desires. Meaning: "Work for your worldly life as if you will live forever" – that is, gather much of the world so that it suffices you until the Day of Resurrection. This is not a correct understanding. The correct understanding is that whatever you miss of worldly affairs today, consider that you will live long and take it tomorrow; as for the matter of the Hereafter, you must hasten to it.

﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is as the heavens and the earth﴾. We know that areas have length and width, because what has length equal to its width is a square; what has width less than its length we call "rectangular." When Allah says ﴿whose width is as the heavens and the earth﴾, we know that width is the lesser of the two dimensions, meaning that it is wider than what we see. It is as if He likened the lesser dimension of the Garden to the greatest dimension we know, which is the heavens and the earth joined together with one another, and so He gave us something wider than what we see. If its width is wider than what we know, then what is its length? It is a limit we do not know.

Someone may say: why did He specify its width, saying ﴿whose width is as the heavens and the earth﴾? Then where is its length? We say: are the heavens and the earth only the universe? He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255]

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says: "The heavens and the earth and what is between them are nothing but like a ring thrown by a king into a desert." Is this not part of the kingdom of Allah?

Thus we see that this Garden has been prepared for the God-fearing. The meaning of "prepared" (u'iddat) is: made ready, fashioned, and the matter is finished! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confirms this, saying:

"The Garden was displayed before me, and if I wished I would have brought you a cluster of its fruit, and I would have done so."

Why? Because the report of an event may mean that the event does not yet exist and will come into existence later; but the existence of the event negates that it does not exist, because its existence has become a reality. So when He says "prepared," the meaning is a matter whose preparation Allah has completed; He will not take raw materials from this world and wait until your world advances so that He takes means and materials that you have developed to prepare the Garden with them. No.

He, glory be to Him, has informed us about it, saying: "In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." And He, glory be to Him, prepared the whole Garden with "Be!" So when He says "prepared," it is a settled matter. And since it is a settled matter, then the destination to it, or to its opposite, is settled.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 134:

And Paradise was prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun). So who are the muttaqun?

﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain their anger, and who pardon people. And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

These are some of the attributes of the muttaqun. ﴿And those who restrain their anger﴾: the battle, the Battle of Uhud, presents us with this image as well. Hamzah, the master of the martyrs and the paternal uncle of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was killed. And it was not only that he was killed; he was mutilated, and a piece of his liver was taken by Hind, who chewed it. This is more than killing. Its meaning is a base rancour.

When news of Hamzah's death reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they told him that Hind had taken his liver and chewed it and then spat it out, since Allah made it forbidden to her (ʿaṣiyyah ʿalayha), he said: "Allah would not punish a part of Hamzah in the Fire." It is as if it were going to the Fire. Had she swallowed it, its cells would have formed within her body, and when she entered the Fire, it would be as if a part of Hamzah had entered the Fire. So her Lord would certainly make her self stir and prepare to vomit, and she would expel that piece she had chewed from the liver of the master of the martyrs.

The Prophet (ﷺ) also described this incident as the most terrible thing he suffered: the killing of Hamzah. He said: "If Allah grants me victory over Quraysh in any of the battlefields, I will mutilate thirty men from among them."

Here restraining anger comes to take the peak and summit of the event with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning one of the people most beloved to him and in the greatest incident that angered him. And the word of the Truth descends:

﴿And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.﴾ [al-Nahl: 126]

So that we know that our Lord, majestic is He, is not moved by emotion for anyone, because emotion belongs to the transient things (aghyar). This is His Messenger, and He, glorified is He, revealed to him: ﴿And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of that with which you were afflicted﴾. Here comes the command to restrain anger. He, glorified is He, gives this command in a matter that concerns the Messenger and in the event of Uhud. Then afterwards He makes it a general principle, to be in peace as it was in war, and to be with people, not only with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because it was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And those who restrain their anger﴾. We know that all abstract matters are taken from sensory ones. The root of kaẓm is to fill a waterskin (qirbah). The qirab, as we know, were carried by the water-carrier (saqqa) in the past, and they were the vessel for carrying water among the Arabs, made of tanned leather. When the waterskin is filled with water, its mouth is tied (shudda ʿala ra'sihā, i.e. its head is bound) tightly so that nothing of what is in it comes out. This act is called "kaẓama al-qirbah", meaning he filled it and tied it. The waterskin is soft, and when it is placed on the back of a person or of an animal, because of its softness the water would come out, so it is tied (kuẓima) and bound firmly so that nothing comes out of it.

Likewise, anger acts upon the human soul; it stirs it. Allah does not prevent agitation in the soul, because it is a natural emotion, and natural emotions, had Allah not willed them, He would have prevented their causes in human constitution.

Rather, He wills them for things. For example: the sexual instinct; He wills it for the continuation of the species, and He places in the legislation what refines it. Likewise the emotion of anger. Islam does not want the believer to be cast in a mould of iron with no feelings. No. He, glorified is He, wants the believer to be moved by events too, but the emotion must be proportionate to the event: the lofty emotion, the fruitful emotion, not the destructive emotion.

Therefore the Truth says:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval.﴾ [al-Fath: 29]

The believer is not naturally inclined to harshness or to mercy; rather, the situation is what shapes a person's feelings. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54]

Is there someone who is both humble and mighty at once? We say: the faith-based method makes the believer thus: humble towards his believing brother and mighty against the disbeliever. So Islam does not cast the believers in a mould so that they do not feel towards events.

Another example: did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not feel emotion when his son Ibrahim died? He did feel, and wept and grieved. Allah does not want the believer to be made of stone. Rather, He wants the believer to be moved by events, but to make the emotion proportionate to the event. Therefore our master, the Messenger of Allah, said at the parting from his son: "The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and we say nothing except what pleases our Lord, and indeed we, O Ibrahim, are saddened by your parting."

And at the moment of emotion we do not say what displeases the Lord. Rather, it is directed emotion. The believer needs anger when it is stirred in defence of the way of Allah, but the believer must restrain it, i.e., he must not let emotion overcome good conduct and good management. And kaẓm, as we said, is taken from a sensory matter. For example: we know that camels, or dumb animals that have two stomachs, one in which food is stored and another from which they feed directly, such as the camel, it ruminates (yajtarr).

The meaning of "yajtarr" is that the camel retrieves food from the secondary stomach and chews it; this is rumination (ijtirar). If the camel refrains from rumination, it is said: the camel has kaẓama. And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And those who restrain their anger and who pardon people﴾.

We said: there is a difference between the emotion in itself, which may remain in the soul and which you restrain, and the meaning of restraining emotion: that a person can bring it out into the sphere of emotional impulse, but he curbs the surge of this emotion. As for pardoning (ʿafw), it is that you remove the anger from your heart, as if the matter had not happened. This is a second rank. As for the third rank, it is that you respond with a counter-emotion; that is, you do not stop at this limit alone, but you replace the offence with goodness towards the one who offended you. So there are three stages: the first: restraining anger (kaẓm al-ghayẓ). The second: pardon (ʿafw). The third: that a person goes beyond restraint and pardon by doing good to the one who wronged him.

This is the ascent through the ranks of certainty (yaqin), because if you do not restrain your anger and react, the one opposite you will also not be able to control his emotion so as to match yours, and will be filled towards you with heat and rage, and the anger may continue to grow and perhaps pass down to generations of children and grandchildren.

But if you restrain your anger, the one in front of you may feel shame before himself, and the matter ends.

﴿And those who pardon people﴾: it is derived from "ʿaffā ʿala al-athar", and al-athar is what the passage of people leaves in the desert, for example, and then the wind comes to erase this trace. And the Truth concludes the verse: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾.

We said, regarding the philosophy of this: all of us are the handiwork of Allah, and all creation is the dependants (ʿiyal) of Allah. Since we are all dependants of Allah, when one person wrongs another, Allah stands on the side of the one who was wronged and gives him much of His mercy, His pardon, and His tenderness. Thus the one who was wronged has gained. Is it not a duty upon the one who was wronged to do good to the wrongdoer?

But the human intellect loses its intelligence in moments of anger; the one who wrongs a person considers him an enemy. But one of us must understand that the one who wrongs you is in fact placing Allah on your side; what has reached you of harm from him is more than what this harm has taken from you. Here you must have good faith and give the one who wronged you a good deed.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on Surah 3, verse 135:

Then God, exalted is He, continues describing the attributes of the people of Paradise: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah...﴾

The fahisha (an abominable sin) is a grievous sin. Does this mean that the archers at the Battle of Uhud, when they abandoned their positions, had left faith? No. It was only a slip, but it was counted as a major sin for those who advised the believers to descend, and counted as a minor one for those who were incited (in the passive voice) to come down from their position.

So the statement is appropriate: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah﴾. God used the expression "remember Allah" as a reminder to us that whoever commits an immorality or wrongs himself has forgotten Allah. At the moment of committing an immorality or wronging oneself, Allah is not in the mind of the person committing the immorality, or in the mind of the one who wrongs himself. What emboldens a person to disobedience in order to fulfil his own desire is that he has not seen Allah, nor seen His recompense and punishment in the Hereafter standing before him. Had he conceived of this, he would have refrained from immorality.

Likewise, the one who neglects obedience has not remembered Allah and His bounty for the God-fearing. Had he remembered Allah and His bounty for the God-fearing, he would not have been lax in obeying Allah. Therefore God says: ﴿remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾. Whoever seeks forgiveness for his sin has remembered Allah.

There is disagreement among the scholars concerning the fahisha. Some scholars said: it is the greatest of the major sins, and wronging oneself is a minor sin among the minor sins. Other scholars said: the fahisha is adultery (zina), because the Qur'an explicitly mentions it, and whatever is beneath that is a minor sin.

But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence."

So a person may not overlook his errors, saying: this is a minor sin and that is a minor sin, because a minor sin added to a minor sin becomes a major one. When we look at the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾, we find that the one who commits an immorality is also a wrongdoer to himself, because he has fulfilled a passing desire for himself and left for himself a lasting punishment.

Why did God not say: "and those who wrong themselves," only? That is, the conjunction would be with "wa" (and) rather than "aw" (or); because God wishes to clarify for us the difference between committing an immorality and wronging oneself.

The one who commits an immorality is only fulfilling for himself a desire or pleasure, even if fleeting. But the one who wrongs himself commits a sin and gains no benefit from it. For example, one who gives false testimony does not achieve any benefit for himself; the benefit returns to the one in whose favour he testified falsely. The false witness wrongs himself, because he has answered an immediate need of another, and has not saved himself from the punishment of the Hereafter. As for the person who commits immorality, he has taken enjoyment in this world, and afterwards he receives the punishment in the Hereafter.

But the one who wrongs himself does not benefit himself; rather he harms himself. What is worse is that you sell your religion for your worldly life; in this case you may take enjoyment from the world, while the life of the world is short.

God did not forbid the enjoyment of this world, but He said of it: ﴿Say: the enjoyment of this world is little﴾. And there are those who sell their religion for another's worldly gain, while they take nothing and wrong themselves.

God says: ﴿so they sought forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ The meaning of "dhanb" (sin) is opposition to a directive of the methodology (manhaj). A command has come from the manhaj and it was not carried out; a prohibition has come from the manhaj and it was not observed. It is not called a dhanb except when God makes us aware of the sins; that is the legislation of heaven. In the sphere of human legislation we say: there is no crime except by text, and no penalty except by criminalisation.

This means it is necessary to clarify what is considered a crime, so that punishment for it may take place, and there is no crime except by a text specifying it. That is, the crime is stated before the penalty is stated. How much more so with the methodology of God? He makes us aware of the sins first, and after that He specifies the penalties that the one who commits the sin deserves.

Let us pay attention to the words of God: ﴿and they do not persist in what they did, while they know﴾. Thus seeking forgiveness is not that you append to the sin the phrase "I seek forgiveness of Allah" and nothing more. Rather, a person must append to the sin his saying "I seek forgiveness of Allah," and must resolve never to commit the sin again.

This does not mean that the sin will never occur from you again. The sin may occur from you, but at the moment you seek forgiveness you resolve not to return to it. The sin may occur, but on condition that it is not done with premeditation, where you say to yourself: "I will commit the sin, and seek forgiveness for myself afterwards." By this you would be like one who mocks his Lord, besides which you may commit the sin and God may not grant you the respite to seek forgiveness. God's words: ﴿and they do not persist in what they did, while they know﴾ make clear to us that there is no penalty except that the crime be specified by a text.

God teaches us, He first makes us know: what is the sin? What is the punishment? And how is forgiveness sought?

Then Allah says: ﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

﴿Those﴾ refers back to what came earlier in His saying:

﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing (muttaqun)﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133]

along with the explanation of the attributes of the God-fearing in His saying:

﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain their anger and pardon people; and Allah loves the doers of good﴾ [Al 'Imran: 134]

They spend in ease with the spending of gratitude (shukr), and they spend in hardship with the spending of remembrance and humble supplication (tadarru'), because a blessing, when it appears in ease, needs gratitude for that blessing, and a blessing spent in hardship calls for humble supplication to Allah so that He may remove from the spender the effects of calamity and affliction. So they spend whether they are in hardship or in ease.

Indeed, many people are made to forget, by ease, that Allah has bestowed favours upon them, and they think the blessing came about through their own knowledge. Some people are distracted by blessing from feeling the pains of others, and they occupy themselves with their own pains. But the believers never forget their Lord, and His command to spend in both hardship and ease. For this reason they say: "So-and-so does not withhold his hand on the day of the wedding, nor on the day of imprisonment."

The attributes of the God-fearing continue:

﴿And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah?—and do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135]

In this is a kind of reassurance to the believer regarding the changes of his own soul, and that when he yields once to the whisperings of Satan, this does not expel him from the enclosure of taqwa, because Allah has made this one of the attributes of the God-fearing. The indecency that results from the whispering of Satan, followed by the servants' remembrance of Allah and their seeking forgiveness while not persisting in returning to it, does not at all remove them from being described as God-fearing. For the Truth is the Forgiving: ﴿and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾

They have been informed of this, for the Truth does not punish anyone except by a text, and does not chastise except for a crime. The saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord﴾ refers to all that has preceded. We note that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, placed for those who act upon this work of taqwa two arcs: the first arc with which He began is His saying, the Truth: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾.

The second arc is the one that ended the matter: ﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾.

So the first garden which Allah mentioned is to stir the emotions of the soul to incline toward what leads to this garden; and after that He mentioned the attributes and categories and made the garden a wage (ajr). ﴿And excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

The ajr is ordinarily what the worker takes as a result of work, and the ajr when the worker takes it as a result of work depends on the evaluation of the work by the employer himself. So the increase and decrease of the wage is an assessment by the employer, and also an assessment of the worker. If several employers seek a specific worker, he may ask for an increase; and if no one seeks him, he accepts the first offer of wage in exchange for performing the work.

So the matter is one of need on the part of an employer, or need on the part of a worker; and when we look at the transaction in the Hereafter, we find that it is between a God who has no need of your work. And although He has no need of your work, He has made a wage for your work.

What is this matter? He does not need your work, yet He gives you a wage for your work, and says to you: this wage is the minimum; but it is for Me to multiply this wage, and for Me to bestow upon you what is above the wage. How many stages, then? They are three stages, although He, glorified is He, does not benefit from this work except that He has set three levels of wage.

So the need is from one side only, which is your side, O servant: you need your Creator, and He does not need you; yet the God, the Truth, gives you the wage not merely according to the measure of the work, but far beyond that. The one for whom you work, of the servants, may give you—for example—what suffices you as a day's sustenance, or a day and a half's sustenance. But when you take the wage from the hand of Allah, He gives you a wage whose period of spending does not end; for He is the One who said: ﴿and excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

This is the wage of which it is said: "Excellent is this wage," because it is a wage that is not commensurate with my effort, but exceeds all the striving I have expended, and comes from a source that has no need of this striving.

He, glorified is He, is bounteous to me first, and bounteous to me last, so that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, shows that you, O servant, when you perform obedience, the effect of the obedience returns to your own self, and yet He gives you a wage for what you have done.

We have clarified that these verses came between the verses about the Battle of Uhud as guidance and a drawing of lessons from the events that took place at Uhud, so that when a person lives in the imagining of the events, the events are fresh, and the taking of the lesson from them is near to the soul, because a reality necessitates and confirms it.

Almighty God says, after that: ﴿Systems (sunan) have passed away before you, so travel through the earth and see...﴾

That is: you are not novel in this matter. "Khalat" (خلت) means "madat" (مضت), that is, they occurred in fact in times that preceded this speech. Usually, reports a person gives may be true or false. But this matter does not require truth or falsehood, because what has happened is not a future matter. It is something that has already passed. So as soon as the speech comes, we do not wait for a reality to confirm its truth, because the reality has already happened before. Thus He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Systems have passed away before you﴾.

The sunan (سنن, divine laws or patterns) are the ways through which God directs His creation to achieve the benefit of that creation, in order to guarantee for the human being, the master in this creation, what achieves his benefit. The benefit of the human being is represented in the truth prevailing in the life of the human being who is given choice, just as the truth prevailed in the creation that is subjugated before the human being.

We have said that in this creation there is subjugation (taskhir), that is, it has no will. There is no will for inanimate matter, nor for plants, nor for animals to do good for you or not. It never happened that a man came to land suitable for cultivation, placed seeds in it, and the land did not sprout and said to him: "I will not give to you." Nor did the land ever say about a man: "He is a disbeliever, so I will not give him provision."

The land is subjugated to serve the human being as long as he takes its causes; so it yields to him. Animals too are subjugated to serve you, not by your choice, nor by your power to subjugate them, but by God's subjugating them so that they act.

We have said: a man may have a beast of burden, like some farmers. Sometimes its owner makes it carry loads of manure, the dung and waste of animals, and afterwards it occurs to him to take it out of this work and make it a mount for himself, pampering it with things you know: a beautiful bridle and a more beautiful saddle, and he makes its life comfortable and cleans it.

In the first case, did the beast refuse to carry the manure, or in the second case refuse to carry the human being? No; you direct it just as you wish, so it has no choice. Plants have no choice, inanimate matter has no choice, and animals too; choice belongs only to the human being.

God has determined the choice of the human being by measures in which the human being is subjugated, so that he does not think he has independently attained sovereignty such that he has self-sufficient power. The Truth governs the human being with things that He makes compulsory for him, so that he remains within the framework of subjugation. And the Truth leaves for the human being things in which he retains choice. When we look at the creation, we find that what has no choice in it proceeds by a system of events without conflict, while what has choice for the human being is what goes awry. Why?

Because the human being may choose other than the method of the One who created him, who is God, glory be to Him. So if you want your affair to be set right, O chooser, then make your choice within the framework of God's method.

When you make your choice within the framework of God's method, you become upright like the rest of the kinds, and matters proceed with you in order.

When you compare something in which the human being has choice and action with something in which the human being has neither choice nor action, you find that what has no human choice in it is upright in its affair, with no disagreement at all, whereas in what has human choice you find disagreement.

For example: if we look at a means of transport among animals, such as camels, horses or donkeys, we find them proceeding on one road, meeting coming and going, and there is no collision between donkey and donkey, nor killing of the rider of one of the two donkeys.

Animals avoid and shun one another even if the rider is asleep. However crowded the road is, the animals do not collide, because that falls within the scope of God's subjugation of the animal.

Now let us look at the human being when he intervened to make a means of transport. The human being made cars of various colours, driven by a human being. Although it is the human being who drives cars, nevertheless violations, collisions and accidents began to come, because the human being has a hand in that.

Almighty God wants to show you that what is created subjugated by God's command and direction does not produce corruption at all; corruption arises only from that in which you have choice. So try to choose within the framework of God's method. When the Truth says to you: "Do this and do not do that," you must believe and obey, because when God subjugated things to the human being they went on in wonderful order, and you, O servant, when you obey God, matters in your life go smoothly.

That is why we have said: people have never complained of a crisis in the sun, nor have they complained of a crisis in air; but why have they complained of a crisis in food? The human being has a share in producing food. So whatever the human being has a share in must be governed by the law of obligation from God: "Do this and do not do that."

The creation is created with truth (bi-l-haqq). The meaning of its being created with truth is that everything in existence performs its function as God intended it, and as it was subjugated for its purpose. If the human being carries out the obligation, everything proceeds in truth. If the human being abandons the obligation and acts by his own choice, he turns to falsehood and what is false results, whereas the creation is founded on truth. ﴿We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Dukhan: 39]. Truth has made for the creation fixed principles, so nothing transgresses against anything else at all. The human being's choice is what brings forth the opposite of truth, which is falsehood. That is why God protects the creation by showing that truth collides with falsehood and falsehood collides with truth, but truth comes and remains, while falsehood is driven off and vanishes, and God shows us this before our eyes, He says:

﴿And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾ [al-Isra': 81].

So His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Systems have passed away before you﴾ means: take lessons from those who came before you, and look at the collision of falsehood with truth. Did the collision of falsehood with truth continue and remain? No, because falsehood was bound to vanish.

For this reason we see practical examples of it, I do not say among people's processions with one another, but in the procession of falsehood against the truth of heaven. The truth of heaven is represented by the messengers and the methods that came from God, and every truth that came from heaven and came from God's methods met a people who were falsifiers.

Why? Because heaven does not intervene except when corruption spreads, and as long as corruption spreads there is a group that profits from corruption, and this group that profits from corruption and falsehood defends it. Then the procession of heaven comes to collide with this falsehood and the faction that supports falsehood, and a battle arises. Then the Truth said: ﴿Systems have passed away before you﴾. He said it so that we would know that falsehood is bound to vanish, and that in all the battles of the people of the earth against the method of heaven, truth has prevailed. That is why the chapter of al-Ankabut comes to show us this, starting from His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, and he said: O my people, worship God and hope for the Last Day, and do not commit corruption on the earth, acting wickedly. But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes﴾ [al-Ankabut: 36-37].

This is the first image. The second image comes:

﴿And [We destroyed] 'Ad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings; and Satan made their deeds seem fair to them, and barred them from the way, though they were discerning﴾ [al-Ankabut: 38].

So look at their remaining dwellings, which show you what happened to them. The third image:

﴿And Qarun and Pharaoh and Haman; Moses came to them with clear signs, but they waxed proud in the earth, yet they could not outstrip [Us]﴾ [al-Ankabut: 39].

When you hear ﴿and they could not outstrip﴾, it is as if there were a need pursuing them, and whoever is pursued by something tries to outrun it, but they could not. Then the laws come clearly after that:

﴿So each We seized for his sin: some of them We sent a violent wind upon, some were seized by the Cry, some We caused the earth to swallow, and some We drowned; and God was not to wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40].

So the struggle of truth and falsehood has already gone before and occurred among nations that preceded you, and their dwellings remain. Whoever wishes to go to them to verify, let him go. The cities of Salih still remain, the traces of 'Ad still remain, and every place has a trace of such traces. That is why the Truth makes clear: if you wish to verify this, I have informed you, and whoever believes in Me, let him confirm My report. To the one who does not believe, or who wants his heart assured, He says:

﴿So travel through the earth and see what was the end of the deniers﴾ [al-Nahl: 36].

Almighty God represents the struggle of truth, which is the fixed thing, with falsehood. This matter exists even in what has no choice, and the Truth brings it about among them, a struggle between truth and falsehood in what has no choice, for the benefit of the human being as well. God has made the struggle between truth and falsehood occur in things that are not from the human being but serve the human being, and we see these in material matters. As for values, the Truth says:

﴿He sends down water from the sky, so the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire, seeking ornament or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus God strikes the parable of truth and falsehood: as for the foam, it passes away as scum, but what benefits people remains in the earth. Thus God sets forth the parables﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17].

He, glory be to Him, sends down water from the sky, and it flows in the valleys. The valleys, as we know them, are the place enclosed between two mountains. When rain falls on the heights, it descends to the lowlands and flows in the valleys. The valleys are the place of fertility, because the silt and alluvium that come down from the mountains with the rainwater settle and become fertile soil from which crops grow. Each valley takes according to its capacity, and the remaining water seeks another course, even into the depths of the earth. This was a familiar sight in the Arabian Peninsula: when the flood comes, the valleys fill with water, each valley taking according to its capacity. ﴿So the torrent carries a swelling foam.﴾ We see it in the fields and call it "al-rim" (الريم, foam), which floats on the surface of the water. What happens to this foam? It gathers, floats, then settles and drifts to one side. Have you not seen the pot in which meat is bubbling? We find the foam has risen to the surface. This foam contains things that are foreign to the substance of what is in the pot; when the heat of the fire comes, it brings it to the surface, and then either the human being takes it out of the pot, or he leaves it to harden on the sides and it ends.

Where did this foam come from? It comes from the earth, and the earth contains many things, such as roots of plants and remnants of what the wind has carried, and these things permeate the pores of the earth. When these things are in the pores, and the tiny roots come to grow, they prevent them from taking their nourishment. Therefore, when the Truth sends down water from the sky, the water causes these things to float on the surface, so as to make a passage for the tiny roots.

God sends down rain to wash the whole soil, and makes these things float, because they are scum (ghuthaa'), and scum floats. And when the scum floats, beware lest you understand that as elevation; it is an elevation towards an end, and so is the surge of falsehood.

Beware

Then, after that, the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿This is an clarification for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who are mindful of Allah.﴾

Look at the phrase ﴿This is an clarification for mankind﴾. When statements (bayanat) come forth, they draw their strength, their force and their greatness from the power of the one who issued them. When you find a revolt in some society, we hear the words "Statement No. 1," and the world trembles at it, and that is a statement coming from a human being. So what of the statement that comes from Allah?

It is a clarification from Allah: I will not seize you unawares. ﴿This is a clarification for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who are mindful of Allah.﴾ And "guidance" (al-huda), as we know, is the path that leads to the desired goal. And "admonition" (al-maw'iza) means moving the soul by encouragement and warning: encouraging it to do good, and warning it away from evil. That is admonition.

All these things came within the verses about Uhud after we had taken the lesson from it while the event was still fresh. Therefore, before He completes for us the story of Uhud, He stirred souls with this matter and set before us the material and moral matters so that we might act upon them in our lives, and so that the story of Uhud would not end and people turn away from the lessons that were in it.

Since the matter is as such, and since those who fought in the way of Allah were the soldiers of the Truth, and they knew this through Allah's support for them and for His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) among them, he being the bearer of the miracle that indicates his truthfulness, then what happened in the battle of Uhud should not weaken you, for you know how Allah supports and strengthens the Truth, and you know Allah's assault upon falsehood. We have made the sunan (divine laws) and the clarification clear to you. Therefore, after that, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And do not weaken, nor grieve, and you will be superior if you are believers.﴾

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 139:

﴿Do not weaken, and do not grieve, for you will have the upper hand if you are believers.﴾

What is meant by His words ﴿Do not weaken﴾ is: do not become feeble. This is a command specific to the physical matter, because the wounds had exhausted many at the Battle of Uhud, to the point that some of them were rendered unable to stand, and to the point that the Prophet (ﷺ) could not climb the mountain, and Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah carried him on his back so that he could stand. Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Do not weaken﴾, because when you keep in mind that you are a believer, and that God will not leave you alone with the armies of falsehood, since you are a helper of the truth, and the truth is from God and is the Truth, He does not hand over His Prophet and his people to their enemies. So on the day these meanings come to you, beware of becoming weak. Weakness is the loss of bodily strength.

﴿And do not grieve﴾. Grief is the stirrings of the heart, and they had grieved, for many of them had died. Seventy-five of them died as martyrs: five from the Muhajirun and seventy from the Ansar, and this is a difficult and arduous ordeal. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved over the martyrs, and he was angered by the killing of Hamzah (may God be pleased with him), and said: "I will never be afflicted by the like of you! I have never stood in a position more enraging to me than this one." Then he said: "If God grants me victory over Quraysh in any of the battles, I will mutilate thirty men of them in your place."

Then the Truth said: ﴿And do not grieve﴾; why? Because you must compare the event with the purpose of the event.

It is true that killing is hard and a taking of the soul, but look at where he went. And look at what he left behind after him. As for him, he went to a life with his Lord, and it is not like your life. Indeed, our life has its measures, and life with our Lord has its measures; are our measures higher than His? No, far be it from God.

So if you look at him, know that he has gone to something better than what he left, so do not grieve over him, but rejoice for him; since the purpose will reach this matter. Thus He has shortened for him the distance of life, and since the purpose is that he reach the mercy of God and life with God in all its meanings, he is happy in the presence of his Lord. In worldly purposes, when we want to go to a place, we are pleased with whoever hastens time for us to reach that place.

Instead of walking to Alexandria, I go riding a horse or riding a car, and the affluent one goes riding an airplane. So if the purpose is desired and beloved to the soul, and afterwards an event comes that brings the distance to the purpose closer to you, why then would you grieve? He has been martyred. Beware of saying: God has deprived me of His strength in support of the truth; no. He has given another strength to many of His creatures by which the truth was supported. When you know that a person has sold himself to God, you must know that the purpose is great; and therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at the Battle of Badr used to send his family forward, because he knew that if one of them was killed, where would he go? So he loved his family, but he loved them with a great love, and people also love their families here, but with worldly love.

﴿And do not grieve﴾ over what escaped you of the spoils, or do not grieve over what escaped you of victory; why? The answer comes: ﴿and you will have the upper hand﴾. And therefore the confirmation of this came when Abu Sufyan called out, saying: "Hubal is high!", meaning that their god had become exalted. The Messenger said to his companions: "Will you not answer them?" They said: "With what shall we answer?" He said: "Say to them: God is higher and more majestic." Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Answer him." They said: "What shall we say?" He said: "Say: God is our Protector, and you have no protector." Then Abu Sufyan said: "Our appointment is Badr next year." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to a man among his companions: "Say: Yes, it is an appointment between us and you."

So ﴿and you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾: as long as you are upon faith, you are the superior ones. And if you want to know the true meaning of "the superior" (al-a'lawn), compare the Battle of Uhud with the Battle of Badr. They killed some of you at Uhud, and you killed some of them at Badr. But you took prisoners from them at Badr, and they took no one of you prisoner at Uhud. And you gained spoils at Badr, and they gained nothing at Uhud.

And you are the superior ones because God protected your city, although there was no defender in it who had the meaning of soldiering. All of this, and you are the superior ones, if we look at one battle against another battle. And if we look at the battle itself, Uhud, and set Badr aside alone, in the light of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾, that matter was established, because when you were believers (and among the conditions of faith is following the command of one who does not speak from desire), you were victorious. And you achieved a splendid victory, for in the first round of the war you killed some twenty-odd of their chieftains, among them the standard-bearer. But when you opposed the command of the Prophet (ﷺ), your faith became shaken in your hearts.

So the event that occurred confirms the truth of ﴿and you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾. You prevailed at the beginning, and when you disobeyed the command, what came to you came; thus the matter was confirmed in God's saying: ﴿and you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾.

Also, if you look at the battle itself, you will find that your enemy did not remain on the battlefield, but rather you were the ones who remained at the site of the battle. And where did he go? Did he go to another place where he attained dominance and victory? There was nothing but Medina, and Medina had no one in it, and your enemy did not go there, but went toward Mecca. So it is he who fled.

And after that, what happened? Did not the caller of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) call out among the people, and pursue the enemy to strike fear into them, so that they would think him strong, and that what afflicted them did not weaken them against their enemy?

And the Messenger of God went out, with whom? Did he bring a garrison that had not witnessed the battle? No.

Rather, he (peace be upon him) called out to the Muslims: "To me, servants of God!" Those who had witnessed the battle were seven hundred; many of them were wounded, and seventy-five of them were killed, among them Hamzah, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, Shammas ibn Uthman, and Sa'd, mawla of Utbah. These five were from the Muhajirun, and the rest were from the Ansar. These were excluded from the number who witnessed the first part of the battle.
