Indeed, the Messenger did not take in place of them anyone from Medina from the people who offered themselves to be with the army pursuing Quraysh; rather, the Messenger preferred that those who had gone with him to the battle themselves should go, and naturally the martyrs or the wounded were not among them.

The Messenger (peace be upon him) accepted from those who had not witnessed the battle only one man: our master Jabir ibn Abd Allah. He had not gone out to the Battle of Uhud, and he apologized to the Messenger of God, saying that his father Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram had left him behind over seven daughters, and said to him:

"My son, it is not fitting for me or for you that we leave these women without a man among them, and I am not one who would prefer you over myself regarding jihad with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So stay behind with your sisters." So he remained behind with them. The Messenger of God accepted his excuse and permitted him, and he went out with him, and the Messenger of God and those with him pursued them to Hamra' al-Asad. As for his father, Abd Allah ibn Amr, he had been martyred at Uhud; yet despite his father's martyrdom, he asked the Messenger of God to go out to Hamra' al-Asad. This is so that we may know that God says:

﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except He﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31]

Moreover, one of the polytheists who was a confidant of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and one of his allies, Ma'bad al-Khuza'i, passed by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) after Uhud and said to him: "O Muhammad, by God, what befell you has grieved us greatly." Then he met Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him at al-Rawha, and they had resolved to return to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions. Abu Sufyan said to him: "What is behind you, O Ma'bad?" He said: "Muhammad has gone out with his companions pursuing you, with a force the like of which I have never seen." He kept at them until he turned Abu Sufyan and those with him, and they turned their faces toward Mecca, fearful and hastening. The Messenger of God had gone to Hamra' al-Asad and found no one, so the Messenger of God encamped there for three days. The meaning of that is that it was they who fled from the battle. So you are the superior ones, but observe the condition: ﴿if you are believers﴾.

Then, after that, God consoles the believers, saying: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has already touched the people, and these days We alternate among the people...﴾

We have spoken before about "mass" (المس), which is a contact without sensation. That is, a touching, but you do not perceive, for example, heat or softness. "Touch" (اللمس) is when you perceive heat or softness in a thing, and it requires temporary adhesion. "Mass" (المس), however, is that by which you barely perceive anything. "Qarh" (القَرْح) is: wounds. In another dialect one says "qurh" (القُرح) with a dammed qaf, and I say: al-qarh (القٌرح), which is the pain arising from wounds, so that the word has meaning.

You may see some words and think that their meaning is one in general, yet each has its own precise nuance. You hear, for example: ra'a (رأى), nadhara (نظر), lamaha (لمح), ramaqa (رمق), and rana (رنا). All of these indicate sight. But each word has its own meaning: ramaqa is to see with the corner of the eye; lamaha is to witness from afar; rana is to look for a long time; and so on. It is also said: jalasa (جلس) and qa'ada (قعد). The general meaning is nearly one, but the precise meaning shows that sitting (julus) is from lying down, and sitting down (qu'ud) is from standing: one was standing and then sat down. Both end in one posture. Likewise qarh and qurh: each word has a precise meaning.

They say, for example, that the lion has many names: al-asad (الأسد), al-ghadanfar (الغضنفر), al-ri'bal (الرئبال), al-ward (الوَرْد), and al-qaswara (القسْورة). Indeed these are names of the lion, but each name has a specific meaning: al-asad is the general term and the designation of this animal; al-ghadanfar is the lion when it bristles its mane; al-ward is the state of the lion when it has stretched its spine. Thus every situation of the lion has a special meaning.

As for His saying, the Truth: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has already touched the people﴾, note that the Speaker is God, so be very attentive to the subtleties of His speech. We know that in the conditional structure, the condition comes first and then the response comes afterward, following from it and being its result, as when we say: "If you study, you will succeed" — success is the response to a condition, which is studying.

As for His saying, the Truth: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has already touched the people﴾, is the meaning intended by this conditional sentence that the touch of wounds upon the disbelievers that happened at Badr was the recompense for the touch of wounds upon the believers at Uhud? No. It can never be the response to a condition, because if it were the response to a condition, the Truth would have said: "If a wound touches you, then a wound will touch the people, similar to it." But He did not say that, because the wound that afflicted the polytheists at Badr preceded the wound that afflicted the believers at Uhud.

It is as if the Truth says: "If a wound touches you, then do not despair; a similar wound has already touched the people." This is not the response to the condition; rather it came to be used as evidence for the response to the condition, that is, it is a justification for the response to the condition. I say this so that no pretender among the pretenders intervenes and accuses the Qur'an — God forbid — of what is not in it.

He, glorified is He, strengthens the believers and consoles them. An example of this is what we say to someone when a calamity has befallen him:

"If such-and-such has happened to you, then a similar thing has happened to your adversary." So we console him. The intended meaning here is that the Truth consoles the believers: "If a wound touches you, then do not despair; let there be consolation for you, let you get through this matter, and let your souls accept it, because the people have been touched by a similar wound."

Does consolation and exemplification come through what has already occurred or through what will occur? It comes through what has already occurred, so it provides a correct justification: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has already touched the people﴾.

Then the Truth released a general principle: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾. What is the meaning of al-mudawala (المداولة)? Dawala means to transfer a thing from one to another. Here we are before two battles: the Battle of Badr and the Battle of Uhud. Victory was for the Muslims at the Battle of Badr by consensus, while at the Battle of Uhud there was no defeat by consensus, and there was no victory.

So His saying, the Truth: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾ means, with the concession for the sake of argument that the disbelievers had won — although this did not happen — We transferred victory from you, O believers, to them.

Do not let this observation escape you: victory did not pass to them except through a violation on your part, O believers. The meaning of "a violation on your part" is that you abandoned the method, that is, you became merely "people" like them.

Since you have become merely people without a method, equal to them, then victory is yours one day and theirs another day. Note that the Truth did not say that the alternation among the people is an alternation between believers and disbelievers.

If you remain believers, then victory cannot pass to the disbelievers; victory will be yours. Look at what He said: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾, and He did not say "between the believers and the disbelievers," that is, between you and the Quraysh.

The "days" intended here are not what people know as periods comprising night and day, but the intended meaning of "days" here is the times of victory or the times of dominance. It is also said: "such-and-such's day over such-and-such," so ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾ does not include alternation between believers and disbelievers, but it is an alternation between those whose gazes inclined toward the spoils, so their faith became loosened, and so the Quraysh triumphed outwardly. Had you remained upon your faith, that would never have happened. But you abandoned the method of your Lord, and thereby you became equal to and like the non-believers, and thus the days are one time for this and another time for that; it is absolute justice.

We must remember the previous condition, not for the absence of defeat, but for superiority and victory:

﴿And you will be the superior ones, if you are believers.﴾

In the matter of the alternation of days, the Truth warns the believers whose faith has loosened: as long as you share with them the condition of being merely "people," victory becomes a day for them and a day for you, and the shrewd, brilliant, perceptive one who handles matters well is the one who prevails, because the battle here turns between human power and human power.

As long as the Muslims have abandoned God's method, they have become merely humans facing humans. That is why we said: when the archers abandoned executing the order of the supreme commander, our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), the genius of Khalid ibn al-Walid (Khalid ibn al-Walid) appeared over the genius of the Muslim fighters.

We must note in His saying, the Truth: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾ that we cannot say that the alternation of days occurs between believers and disbelievers; rather it is among "people," because "people" (nas, الناس) is the collectivity of humanity. If they strip themselves of the method of heaven, they are equal, and the one with cunning prevails, or the one with strength prevails, or the one with numbers or equipment prevails.

But what compensates for all those capabilities and achieves victory? If you take God on your side, no creature will dare to stand against the Truth in battle. We have said in the past, and must understand it well: when a small child is oppressed by his peers, he runs to his father's embrace; then each of them goes his own way, but his peers can defeat him when he is away from his father. How much more so are we the dependents of God? Likewise is the case of the disbelievers with the believers.

The disbelievers are able to isolate the believers when the believers abandon the method of God, because God will not give victory to people who are not upon His method. If God gave victory to people upon other than His method, that would nullify the matter of faith. When we survey the noble Qur'an, we find that every report about the human being when isolated from the divine method is a report entirely of evil.

He, glorified is He, says:

﴿By time. Indeed, mankind is in loss.﴾ [al-'Asr: 1-2]

Indeed, mankind in general is in loss. But who is it that is saved from loss? The answer comes from the Truth, who says:

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience.﴾ [al-'Asr: 3]

The matter is confirmed in another place in the noble Qur'an, where He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious. When evil touches him, he is distressed. And when good touches him, he is withholding. Except for the observers of prayer.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 19-22]

Thus every statement in the Qur'an about the human being in general comes from the side of evil. And what saves him from that? It is the divine method.

Thus the Truth's saying: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾ carries a rebuke and a light sting for those who declared faith but lagged behind the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) command at Uhud.

After that the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And that God may know those who believed and take from among you martyrs, and God does not love the wrongdoers.﴾

In a time of victory you find even the one who did not take part in the battle wanting to include himself among the victors.

But in a time of defeat, the Truth becomes manifest, and whoever remains on the side of defeat, acknowledging that he took part in bringing it upon the Muslims — and even if he did not take part, he either excused or blamed the one who was the cause of it — he nevertheless shares in bearing its burdens and its harmful effects, and bears and shares in the responsibility; in this way he is truthful.

Someone may say: does God not know those who believed? No. He, glorified and exalted is He, knows those who believed whether or not a battle occurs. But God's eternal, unseen knowledge is not the proof we see, and therefore the proof is not manifest among us. However, when God's knowledge comes forth into existence before us, it becomes knowledge by which proof is established clearly against the one who believed and against the one who did not properly believe, so that no one may claim for himself that he would have acted, but the opportunity did not come to him.

Thus test situations and trials come, so that each of us may know himself and the proof may be established against us all. So: there is a difference between God's eternal knowledge of things as they will happen, which does not establish proof against us, and... [the passage ends here]

Afterwards, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe...﴾

Tamhis (purification through testing) differs from mahq (total annihilation), because tamhis is the cleansing of things and the separating of them from harmful elements, whereas mahq is the removal of them entirely.

Then the Truth says after that: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strive and made known those who are patient?﴾

Faith is not merely a word spoken in this way; rather, there must be a trial that proves you have been tested (futintum) and have succeeded in the test, and fitna (trial, test) is examination. So do not think that the matter will pass easily, and that it will suffice of you to say, "We carry the call of truth." No. If you are truthful in your saying, it is incumbent upon you to be an example (uswa) when the truth is weak; for truth when it is strong does not need an example. Rather, the cause of true faith needs an example at the time of weakness. And entering Paradise has a test which the believer must pass.

And the Truth says: ﴿And that Allah may know those among you who strive and may know the patient﴾. When we hear that, we must know that Allah knows, with eternal knowledge (ʿilm azali), who the striver is and who the patient is; but it is a knowledge by which proof is not established against others. When it occurs as a reality in the world, however, it becomes proof against others.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 143:

Then after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿And you certainly used to wish for death before you encountered it. Now you have seen it while you were looking on.﴾

Those people who had missed the honour of taking part in Badr had wished to go out with the Messenger to take part in the battle of Uhud. The Truth makes clear to them: Did you think that wishing for battles alone brings victory? And did you think that every battle the believers enter must necessarily end in victory? If you thought that the matter was victory merely by wishing, then this means that you entered the camp of faith for the sake of omen, good fortune and triumph. We want to know who it is that enters the camp of faith while he is one who sells his soul and counts his life as an offering in the way of God.

Now, if the matter passed smoothly, everyone would enter the camp of faith. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive and made evident those who are steadfast?﴾ So have you thought that you would enter Paradise without the Truth bringing out into the open what He knows unseen, and without it being translated into events that He causes to occur, so that it becomes a reality and a proof against you, and so that Allah, glorified is He, makes evident those who struggled, that is, those who entered the company of the Truth, and those who were patient under harm for the sake of the Truth.

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And you certainly used to wish for death before you encountered it. Now you have seen it while you were looking on.﴾ That is, what you used to wish for in the past has now come before you. For if the wishing had been sincere, you would have advanced toward death just as you advance toward life.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 144:

He, glorified is He, says after that: ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger; messengers have passed away before him...﴾

We know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has a first name, which is "Muhammad", and a second name, which we know from the Qur'an and which is found in the Injil: "Ahmad":

﴿And when Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming that which came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a Messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad." But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."﴾ [al-Saff: 6]

The name of the Prophet (ﷺ) "Muhammad" occurs in the Qur'an four times, and "Ahmad" occurs once.

The verse we are concerned with, in which the name Muhammad is mentioned, is: ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger; messengers have passed away before him.﴾ Let us also read the words of the Truth:

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, and ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40]

And His saying:

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds and believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad—and it is the truth from their Lord—He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition.﴾ [Muhammad: 2]

And here is the noble statement:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval.﴾ [al-Fath: 29]

The name is that which is established as a proper noun (ʿalam) for the named thing, such that when the name is mentioned, the named thing comes to mind. If two people in one environment share a name, then they must be distinguished by a description. If there are two boys in one family each named Muhammad, they must be distinguished by an attribute; and in the countryside we find someone called "Muhammad the Elder" and "Muhammad the Younger".

The word "Muhammad" and the word "Ahmad" share the same root, because both are from "ḥ-m-d" (ḥāʾ, mīm, dāl); the root is ḥamd (praise). However, the derivational orientation in "Muhammad" differs from that in "Ahmad", because a name, before it becomes a proper noun, if it is taken out of its original meaning, is loosed from its original meaning and becomes a proper noun for the person.

For this reason we may find a man who has a black slave-girl and names her "Qamar" (Moon), and a man may have a miserable slave whom he names "Saʿid" (Happy). When a name becomes a proper noun for something, it moves away from its original meaning and becomes a proper noun for the named thing; but people, when they name their children, glimpse optimism in that the original meaning becomes a reality.

The plain-faced girl whose owner names her "Qamar" has lost the beauty of the named thing, and therefore he wants her to take on the beauty of the name... When we look at the word "Muhammad" in its derivation, we find that it is one upon whom praise falls from others, just as you say: "So-and-so is honoured (mukarram)", meaning honour has fallen upon him from others.

And the word "Ahmad" we find to be one who is the subject of praise from others.

And when we say: "Mukarrim" (with a dammah on the mīm, a fatḥah on the kāf, and the rāʾ doubled and kasrah), meaning honour was bestowed by him upon others. We have two names of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Qur'an, and both are from the root "ḥamd". So "Muhammad" implies that praise has fallen upon him from others many times. But if the intention were that praise fell upon him without multiplicity in it, the name "Mahmud" would be the one applied to him alone.

As for "Ahmad", we have said that it implies that praise proceeded from him to others. And "Ahmad" corresponds to the elative form (afʿal al-tafḍīl): we say, "So-and-so is generous, and so-and-so is more generous than so-and-so." So "Ahmad" means one from whom praise proceeds to others abundantly; had praise proceeded from him in a limited measure we would say "Hamid" (one who praises). Thus "Ahmad" is an intensive form of "Hamid", one from whom praise proceeds to others abundantly, and so he became Ahmad. And "Muhammad" is an intensive form of "Mahmud", upon whom praise falls from others abundantly, and so he became Muhammad.

Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was granted by Allah both matters together: he is Muhammad from Allah, and Hamid to Allah; for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was granted by Allah two stations: the station of election (iṣṭifāʾ) and the station of striving (mujāhada). By election he was "Muhammad" and "Mahmud", and by striving he was "Hamid" and "Ahmad". So here we are before two stations of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am Muhammad, Ahmad, al-Muqaffi, al-Hashir, the Prophet of Repentance, and the Prophet of Mercy."

There will be more to say on this, and we are here dealing with reflections on the Battle of Uhud. After the archers departed from his command, and the enemy's counterattack came upon them from the Qurashi polytheists, the Companions then turned here and there to flee, and the polytheists massed upon the Messenger of Allah to such a degree that Ibn Qami'a took a stone and struck the face of the Prophet (peace be upon him), breaking his rabāʿiyya (a front tooth), and the two rings of the helmet were driven into the Messenger's cheeks, and blood flowed from him. The Messenger (ﷺ) tried to climb a rock on the mountain to ascend it but could not, so Talha ibn ʿUbaydullah sat beneath him and rose with him until he stood upon it. All of these are human struggles.

Was Allah not able to spare His Messenger all of that? Indeed He, glorified is He, is able. But all of that was an honour from Allah, and He, glorified is He, did not wish to deprive His Messenger of the pleasure of striving. And so that Allah may make the believers know Muhammad, we say: Allah did not bring Muhammad to guide His creation to him, but to show every believer that the Messenger of Allah, when what happened to him happened, had tasted striving. Some fighters fled from the battle at Uhud, and the wind of defeat nearly blew upon the camp of faith. Behold, our master Abu ʿUbayda (may Allah be pleased with him) goes to the Messenger of Allah and finds the two rings of the helmet in his cheeks (ﷺ); so our master Abu Bakr tries to pull out the two rings of the helmet, and the Messenger (ﷺ) is pained; so our master Abu ʿUbayda says:

- "To you, O Abu Bakr! By Allah, leave me alone." And Abu ʿUbayda takes hold of one of the two rings and pulls it from the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his front tooth fell out; then he pulled out the other ring and its front tooth fell out too, so Abu ʿUbayda (may Allah be pleased with him) lost both front teeth. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said of him: "Every nation has a trustee, and the trustee of this nation is Abu ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrah." The blood of the Messenger (ﷺ) flowed, and our mistress Fatima, Allah inspired her, came with a piece of mat and burned it, took the remaining ash from the burning and applied it to the wound. Indeed Allah did not will to deprive His Messenger of the pleasure of striving.

Anas ibn al-Nadr came and found the Companions, among them ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and Talha ibn ʿUbaydullah, who had cast down what was in their hands; Anas asked them: "What makes you sit?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been killed." He said: "Then what will you do with life after him? Rise and die upon what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died upon." Then he faced the polytheist host and fought until he was killed.

These are all positions that would not have come into being and appeared except in this battle. ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger﴾ meaning: listen. This is Muhammad, and this is his rank; he is a Messenger from Allah who came after ʿIsa ibn Maryam, and it was necessary for us to know that the Messenger (ﷺ) emphasised his humanness. ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾

Did the followers of the earlier Messengers turn back on their heels when their Messengers died? How then will you be lesser in standing than these nations? Suppose that it had happened; why should the good which the Messenger of Allah conveyed to you not remain until the Day of Resurrection? The man who has done good dies with his death; would he then have done anything? No; whoever wishes to do good must do good that will outlast him.

Therefore failed leaderships are those in which the individual is a leader, then he dies, and we look for a leader after him and find none, and we ask: why did the leader strangle his companions and colleagues? Was he afraid of them? And we keep wishing that the leader had raised people who, when he departed, would produce someone to succeed him; for no human being guarantees his life. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger; messengers have passed away before him.﴾

When you hear the noble words ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger﴾, this is a style called the style of restriction (qaṣr). He, glorified and exalted is He, restricts Muhammad to the messengership. So when Muhammad (ﷺ) is restricted to the messengership, this means that some of his contemporaries believed that Muhammad was greater than a messenger and would not die.

So Allah, glorified is He, made clear that Muhammad is a messenger, that messengers have passed before him, and that Allah will not make anyone immortal.

Did this escape the mind? Yes, this used to escape the mind, as evidenced by the fact that even after this verse was revealed and became a Qur'an recited, we find that our master ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), who had a pure nature that agreed with Allah's revelation, was a muhaddath (one inspired).

Behold, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and passed into the presence of Allah, said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has not died and will not die until he cuts off the hands and feet of many hypocrites." ʿUmar said that out of the horror of the calamity, and forgot the verse. Then our master Abu Bakr came and said: "Whoever worshipped Allah, then Allah is Living and has not died; and whoever worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad has died." And he recited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.﴾ ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "It was as if I had not recited it until that day."

Then after the Muslims had given the pledge (bayʿa) to Abu Bakr for the caliphate, ʿUmar said: "As for what follows, I said to you yesterday a statement, and it was not as I said; by Allah, I did not find the statement I made to you in a Book which Allah revealed, nor in a covenant which He made with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); but I was hoping that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would live until he managed our affairs. So Allah, mighty and majestic, chose for His Messenger what is with Him over what is with you. This is the Book with which Allah guided His Messenger, so hold to it and you will be guided as the Messenger of Allah was guided."

This gives us two matters:

The first matter: the Companions' love (ʿishq) for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The second matter: the need for faith; for love does not stand upright and must not take us out of the bounds of the faith-based conception. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "When I heard Abu Bakr recite this verse, I knew that my legs could not bear me, and I fell to the ground."

So His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And Muhammad is but a Messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾ means: do not raise his messengership, you believers, above what I have raised it.

The meaning of ﴿turns back on his heels﴾ is: returns. Is this return a return from the battle, or a return from the foundation of the legislation, the foundation of the religion, and the foundation of the messengership which Muhammad brought? It may be correct, and that is correct too. His saying, the Truth: ﴿If he dies or is killed﴾ is a clear statement; we have previously addressed death and killing, and we said that death and killing amount to one thing, which is the departure of life; however, departing from life sometimes occurs through the breaking of the structure in which the soul does not dwell except with its specifications; if the structure is broken and the soul does not find a suitable dwelling for it, it leaves it. But death in its absolute sense is that life departs.

Next, the Almighty turns us to a general matter, a matter for all people: ﴿It is not for any soul to die except by Allah's permission, at a term decreed...﴾

When you hear "ma kana" (ما كان), it means "ma yanbaghi" (ما ينبغي, "it is not fitting"). In our everyday speech we say: "ma kana laka an tadriba Zaydan" ("it is not for you to strike Zayd"), meaning that it is not fitting for you to strike Zayd. So His saying ﴿It is not for any soul to die except by Allah's permission﴾ may prompt the question: is death something within a person's choice? No, but the Almighty's expression carries an implication. When you say "ma kana li-fulan an yaf'ala kadhā" ("it is not for so-and-so to do such-and-such"), this means that so-and-so has the choice to do it or not to do it, and it is within so-and-so's capacity to act or not to act. As for the power of Allah, no one can say that.

We understand it on the assumption that the soul pushes itself toward destructive places. Yet it has no power to die except by Allah's permission. If the soul is the one that pushes itself toward destruction, and yet it cannot die on its own, then how much more so if it does not push itself toward destruction. Thus, if the soul desires death, it will not come except with Allah's permission. We find in the realities of life various forms of this.

We find one who is distressed by this life, because his faith-capacity cannot bear the trials and toil of the world, so he kills himself. He wants to flee from what he cannot repel by its causes. But the one who possesses a vast faith-capacity, whatever hardship or affliction meets him, says: "I have a Lord, and whatever my Lord has ordained for me, He is the Nurturer, the Wise, who knows my interest better than I know it, and perhaps this affliction is an expiation for me for a sin."

This is the opposite of one who flees from what he cannot repel by its causes, and so tries to kill himself. Each of us has seen or heard of some who want that, but they are rescued, and those who carry out Allah's will in rescuing them reach them: such as stomach pumping for one who swallowed poisonous tablets, or putting out a fire for one who set himself alight. The suicide wants death for himself, but if Allah does not permit it, Allah does not let him reach it. You may find a suicide who wants to shoot himself with a pistol, but the bullet does not fire; or another suicide who wants to hang himself with a rope fixed to the ceiling, but the rope snaps. Why? "None takes life but He who gave life."

Someone may say: "But there is the murdered person, whom another human kills." Here the popular proverb applies: "If the killer had been patient with the victim, the victim would have died on his own." The moment the soul departs the body's matter is appointed a limited term. Sometimes the moment comes without any cause, and a person dies a natural death, and his friends say: "He was with us just a little while ago." They forget that he died because he dies by a decreed term.

Therefore we find a person who seeks the health of life, goes to undergo some surgery, and during the surgery he dies.

May Allah have mercy on the Prince of Poets, Ahmad Shawqi, when he says on this:

"In death there is what overwhelms, and in its causes; every person is bound by the folding of his Book.

By your life, the lion's one who dies by its claw at the encounter is like one who dies by its fang.

If death sleeps toward you, every beneficial medicine suffices; if it does not sleep, medicine is among its tails."

When the Book is folded, the matter is finished, even when a person meets a lion: death by its fang is the same as death by its claw. If death sleeps away from a person, a tablet of medicine or a sip of water may cure him of his illnesses. But if death is awake, medicine and treatment may become a tail, an instrument of death. The killer has done nothing except break the constitution of the victim, and this is what he is punished for.

So the Almighty's saying ﴿It is not for any soul to die except by Allah's permission, at a term decreed﴾ states a general principle. The "decreed Book" is sometimes applied to the whole span of life, and sometimes to its final end, which is true death. The killer, when he breaks the victim's constitution, is only agreeing with the written term that Allah willed. But then why do we punish the killer? We punish him because he broke another human's constitution.

And the Almighty says: ﴿It is not for any soul to die except by Allah's permission, at a term decreed﴾. Note His saying ﴿by Allah's permission﴾: it shows us that Allah is the one who issues the permission. Permission may be given to angels to carry out this matter. That is why the Qur'an, when it addresses this matter, sometimes ascribes this process to Allah, saying, glorified be He:

﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep; then He withholds those for which He has decreed death, and sends the others until a named term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]

And another time the Qur'an ascribes this process to one angel:

﴿Say: The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you; then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ [al-Sajdah: 11]

And another time the Almighty ascribes it to messengers who assist the Angel of Death:

﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fall short.﴾ [al-An'am: 61]

The Almighty, glorified and exalted, is truthful in every report from Him, because every command that fixes the term is not the will of the one entrusted with ending the term; rather it is by permission from Allah, who determines that. And since every command has issued from Him, it is He, glorified be He, who takes the souls. After that, the angel who takes the souls, Azrael, has assistants; when he receives the command from Allah, he conveys the orders to his assistants so that each may carry out his task. Thus the final ruling on death returns to Allah.

The command of death passing to the angels by a message from Allah: this is the permission, and permission requires one permitted, and the permitted ones are the angels of death whom the Angel of Death has authorized; and the Angel of Death received the permission from Allah, glorified and exalted.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him of it﴾. So whoever desires the reward of this world, that is, seeks the recompense of his activity in it, takes it, even if he is a disbeliever:

﴿Whoever desires the hasty life, We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blamed and banished.﴾ [al-Isra: 18]

And the Almighty says in another place of the Qur'an:

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Shura: 20]

This ends the claim that the disbelievers' condition is better than ours, that the disbelievers are advanced while we are backward. Has there not been a period when believers were far advanced? Indeed there came a period when believers advanced, and they were ahead for a thousand years, and they were the first state in the world. The disbelievers used to call their own era and their states as living in "the ages of darkness." Why do you deny this? Because history came to us from their side, and they distorted it. That is why we say to them: we were advanced, and you, and history bears witness to that.

For this reason we have said: the believer in Allah must be jealous for Allah's causes; he must not leave Allah's causes to the disbeliever in Allah. Shall the disbeliever take up Allah's causes while you, O believer in Allah, leave the causes for him to take? No; because whoever worships Allah has more right to His secrets in existence. Our leaving them to take the scientific secrets and not competing with them in this field is a shortcoming on our part.

﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him of it, and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him of it, and We will reward the grateful.﴾ We note that the Almighty has used the word ﴿the grateful﴾ twice, and the Qur'an affirms this meaning. He, glorified be He, has given you causes; if the causes have brought you the matters of this world, then they deserve gratitude; and if they bring you a duty along with the causes, this duty will give you the good of the Hereafter, which is also deserving of gratitude.

After this theoretical discussion, ﴿It is not for any soul to die except by Allah's permission, at a term decreed﴾... He mentions what confirms its existence in the procession of faith that preceded you, because there is a difference between speech and the actual occurrence of what speech signifies. The reality of the saying preceded you, so He says: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, with whom were many devoted followers. They did not weaken for what afflicted them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor did they submit...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 146:

﴿And how many a prophet fought, along with him many devoted men (rabbiyyun kathir). Yet they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they grow feeble, nor did they abase themselves. And Allah loves the steadfast.﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّن﴾ (wa-ka'ayyin): they say it is for multiplication, like "kam" (how many). For example, when a person says to you: "Why do you shun me?" you say to him: "How many times have I visited you?" Your words "Kam zurtuka!" (How many times I have visited you!) outwardly take the form of a question, yet you do not mean to ask him how many times you visited him. Rather, you are telling him that he is the one who must say it, because by his own words he will acknowledge that you visited him much, so that his answer conforms to what you did. You would not say "kam zurtuka" unless you were confident that, if he wished to answer, he would say, "You visited me many times." Had you not been confident that he would say, "You visited me many times," you would not have said it. So when you say, "How many times I visited you, how much I favoured you, how much I comforted you, how much I honoured you," then "kam" comes for multiplication, and similar to it is "ka'ayyin," which is also for multiplication, as when you say, "Ya ma hasala kadha" (how often such-and-such has happened), where "ya ma" means "ka'ayyin."

And a friend may ask you, "How did this story happen?" and you say to him, "Like many a man who does such-and-such and such-and-such happens to him," meaning the matter is not strange, for your saying "ka'ayyin rajul" means it has spread widely. Both usages, "kam marra zurtuka" and "kam min marra zurtuka," are correct. The meaning is: many a prophet fought, and along with him were believers in his message, as happened with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His saying, the Truth, ﴿rabbiyyun﴾ means people who are jurists, understanding the ways of war; "rabbiyyun" also means followers who fight, and its meaning may extend to their method being divine, like "al-rabbaniyyun" (the godly ones).

His saying, the Truth, ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ﴾ (fa-ma wahanu) means they did not weaken. He intends by this to bring an example, as if He, glory be to Him, is saying: Why did you weaken in your stand at the Battle of Uhud while you were fighting with the Messenger of Allah? It would have been fitting for you that your zeal in fighting alongside him should be greater than the zeal of any followers of a prophet with their prophet, because he is the Seal of the Prophets, who will establish the principle upon which the Hour will stand, and no one will come after him. So you ought to have been zealous, for you are the best nation brought forth for mankind, and I have reserved you for that.

The Truth gives them this example, which contains a rebuke and a reproach to them, and in this statement there is also instruction. He says: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِيٍّ﴾, that is, and many prophets ﴿قَاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمْ﴾. From the word ﴿وَهَنُواْ﴾ we draw the meaning that they did not weaken. It is as if something that causes weakness had happened in the fighting: ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمْ﴾, that is, no setback befell them as it befell you.

﴿وَمَا ضَعُفُواْ وَمَا اسْتَكَانُواْ﴾. Each of ﴿وَهَنُواْ﴾, ﴿ضَعُفُواْ﴾ and ﴿اسْتَكَانُواْ﴾ has come in its correct place, because "al-wahn" (weakness) is the beginning of weakness, and its seat is the heart, from which it seeps into the limbs as weakness.

And what does ﴿اسْتَكَانُواْ﴾ mean? It derives from "sakana" (to be still), and stillness is the opposite of motion. War requires motion, and whoever comes to war needs advance and retreat. As for one who does not move, this means he has no capacity to move. When you hear the alif, sin and ta' (alif-sin-ta') followed by a word, we know that the alif, sin and ta' indicate seeking, as in "istafham," meaning he sought to understand, and it comes to seek the matter that follows it. We say "ista'lama," meaning he sought to know, or "istakhbara," meaning he sought information. "Istakana" means he sought to have kawn, that is, existence. It is as if they reached such a degree of weakness and feebleness that they sought merely to have existence, because existence is manifested by motion, and motion has ended. This is the meaning of ﴿اسْتَكَانُواْ﴾.

Since it is from "kawn," its pattern, as the morphologists say, would be "istaf'ala," meaning seeking existence and seeking being. But its pattern may not be so if it is from "sakana," and in this respect the seeking element would not be present, because the sin would be original, so its pattern would not be "istaf'ala" but "ifta'ala." So does "istakanu" mean they sought stillness? No, because they were already still; therefore it is more appropriate that its meaning is that they sought mere existence. This is what I incline to and prefer. It has also been said regarding its meaning: they did not submit or abase themselves; from "istikana," which is humiliation and submission.

﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَمَا ضَعُفُواْ وَمَا اسْتَكَانُواْ وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ Whatever trial befalls a servant is from Allah, and in the hadith: "When Allah loves a people, He tests them." All that weakness and feebleness does not distract them from the battle, for if they had been patient in enduring, Allah would have supplied them with aid from Him, because when the causes of creation are exhausted and come to an end, the provision of the Creator arrives.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, draws our attention by concluding the verse with: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾, that is, it is sufficient reward for patience that you are beloved to Allah. For we said earlier: we may love Allah for the blessings He bestows upon us, but the matter is not that you love Allah, rather that by applying His method within you, you become beloved to Allah. It has been related from some of them the saying:

"Have you not seen that many love the blessings but are not loved (by Allah)?!"

You love the blessings, but you want to be loved by Allah, because your love of blessings is not sufficient; such blessings are taken by the disbeliever too, so there is another need. There is a first and a last: the first is the blessings of life, in which all people are partners, believer and disbeliever alike; but the last is the reward of Allah in the Hereafter, and that is the essential.

So, if people had grasped the words of Allah, ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾, they would have said: it is sufficient reward for patience that we be beloved to Allah, when a calamity befell them. It is true that the affliction did not produce in them weakness, feebleness or abasement, and this means that in them there is a remnant of certainty in Allah.

That remnant of certainty in Allah makes them worthy of Allah's support. So you have no choice but to be patient in your situation, that you may come to know Allah's aid to you. Allah's aid to you is truly manifest only at the time of weakness, for at the time of your strength you may act like those of whom it was said:

﴿فَإِذَا مَسَّ الإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَانَا ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلْنَاهُ نِعْمَةً مِّنَّا قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 49]

But the believers, when a calamity befell them, ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُواْ﴾ (did not weaken), because they were alert to a matter of faith: that Allah does not leave you to yourself except when you are absent from Him. So they said: "Why has this happened to us?" They did not say, "Our Lord, help us so that we may come out of weakness." Rather, they reflected on the causes that led them to this: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ ربَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 147:

﴿And their only words were that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, and make firm our feet, and give us victory over the disbelieving people."﴾

So what happened appears to be the result of a sin that had preceded it, and they realized the cause. It was supposed that they were in a battle, and this battle exhausted and wore them out. It is true that they did not weaken, and it was supposed that they would say: "O Lord, grant us victory first." No. Rather, they said: "We must know the cause of the first setback. The cause of this setback is that God does not hand me over to any soul except because I have forgotten Him."

﴿And their only words were that they said: "Our Lord"﴾, ﴿"Our Lord"﴾. Note the word of address in ﴿"Our Lord"﴾. They could have said: "O Allah." Why did they use the word "Rabbana" ("Our Lord")? Because the servant's relationship with lordship (rububiyyah) precedes his relationship with divinity (uluhiyyah). Divinity imposes obligation: the meaning of "ilah" is "one who is worshipped" (ma'bud), and as long as He is worshipped, He has an obligation that is to be obeyed; this obligation comes afterward. He, glorified is He, has His lordship in creation before He imposes obligations. Since the Lord is the One who undertakes nurture and upbringing, it would be more fitting to say "Ya Rabb." Thus their saying "Rabbana" means: You are the one who takes charge of our affairs, You are the One who nurtures us.

﴿"Our Lord, forgive us our sins"﴾. It is as if nothing befalls us except because of a sin of heedlessness that we have committed. From the word "dhanb" (sin) we know that one who grasps its meaning will never commit it, because the word "dhanb" is derived from the root "adh-dhanab" (tail). A "dhanb" is followed by a punishment; the word itself suggests that something will come after it, and when you remember the punishment for sin, you do not commit it.

﴿"Forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair"﴾. Because every act of disobedience is a transgression beyond what God has made lawful for you, and an addition that is not legitimate, even if it is of the kind God has made lawful. It is an excess beyond the necessities of your life. God legislated marriage so that children may come, and when we take more than this without marriage we have committed excess. God gave us wealth in proportion to our effort, so if we covet the wealth of others, we have committed excess. "Israf" (excess) means taking something that is not necessary for the sustenance of your life. For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]

He, glorified is He, clarifies: I have made lawful for you such-and-such women, so what made your eyes wander and incline toward what Allah has not made lawful for you? I have made lawful for you the earnings of your hand, and even if you are poor you will receive charity. Why did you commit excess? Therefore every matter that exceeds the limit required for the continuation of life is called "israf". ﴿"And our excess in our affair, and make firm our feet"﴾. They had begun to enter into the truth, but at first they saw falsehood, and falsehood is one of the causes for the Truth abandoning us in support first. But when God forgives the sin and forgives the excess in the affair, we become worthy of reinforcement and worthy of God's making us firm.

﴿"And make firm our feet"﴾. How can the Truth say this, when it is understood in battle that feet do not remain firm? Battle requires the fighter to be agile, roaming and moving. So what is the meaning of ﴿"make firm our feet"﴾? The Truth's saying ﴿"make firm our feet"﴾ means: do not make us flee from the battlefield, and do not let us ever leave the battlefield.

For this reason we have said that when what happened to the disbelievers happened, they did not remain on the battlefield, but left the battlefield and departed. As for these believers, although they were defeated, they remained on the battlefield for a period, turned back against their enemies and pursued them. Humanity has finally arrived at this meaning: in France there is a decoration they call "the fly decoration" (nishan al-dhubabah). Why the fly? Because if you drive a fly away from a place, it must return to it. Likewise, a commander who has withdrawn from an area should be determined to return to it, so they give him the fly decoration.

So His saying ﴿"make firm our feet"﴾: in what area? And in what battle? We must not leave our positions, because the moment we leave them, that is the first defeat, and this is a matter that emboldens the enemy against us.

﴿"And make firm our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people"﴾. The phrase ﴿"give us victory over the disbelieving people"﴾ is a justification (haythiyyah). Since they said ﴿"give us victory over the disbelieving people"﴾, they are therefore believers, and truly believers. For this reason, our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, made his famous statement: "You will be victorious over your enemy through obedience to Allah. If you and they are equal in disobedience, they will overcome you with their equipment and their numbers."

Therefore faith requires that you first pay attention to the point of weakness in you, which made what befell you necessary. Indeed, you did not weaken, nor did you give in, and some fatigue and pain from the battle afflicted you. It is as if the Truth is clarifying for us that they had become aware and first searched their souls well. They spoke of sins and asked for forgiveness, and spoke of excess against the self, and after that they spoke of the battle. So what was God's bestowal?

The answer comes in His saying, the Truth: ﴿"So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter..."﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 148:

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾

That is, whoever desires this world, Allah gives him from the world spoils and things. We should note that when the Truth (al-Haqq) speaks here about the world, He does not describe it with goodness or with anything else; He only said ﴿ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ (the reward of this world). But when He spoke about the Hereafter, He says ﴿وَحُسْنَ ثَوَابِ الآخِرَةِ﴾ (and the good reward of the Hereafter), and this is the beauty that ought to be loved, because the world, however long it lasts, is enjoyment, delusion, and a passing adornment, and however blessed you are in it, you are awaiting one of two things: either the blessing will be removed from you, or you will be removed from the blessing.

The Truth concludes the verse with His words ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ (And Allah loves the doers of good). They did good when they whispered to their Lord after what had afflicted them. They asked for forgiveness, and they asked that He forgive them their excesses in their affair, that He make their feet firm, and that He grant them victory over the disbelieving people, because they saw that their human strength, when the support of Allah is withdrawn from them, becomes mere dust with no weight.

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾ As we said regarding patience: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ (And Allah loves the patient), it is enough as a reward for patience that you be beloved of Allah; likewise, it is enough as a reward for doing good that you be beloved of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 3, verse 149:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.﴾

As long as you are believers and they are disbelievers, how could it be possible for you to obey the disbelievers? You and they are different from the very first stage: you are believers and they are disbelievers. The disbeliever and the hypocrite will seize the opportunity of weakness in the believing Muslim soul and try to slip into it, just as we have said: a group of the hypocrites said, "Muhammad has been killed, and there is no longer a Messenger among us, so let us turn to the religion of our fathers." And the believers whom a moment of weakness had struck said, "Let us go to Ibn Ubayy, the foremost hypocrite in Madinah, and ask him to intercede for us with Abu Sufyan so that he may obtain safe-conduct for us."

Therefore the Truth says: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.﴾ So if the situation requires a helper, do not seek help from the disbelievers, but seek it from the One in whom you have believed. And the True Word descends: ﴿Nay, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 150:

﴿Nay, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Did not Abu Sufyan say: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no al-'Uzza"? Then the Prophet said to them: "Say to them: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector." When he said: "A day for a day" (i.e., the day of Uhud against the day of Badr), "war is a series of alternating turns" (sijal). 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) answered him and said: "There is no equality (la sawa')": that is, we are not like you; our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire. So how can it be equal, and how can it be alternating turns?!

﴿Nay, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾ We understand the words of the Truth: ﴿the best of helpers﴾, meaning that it is possible for Allah to make people, whether disbelievers or not, help you with a superficial help. We do not say that this is help; true help is only the help that comes from Allah. Why? Because help first comes from the side of Allah, so be assured that you are sincere and devoted to Allah, for otherwise His help would not come to you. So when the help of Allah comes to you, be assured of your own faith and that you are with Allah. The words of the Truth ﴿the best of helpers﴾ are evidence that it is possible for there to be a helper in the customs of mankind. The believers said: "O Lord, we are weak now, and if we do not go to someone to protect us, what shall we do?" So the Truth makes clear to them: be a faithful camp facing the camp of disbelief, and beware of seeking refuge with those who disbelieve in your Lord, for they cannot be trusted with you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 151:

And if you wish to know what I will do: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. So if terror is cast into the hearts of the disbelievers, what benefit is their number to them? Their numbers and their wealth become yours to possess, and they become spoils and booty.

Indeed, the Truth cast terror into their hearts in fact. When they told Abu Sufyan: "Muhammad is coming toward you with a dense army from Madinah, and men who had never fought before have joined him, and he is coming to you at Hamra' al-Asad," what did Abu Sufyan and his people do? God cast terror into their hearts and they fled.

The word ﴿We will cast﴾ (sanulqi) is derived from "al-ilqa'" (casting), which can only occur with a material substance and a location. The Qur'an clarifies this matter when it says: "And he cast down the Tablets" (fa-alqa al-alwah). This is a material need. God says:

﴿And he threw down the Tablets and seized his brother by the head, drawing him toward himself. He said: "Son of my mother, indeed the people have oppressed me"﴾ [al-A'raf: 150]

This is a material matter. We say: "He threw the stone." And the Exalted says:

﴿So they threw down their ropes and their staffs and said: "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed we are the victors"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 44]

These are ropes, which is a material matter. And the Exalted says concerning the revelation to the mother of Musa:

﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa: "Suckle him, and if you fear for him, then cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers"﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]

So casting (al-ilqa') is a material matter, as if God wished to make the meaning, which is terror, widespread, so He said: "I will gather the terror and place it in the heart, and its action will be material." When terror settles in the heart, faintness comes, and when faintness dwells in the heart, it spreads over all the limbs as feebleness. So He says: ﴿We will cast into the hearts of those who disbelieved terror﴾. It is as if He presents terror to us as a thing, while terror is an immaterial matter, namely fear of everything. So He clarifies that He will bring terror upon them and cast it into the heart, and it will remain there to produce faintness and abandonment.

﴿We will cast into the hearts of those who disbelieved terror﴾. Observe the expressions proceeding from God: here He comes with "the plural of majesty" (nun al-'azamah), ﴿We will cast﴾. We notice that when the Exalted speaks of a matter that requires action, He uses the "plural of majesty," as in His saying:

﴿Indeed, We: it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]

Because sending down the Reminder is a great undertaking, we use the "plural of majesty." For We will send it down with power, We will send it down with wisdom, We will send it down with knowledge, We will send it down with insight, We will send it down with self-subsistence, We will send it down with contraction, We will send it down with expansion. So His saying ﴿Indeed We﴾ is as if the plural of majesty comes here. But when the Exalted speaks of the Essence on High, He says: "Indeed I am God." He did not say "we." Yet in the matter of sending down He says:

﴿Indeed We sent it down in the Night of Decree﴾ [al-Qadr: 1]

Because this is a great and sublime undertaking, the "plural of majesty" comes with what is an event that is done; and this event that is done requires many attributes. That is why we say when you begin any work: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Why? Because the work you will do requires power over it, requires knowledge before you do it, requires wisdom; that is, it requires many attributes. So you enter upon the work in the name of the Powerful who empowers you, in the name of the Knowing who teaches you, and in the name of the Wise who judges you.

All these attributes converge in bringing the work into being, so that He may show mercy to you even in seeking help. He does not say to you: "Bring all the attributes your action needs," because there are attributes you do not know. So He says to you: "Bring the Name that gathers all the attributes of perfection." He said: "In the name of God," and it comprises all the attributes of perfection.

Thus you notice that when you see the "plural of majesty," which we call the "plural of union," we find that we say "we" for a group, or for a single speaker who magnifies himself. That is why we notice it even in human law; did they not say of kingship: "We, the King"? But this "nun" with respect to God is not the "nun" of the group. Rather it is the "plural of majesty," the majesty gathering all the attributes of perfection that any act requires. Therefore He, glorified be He, said: ﴿We will cast into the hearts of those who disbelieved terror﴾. So every heart in which there is disbelief requires the casting of terror into it. Thus the "plural of majesty" comes to encompass all these disbelieving hearts?

He, glorified be He, does not wrong them by casting terror, but they are the ones who deserved to have terror cast into their hearts. Why? ﴿Because they associated with God﴾ (bima ashraku). It is associating partners with God that brought them terror, because God acts, while the partners do not act. Had their partners been true, they would not have abandoned them. So why did they not bring their partners to help them? Terror came to them because they have no protector; and had they had powerful gods, as they claim, they would have said to those gods: "The Lord of Muhammad acts with us thus; why do you not stand against him, O our lords?" But they associated with God what neither harms nor benefits, rather its harm is nearer than its benefit.

﴿For that they associated with God that for which He had sent down no authority﴾. Authority (sultan) is force, proof and evidence, derived from the root "sin, lam, ta'" (s-l-t'). We say: "So-and-so exercised authority (tasallata) over so-and-so," meaning he compelled him by his power over him. And they say: "So-and-so is sharp-tongued (sulaytu al-lisan)," meaning able to revile. So authority (al-sultah) is: coercion and power that compels action; and in matters of meaning it is argument and proof. The believers are always possessed of authority from God; for if they triumph materially, that is the authority of coercion, and if they are materially defeated, they have the authority of truth and proof. That is why we said earlier that Iblis will come on the Day of Resurrection and say:

﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]

We said that authority is of two kinds: either a power that coerces us into doing disobedience, or a proof and evidence that makes us do disobedience.

The difference between coercive force and the authority of proof is that coercive force makes you act while you are compelled and unpleased with the act. As for the authority of proof, it persuades you to act, so you have acted by your own consent. Thus sometimes authority means: a power that coerces you into the act while you are compelled.

Whereas the force of proof persuades you to act. So Satan comes to confess against himself in the Hereafter and says: ﴿I had no authority over you﴾, meaning: I have no power that coerces you into disobedience, and I have no proof that persuades you until you commit disobedience. Neither this nor that. So what is the story then? He said: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me.﴾ That is: you obeyed me and responded to my call without any authority of force by which I compelled you to anything, nor any authority of proof by which I persuaded you.

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾. That is: the place to which they return is the Fire. The refuge (ma'wa) is the place to which you return. It is as if in this destination there is an intrinsic quality of the disbeliever that casts him into the Fire; so he, that is the disbeliever, has his refuge and abode to which he returns. That is why we must attend to His saying in certain constructions: "And to Him you are returned" (wa-ilayhi tarji'un) and His saying: "And to Him you are returned" (wa-ilayhi turja'un). ﴿And wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾. That is: an abode after which there is no escape forever. Every abode it is permissible for us to leave, but the abode that will remain as eternity for the wrongdoers is the Fire, and it is a wretched abode.

And after that, the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love...﴾

We know that in ﴿صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ﴾ there are two maf'ulain (direct objects). The first is the pronoun of the addressees in His words ﴿صَدَقَكُمُ﴾, and the second is the word "wa'd" (promise), which is made genitive by the pronoun referring back to the Name "Allah." So He, glory be to Him, has brought about a promise, and the reality came in accordance with what He promised. The Truth said:

﴿If you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm﴾ [Muhammad: 7]

And He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will be the victorious﴾ [As-Saffat: 173]

The two verses affirm a matter of promise. After that came the practical application. Did the promise come to pass or not? It did. And when? Does the Truth, in this verse, refer to the Battle of Badr?

﴿إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ "Tahussunahum" means you remove their sense (hiss) from them. The "hiss" is the five senses, and the meaning of "I removed his hiss" is that I deprived him of those senses. ﴿إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ﴾ happened, and you gained power over them: you killed them and took them captive. Or "hiss" is the sound that comes out of a person, and as long as the hiss is gone, it means he has ended. ﴿إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾: when you were true to your meeting with your enemy in accordance with Allah's method, Allah was true to His promise. This was at Badr.

As for here, at Uhud, His words have come to you: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ﴾, meaning you became cowardly. ﴿وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُمْ﴾, meaning you disobeyed the Messenger's command, ﴿مِّن بَعْدِ مَآ أَرَاكُمْ مَّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾, which refers to the spoils. ﴿مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الآخِرَةَ﴾. It is as if He, glory be to Him, is giving us a lesson from two battles: a battle in which Allah's promise was fulfilled and you actually won, and also Allah's promise was fulfilled when you abandoned the Messenger's command and what happened to you happened. So the matter is laid out before you through practical experience, not through theoretical speech alone, nor through verses only, but through reality.

Or the whole matter revolves around Uhud. Let us suppose, for argument's sake, that it revolves around Uhud, and leave Badr aside: when you, O Muslims, first entered the battle, did you gain victory or not? You did gain victory. Talhah ibn Abi Talhah, who was carrying the banner of disbelief, was killed, he and about twenty-some others. The banner of disbelief fell at the beginning of the battle, and the banner-bearer was killed. This is what His saying, the Exalted, clarifies: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter﴾. A group said: "Let us remain on the battlefield," and another group said: "Let us withdraw." You saw the spoils, and so such-and-such happened among you. Then the setback came. Had what happened not happened, you would have had the right to doubt this religion. So what happened is evidence of the truth of this religion, and that if you abandon one of the methods of Allah, your fate will inevitably be failure, disappointment and defeat.

﴿حَتَّى إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الأَمْرِ﴾: a group said, "We will remain as the Messenger commanded us," and a group said, "We will go for the spoils." ﴿مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الآخِرَةَ﴾. Since you disputed, and one group said, "Let us hold to our positions," and another group said, "Let us go for the spoils," then whoever wanted to continue fighting was in fact seeking the Hereafter, and the spoils did not distract him. And the group that wanted this world said, "Let us go for the spoils."

Regarding this matter, Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By Allah, I did not know that any of the companions of the Messenger of Allah wanted this world until there was revealed concerning us what was revealed on the Day of Uhud."

That is, he could not imagine that among the Companions there were those who wanted this world. Rather, he thought they all wanted the Hereafter. When Allah's saying was revealed, ﴿مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ الآخِرَةَ﴾, Ibn Mas'ud realized that among the Companions there were those whom changing circumstances affected. This does not diminish them, because they had seen victory and thought the matter was over: the banner of disbelief had fallen, and the believers had killed a number of the chieftains of Quraysh. Allah pardoned the believers and forgave them what had proceeded from them of opposition to the command of His Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ﴾ Yes, because you were occupied with fighting them before you looked at the spoils. When you looked at the spoils, your gaze turned toward what your worldly desire sought, and so you turned away from them. You did not finish them off, and their defeat and subjugation were not completed for you. ﴿ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ﴾. Your being tested in this battle was only a training and drill in the method, as if it were a battle intended for testing, so that you would see from it everything that happened. After that, the experiment succeeded: after this battle, the Muslims were never defeated in any battle.

For this reason they say: "A lesson that teaches victory in much is not considered a defeat in little." An example of this: suppose a child failed a year, then bore the humiliation of failing. We find that because of it he attains a distinguished rank afterward among the top ten. So his first failure was good for him.

﴿وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنْكُمْ﴾ Because you also had a point of view when you imagined the battle was over, with the fall of the banner of disbelief, the killing of Talhah ibn Abi Talhah, and the killing of some chieftains in the enemy camp. So you thought the matter was finished. But you should have remembered that the Messenger had told you: "Hold your positions and your places, even if you see us following the people to Makkah, and even if you see them entering Madinah."

Is there any warning more than that? ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. Glory be to Him, the Most High, did not expel them from the enclosure of faith by this wise statement.

Then the Truth (Allah) says, after that: ﴿When you were climbing up and not turning aside for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you...﴾

﴿When you were climbing up and not turning aside for anyone﴾ Here He brings them a snapshot from the battle, so that when each one of them hears these words he recalls the shameful scene that should not have occurred: ﴿when you were climbing up﴾. There is "taṣʿadūn" and there is "tuṣʿidūn," and here it is ﴿tuṣʿidūn﴾ from "aṣ'ada." "Aṣʿada" means to go down into the ṣaʿīd, and the ṣaʿīd is level ground, since that helps you in speed of flight. Whereas "ṣaʿida" requires that there be a high place to climb up to. At the moment they wanted to flee, they ran and walked toward the easy, flat ground, each one not wanting to stumble here or there. So the fitting description is ﴿when you were climbing up and not turning aside for anyone﴾, for the fugitive does not look here or there; there is nothing before him but the easy ground.

﴿And not turning aside for anyone﴾ means you did not pause for anything. More important still, there was a warning from the Supreme Commander, who is the Messenger (ﷺ), who was calling you: ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾, that is, calling out to you from your rear, demanding that you return to the field of battle. ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief.﴾ You caused grief to the Messenger (ﷺ) by disobeying his commands, so God placed you in this position.

The word ﴿fa-athābakum ghamman bi-ghamm﴾ seems to say: He punished you. But He, glory be to Him, presents it wrapped in the tenderness of divinity: ﴿fa-athābakum﴾. So it is a reward... that is, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, by His lordship and His divinity, knows that these are believers, so He was not harsh with them. He said ﴿fa-athābakum ghamman bi-ghamm﴾, as if what happened to you was a settling of a right.

﴿So that you would not grieve over what escaped you﴾: had the matter of grief, disgrace and humiliation not occurred, the matter that you lost the spoils and the victory would have occupied you, and your concern would have remained with the spoils, because they were the cause of this. It is as if the grief that occurred came to remove from your hearts the pang of longing for the booty. And [He also made you not grieve] over what befell you of killing and defeat: ﴿so He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you or over what befell you, and God is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ That is, He, glory be to Him, measures what took hold of you, because it is possible that ﴿and the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾ they did not hear the call because of the terror of the battle. ﴿And God is Acquainted with what you do﴾: He, glory be to Him, is aware of every deed and every feeling.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 154:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿Then after the distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a group of you, while another group was concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah...﴾

The word ﴿sent down﴾ indicates that this is a gift from on high, having nothing to do with material causes or human laws. Sleep is a condition that befalls living beings. This condition requires chemical processes within you, and until now they do not know what these chemical processes are. The most that has been understood about it is that it is a self-restraint (radd dhati) of the human body. It is as if the moving apparatus composed of a brain that works, an eye that sees, an ear that hears, and senses and movement, this apparatus has energy; when the energy runs out, it does not say to you: "You are the one who stops working." No, rather it says to you: "I am no longer fit for work." It is a self-restraint, just as they now wish to reach it in the field of machines, by simply cutting off the electric current automatically from those machines, and they stop.

Thus self-restraint is in sleep, and drowsiness comes upon you. Scientific research has shown that there are things in the body that are not expelled as waste, but rather need to be balanced and chemically equilibrated. We know that there are residues as a result of movement, and there is combustion of energy, and every movement involves combustion, and the residues of this combustion come out sometimes as urine, sometimes as feces, sometimes as mucus, and so on. Therefore many of these wastes are the result of combustion processes, but there are things we do not want to be expelled, but rather we want them to be balanced. When you sleep, you have no movement, and the chemicals within the body begin to balance, and this is what the sleep that your material causes require does for you.

The one who is troubled and grieved never sleeps at all; he forgets himself and wears out his body even more, and the calamity becomes great upon him. Here the Truth sends down His grace upon you by sleep, because your causes do not help any of you to sleep.

You remember from long ago that we said: when Imam 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, became famous for issuing fatwas, and whenever they asked him about a matter he gave a fatwa on it, they said: "Let us bring him a complicated question and see how he gives the fatwa." It was as if they forgot that he issued fatwas because he was raised in the bosom of prophethood. Prophethood came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while Sayyidina 'Ali was still young, whereas the other Companions, prophethood came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they were advanced in age. So there was information that had entered them from the days of the Jahiliyyah, but Sayyidina 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, no information from the information of the Jahiliyyah had entered him. All the information he had was prophetic, so all this interaction gives rise to fatwa; therefore he was swift in issuing fatwas.

For example, a woman came to him and said: "O son of Abu Talib, how do they give me a dinar out of six hundred? My deceased left six hundred dinars, and they gave me one dinar." He said to her: "Perhaps he died leaving a wife, two daughters, and a mother. The wife takes the eighth (seventy-five dinars), the two daughters take two-thirds (four hundred dinars), and the mother has the sixth, which is one hundred dinars.
