And perhaps he had twelve brothers and one sister, full or paternal, and you are this sister, and there remains from the estate twenty-five dinars to be distributed among the twelve brothers and the sister, so your share is one dinar."

How did he know that? It is the precision of calculation in one who was educated in the House of Prophethood.

In the verse we are contemplating, we find that the Truth sent down drowsiness upon them to give them security, so the sleep did not arise here from an act of choice, but Allah sent it down. The meaning of "sent it down" is that He sent a new mercy from the heavens to bring out the people who had been afflicted with grief over what they had done in their situation. Therefore Abu Talha said: "Drowsiness overcame us while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud, so the sword would fall from one of us, then he would take it, then it would fall and he would take it again."

So it is a compulsory process. Drowsiness, when it descends from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, is a process of rescue from a movement that the human soul had missed its opportunity for, so Allah compensated them. But the hypocrites, what was their state? There is no doubt that those who came as hypocrites were not afflicted with grief over what happened. Rather, on the contrary, joy or contentment over what happened must have befallen them, and these are not fit for Allah to send down upon them the security of drowsiness. Rather, Allah leaves them to themselves, because they were not in the fortress of Allah by following the method of Islam, or at least by sincerity to the idea of Islam; Allah hands these over to themselves.

Thus security of drowsiness will not be sent down upon them. And since security of drowsiness will not be sent down upon them, they have become in anxiety. Why? Because their souls have concerned them. The person who believes and accepts Islam from his Lord has sold his soul to his Lord, and since he has sold his soul to his Lord, the faith transaction must continue. If the Muslim wakes up once for his own self, we say to him: "You have gone back on the contract of the sale." And since you have gone back on the contract of the sale, Allah, who had bought, leaves you to yourself. So His saying ﴿their own selves concerned them﴾ means they departed from the transaction of faith, because the one who concludes a transaction of faith with his Lord is the one of whom Allah said:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise from Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is truer in fulfilment of his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction you have contracted. And that is the great triumph.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111]

Since Allah has purchased from the believer his self, the believer must not be concerned for his self; he enters the battle with the transaction of faith. If his self concerns him, anxiety, confusion, agitation begin, and he imagines things, and he imagines one thing in a thousand ways. So his self becomes unsettled, and as long as a person is preoccupied with concern for his self, even if drowsiness were a response to a natural matter from the self itself, drowsiness will never come.

Therefore we find that Imam 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him and honour his face, when he was asked about the strongest of Allah's soldiers, extended his hands and said: The strongest of Allah's soldiers are ten: the firm mountains, and iron cuts the mountains, so iron is stronger than mountains; and fire melts iron, and water extinguishes fire, and the cloud subjected between heaven and earth carries the water, and the wind moves the cloud, and the son of Adam overcomes the wind by covering himself with a garment or something and proceeds to his need, and intoxication overcomes the son of Adam, and sleep overcomes intoxication, and concern overcomes sleep. So the strongest of Allah's soldiers is "concern."

So when concern enters the human soul, that is the strongest of Allah's soldiers, because concern enters the human soul in many forms for one matter, so it imagines complicated matters in one issue, and centred on one aspect, yet concern roams with it through every aspect. These people, their own selves concerned them, and as long as their selves concerned them, they departed from the transaction of faith. And as long as they have departed from the transaction of faith through which Allah purchased the selves of the believers, Allah abandons them. And as long as Allah has abandoned them, they must face their fate.

Anxiety and agitation dominate them, and they are struck with terror at everything. But the condition of the first category and the first group is different: Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, treats them as one who remains in the transaction of faith, even if their human souls have interpreted the events incorrectly, so they thought the matter in the battle was over, so they went to take the spoils. Allah honoured their remaining sincere to Islam, and disciplined them for their interpreting the events in a way that was not true, so He rewarded them with grief for what they opposed, and sent down security upon them for their sincerity in the cause of Islam.

﴿And a group who were concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾. When you hear the word "ṭā'ifah" know that it means a group, but this group has special characteristics that bring them together upon one idea, as if they circle around it. It is not any group, but a group revolving around one idea. The wise word comes here to show you what they said in their souls, and since they said in their souls, did anyone hear them? No, but Allah informed of it, and informed of what is in all their souls with one statement, which indicates that they circle around one idea. The spontaneous inner sense makes them say one sentence: ﴿Do we have any say in the matter?﴾ And since they would say in their souls, who heard them while they were a group? It is Allah, Glorified: ﴿And Allah knows what is within the breasts﴾.

When you say "ṭā'ifah," you find that in the usage of the word it is singular, and when you pluralise it you say "ṭawā'if," but it is a singular word indicating a plural. So sometimes the singular is considered, and sometimes what the singular conveys of plurality is considered. This is not noticed except by the eloquent, who distinguishes between it as a singular word and what it indicates as a plural, and therefore you find this in the inimitability of the Qur'an, for the Truth says:

﴿And if two groups among the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9] When He says ﴿And if two groups among the believers﴾, He here brings the report: did they fight as two or as a plurality? He, Glorified, says ﴿fight﴾ in the plural. The expression "two groups" but the rhetorical precision noticed that each group is composed of a company. ﴿And if two groups among the believers fight﴾, so what do we do? ﴿Then make peace between them﴾. So once He returned to the group, and once He returned to the two. In the hour of fighting, a group does not stand with one sword and strike one blow; no, in the hour of fighting each member of the group has a task. So the individuality constituting the group is multiple.

But when we make peace, do we bring every individual of this group and every individual of the other group, or do we take this group represented by its heads and the other group represented by its heads, and conclude peace between the two groups? The precision of the Qur'an says: ﴿And if two groups among the believers fight, then make peace between them﴾, and after that the Truth returns to the dual, saying: ﴿But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them﴾, and peace is between a company represented by a leadership and another company represented by a leadership.

And the Truth's saying: ﴿And a group who were concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah, saying: "Do we have any say in the matter?" Say: "Indeed, the matter is entirely up to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you, saying: "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here"﴾. This statement indicates that it is a group revolving around one movement, and it indicates that the hypocrisy is an agreed-upon hypocrisy, and not every one of them is hypocritical in himself. No, it is a group of hypocrites, who have formed a company, have a particular policy, have a particular speech, and have unity of speech; you recognise them from the Truth's saying: {And a group who were concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth

Allah says next: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met—it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned...﴾

When we read the word ﴿istazallahum﴾ (اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ), we know that the prefix elements alif, sin and ta' (الهمزة والسين والتاء) indicate seeking (lil-talab), requesting what follows them. Like: istafhama (استفهم), meaning he sought understanding (talab al-fahm); musta'lama (استعلم), meaning he sought knowledge (talab al-'ilm); istaqwa (استقوى), meaning he sought strength (talab al-quwwa). And "istazalla" (اسْتَزَلَّ) means he sought slipping (talab al-zallal). The "zallal" (الزَّلل) means a stumble and a lapse, that is, a person falls into error. So Satan sought to make them slip.

﴿because of some of what they had earned﴾: it is as though Satan does not dare to make slip anyone among the believers unless he finds in them some laxity on one side. But the one who has no laxity, Satan cannot prevail over him. The moment a person gives himself some desire of the desires, Satan marks him, puts a sign on him, and says: "This one is weak; we can make him slip." But the one who, when he sees himself, does not obey his soul in any laxity, Satan never approaches him.

Therefore the soul (al-nafs) is the mount of Satan toward sins. In the noble hadith: "Indeed, Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs" (إن الشيطان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم). When Satan sees a person whose soul overcomes him in a need, Satan says: "This one has hope!" And he is the one through whom he runs like blood, as mentioned in the hadith. As for the committed person, whenever his soul suggests something to him and he refuses, Satan fears him. So Satan makes slip only the weak; therefore the one whose Lord is ever in his remembrance, Satan never dares against him.

Allah, glorified is He, has named Satan "al-waswas al-khannas" (الوسواس الخناس). He whispers to people, but he is a khannas: when Allah is remembered, he withdraws (yakhnis), that is, he draws back and hides. But he isolates you when he sees you cut off from your Lord. However, when you are with your Lord, he cannot prevail over you; rather he hides away and refrains from whispering when you seek refuge in Allah from him.

So His saying ﴿innama istazallahumu al-shaytan﴾ means: he sought that they slip as a result, because he knew they had done things in which they displayed and showed their weakness. ﴿innama istazallahumu al-shaytanu bi-ba'di ma kasabu﴾ And the phrase ﴿bi-ba'di ma kasabu﴾ ... it is as though Allah's saying ﴿and Allah has certainly pardoned them﴾ means that He did not seize them for all that they had earned, because our Lord pardons much. ﴿Indeed, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned, and Allah has certainly pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

Why ﴿Allah has pardoned them﴾? He pardoned them out of honor for the principle of Islam into which they had entered sincerely, but their souls grew weak in some matter, so He gives them a punishment in this, yet He pardons them; this is the right of Islam. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

Almighty Allah then says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers when they traveled throughout the land or were raiders, "If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed,"﴾...

To strive throughout the land (ḍarb fī al-arḍ) means to seek provision and to seek the bounty of Allah in the land, and to strive in His cause for the elevation of His word. The disbelievers attribute death, killing, and the events by which a person departs from life to what? To the fact that he traveled through the land or went out to fight in the cause of Allah. They said: "If they had not gone out, this would not have happened to them!" We shall respond to them and say to them: It is as if you have never seen a person die in his bed. It is as if you have never seen a person killed by a falling wall, or attacked by a camel, or struck by a stray bullet. Does everyone who dies or is killed become one who travels through the land for some purpose, or one who goes out to strive in the cause of Allah?!

So this is foolishness in reading reality. The Truth brought this to give us a picture of their judgment on things: it is a judgment not based on sound inductive principles. If we know that they are disbelievers, we say: this is their nature, because we find that their judgment is not correct regarding obvious matters, and since their judgment is not correct or true regarding the particular events that occur—if you know that they are disbelievers, then this is logical speech from their perspective—their way is that they do not verify their judgments, so it is no wonder, then, that they are disbelievers.

﴿Or were raiders﴾: ghuzzā is the plural of ghāzin (raider), like ṣuwwam and quwwam, meaning the plural of ṣā'im (fasting) and qā'im (standing). ﴿If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed—so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts.﴾ Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, depicts for them what they say in order to punish them with it. How? Because when they say, "If they had been with us, we would have prevented them from going out or being killed," then they themselves are the cause.

Thus we find that whenever they mention their slain or dead, they know that they erred, and this is a regret in their hearts. Had they referred this matter to the Supreme Truth, it would have brought them comfort and they would not have thrust themselves into a maze. This happens from them so that we also know their foolishness: they are foolish in all their movements and in the inductive reading of particular events, and foolish in deriving the universal faith principle; foolish in that they thrust themselves into and entered a matter that was not their concern. So our Lord, glorified and exalted, willed that this become a regret upon them.

﴿If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed—so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts.﴾ The principle of faith is ﴿And it is Allah who gives life and causes death﴾, meaning He is the One who grants life and the One who grants death. Neither traveling through the land nor going out in the cause of Allah is the cause of death. For this reason Khālid ibn al-Walīd, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I have witnessed a hundred battles or thereabouts, and there is not a spot on my body the size of a span without a sword-strike or a spear-thrust in it, and here I am dying on my bed like a donkey dies—that is, of his own nose [natural death]. May the eyes of the cowards never sleep."

And the poet says:
"Unquestionably, O you who rebuke me for attending the battle
and for witnessing pleasures: will you make me immortal?"
That is: O you who prevent me from attending war, can you guarantee me immortality and lasting survival if I refrain from fighting? The poet continues:
"If you cannot repel my death,
then leave me to hasten toward it with what my hand possesses."

The verse concludes with the Truth's words: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. It is as if they had reached such foolishness that they did not even conceal their disobedience, but made it a visible movement. This statement here is stronger than "Knowing," because "Knowing" would lead us to understand that they possess some measure of shame and conceal things; but the knowledge of Allah is what exposes them. No—it has become a clear movement, such that it is seen. Hence His words: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or you die, surely forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass.﴾

The one who is eager not to take part in the battle, for fear of being killed, what is it that makes this course of action seem preferable to him? He seeks good through life. And since he seeks good through life, then in his imagination his movement in life will bring him good, so he fears that he will die and leave that good behind. He has not possessed an insight of faith. We say to him: the good in your life is in proportion to your movement: strength, knowledge and wisdom. As for your enjoyment when you meet Allah as a martyr, it is in proportion to what Allah has of bounty and mercy, and these are gifts without limits. So you have lost for yourself the distinction between your power, your wisdom, your knowledge and your movement in earning, and what is attributed to Allah in all of that. For this reason Almighty Allah says:

﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or you die, surely forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass.﴾

Afterward, the Truth says: ﴿And whether you die or are killed, it is to Allah that you will be gathered.﴾

We may observe that the Truth's words in the first verse placed killing before dying, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die﴾. In this verse, He placed dying before killing, as He, majestic is His affair, says: ﴿And whether you die or are killed﴾. Killing was placed before dying in the first verse because it was revealed concerning the fighters, and the usual case with them is that whoever among them meets Allah and goes to his Lord does so more often by way of killing than by way of dying of natural causes. As for this verse, it was revealed to show that the destiny of all servants, and their return on the Day of Resurrection, is to Allah, exalted is He, and that most of them have their souls taken and their spirits removed from their bodies through death. Therefore, dying was placed before killing here. Thus every word and clause has come appropriate to its position. Indeed, it is the saying of the All-Wise, the All-Aware.

Then, after that, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them. And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter...﴾

As we can see, the verse begins with a declarative statement: ﴿So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them.﴾ It is as if He, glorified is He, were saying: Your nature, O Muhammad, is a nature suited to what is asked of you in this matter. They opposed you, they did not respond to you when you said: "Come to me, servants of Allah, come to me, servants of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah." This is something that vexes and angers. But it does not vex your nature or upset your disposition, because you were created, together with your community, upon mercy. He wants to soften the heart of the Messenger of Allah toward his community, which had afflicted him with grief. So He said to him: Beware of repaying them for this, because your nature is that you are merciful, your nature is that you are not harsh, your nature is that you are not hard-hearted. So do not depart from your nature in this matter. It is like when you say to someone, for example: "Your character is good," meaning: make it good in this too.

﴿So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them.﴾ That is, by what mercy You have deposited in you. When you say "by what mercy," you leave the matter vague, and when you leave a thing vague, it is as if it were something great. A thing is left vague either because it is very small or because it is very large. A thing that is very large lies beyond the level of perception, and a thing that is very small lies below the level of perception. Thus, very huge things, we see one side of them and not the other side, and a very fine thing we do not see at all. That is why they say: this thing is indefinite (nakira). This indicates sometimes magnification, sometimes belittlement, sometimes multiplicity, and sometimes paucity. If you consider that perception cannot encompass it because of its vastness, then it is abundant. If you see that perception cannot encompass it because of its subtlety and fineness, and that it is not within reach of sight, then it is little or fine.

So the words of the Truth ﴿so it was by a mercy﴾ originally mean: by a mercy from Allah with which you were created, you were gentle with them. Why does "mā" come here? You may take it as indefinite, meaning: by some mercy beyond the level of perception, a great mercy. Or you may say: "fa-bi-mā raḥmatin," with "mā" being a relative pronoun. It is as if the Truth were saying to him: by the mercy deposited in you by your Creator, which is suited to your mission among the community, you were gentle with them. Since that is your nature, be gentle with them in this matter, pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them.

This verse came after events that took place at Uhud. The first event: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged that he should not go out to fight the Quraysh outside Madina, but remain in Madina. Those who longed for martyrdom, those who longed for fighting, and those who wanted to compensate for what they had missed of the honour of fighting at Badr advised him to go out to them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their opinion, and put on his armour. When they sensed that they had advised the Messenger of Allah contrary to what he had already decided, they backtracked and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you wish, we will not go out." He said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet, when he has put on his armour, to take it off until he fights." Since he had prepared for war, the matter was settled. This is the first issue, which is the issue of consultation.

After that, Ibn Ubayy withdrew with a third of the army. This is the second issue. The third issue is the archers' disobedience of his command (ﷺ), and their leaving their positions, although the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had warned them against that. He had said to Abdullah ibn Jubayr, whom he had placed in command of the archers: "Keep the horses away from us with arrows. Let them not come at us from behind. If we are victorious or defeated, stay in your place. We shall not be attacked from your side." But they disobeyed the order of the Messenger of Allah. The fourth issue is their flight when it was said: "The Messenger of Allah has been killed." The fifth issue is that when he was calling them, they fled without turning back for anything.

All these events nearly left traces in the soul of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So it is as if Allah, glorified and exalted, is saying: I have created you upon a mercy that encompasses all these lapses. The mercy is from Me, and since mercy is bestowed by Me, I must have placed in you a capacity to bear every opposition from your community and your followers. Do not think that you were sent to angels. You were sent to human beings who err, mere humans among the creatures. So make this matter a lesson. I have made your nature upon mercy, and you yourself have asked Me for much good for your community. Among His mercy is that Jibril called out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Allah has heard the words of your people to you, and how they replied to you. Allah has sent to you the angel of the mountains, so that you may command him as you wish concerning them." He said: The angel of the mountains called to me, greeted me, and then said: "O Muhammad, Allah has sent me to you, and I am the angel of the mountains, so that you may command me by your command. What do you wish? If you wish, I will bring down upon them the two mountains (al-Akhshabān)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who worship Allah alone and do not associate anything with Him."

So I ask you for the mercy that I have deposited in your heart, which you have used in every field. By this mercy you were gentle with them, and by this mercy they gathered around you. They gathered around you for your good manners, your abundant humility, the beauty of your character, your kind smile, your consoling gaze, and your appreciation of the circumstances of each one of them. So much so that if any one of them placed his hand in yours, you did not withdraw your hand until he withdrew his. This is a lofty character. All of this I make a reason for you to overlook those lapses, and let your character embrace them and let your forbearance embrace them, because you are in the stage of nurturing and training. Nurturing and training do not require that you become angry at every slip that comes from them. Otherwise you would not be a nurturer or a trainer.

﴿And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you.﴾ Why? Because you would have taken them out of what they were accustomed to from the affairs of the Jahiliyya (pre-Islamic ignorance).

Whoever takes a person out of what he is accustomed to should not combine with that a harsh and rough manner, because such a person needs kindness and mercy. Do not combine upon him two things: condemning his action, and removing him from what he has become used to and attached to. That is why they say of the one who advises someone that advice is heavy, because advice means condemning the act in the one advised. When you say to someone: "Do not do this," what does it mean? It means that this act is bad. So since you are condemning his act, do not combine two things upon him. You have condemned his deed and taken him out of what he was used to. Then you advise him in what he dislikes. No, he needs gentleness and softness, so that you may draw out of him the ugly traits. We do this with ourselves when we find an illness that needs a bitter medicine, so we coat the bitter medicine in a sugar coating, so that it passes through the zone of taste without pain or discomfort, until it reaches the zone where the bitterness is not felt, because all feeling is in the mouth.

If you do this with material matters, then it is necessary that we apply this also to moral matters. Since advice is heavy, do not make it a dispute, and do not send it as a mountain. Lightness of expression conveys it for you without provocation or incitement, and with kindness that leads to acceptance.

By this you reach what you want. An example of this is the story of the king who saw in his dream that all his teeth had fallen out. He went to an interpreter to have it interpreted, and he said to him: "All your family will die." The interpretation did not please the king, so he went to another man, who said to him: "You will be the longest-lived of your family." It is the same interpretation. Since he will be the longest-lived of his family, then they will die before him. It is the same. That is why they said: "Truths are bitter, so borrow for them lightness of expression."

﴿And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you.﴾ So by mercy you were gentle with them, and with gentle speech they followed you, became attached to you, and loved you. And "al-fazz" (the harsh one) is the water of the paunch. When camels find water, they drink enough to last them a long time, and then when they find no water, they chew the cud from the water stored in their paunch and drink from it. In one of the battles, they found no water, so they slaughtered the camels and took the water from their paunches. The water from a camel's paunch is unpalatable. This is the meaning of "fazz." Since this causes discomfort, they called "roughness of speech" fazāza, and hardness of heart is that which produces roughness in words.

﴿And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you.﴾ It is a mercy with which you were created, O Messenger of Allah, from the Truth that sent you. By mercy you were gentle with them, and the effect of that appeared in their coming to you and their love for you, because if you had been the opposite of that, you would not have found anyone around you. So the precedents prove that this is your nature and your character: mercy and gentleness.

After that, "pardon them." We have said that "al-ʿafw" (pardon) is the complete erasure of a sin, and it differs from swallowing anger (kazm al-ghayz). Swallowing anger means that the matter is still present in your soul, but you do not punish for it, because you restrained your limbs and guarded your tongue. But the matter is still in your soul. Pardon, however, means that you erase the whole matter entirely. To confirm this pardon, you may say: "I, on my part, have pardoned."

No. The matter does not concern you alone, because you must also ask Allah to forgive them. It is possible for the one wronged to pardon, but my Lord and the Lord of the wrongdoer does not pardon in that way. So the Truth clarifies: you pardoned, and that is from you, but He asks you to ask forgiveness on their behalf, so that Allah does not punish them for what they did toward you.

﴿So pardon them﴾ this is specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And ask forgiveness for them﴾ because of what they did, and what followed from it of your defeat at Uhud and your wound and injury. Do not say: "I consulted them and obeyed them in consultation, and then what happened happened, so you dislike consulting them." Do not close this door despite what happened as a result of that consultation and that it was not in the interest of the battle. The lesson in this hardship is that Uhud should be a battle of discipline, a battle of refinement, and a battle of purification. So do not let it lead you to dislike consultation. Rather, you must consult them always. Since you have accepted pardon and you ask your Lord to forgive them, and asking your Lord for forgiveness may be done apart from them, then when you consult them about any matter after that, it is as if the first matter has ended. Since the first matter has ended, we have begun a new page and taken the lesson and admonition that will benefit us in many things afterward.

That is why, after this battle, you find that affairs proceeded on their victorious course, because the experience, teaching, and training had taken effect and borne fruit, to the point that our master Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), when the wars of apostasy (ridda) came, what did he do? He consulted his companions. Some of them said to him: "Do not do it." Did he hear their advice? No. He did not heed their advice; rather, he consulted them. So accepting advice has a ruling, and rejecting advice has a ruling. The important thing is that consultation takes place, and that we act upon the best of opinions. Consultation is the cross-fertilization of opinion with many views. That is why the poet says:

"Consult others when a calamity befalls you one day, even if you are among the people of consultations."

The poet has guided us to how to bring the meaning near to us. Even though a person may be one of the people of consultation, and people take his opinion, he should still ask others for opinion and consultation. Why? Here the poet completes the advice:

"The eye sees what is near and what is far, but it cannot see itself except in a mirror."

The eye sees the near thing and the distant thing, but this same eye is unable to see itself except in a mirror. Likewise is the matter concerning others that is presented to you: your mind looks at it with balance and without emotion, because you have no desire in it, and the truth is what attracts you. But your own personal matters may be entered by your desire, which makes them seem sweet and good to you.

So the consultation at Uhud had the result you know. It is as if Allah is saying to His Messenger: Beware that you take from the precedent of that consultation that consultation is not beneficial, so

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 160:

And after that the Truth says: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?...﴾

The Truth says here: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ The believers in whom? In Allah. And as long as they believe in Him, part of their belief is that He is a capable, wise God who knows what is in the best interest, and there is no better thing than that you rely on Him.

When we read ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you﴾, we may ask: what is the counterpart? The counterpart is ﴿and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ So you have entered upon the means that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has spoken of, obeying the command of the heavenly leadership that is represented in the Messenger who conveys from Allah, and you have taken your equipment according to your ability. Beware of comparing your number with the number of your enemy, or comparing your equipment with the equipment of your enemy; Allah does not require you to match number with number or equipment with equipment. Rather, He said: you prepare what you are able to. Why? Because Allah wants the caravan of faith to be accompanied by the help of the believer in Him; for if matters were measured only by their quantity, it would be strength against strength. But Allah wants the number to be small and the equipment to be less, and that we acknowledge and say: this is what we were able to do, O Lord. And we trust that You, O Lord, will add to the small number a reinforcement from Yourself, for You are the Highest Helper. So glorified are You, who said:

﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector.﴾ [Muhammad: 11] And the Truth here says: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you.﴾ So you are guaranteed Allah's victory if you have entered in order to help Allah.

How do we know that we are helping Allah? We know it when the result comes with our victory, for He, glorified is He, does not give a principle in the universe and then bring reality to contradict it; otherwise the Muslims would have been deceived, God forbid, for if the religion brought a principle and then reality came to refute it, they would have to say: reality has refuted that principle. But the Truth said: ﴿If you help Allah, He will help you﴾, and reality comes confirming this principle. Then we do not believe in this principle only, but we believe in everything that is hidden from us. When a material, tangible, sensed particular appears to prove to me the truth of the Qur'an on one matter, I do not content myself with this matter alone, but I say: everything I do not know falls within the scope of this matter.

For this reason we have said: the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has left some of His secrets in His universe, and these secrets that He has left in His universe are secrets that do not serve necessities; if we know them we benefit from them only a little in refinements, and the Truth leaves some secrets in the universe for the intellects to derive. Thus a thing at which the intellect used to stop in the past becomes, with the discovery of Allah's secrets, acceptable and rational. As if the thing at which the intellect stood previously was proven by the passing days to be true. So whatever is not known of things is taken by this principle, or by what has been taken from others.

They say, for example, that the microbe was discovered by "Pasteur." But was the microbe not existing before "Pasteur"? The microbe existed, and no one saw it, because a thing when it is minute and fine we cannot perceive it; we did not have the instrument that perceives it, and we had not yet invented the microscope that magnifies minute things thousands of times.

Likewise people invented the telescope: whereas a thing could not be seen because of its distance, it became visible through the telescope, and even if a thing is extremely tiny and we do not see it, we were able to see it through the instrument called the "microscope."

The "telescope" brings the distant near, and the "microscope" enlarges the small, so we see for it movement and life, and we find for it a domain in which it swims. This has made me, when the Qur'an tells me that Allah has a creation hidden from the senses that is not perceived, such as jinn and angels, not deny that, because there are things that existed and did not fall under my senses or my perception, although they are of my own substance. So if other things are of another substance, such as the angels of light or the jinn of fire, and He, glorified is He, tells me that they are created and existing, I do not deny what came from the Truth, because there are things of my own kind that existed and I was unable to see them.

Thus this has brought the matter close to me. So when the Truth says: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you﴾, we know that Allah's help is contingent upon your entering the battle wanting to help Allah, and helping Him by what? By your realizing His word and making it the highest; and this is not the only requirement, but also that you make the word of those who disbelieved the lowest.

﴿And if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ In outward appearance He is with you, but we feel that He has abandoned us. Why? Because we leave some of Allah's teachings. So in the general outward sense He is with you as Muslims, and from His companionship with you is that He disciplines you for disobedience, so He forsakes you when you turn away from His command.

The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ And in the previous verse He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him].﴾ And whoever does not rely upon Allah should review his faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 161:

Then, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to commit ghulul (embezzlement). And whoever commits embezzlement will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection...﴾

What is the meaning of "yaghull"? Firstly, "al-ghulul" is taking something in secret. It is derived from "aghalla al-jazzar", meaning the butcher: when he skins an animal, he takes some of the meat along with the hide, then folds the hide, concealing what he has taken of the meat. This is the original sense, and it was then applied in the Shari'ah (ash-shar'an, in legal usage) to misappropriation of the spoils of war. In the terror of battle a fighter may find something valuable and take it secretly; this is called "ghulul". Also, the expression "ghill fi al-sudur" (rancour in the breasts) means the concealment of hatred. The whole root conveys concealment.

And the Truth says: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to commit ghulul﴾. Why? Because it is possible that the archers at the Battle of Uhud, when they saw the spoils, rushed towards them, since the spoils of Badr had not yet been divided among all who had taken part in the fighting. Whoever came upon a spoil would take it. Badr was the first battle, and the purpose of this was to encourage the fighters. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said: "Whoever kills an enemy, he has his spoils (salab)."

The fighters at Uhud thought the matter would be like Badr, and some thought the Messenger would not give them spoils. So the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, makes clear: this is one matter and that is another matter, and whoever does such a thing has committed ghulul. When you hear ﴿It is not for a Prophet to commit ghulul﴾, it means that by his nature, his innate disposition and his character (ṣ. sajiyyah), such a thing could never occur from him at all. But it is possible that such a thing might happen from one of his community. Thus there is a difference between the believer's abstention from being a ghall (one who embezzles, i.e. taking something of the booty for himself), and the Messenger's abstention from being a ghall, because his nature and character do not accord with this. But the matter differs with the fighters; it is possible that one of them could be like that. For example, Sayyidina Umar, in the battle of the Persians, when a group brought the crown of Kisra, and the crown contains all the precious things, which is the mark of the greatness of kings, Al-Faruq Umar said: "Indeed, these people have delivered it to their amir faithfully." For it was possible that they might have concealed it.

﴿It is not for a Prophet to commit ghulul﴾. When you hear ﴿mā kāna﴾ (it is not for), it means: it is not fitting, and it is not valid, that such a matter should occur. After that, He gives the general ruling: ghulul may happen from someone, so He says: ﴿And whoever commits embezzlement will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾. So whoever embezzles something and betrays in it will bring it on the Day of Resurrection, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) depicted it:

"By Allah, none of you will take anything without its right except that he will meet Allah carrying it on the Day of Resurrection. So let me not find any of you meeting Allah carrying a camel that bellows, or a cow that lows, or a sheep that bleats." Then he raised his hands until the whiteness of his armpits was seen, saying: "O Allah, have I conveyed?"

Whoever takes what is forbidden secretly will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel, or a cow, or a sheep, for example. And woe, if what he took was a donkey, it would bray!!

So if he will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection, then what he took will expose him, and for this reason it is called "al-Fadiha" (the disgracer) and "al-Tamma" (the calamity). So it is possible in this world that he takes it secretly and embezzles, but he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying what he took on his back, then he will call out to the Messenger of Allah: "O Muhammad... O Muhammad", because every Muslim knows and is assured that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is kind and merciful, and that he will not be pleased with this story. But the Messenger of Allah informed of the punishment for whoever does that during his lifetime, and it is incumbent upon all believers in him not to think of embezzlement and of taking spoils secretly.

And why is embezzlement of spoils in war a evil? Because the fighter, during the fighting, lives on a mission that the word of Allah be the highest; so how can he accept for himself this humiliation, which is concealing the spoil? He fights so that the word of Allah may be supreme, and he must be on the level of that.

After that, the Truth brings the general matter: ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾. This includes embezzlement of spoils and embezzlement in other than spoils. Let us picture this in regard to everyone who betrays a trust that has been entrusted to him: that he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a building, for example, because he built it without trust; or carrying tons of fish because he stole them; or carrying tons of spoiled cheese that he imported. So everyone who has stolen something will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying it. And if we witness that people cannot bear to be exposed before creation, and creation is limited because they are the contemporaries, then how much more will the disgrace be for all creation from Adam until the Hour is established. So every person must guard himself, because the matter will be exposed.

﴿And whoever commits embezzlement will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. And since He, glory be to Him, will pay every soul what it earned, each will receive according to what he did, so there is no injustice; for if the matter were left without accounting, that would be injustice, and far is Allah from wronging anyone.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 162:

After this preparation and clarification, He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has returned with wrath from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.﴾

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, presents certain matters in the form of a question, He does not present them so that He may learn, for He is All-Knowing. Rather, He presents them so that the listener may be made to speak, and the listener's own speech is a proof above the report of the one who reports. Had He said, "One who follows the pleasure of Allah is not equal to one who went forth with the wrath of Allah," that would have been a report from Him, and He is truthful in what He says. But He, glorified is He, wants to draw His servants to articulate the matter themselves: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has returned﴾, and ﴿returned﴾ (bā'a) means came back, ﴿with wrath from Allah﴾.

There is no doubt that everyone who hears this distinction between following the pleasure and returning with wrath will say: following the pleasure raises a person's rank, and one who returns with wrath descends to the depth of loss. The matter has thus been stated by the listener himself. It is as though the Truth draws us to speak of the matter so that it becomes a proof against us. So, one who follows the pleasure of Allah through obedience, would he be equal to one who returns to the wrath of Allah through disobedience?

Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah, by not embezzling from the spoils and not betraying the trust, like one who embezzled from the spoils and betrayed the trust?

Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah, by listening to Allah's commands when He calls him to fight the enemy, like one who did not respond to the call of Allah to be a fighter in the army of Allah against the enemy of Allah? No. The one who does not respond to the call of Allah is the one who returns with the wrath of Allah.

"Sakhat" (wrath) means the manifestation of disapproval. But the manifestation of disapproval may not affect people of coarse sensibilities, on whom cursing or reviling has no effect. Therefore, He, glorified is He, brought the judgment: ﴿And whose refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ ﴿And whose refuge﴾ means the place where he takes shelter and to which he returns is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 163:

After that, the Truth says: ﴿They are of varying degrees with Allah...﴾

﴿They are of varying degrees﴾ means they will be lodged in the Hereafter in stations according to their deeds. Just as you see that degrees lead up to high ascents, so in the Hereafter every person is held accountable for his deeds and is granted a degree for them. We should note that the Truth uses the word ﴿darajat﴾ (degrees) with regard to Paradise, because in it there are stations and ranks, whereas with regard to the Fire the word "darakat" (lower depths) comes, for the "daraka" (depth) is a descent, while the "daraja" (degree) is an ascent.

﴿They are of varying degrees with Allah﴾. Allah is the Just, who regards all His creatures as His creation, so He does not show enmity to anyone. He decides the matter in this regard, whether it is in their favour or against them. Then He follows it, glorified is He, with His words: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, to reassure these people that Allah is Seeing of what they do, so that no good deed will be lost with Him, and no evil they have committed will be wasted in His sight. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ We hear the word "ya'mal" (works/does), the word "yaf'al" (does), and the word "yaqul" (says). The "'amal" (work) is the most comprehensive of actions, because "'amal" is the engagement of a bodily organ (jariha) with that to which it is assigned. The heart is an organ whose work is intention (niyya), the tongue is an organ whose work is speech (qawl), the ear is an organ whose work is listening, and the eye is an organ whose work is seeing. Thus every bodily organ produces an activity in order to perform its task in the human being, and so every performance of a task by an organ is called "'amal."

However, "fi'l" (act/deed) is the engagement of every organ other than the tongue in an activity, whereas the engagement of the tongue is called speech (qawl), and its counterpart is fi'l (deed). Thus there is speech and there is deed, and both are "'amal." Therefore "'amal" includes and encompasses both speech and deed together, because "'amal" is the occupation of an organ with the activity required of it, whereas "fi'l" is the occupation of an organ other than the tongue with the work required of it. The occupation of the tongue with its task is called qawl (speech) and is not called fi'l (deed). Why? Because a person speaks much, but to compel oneself to do what one says is another process. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 2-3]

Thus speech has as its counterpart deed, and all of it is "'amal": ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, whether speech or deed.

And after that, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers when He raised among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and the Wisdom...﴾

The one who bestows a favour (mann) upon another is the one who gives him a gift that this recipient needs. It is as if the Truth were saying: "Am I in need of your faith? Of your Islam? Is one of My attributes idle, so that you must come to complete it for Me? No. So when I send you a Messenger who is merciful towards you, the favour belongs to Me alone."

﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers when He raised among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾.

Was He sending an angel? No. Rather, He sent him from humankind, so that the example in him would be comprehensible. When he says to every Muslim, "Do as I do," the Muslim must apply what the Messenger commands him. But if he were an angel, would the example benefit anyone? No. For he might say to you, "Do as I do," and you would reply, "I cannot, because you are an angel." Whoever claims divinity for a Messenger negates the example in him, because when he says, "Be like me," you can say, "Can we? Your nature is different; how could we attain that?! We cannot." Therefore those who say the Messenger is divine are in fact losing the example in him. The concept of the Messenger is that he is a behavioural example, that he conveys God's method from God, and that he declares his humanity and says: "I am a human being, and I am able to embody and apply the method." Thus he is a practical, behavioural example.

The Messenger is sent to everyone, so why is the favour upon those who believed alone? Because he is the one who benefited from this message, while the rest forfeited their right to the example; therefore the favour is upon those who believed.

﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers﴾. And what is the favour? Al-mann (favour) originally means "cutting" (qat'). But when we hear it, we find it used for opposite things. For example: al-mann is giving without return, and al-mann is also: spoiling a blessing by talking about it, as in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of God, then do not follow what they have spent with reminders (mann) or injury, for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 262]

So the favour we are concerned with here is giving without return; but mann has also been used for spoiling a blessing through excessive talk about it. A person may say to one who confers a favour upon him: "I do not want the blessing you keep speaking about." So mann is used both for the blessing and for the spoiling of the blessing. You say: "He conferred a favour (mann) upon so-and-so when he rescued me from a distress I was in." And it is said: "So-and-so has no mann in him," meaning he has no strength, and all these meanings revolve around the idea of cutting. When it is used for a blessing and a gift, we say: there is in it a cutting, because the blessing came to cut off need. There was a need, then a gift came, and the gift cuts off the need. So it is used in its meaning.

When a blessing comes after a need, and the need is ended by the blessing, there must follow it an action, which is that you thank the one who blessed you, especially since it is God. For favour (mann) cuts off thanks, because if you confer a blessing and display your superiority in it over the one to whom you have shown it, you have caused the recipient not to thank you, but rather to feel constricted by your blessing, and he may even return it to you.

So here there is a cutting of thanks. If you meet the need of one in need, this is called "blessing" (ni'mah). But if you boast of your blessing upon him until you spoil it, you have cut off and prevented his thanks to you, and this is called "mann," that is, harm, because it injures the feelings and perception of the recipient. And if the cutting is absolute, it is specifically called "al-minnah": they say, "So-and-so has no minnah in him," meaning he has no strength in him to cut through affairs. And here He says: ﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers﴾, and "mann" here means "gave a blessing." The blessing in this world gives you according to your worldly measure, while the favour of God through His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, gives me a gift according to the measure of this world and across the extent of the Hereafter, so this is a great favour.

﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers when﴾, and "idh" means "at the time when"; when He raised among them a Messenger from among them, He performed a favour among them, presented to them, bestowed upon them a great beauty, and conferred upon them a blessing: ﴿when He raised among them a Messenger﴾. If the mere sending of a Messenger to guide people to God's method is a blessing, then what if the Messenger is from themselves? This is another blessing, because as long as he is from their own selves, from their kin and their group, known for lineage and noble descent, known for trustworthiness so that he does not betray, known for truthfulness so that he does not lie, all of this is a "favour," and no one had to exert themselves searching behind him: Did he lie before that, so that we might count it a lie? Did he betray before that, so that we might count it a betrayal? No. Is he one of those pretentious people who want to create a commotion around them? No. Rather, he is known for lineage and noble descent; his grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib was the lord of al-Batha, and not one of his family was insignificant.

And everyone knew of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his trustworthiness from his childhood. So the premises cause people not to exhaust themselves investigating whether he is truthful or not. Thus he is a favour, and therefore, when God sent the master of creation to creation, there were people who, the moment he said to them, "I am the Messenger of God," believed in him. He had not presented a miracle, and they did not say to him, "What will you say, or what will you do?" As soon as he said he was the Messenger of God, they affirmed him. On what basis, then, did they rely in affirming him? They relied on his past. You named him "the trustworthy of the people" in youth, and the trustworthy is not believed on the word of his accusers.

Here is our master Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, saying: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." So the premises they knew of him were the proof in affirming the Messenger. And Khadijah, may God be pleased with her, believed in him. Did he present miracles and the Qur'an to her? No. Rather, the moment he said to her, "I am the Messenger of God," she said to him, "You have spoken the truth, so you must be a messenger." He himself was doubting while she believed in him; he himself was asking: "Perhaps it is such-and-such." Khadijah, may God be pleased with her, took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, and clarified to the Messenger of God that what he was saying could not cast him into calamity, disgrace, or humiliation, because his qualities came as premises to this conclusion: that you are a noble messenger, "Indeed you carry the burdens, earn for the destitute, aid in the calamities of time, and by God, God will never disgrace you." A person with these qualities cannot be approached by a devil. "Come, let us go together to the People of the Book who have knowledge of this matter."

It was as if she had believed in the message of the Messenger of God before Waraqah ibn Nawfal said anything to her.

So His saying ﴿from among themselves﴾ means "known to them." He did not bring them someone who fell upon them from the sky and said, "This is a messenger." No. He is a messenger ﴿from among themselves﴾, and this is the first favour. ﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers when He raised among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾: this applies if you take the immediate circle, that he is of their clan and tribe and known to them. ﴿from among themselves﴾, or from the kind and type of the Arabs, and this too is a favour: as soon as he speaks, they understand him and need no intermediary or translation. The Messenger, when he comes to bring people out of darknesses into light, wants people who understand him. So he made clear to them: "I did not charge you with having to guess what he means. No, he is from yourselves, and he is a human being with your attributes." But because of their extreme obstinacy they did not believe. Its confirmation is His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: "Has God sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94]

They find it outrageous that God would send a human and make him a messenger, and this is stupidity in objection, and the beautiful response comes from God:

﴿Say: Had there been angels walking securely upon the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ [al-Isra': 95]

You are human, so We must bring you a messenger of your own kind, so that when he tells you to do something you say, "Yes," because he is human and works, and we are human and can work as he does. But if he were an angel, one of you would say: "Am I able to be like the angel?" Therefore this argument does not work, and thus God conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger ﴿from among themselves﴾. If you take it as a limited and known tribe, it is a favour; if you take it as of the Arab kind, so that the tongue is one, it is a favour; and if you take it as of the general kind, which is humanity, it is also a favour.

Does considering one meaning among the meanings negate the others, or do they all come in one thread? They are meanings that all come in one thread, because the Speaker is God, and since the Speaker is God, the gift of His utterance is greater than the gift of the words of creatures. ﴿Certainly did God confer favour upon the believers when He raised among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾. And there is a reading, though it is an irregular (shadhdh) reading, that says ﴿min anfusihim﴾ with a fatha on the fa', meaning "from among their noblest," because he is of the Banu Hashim, and they are the best of Quraysh, and Quraysh are the best of the Arabs.

And what does the Messenger do? It is understood from His saying "a messenger" that he does not bring anything from himself. Rather, he, with this lofty rank, his beautiful character and his bright past, is nevertheless a messenger, and has no part in the matter. So the one who sent him is better than he is. Therefore you should not only take notice of this great man, but you must ask: Where did he come from? You must turn your attention to the fact that the One who sent him is greater than he.

﴿a messenger from among themselves who recites to them His verses﴾. The word ﴿yatlu﴾ means "recites," because a word follows a word; the one who recites, that is, pronounces word after word, one following word after word. ﴿reciting to them His verses﴾. And the word "verses" (ayat), as we know, is used for wondrous matters, those that strike the eye. You say, for example, "So-and-so is a sign (ayah) in beauty," meaning his beauty is striking. You say, "So-and-so is a sign in intelligence." It is true there are many intelligent people, but he is a sign in intelligence, meaning this person's matter is wondrous in intelligence. So the word "ayah" means: a wondrous matter, one at which a person stops for a long time to contemplate its marvels.

Verses are of two kinds: visible verses in the cosmos, such as the Truth's saying:

﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to God who created them, if it is Him you worship.﴾ [Fussilat: 37]

And all the phenomena of the cosmos are considered wondrous things. The second kind is the verses of the Qur'an, such as the Truth's saying:

﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse, and God knows best what He sends down, they say, "You are only a fabricator." Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Nahl: 101]

So verses are wondrous matters, and they are of two kinds: seen and recited. The seen is the whole cosmos; the recited is the Qur'an. The Qur'an explains the verses of the cosmos, and the verses of the cosmos explain the verses of the Qur'an. The Messenger came reciting the verses of the Qur'an, and these were wondrous to them. But the other verses in the cosmos they witness and see. The Messenger brought recited verses in order to draw people's attention to the seen verses, and through those seen verses the wonder arises at the precision of the creation of the cosmos, so that a person arrives at faith in the One who created this cosmos.

The Truth says concerning the Messenger: ﴿reciting to them His verses and purifying them﴾, and the matter is not merely that he recites the verses so that they marvel at them. No. The Messenger has a faith-related mission that draws every hearer of the Qur'an to the One who created that beautiful, wondrous cosmos in which are the wondrous signs. Then he gives the Messenger...

Almighty Allah says: "Why, when a calamity strikes you, though you had inflicted twice as much (on the enemy), do you say: 'How is this?' Say: 'It is from yourselves...'"

Why do you say: How does the disbelievers defeat us? It happened to you because you disobeyed the Messenger whom your Lord favoured you with, who gave you (what you have), purified you, and teaches you the Book and the Wisdom. It was necessary, given this, that whatever the Messenger, who possesses these qualities, says, you should obey him. None of you should say: Why does this defeat occur? Nor should anyone say: Why the story of Uhud, and how do the disbelievers defeat us? This does not harmonize with what was said, that Allah bestowed His favour upon you and sent among you a Messenger. Then, Uhud was not a calamity that began with you; rather, it was a calamity that came after you had inflicted a calamity upon your enemies, and you had obtained from them twice what they had obtained from you.

You began at Badr, and Allah gave you good. You killed seventy and captured seventy, while they killed seventy and did not take a single captive at Uhud. You took spoils at Badr, while they took no spoils at all at Uhud. What is so strange about this!? You should have examined yourselves and your souls: were you consistent with your faith and with the leadership of the Messenger over you!? Would you say that question, "How is this?" because "anna" (how/whence) means disapproval: that this is happening, i.e., from where has this defeat and killing befallen us, while we are fighting in the way of Allah, with the Prophet and revelation among us, and they are polytheists? We say to you: Were you at the required level of faith? The required level of faith demands that you carry out what the Messenger said, and you were not at this level, the level you had been at at Badr.

When you hear "a-wa lamma," there is the interrogative hamza, then the conjunction "wa," as in: "a-wa lamma aṣābatkum muṣībatun qad aṣabtum mithlayhā qultum anna hādhā". Here "lamma" is the temporal "ḥīniyya" (when). So what is the meaning? You believed in God as deity and believed in the Messenger as conveyor (of the message): when a calamity strikes you, though you had inflicted twice as much, do you say, "How is this?"

Logic would have required that you never ask this question, because you believe in a just God who has laws that do not change or transform. Would He abandon His laws for your sake!?

"Sunnata Allahi fi alladhina khalaw min qablu, wa lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi tabdilan" [Al-Ahzab: 62]

In another place in the Qur'an He, glory be to Him, says:

"Wa la yaḥīqu al-makru al-sayyi'u illa bi-ahlihi, fa-hal yanẓurūna illa sunnata al-awwalīn, fa-lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi tabdilan, wa lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi taḥwilan" [Fatir: 43]

If you had kept in mind faith in the God who set laws in the universe to govern His kingdom by what achieves the matter of benefit, you would not have said this. And since you have believed that God is the One who made those laws, it was incumbent upon you to know that God will not flatter you by annulling His laws because you were first attributed to Him as Muslims. If you oppose, the laws of God are in effect, and you should have understood this matter. You should not have asked this question, since you believed in God as deity who has laws, and believed in the Messenger who conveys from God.

When a calamity strikes you with this faith, though you had inflicted twice as much, and you say, "How is this?" You have something that happened from you: you struck your opponents. Would that you had struck them with the same as they struck you, but instead you inflicted double. You should have presented your conduct to the scales of faith; if you presented it to the scales of faith, why did you ask this question: "How is this?"

When you hear "anna hādhā," it has two meanings: either it comes to mean (how does this happen?), or it means (from where does this happen?). If it is about specifics and you want to know, like Zachariah wanted to know: from where does the provision come to our lady Mary while she was in the sanctuary:

"Kullamā dakhala 'alayhā Zakariyyā al-miḥrāba wajada 'indahā rizqan, qāla yā Maryamu anna laki hādhā? Qālat huwa min 'indi Allahi, inna Allaha yarzuqu man yashā'u bi-ghayri ḥisāb" [Al Imran: 37] — i.e., from where? And it comes another time with the meaning "how":

"Aw ka-alladhī marra 'alā qaryatin wa hiya khāwiyatun 'alā 'urūshihā, qāla anna yuḥyī hādhihi Allahu ba'da mawtihā, fa-amātahu Allahu mi'ata 'āmin thumma ba'athahu" [Al-Baqarah: 259]

i.e., how will He give life? So sometimes it means "from where," and sometimes "how." Those who entered the battle of Uhud were denying and hastening because they had not been victorious. So the Truth clarified for them: if you had kept in mind the matter of faith in a just God who placed laws in His universe, and He will not change His laws or transform them for your sake, you should know that God does not change for anyone, but you must change for God's sake.

"Aw lamma aṣābatkum muṣībatun qad aṣabtum mithlayhā": "wa lamma" means "when" (ḥīna), and it is called "lamma al-ḥīniyya." "Lamma" also functions as one of the particles of jussive (jazm) like "lam," which negates; and "lammā" also negates, as in His saying:

"Wa lammā yadkhuli al-īmānu fī qulūbikum" [Al-Hujurat: 14]

That is, faith has not yet entered your hearts. It is permissible that it may enter later; this is called "lammā al-jāzima." There is also the conditional "lamma," as in our saying: "lamma yaqūmu Zaydun yaḥrithu kadhā," which contains a condition and a time: whenever he stands, such-and-such happens. As in His saying:

"Falammā aslamā wa tallahu lil-jabīn * wa nādaynāhu an yā Ibrāhīm * qad ṣaddaqta al-ru'yā" [As-Saffat: 103-105]

That is: when they submitted and he laid him down on his forehead, and We called to him: "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision," i.e., We called him. The "wa" here is superfluous (muqḥama), as in His saying: "Ḥattā idhā jā'ūhā wa futiḥat abwābuhā wa qāla lahum khazanatuhā" — i.e., "its keepers said to them." "Muqḥama" means it is brought for emphasis and strengthening, or the "wa" here indicates that God's call to Abraham came accompanied by the laying down of his son Ishmael on his face to slaughter him.

So "lamma" here, and in the verse we are discussing, is "lamma al-ḥīniyya": "When (awqāt) a calamity strikes you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you say, 'How is this?'" You should have compared why you struck the enemy at Badr with double what they struck you, and why your enemy struck you at the Day of Uhud. You should have asked yourselves this question, because the scale is set up and placed, and as long as you neglected this, the answer will come to you. Say, O Muhammad, in reply to them: "It is from yourselves." You disobeyed the command of the Messenger, and since you disobeyed the command of the Messenger, this had to happen by the requirement of your faith in a God who has laws that do not change or transform. "Aw lamma aṣābatkum muṣībatun qad aṣabtum mithlayhā qultum anna hādhā qul huwa min 'indi anfusikum."

Then the verse concludes with His saying, glory be to Him: "Inna Allaha 'alā kulli shay'in qadīr." What is its place here? Its place is that since God has laws, and God's laws do not change, and God is described with unique power, no other god will come and say: "We will annul these laws." And since no other god says so, He is capable of everything, and He is capable of keeping His laws enduring, and no force can shift this matter, because God established the laws. Who then changes them? They will not change except by a higher power, and God forbid that there be a power higher than God's power; therefore He clarifies: I am capable of everything and capable of preserving My laws in the universe, so they do not fail, and no other force transforms or changes them.

Do not think that what befell you came only because the laws do not change. No; this happened by God's permission. God has made clear to the universe: whoever opposes My command, I will do such-and-such to him. Thus nothing happens in the universe without God's knowledge and permission.

The Almighty then says: ﴿And whatever afflicted you on the day the two hosts met, it was by the permission of Allah...﴾

That is, He, glory be to Him, gathered the believers and gathered the disbelievers at Uhud by His permission and His knowledge, and the outcome is known to Him, and that such and such will happen from you. So this is a matter already known. Or ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾ means in the laws (sunan) that never fail. The matter did not come about without the knowledge of Allah; no. It came about by the permission of Allah, and it does not fail, in application, for anyone of His creation at all, whatever his rank.

﴿And whatever afflicted you on the day the two hosts met, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might know the believers﴾: when you see a matter that Allah caused to happen in order to know those who were hypocrites, and to know the believers. We know that Allah knows them before the events occur. But His knowledge is not a proof against others unless it actually takes place from Him, because someone may say: "My Lord, You held me accountable by Your knowledge that this would happen, but I would never have done it." So the Truth clarifies: No. You were known to have done it because you did it, and it became an actuality from you, and the proof is established against you by it.

I will strike this example, and to Allah belongs the highest comparison: you are like a teacher who tells one of the students: "You are going to fail." He says to you: "No, you must examine me." You tell him: "I know that you will fail." He says: "I do not accept your knowledge; you must examine me." You tell him: "Come, I will examine you," and you give him some questions and he fails. Here his failure, as known to you, becomes an actual matter. He was known to you through prior knowledge, but now he cannot argue, because it has become a tangible reality.

The Almighty says: ﴿and so that He might know the believers﴾, and among them are those whose faith is firm and does not waver, who know that if a calamity befalls them, it is because of what they have put forward for themselves, and this calamity increases them in faith in their Lord.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 167:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿And that He might make evident those who were hypocrites. It was said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend," they said, "If we knew [how to] fight, we would have followed you." They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith...﴾

His saying ﴿And that He might make evident those who were hypocrites﴾ means: He makes them appear and be exposed before the people. Otherwise, if these events had not happened, how would you have known the hypocrite? He would have concealed himself. Events must therefore come to reveal him and expose him, for the hypocrite is evasive; so the Truth brings events upon him so that he appears in his true state, and so it was.

﴿And that He might make evident those who were hypocrites. It was said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend"⦆ — Al-Madina was under attack, and if the disbelievers were victorious they would enter, take captives among the Muslims, and commit every kind of abomination!! 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram al-Ansari said to the hypocrites: "Go out and fight with us; and if you do not go out to fight with us... go out to defend yourselves, your wealth, and your women, for if they defeat the Muslims they will enter and do such and such." He called them to fight by way of stirring up zeal and pride in them, after he had despaired that they would fight in the way of Allah. When he saw their insistence on not going out, 'Abdullah said to them: "Go away, enemies of Allah! Allah will suffice His Messenger without you."

So there is a distinction between fighting in the way of Allah and defending oneself; hence He said ﴿Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend﴾ — or defend us, even merely by increasing our numbers and showing our multitude, so that the polytheists think there are many people with us. ﴿They said, "If we knew [how to] fight, we would have followed you."﴾ When we follow this reasoning within the story itself, we find that Ibn Ubayy's view was that the Messenger of Allah should remain in al-Madina. Why? Because experience had established that when a people came to raid al-Madina and entered it, the people of al-Madina would defeat them, and if the people of al-Madina went out to face them, they would be defeated.

So the matter was clear in Ibn Ubayy's mind: he did not agree to go out, because experience had shown him that if they went out of al-Madina to fight the enemy, the enemy would defeat them, and if they stayed they would be victorious. Thus he was certain of the outcome of going out. But since the matter came from the head of hypocrisy, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, you cannot judge where the truth lies. It is possible that the traces of the day of the Messenger's migration (peace be upon him) from Makkah to al-Madina remained in the soul of Ibn Ubayy. On the day the Messenger came to al-Madina was the day the hypocrite Ibn Ubayy was about to be crowned king over al-Madina; then when the Messenger brought this great event, the situation changed and the crown became a head without something to wear it. He carried this in his soul.

﴿They said, "If we knew [how to] fight, we would have followed you."﴾ Ibn Ubayy claimed that going out of al-Madina was like throwing oneself into destruction, and not fighting; for fighting entails that you have a prospect of victory, whereas this is casting oneself into destruction, not fighting. But did he say ﴿If we knew [how to] fight, we would have followed you﴾ while being truthful?

The Truth exposes them: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾. Before that they were in concealed hypocrisy; and as long as hypocrisy is concealed, the tongue speaks while the heart denies and rejects, so they vacillated between that and this, belonging neither to these nor to those. This matter made him near to manifest disbelief.

﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾. So the heart's action is the intention of faith, and the tongue may say what it does not do. That is why we said: the hypocrite is divided in self and divided in faculties; he says with his tongue words while his heart harbors denial, and therefore they will be in the lowest level of the Fire, for they are deceivers, and their souls are divided.

﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ — speech must be by the mouth, for speech is used to mean clarifying what is in the soul; so a person's clarifying what is in his soul in writing is considered speech linguistically. Therefore, one who is shy to speak to someone writes to him on a sheet of paper, and at the time he writes he has spoken. These hypocrites, however, utter their words not through a writing but through their mouths, and this is brazenness in hypocrisy. Had they been modest, they would have whispered it: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾. Thus the tongue did not agree with the heart: the heart is fixed upon and insistent on disbelief — and we seek refuge in Allah — while the tongue boasts and proclaims faith.

We know that "truthfulness" (al-sidq) is that the speech conforms to the reality, and the reality in the matter of faith is an intention in the heart and a movement that confirms faith; but the hypocrites' tongues do not conform to their hearts. When what was in the heart was concealed and then appeared in the limbs, they were exposed. This is the reason they were nearer to disbelief: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾.
