This is a kind of deficiency in the image of faith in the heart, as if they dealt with Allah the way they deal with human beings like themselves.

Then Allah says: ﴿Those who said of their brethren, while they themselves sat back, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say: "Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful."﴾

When Ibn Ubayy (Ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites) wanted to demoralize the army, some of the hypocrites agreed with him and some did not. Those who went out to fight and jihad (jihad, struggle in the way of Allah) and did not agree with them, and were then killed, [the hypocrites] rejoiced over them and said: "If they had obeyed us and stayed in Madinah and not gone out, they would not have been defeated and would not have been killed." It is as if Allah is clarifying their method for us; therefore we will take them on their own logic. They sat back and said of their brethren who were killed in the battle, and who were of their own group: ﴿If they had obeyed us﴾. It is as if a statement had come from them: "Stay behind." But the other people, who were less hypocritical, did not comply with them and went out, and so what happened to them happened.

So how does Allah respond to this? Observe the beautiful response: you say ﴿If they had obeyed us﴾, as though your obedience was a means of their safety from being killed. Then you know the path to safety from being killed. And does one who knows the path to safety from being killed know the path to safety from death? For this reason Allah says, mocking them: ﴿Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful﴾. In this there is a refutation of them from their own words: ﴿If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed﴾.

Since you know a means of safety from being killed, then use this means to avert death from yourselves. You, along with your elders and those present, will die, and you cannot ward off death from yourselves. So you do not know the path to safety from death. For how many a warrior has returned from war safe, and how many a deserter from fighting has died and perished? Suppose that some of the believing fighters were killed: indeed, the one who is killed in the battle is not less honored by Allah than the one who came out of the battle safe. These are more beloved to Allah, and Allah has hastened their meeting and lodged them in the near station with Him.

We know that an action is praised or blamed in relation to its goal. Every action that brings you closer to the goal is praiseworthy, and every action that takes you away from the goal is not praiseworthy. If the goal is, for example, to go to Alexandria, you may go on foot and need several days, or you may go riding an animal and need less time, or ride a carriage and the time decreases to hours, or ride an airplane and reach it in half an hour. The stronger the means, the less time it takes, because we know that the driving force in motion is inversely proportional to the time. As the force increases, the time decreases. And since my goal is to go to Alexandria, is the one who hastens and shortens the time for me to get there better or not? It is the better means.

So since the goal is to go to meet Allah and to live in His nearness and company, when Allah hastens some of us and takes them by the shortest route, is this better for them or not? This is better. Thus we see that people look at death with a foolish gaze. The death of a true believer of sincere faith brings him closer to the goal, so what should sadden me!

You fear death, but those who were killed in the way of Allah are not dead, because their life is a continuous life.

There is a great difference between death and martyrdom. The one who is killed as a martyr has a continuous life, and he will not pass through a period of death as we do. Let us understand that they are alive with their Lord, meaning under His law, glory be to Him. So do not judge by your own law. You, as you yourself said, if you opened the grave you would find these slain merely as remains. To you they are remains and dead according to your law. But they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision?

So in what does life differ from death? When a person's soul departs from his body and is separated from it, his life ends. Outwardly the matter is over, and he no longer benefits from provision or food, because provision was made to sustain life. Then there is no provision. Yet Allah, glory be to Him, wants to give us attributes that confirm the martyr is alive. Among the necessities of life is that he is provided for, that is, he benefits from what sustains life. We must understand that being "with" you is not the same as being "with" Allah. The martyr is alive with his Lord and is provided for with his Lord with a provision suited to the life which his Lord intended for him. We know that provision is the characteristic found in the living. When we read the saying of Allah: ﴿They are alive, with their Lord, receiving provision﴾, someone may say: It is possible that you take a person and keep him alive, and give him food and drink, but is he happy with his place? No. Therefore we must realize and know that the life of the martyr is not in his grave, but with his Lord, and he is joyful with his place, so the Truth says: ﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there shall be no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 170:

﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾

Justice among mankind is realized in that each of them dies. But the bounty is that Allah hastens the ending of life in this world for those whom He loves, by martyrdom, and transports them to His good pleasure and His bliss. ﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾. And this is not all. Rather, we find that the brotherhood of faith remains among them, not like the attribute of the living but purer and more lasting than the attribute of the living. The quality of faith requires that the believer love for his brother what he loves for himself, and the martyrs in their life with their Lord are likewise, which indicates that the life the martyrs live is a growing life in which there is provision, spiritual experiences and joy, and every martyr considers this a bounty from Allah with which He has favoured him. Therefore the martyr rejoices over those of his brothers among the believers who have not yet come after him, and says: "Would that they came to see what we see."

﴿And rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them﴾: ﴿Yastabshirun﴾ is from al-bushra (glad tidings), and al-bushra is the news that gladdens. ﴿And rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them﴾, and "yalhaqu" means they come after them. The martyrs say: they will come to us, and since they will come to us, we love for them to be with us in the bliss and good in which we live. Each of them feels love for his brother, because he knows the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." And on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck down at Uhud, Allah placed their souls in the crops of green birds that drink from the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits, and take shelter in lanterns of gold in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food and drink and the excellence of their favour, they said: 'Would that our brothers knew what Allah has done for us, so that they would not abstain from jihad nor shrink from war.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will convey it to them on your behalf,' and Allah revealed these verses: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾, and what follows."

We know that al-bishr is usually joy, and it appears on the skin of a person. When a person is happy, the joy shows and shines upon his face, and therefore we call it "bishara" (glad tidings), because it produces in the face of the one given the good news some joy, which gives it sheen, brightness and attractiveness.

﴿And rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾ That is, those who have not yet joined them from behind them: no fear will be upon them. These who have not yet been martyred may face some battle, so the Truth says, on the tongue of the martyrs, to each of them: Do not fear, for you will go to good in life. ﴿That no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾

Then after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and a bounty...﴾

Indeed, the Truth, glory be to Him, does not waste the reward of those who fought in the way of Allah.

Here, may He be glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Those who answered the call of Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them...﴾

Look at this lofty station, so that you may know that the tremor that occurred at Uhud restored the arrangement of the faith-atoms in the souls of the believers. For this reason, Allah willed that the distress of those who regretted what had happened on their part should not last long, and that the duration of the unbelievers' joy at the harm inflicted on the believers in the last battle should not last long either. Those polytheists were rejoicing, and these Muslims were in grief. This is because we said: as long as they are Muslims and believers, they have rights, and if they fell short, they incur a punishment. Allah had indeed inflicted the punishment upon them, yet their Islam still retained a right upon Allah, because He ran those decrees in order to refine, purify and train them. So He does not prolong the grief of the believers, nor does He extend the joy of the unbelievers. Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, with the situation as you know it to be, and his caller (ﷺ) announced among the people, in response to the request of Quraysh, saying: "Let no one go out with us except those who were present with us in the fighting."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to them with a number not exceeding the number of the fighters who had faced them, so that it could not be said that they had come with additional reinforcement. Rather, on the contrary, those who went out to pursue the unbelievers were those who had remained with the Messenger at Uhud, minus those who had been killed, and minus also everyone whose wounds had weighed him down. They were fewer than those who had been in the battle, as though Allah wished to show us that the purification had achieved its aim.

In this state they answered the Messenger, as if the matter came as a restoration of honour to those who had witnessed the battle, so that they would not weaken before their own souls, and so that they would not make it a slip that pursues them and follows them throughout their long history, but rather they would know that the battle of Uhud had ended and they had recognised its effects.

Immediately upon the call of the Messenger's caller (ﷺ) with the aforementioned proclamation, they all responded, and none was permitted to join them except Jabir ibn Abdullah, because he presented an excuse, that he had not been with the people, since he had seven sisters, and his father had ordered him to remain with his sisters to look after them, so the Messenger of Allah permitted him.

As we have said, Allah willed through all the events of Uhud to restore the arrangement of the faith-atoms. Since the faith-atoms have become orderly, the apparatus of reception from Allah has been repaired, and in a single moment they answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in that they pursue the unbelievers, and they went to Hamra' al-Asad, and what happened happened. After that, Allah sent to them some of His soldiers who would dishearten these disbelieving people and say to them: "Muhammad has come out against you with a great army."

We observe that the Truth, glorified be He, says here ﴿Those who answered﴾, which corresponds to "those who disobeyed" the Messenger's command, namely the archers: ﴿Those who answered the call of Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them.﴾

They answered while exhausted, in pain, and covered with wounds. Each one of them had received a share of the exhaustion of the fighting, yet they answered Allah and the Messenger. Each of them had been struck by the *qarh* or *quruh*, that is, the pain or the wound. ﴿For those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward﴾, and they had done well in responding; therefore for them is the great reward, ﴿a great reward﴾, because what had occurred from them of disobedience had been punished.

The Almighty then says: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it only increased them in faith...﴾

The matter is not only that. The matter is that the hypocrites began spreading false rumours that the polytheists had summoned a new force from the disbelievers of Makkah in order to frighten the believers, yet not a single believer was frightened. ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them."﴾ Whenever you hear the word "people" (al-nas), know that faith is far from it. For as long as they are "people" (unas), they confront other people, and whoever prevails does so by his effort, cleverness and good handling of affairs. But the believer confronts the disbeliever, and the believer receives reinforcement from his Lord.

It has been said that Satan may appear in the form of a crowd of people in order to terrify the believers. Satan is of the world of the jinn, and the world of the jinn sees you, he and his tribe, from where you cannot see them. God has given him the power to take on whatever form he wishes. He may take the form of a human, an animal, or whatever he likes. But once he takes a form, that form governs him, because he has agreed to step out of his own reality in order to take on another shape. So if he takes the form of a human being, the law of human beings applies to him: if you have a pistol, a sword or a dagger and you overpower him and stab him, he dies. This is what protected us from their intimidation.

That is why you find that Satan appears in a fleeting glimpse and then vanishes, because he fears that the human before him may be aware that the form governs him. Whatever shape he takes before you, if you choke him, he is choked. Therefore he fears the human being, and so he appears only in fleeting glimpses.

We may also understand the Almighty's words ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you"﴾ as meaning that some of the disbelievers spread the report that Abu Sufyan and his companions had mustered their forces. The word "gathered" (jama'u) suggests that they had brought other fighters, or that their scattered remnants had regrouped. Whether this or that, when they fled, they fled in scattered groups, for defeated people do not travel in an orderly formation held together; rather each one goes at his own pace. It is also possible that they regrouped again or brought other people. We may note that the wording admits all of this.

﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them"﴾ Such a saying may weaken the resolve of the believers, but the testing of faith had refined the camp of belief, so they paid no heed to these words. Thus the first lesson bore fruit. They learned that opposing the command of God, represented in the command of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), by mere opposition causes weakness to creep into the soul, whereas steadfastness and adherence to the commands of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) strengthen the sense of power. Therefore they did not heed this threat, but said: ﴿"God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ They did not concern themselves with numbers, and they understood that faith requires them to fight the disbelievers so that God may punish them at their hands. In this is a lesson for every warrior: when you fight, you are either made victorious by your faith in God, or you are the opposite of that:

﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17]

They came to their senses, and the order of faith changed in their depths. We see this in the fact that some people came to hinder and dishearten them, but they could not do so; rather this saying only increased them in faith: ﴿and they said, "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ They came to realise that it is the power of God that gives them victory, and that God is sufficient for them against any number of enemies, and He is the best Disposer. The meaning of "al-Wakil" (the Disposer) is that when I am unable to accomplish a matter, I entrust someone to act on my behalf, and when we entrust to God what we cannot do, He is the best Disposer. Why? The answer comes: ﴿So they returned with a blessing from God﴾. They were victorious through the terror that God cast into the hearts of their enemies, and they did not engage the disbelievers in combat. Thus the word of God was fulfilled:

﴿I shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 3, verse 174:

This principle that comes after that, confirming the matter: ﴿So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah...﴾

Every believer who is subjected to the testing (tamhis, the process of sifting and purification) of the truth must feel this principle, and every Muslim must remember that experience, the experience of Uhud. One night was the difference between the day of the battle of Uhud and the day they went out to pursue the disbelievers at Hamra' al-Asad. That one night was within God's care and in remembrance of the testing that the believers had undergone, and it worked wonders. When they pursued the disbelievers, they paid no heed to the psychological warfare that the enemy waged against them. Rather, it only increased them in faith, and they said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.﴾

Thus they stripped themselves of their souls, of what surrounded them, of their strength, of their numbers, and of everything else, except that they said: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian for whoever is unable to attain his aim. They understood the important matter, which is that each of them should always be within the care of his Lord. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah and the Family of the Messenger of Allah took this dose of faith and derived much from it in resolving their problems.

The saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian﴾ reminds us of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, son of Sayyidi Muhammad al-Baqir, son of Sayyidi Ali Zayn al-Abidin. He was among the most learned of people in the Qur'an and among the most knowledgeable in deriving the secrets of Allah from the Qur'an. He used to find in the words of the Truth ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian﴾ a wonderful inference. He would marvel at any person who was seized by fear of anything that frightens. A person does not fear except a matter that disrupts the regularity of his ease, that worries him and threatens his safety, security and tranquillity, and this fear has a known source. So when a believer is exposed to such fear, he must remember the words of the Truth: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian,﴾ because it is a principle that benefited the entire army in its battle with the disbelievers. When an individual takes this dose, he regains composure (rabatat al-jash, steadiness of nerve) and the firmness of the heart, so that he does not flee in the face of terror.

Our master Ja'far al-Sadiq draws our attention to this principle so that we may turn to it whenever something frightens us. He says: I marvel at one who fears and does not turn to the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian.﴾ With his faith-based insight, he marvels at a person seized by fear who does not turn to this noble saying, ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian,﴾ and then, through his illuminations, he derives the secret of this, saying: For I heard Allah following it say: ﴿So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them.﴾ Note the words of our master Ja'far al-Sadiq: "For I heard Allah following it say." He read with the disposition of a sincere believer. A believer, when he reads the words of Allah, is conscious that he is hearing Allah speak. It is as if he is saying: For I heard Allah following it say: ﴿So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them.﴾ For this reason the Truth says:

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 204]

So when you listen to the Qur'an, it is Allah who is speaking. It is shameful for your Lord to speak into your ear and yet you be distracted from Him, when He is your Lord. Thus the remedy for fear is that you say from your heart: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian,﴾ and that you say it in its proper sense. If you say it in its proper sense, Allah will spare you the evil of that fear, because Allah says after ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian﴾: ﴿So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them.﴾ Look at the favour and the bounty: they are both from Allah. Favour may reach you, and bounty too, but you appreciate that only in the final outcomes of matters. So Allah made clear that the favour increased in that it was a cool spoil (ghanima barida, gain obtained without hardship), and no harm touched us in it. That is the peak of giving, its head and its hump. If you measure it only by the final outcomes, you have miscalculated. ﴿So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them.﴾ As a result of that beneficial experience, ﴿they followed the pleasure of Allah,﴾ and the experiment succeeded with the believers.

Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq goes on, to complete the remedy for the aspects of the human soul, and prescribes the medicine. The human soul is frightened, disturbed and made anxious by the fear of an evil that may befall it, and the remedy for this is: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian.﴾ He adds: I marvel at one who is distressed (ightamma) and does not turn to the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]

Ghamm (distress) is an anxiety in the soul, but you do not perceive its causes, for its causes are complex. The chest tightens, and so you say: My chest is tight, I am exhausted, and I do not know why. That is, nothing has happened to you just now that would call for this; rather, it may be the sum of reactions to events and matters that you do not remember now. This is called ghamm. When the servant turns to the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers,﴾ the servant acknowledges his sin and says: This distress has come to me only because I departed from the path. Our master Ja'far al-Sadiq reminds us that he heard, after it, the saying of Allah:

﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress, and thus do We save the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 88]

The one who said this was our master Yunus (Jonah), upon whom be peace: ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from the distress.﴾

This response from Allah was not a privilege specific to Yunus, peace be upon him, because He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And thus do We save the believers.﴾ That is, it is a wide door through which Allah admits all the believers. Our master Ja'far al-Sadiq adds: I marvel at one who is plotted against (mukir bihi) and does not turn to the saying of Allah:

﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾ [Ghafir: 44]

For I heard Allah following it say: ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted.﴾

Makr (plotting) bihi means that evil is schemed against him in a concealed manner, because makr is the scheming by your adversary of an evil that will befall you while you stand by the truth. So this makr is an evil plotted against good and truth, and this is the evil plotting. Opposite to it is good makr, and so the Truth says:

﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43]

Thus there is a makr that is not evil: for example, when the possessor of truth plots against the possessor of evil in a way that is hidden from him. This is called good makr, because it is a fight against evil. For this reason Allah clarifies this matter for us: consider this. If they scheme and plot, they cannot plot against all creation in a way that escapes Allah, because He, glorified is He, is the All-Knowing, the Creator, the Sustainer. And if Allah schemes against them, they will not be able to uncover that scheme. So Allah is the best of schemers, because their scheming is exposed before the Creator; therefore it is a weak scheme. As for the true scheme, it is the one for which there is no means by which you can know it.

We continue with our master Ja'far al-Sadiq's words on the remedy of the human soul, where he says: I marvel at one who seeks the world and its adornment, how he does not turn to the saying of Allah:

﴿What Allah wills [has come to pass]; there is no power except by Allah﴾ [al-Kahf: 39]

For I heard Allah follow it with His saying:

﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children, perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ [al-Kahf: 39-40]

Our master Ja'far al-Sadiq derived this from the account of the owner of the garden:

﴿And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: What Allah wills [has come to pass]; there is no power except by Allah? If you see me as less than you in wealth and children, perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ [al-Kahf: 39-40]

When you say: ﴿What Allah wills [has come to pass]; there is no power except by Allah,﴾ the world comes to you hastening, because you have stripped yourself of what surrounds you, of the strength of your stratagems and your means, and you have left the matter to Allah, glorified and exalted, who is capable of every giving.

Thus the human aspects of the soul are: fear, which has a remedy and a prescription; worry, which has a remedy and a prescription; plotting against you, which has a remedy and a prescription; and the seeking of the world and happiness, which has a remedy and a prescription. The prescription we are concerned with here is: ﴿And they said: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian. So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them.﴾

Favour (ni'ma) is that Allah gives you according to the measure of your deed, and bounty (fadl) from Allah is that He increases your giving. No harm touched any of the believers who pursued the fighters of Quraysh. As a result, they combined everything Allah had granted them, of favour and bounty, together with their following the pleasure of Allah. The matter became for them a sensed and tested experience: ﴿And they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is possessed of great bounty.﴾

The hypocrites tried to discourage the believers from meeting the disbelievers of Quraysh, so the Truth wished to expose them and to show the motive for such a stance among the hypocrites. Therefore they said to the believers: ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.﴾

Allah makes clear to the believers the true position of the hypocrites: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies, so do not fear them...﴾

This is the cry of Satan, who frightens his allies. It is possible that Satan utters this cry while taking the form of a human being. It is also possible that Satan incites one of mankind with this cry, so that the person utters it under Satan's incitement: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies.﴾

When we read the Qur'an with precise, pure faith, we must understand it deeply. Who are the allies of Satan? In this context, the allies of Satan are either the disbelievers of Quraysh, or the hypocrites, or both together. ﴿His allies⁠﴾ are his beloved ones who support his idea.

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to convey to us: "It is only that Satan who said: 'The people have gathered against you, so fear them.' This Satan only frightens his allies."

At first glance, one would expect Satan to frighten his enemies. Here we face a Satan who incites through the expression of frightening. So who is afraid, and of whom is he afraid?

It would be expected that Satan frightens his enemies; this is the logic.

In our ordinary life we say: "I frightened so-and-so of so-and-so," or "I frightened so-and-so, so-and-so." So Satan here tries to dominate the believers and frighten them of his allies, the disbelievers and the hypocrites. In the Arabic language, we know that in some contexts the preposition may be omitted and the verb connects directly to its object; this is called the *maf'ul minhu* (the object governed by *min*, i.e., an object taken with the preposition removed). An example of this is the saying of the Truth:

﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men﴾ [al-A'raf: 155]

So Moses, peace be upon him, chose from among his people seventy men.

On this basis, we read the saying of the Truth: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies⁠﴾ and understand from it: that Satan frightens you from his allies, because the preposition in the noble verse is omitted. This is reinforced and strengthened by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿frightens you with his allies⁠﴾. And the Truth alerts the believers not to fear the allies of Satan, so He says: ﴿so do not fear them⁠﴾.

This makes clear to us that Satan only wanted to frighten the believers of his allies, who are the hypocrites and the disbelievers. Some exegetes said: ﴿frightens his allies⁠﴾ means that Satan frightens his allies so that they become cowardly about fighting; so he incites them to think that if they go out to fight they may die. But if that could apply to the hypocrites, who did not go out with the Messenger to meet the polytheists, how could it apply to the second category of his allies, the disbelievers? The disbelievers had indeed actually gone out to fight the believers. And from the saying of the Truth: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me⁠﴾ we understand that Satan's allies are not the ones who are afraid, but rather they are the ones who frighten: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.⁠﴾

So the Truth, glory be to Him, asks the believers to make an equation and a comparison: Will they fear the allies of Satan, or will they fear Allah? They must arrive at fearing Allah, who is able to repel the allies of Satan.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 176:

Then, after that, the Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says: ﴿And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you. Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all...﴾

The hypocrites (munafiqun) at the beginning of the battle were hidden and concealed. Then a sign of withdrawal (inkhidhal) appeared from them at Uhud, so they were closer to disbelief than to faith. But after that they hastened to disbelief, as if there were someone driving them with a whip so that they would race towards disbelief.

And here is the Truthful, glory be to Him, who has defined the elements of the battle, or the forces of the battle, or the field of the battle, or the soldiers of the battle, and so He alerts His Messenger: ﴿And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you﴾. He did not say: "They will not harm you at all," because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions who believed are not a party to the matter. The enmity of those who hasten to disbelief is enmity towards Allah. Therefore the Truthful says: ﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾. It is as if the battle is not with the believers, but rather it is the battle of the disbelievers with Allah. And as long as the battle is with Allah, the believers are the soldiers of Allah, and they are the form which Allah wanted for the defeat of the disbelievers:

﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them, and give you victory over them, and satisfy the hearts of a believing people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14]

So if the battle of disbelief were only with those who believe in Allah, Allah would have said: "And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you; indeed, they will not harm you at all." But the matter is not like this. The camp of disbelief and hypocrisy wanted to enter a battle with Allah, and there is no power capable of that. For this reason Allah reassures the believers even more, so that they may increase in steadfastness upon faith, because all of mankind, believers and disbelievers, are changeable (aghyar), and some of the believing humans may turn slightly away from the method. When the battle is between humans and humans, one of the two sides may prevail by its strength.

And for the sake of complete reassurance, Allah transferred the battle with disbelief to another matter: He, with His majesty, perfection and might, is the one who stands against the camp of the disbelievers. The only important thing is that the believers remain under the care (hadanah) of Allah. The Messenger was grieved that some hastened to disbelief. Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not know that he had come only as a conveyer of the message? He knew, but he was keen, (ﷺ), that all people should believe so that they might taste the sweetness of what he brought. This eagerness is what brings grief to the heart of the Messenger, and when he sees one who does not taste the sweetness of the method, the Messenger hopes that all people will taste the sweetness of faith, because he (ﷺ) is kind and merciful to the believers, and indeed to all people: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾. The evidence of this is that the option (al-takhyir) came to him. "Gabriel called the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Indeed Allah has heard the words of your people to you and how they replied to you, and He has sent to you the angel of the mountains, so that you may command him as you wish concerning them.' He said: The angel of the mountains called me, greeted me, then said: 'O Muhammad, indeed Allah has sent me to you, and I am the angel of the mountains, so that you may command me as you wish. If you wish, I will close the two mountains upon them?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who worship Allah alone and do not associate anything with Him.'"

So the Messenger (ﷺ) does not spare only these people, but he is also keen about future generations. And it happened: from the children of the chiefs of Quraysh came champions, heroes, soldiers of the call, and martyrs. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as Allah informed us in the verses of the Qur'an, would be grieved when no one tasted the sweetness of faith, and the Truthful says:

﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this message, out of sorrow﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]

And in another place the Truthful says:

﴿Perhaps you will destroy yourself because they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them from the heaven a sign, so that their necks would remain humbly subservient to it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3–4]

The Truthful, glory be to Him and exalted, does not want necks, but He wants hearts that come to Him by way of choice and love. He, the Most Generous Creator, is able to create mankind in a form not susceptible to disobedience, as He created the angels. Indeed all kinds of creation glorify His praise. So the Qur'an shows His (ﷺ) eagerness that all people should believe and taste the sweetness of meeting their Lord, and of following the method of Allah, and the sweetness of the legislation that makes them happy and makes all their faculties happy. When matters come other than what the Messenger of Allah loves, here is the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you﴾.

This is evidence that Allah wants to convey to mankind: O people, out of the abundance of the Messenger's love for you, he grieves over your disobedience, and I am the One who says to him: "Do not grieve." The Messenger (ﷺ) is merciful to the whole community, as the Qur'an says:

﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107]

His stance (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection suffices, when every nation goes to its messenger to return it, and the nations come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah honors him by accepting his intercession, so that Allah hastens the judgment and reckoning. This is a mercy to the worlds, because from the terror of that station they wish to depart, even to the Fire.

We have said earlier: the Truthful, glory be to Him, knew the preoccupation of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with his community and his mercy towards them. So Allah said to him, to ease his feelings and his emotions, what came in the noble hadith:

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, concerning Abraham: ﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray. So whoever follows me is of me﴾.

And the saying of Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. "Then he raised his hands and said: 'O Allah, my community, my community,' and wept. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'O Gabriel, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what makes him weep.' So Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what he had said, and he knows best. Allah said: 'O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: "Indeed We will please you concerning your community, and We will not grieve you."'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has another stance that shows the perfection of his mercy towards his community. Allah sent down, among what He sent down of the noble Qur'an after a pause in revelation, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾.

Look at what is reported from our master Ali concerning this verse: it is narrated that he, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the people of Iraq: "You say that the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah is: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins﴾." They said: "Yes, we say that." He said: "But we, the People of the House, say that the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah is His saying: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾." In a hadith: when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then I will not be satisfied while one of my community is in the Fire."

It is also narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every prophet has a granted supplication, and each prophet hastened his supplication, but I have kept my supplication as my intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection."

Thus we see the Messenger's preoccupation with his community as a clear matter situated at the centre of his consciousness.

So Allah's saying, ﴿And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you﴾, is a clarification from Allah to His Messenger that they did not hasten to disbelief because of any shortcoming on your part; you have fulfilled your duty. He adds, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾. He did not say, glory be to Him: "Indeed, they will not harm you," or "they will not harm the believers." Rather, Allah, glory be to Him and the Mighty, the Possessor of might, made the battle to be with Himself, and so here He reassures the believers.

Allah wants not to give those who hasten to disbelief any share in the Hereafter, so He says: ﴿Allah wills not to give them any share in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment﴾. Since these are Allah's wills that He should not give them a share in the Hereafter, could there be for them any action that contradicts the wills of their Lord? No.

He, glory be to Him, by what He has legislated as a method, wants His sunnah to reach them, and Allah punishes whoever opposes the sunnah He has legislated, because He, may His power be exalted, requires those who are obligated to apply the sunnah He has legislated for them.

There is a difference between the "lam of consequence" (lam al-'aqibah), which occurs when the servant has an intention but a higher power wills something else, and the "lam of will and causation" (lam al-iradah wa al-ta'lil). The "lam of will and causation" is clear in our saying: "The student studied in order to succeed (li-yanjaha)," because the cause of studying is the desire for success. As for the "lam of consequence," it is clear when a father says to his son: "I spoiled you so that you would fail at the end of the year."

Did the father spoil his son so that he would fail? No, but the father here uses the "lam of consequence": the father had an intention, but a higher power came contrary to the intention.

Let us clarify the matter further. The Truthful says concerning the story of our master Moses:

﴿And We inspired the mother of Moses: Suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve; indeed We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]

We must pay attention to the saying of the Truthful: ﴿cast him into the river﴾. An ordinary person, if he said to a woman carrying her infant: "If you fear for your son, cast him into the sea," this woman would not believe this speaker. But the mother of Moses received this inspiration from Allah, and reception from Allah is not contradicted by the thought of a devil or the thought of a human. Inspiration from Allah is manifest in His saying: ﴿And We inspired the mother of Moses﴾. And since Allah is the One who inspired her, the suggestion of Satan does not come. Therefore the mother of Moses carried out the command of Allah. And Allah reassures her, saying to her: ﴿And do not fear and do not grieve; indeed We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾.

Allah warns the mother of Moses that He will not return him to her merely because he is the comfort of her eye, but because Moses also has a mission with Allah. In another scene, the Truthful speaks about the matter of the inspiration to the mother of Moses:

﴿When We inspired your mother with what is inspired: Put him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his. And I cast upon you love from Me, and that you may be raised under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 38–39]

Here, in this scene, the Truthful describes the time of carrying out the operation that He inspired. There is a difference between preparation for the operation before it occurs, as in the previous scene where the Truthful said to her: ﴿And when you fear for him, cast him into the river﴾. That was the preparation. Then the time of execution came, and the Truthful said to Moses: ﴿When We inspired your mother with what is inspired﴾. It is a series of successive commands showing that this operation took place at the time when Pharaoh's soldiers were taking the children of the Children of Israel to kill them. He, glory be to Him, shows us that the soldiers of Allah, from among the inanimate things that do not understand, received the divine command to protect Moses. The word "cast" (iqdhifihi) indicates speed, and the "river" (al-yamm) received the command from Allah that when Moses is cast into the river, it must cast him onto the shore.

Then the Lord says: ﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith...﴾

They will not harm the Messenger and his Companions, because they are in the company of Allah; and they will not harm Allah. In this there is reassurance for the believers, as if the Exalted and Glorified One is saying: O believers, who believe in Me and affirm Muhammad, the struggle against disbelief is not a struggle between the believers and the disbelievers; rather, it is a struggle between your Lord and these disbelievers. In this there is great reassurance.

﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith﴾. The word "ishtira'" (purchase) is a transaction (safqah), and a transaction requires a "thaman" (price) and a "muthman" (the thing purchased). The "thaman" here is faith, because the preposition "bi" (with) enters upon what is given up, and the "muthman" is disbelief, because it is what is taken. Did they take disbelief and pay faith as its price? Does this mean that faith was present with them?

Yes, faith was with them, because the earlier faith is the faith of the primordial nature (fitrah) and the faith of the old covenant that Allah took from the offspring of Adam before alien influences and desires came into existence:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."﴾ [al-A'raf: 172]

Or, at the least, faith and disbelief were within their reach, given the regulated law of choice in the human soul; but they took disbelief instead of faith. The substitution is clear: they replaced faith with disbelief, so the "ba'" (with), as I said, entered upon what was abandoned. They abandoned the earlier faith, which is the faith of the offspring (dharr), or they abandoned the faith of the fitrah, for the noble hadith says: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, and then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian."

They have departed from faith and thrown it away as the price of disbelief. So when a person takes disbelief, he has taken disbelief in place of faith. And they ﴿will never harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment﴾. Why? Because if we suppose that the whole world had believed, this would not benefit Allah at all. The sacred hadith says:

Allah the Exalted said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me, nor reach My benefit so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not add anything to My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease anything from My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one place and asked Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not decrease what I have except as a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped into it. O My servants, they are only your deeds which I count for you and then repay you for. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself."

Thus, human faith adds nothing to Allah, and disbelief decreases nothing from Allah; for man has come into existence within the dominion of Allah, and man has brought nothing additional into the dominion of Allah. Man is the creation of Allah and His handiwork, from the elements of His dominion, may His power be exalted. The discussion continues to clarify that the Exalted does not work on a thing with His hands so that it takes time from Him. No, He, whose will is exalted, says to a thing "Be," and it is.

The word "kun" (be) itself is the shortest command. His command is too subtle and fine for a created being to grasp in its reality, but the Truth brings it to us in a light image that makes our humanity understand the matter. Those who exchanged disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment. They will not live in safety or distance from punishment; rather, a painful punishment will be theirs.

We find that the Truth says, once in describing the abode of the disbelievers, that it is a "painful punishment," and once that for them is a "great punishment," and once a "humiliating punishment." Why?

Because punishment has several aspects. There may be a punishment that is painful, but the one punished puts on a show of endurance before the one who punishes him and displays that he still possesses some remaining steadfastness; he feels the pain but holds himself proud over the pain. For this reason the poet said: "And my steadfastness before the scorners, I show them that I am not broken by the misfortunes of time."

So steadfastness is a kind of pride over the reality. Therefore, after that comes His saying, the Truth, that for such people there is a humiliating punishment, meaning they will taste humiliation and pain, and none of them will be able to show steadfastness. This kind of punishment does not stop merely at the limits of ordinary pain; rather, it is a great punishment in its quantity and measure, painful in its impact, and humiliating in abasement and in crushing the human soul and its arrogance. Therefore, when we find that the punishment Allah has prepared for the disbelievers is described as "painful punishment," and once as "great punishment," and once as "humiliating punishment," let us know that each has its own meaning; the matter is not phrases said in this way without an intended meaning.

I want to pause here in this discussion at "the lam of consequence" (lam al-'aqibah), because some try to create difficulties from it. Those who lie in wait for the words of Allah try to attack them, and they only search in what they imagine, out of ignorance, to be points of weakness. And He, glory be to Him, says about the disbelievers, may Allah protect us, while they are in the Fire:

﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return [to disbelief], we will be wrongdoers. He said, "Remain in it, and do not speak to Me. Indeed, there was a party of My servants who said, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful.' But you took them in ridicule until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 107-110]

The disbelievers occupied themselves with mocking the people of faith through gestures, sneering, winking, accusing them of backwardness or mysticism, or similar kinds of mockery, to the extent that they forgot the matter of faith. What made them forget the remembrance of Allah? Their occupation with mocking the people of faith made them forget the remembrance of Allah.

The disbelievers spent all their time mocking the people of faith until they forgot and did not remember that there is a Creator of the universe. This is what is called "the ultimate consequence" (ghayat al-'aqibah), and not a purpose and cause of the will, because they did not intend to forget the remembrance of Allah, but their affair ended in that.

Allah will punish the disbelievers with a painful, great, and humiliating punishment. Each description has its intended meaning in the text, so as to encompass all states of humiliation, from pain: the one who does not feel pain from a small thing and cannot bear strong pain will find great pain, and likewise the one who shows steadfastness against great pain will find humiliating pain.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾

When we hear the words of God, "and let not suppose" (wa-la yahsabanna), it is a prohibition. And what has God forbidden the disbelievers? When the disbeliever finds himself having escaped the sword of the believers in battle, and his life has been prolonged in disbelief, he thinks that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has left him alone because it is good for him, since he understands that his life is the most precious thing he has. So long as his life has been preserved for him, that is the good. We say to such a disbeliever: life is time, and time is the vessel of events. Therefore time in itself is not praised except by the event that occurs within it. If the event that occurs in time is good, then time is good; and if the event that occurs in time is evil, then time is evil. And since these people are disbelievers, it is necessary that all their movements in existence and the events they carry out are of the kind of evil and not of the kind of good, because they walk on other than God's method. Indeed, they may be following a method opposed to God's method and harmful to it.

And that is evil. Therefore God does not give them respite for the purpose of good; rather, God gives them respite because, so long as they remain in disbelief, they occupy the times of their lives with evil events that contradict God's method. And every evil event has its punishment and its recompense. Therefore, prolonging their life is evil for them.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is good for them.﴾ "Yahsabanna" is an imperfect verb, and its past tense is "hasiba" with a kasra on the sin. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, said in another place in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2]

The past is "hasiba" with a kasra on the sin, and the imperfect is "yahsabu" with a fatha on the sin. As for "hasaba" (yahsibu), with a kasra in the imperfect and a fatha in the past, it comes from calculation and counting, which is a precise numerical count.

The verbs "hasiba" and "yahsabu" come to mean supposing (zann), and supposition, as we know, is an imaginary matter. The Truth, glory be to Him, reminds them that their suppositions, that the continuation of their lives is good for them, are not truth. Rather, they are guesswork and conjecture that do not reach certainty.

It is true that a life is counted in years, because life is the container of events; and life in itself, stripped of events, cannot be described as its prolongation being good or evil. Rather, it is said that life is good or evil by the events that occur within it. The events that occur from the disbeliever occur outside a faithful method, so they must be evil, even if he does what outwardly appears good, for he does it to harm God's method. Had the matter been one of numerical arithmetic, we would say "hasaba" and "yahsibu" (with a fatha on the sin in the past and a kasra in the imperfect). But it is a matter of imagination and supposition; therefore we say "yahsabu" with a fatha in the imperfect, that is, yazunnu (he supposes).

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, We give them respite﴾. What is al-imla' (giving respite)? Al-imla' is the extension and prolongation of time. Therefore we find in the Qur'an:

﴿He said, "Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me alone for a long time."﴾ [Maryam: 46]

He commands Abraham, peace be upon him, to forsake him for a long period. This is the meaning of ﴿and leave me alone for a long time﴾.

The intended meaning here is that the prolonging of their lives after they have escaped the swords of the believers is not good for them, and it is not correct that they suppose it is good for them, because God only gives them respite; ﴿so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾. Here we find the "lam of consequence" (lam al-'aqibah).

And beware, O believer, of saying that God has done this in order to punish them. No; for God, glory be to Him and exalted, has established His laws in the universe and applies them to whoever departs from His method. Whoever commits sin, God punishes him for it. ﴿We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin﴾; so every span of time that passes over them, they perform sinful deeds in it, contrary to the method.

﴿And for them is a humiliating punishment﴾. The word "humiliating" (muhin) comes as a description of the punishment that fits perfectly; because the disbeliever may come out of the battle with pride and conceit that no one could cut off his neck with a sword, and he swaggers in sinful might. Therefore, mere pain is not sufficient here, for he may conceal the pain and endure it; but when the punishment is humiliating, it is the fitting retribution for such a situation. And the Speaker here is God, and He is the All-Knowing of what is fitting for every state.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 179:

And after that, the Truth says: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen...﴾

When we hear "ma kana" (it was not/would not be), let us know that here is "juhud" (negation), meaning that there is someone who denies the matter, and they call it "lam al-juhud" (the lam of negation/denial). Before the incident of Uhud, the hypocrites were mixed in among the believers. Would Allah leave the matter so mixed up, and not expose the hypocrites through events that show their true positions regarding faith? No, He, glory be to Him and exalted, does not accept that, so that the hypocrites do not remain a plot within the ranks of the believers. The events had to come to expose them. And the events of Uhud came to shake the ranks attributed to faith and sort them out, so that the wicked is distinguished from the good, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth:

﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but as for that which benefits mankind, it remains on the earth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17]

Thus the events of Uhud were necessary.

And the saying of the Truth: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers﴾ is intended to mean that Allah would not have left the believers and abandoned them, exposed to the mixing of the hypocrites with them without the hypocrites being distinguished by anything at all, so that the matter would not remain confined to what Allah informs His Messenger of regarding the hypocrites. For if Allah had informed His Messenger alone of the matter of the hypocrites, and if the Messenger had announced that to the believers without a real test of the hypocrites, that would have been merely a theoretical diagnosis of hypocrisy coming from one side. Allah willed that a clear event and a real experimental trial should come, showing and revealing the reality, so that the hypocrites would be exposed, so that none of them could object when described as a hypocrite, and so that this description would not be mere words from an opponent, but by an act they themselves committed in practice. In this way the proof is made extremely strong.

The hypocrites were the first of people to rush to the front rows in prayer, because each hypocrite wanted to conceal his hypocrisy and hide it, so he was eager for what the believers rushed toward. The hypocrite knew that the believers compete to attend prayer, so he hastened to be in the first row of the prayer. Allah, glory be to Him, informs His Messenger:

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would surely know them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 30]

That is, if you observe their speech, you would know them, just like all the hypocrites in the world: you notice in their speech a glimpse of hypocrisy. When the believer sits with a group of hypocrites and the time of the noon prayer comes and the adhan calls to prayer, you find the believer saying: "Let us rise to the prayer," and here the hypocrite mocks and says to the believer: "Take me upon your wing to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection." Such a remark is "lahn al-qawl" (the tone of speech). Or when a believer enters upon a group of people among whom is a hypocrite, the hypocrite greets the believer with a tone of mockery: "How are you, O Shaykh (so-and-so)?" Meaning that he is not at ease with the presence of the believer, so he mocks him.

This is from "lahn al-qawl" by which the hypocrite is revealed.

Such operations, when faced by the conscious, enlightened believer upon whom Allah bestows radiant illuminations, become fuel for the believer and increase his faith, because the believer is upon the path of truth and is in control of himself; the hypocrite is not in control of himself. Therefore he wants to draw the believer away from his creed so that he may be with him in hypocrisy, God forbid.

The believer must prepare himself to face hypocrites who want to turn him away from faith, and he will find people who mock him and wink at him, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as guardians over them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-33]

The hypocrite or the disbeliever may say to his family: "Today I saw a shaykh, or a religious man, or a pious person, and I mocked him and humiliated him," and the hypocrite jokes with such a saying in his corrupt environment, and the Truth reveals it to us in His noble saying, to reassure the believers and to compensate every believer for what afflicts him from the people of hypocrisy and corruption:

﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34-36]

So the Truth, glory be to Him, asks the believers on the Day of Resurrection: Have We been able to requite the disbelievers and hypocrites who mocked you? They will say: Yes, O Lord of the worlds, they have been repaid and recompensed for their deeds, in full and complete recompense.

Indeed, the mockery of the hypocrites and disbelievers toward the believers has a worldly term that ends, but mockery in the Hereafter never ends. When we, the believers, measure it, we find that we are the winners and the victorious, God willing. For if any hypocrite were left to infiltrate the embrace of the believers without this being shown to the believers, the matter would be difficult to remedy, and therefore the Truth says to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would surely know them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 30]

And the Truth does not suffice with that, but He reveals to us the reality of the hypocrites through experimental trials, so that none of them can say: "I am not a hypocrite." When Allah exposes the hypocrite and reveals him through a resounding and shameful incident which shows that he is a hypocrite, he is then branded with hypocrisy, because many people who remain all their lives practising hypocrisy, relying on the fact that they are Muslims outwardly, are not left alone by Allah; rather, Allah must bring upon them some thought or some circumstance so that they fall into the trap of the believers discovering them, so that the believers may know them and assess them for what they really are. Glory be to Him, the One who said:

﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾

The word "yadhar" means "to leave" or "to abandon." Grammarians know that there are two verbs, "yadharu" and "yada'u" (ي��در / يدع), whose past tense the Arabs did not use; these two verbs have no past form. We use them in the present tense.

Allah, glory be to Him, would not have left the believers in their state of mixing, with the hypocrites infiltrating among them and the believers not knowing the hypocrites; therefore He distinguishes and makes manifest the wicked from the good.

He does not suffice with informing the Prophet of the matter of the wicked only, but He exposes the wicked through a real act. He says: ﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen﴾; for if Allah had disclosed the unseen to you so that you would know the hypocrites, they would have denied themselves before you and concealed them from you. Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, causes events to occur so that the wicked is revealed from the good, and after that the hypocrite is branded with hypocrisy through his own admission and the admission of his act.

﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾. He, majestic and exalted, chooses from His messengers whom He wills to inform them of some of the unseen, so that they may increase in confidence that Allah does not abandon them; that is, He gives the Messenger indications about the hypocrites, so that the Messenger increases in confidence that Allah does not abandon him.

And Allah, in His mercy, does not disclose the unseen to all the believers, for if the believer were to know the unseen, many affairs in the universe would be corrupted. Suppose Allah had informed a person of the unseen of his life, so that he knew a thousand happy events and then one troubling event; the troubling event that occurs after twenty years would spoil for him his enjoyment of the happy events.

And if a person wishes to know the unseen of people, would he accept that someone else know his unseen? Why, O human, do you want to know the unseen of others? Would any one of us accept that people know his unseen? No. Therefore, concealing information from people and making it unseen is a great blessing.

Nevertheless, people insist on knowing the unseen. And we see those who go after charlatans and soothsayers, and those who falsely claim to be friends of Allah, all for the sake of knowing some of the unseen. Here we say: the skill of the soothsayer is not in telling you what will happen to you in the future, but in one of these pretenders to knowledge of the unseen saying: a harmful event will befall you, and I will prevent it or push it away from you. No one can repel the decree of Allah, so let us leave the future until it happens. Why? So that one does not live in worry and grief before it occurs. Therefore the saying of the Truth: ﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen﴾ is a sunnah from Allah, for the order of dominion is arranged by it and needs it.

Every person has fluctuations with himself, and there may come a period in which he becomes weak in some matter. If another learns the area of weakness in one person, and this person learns the area of weakness in his brother, then all people will appear weak in each other's eyes. It is among Allah's favours that He has concealed the unseen of people from people, and made a person strong in what we do not know, and so the movement of life proceeds in the orderliness that Allah willed.

﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾. The Truth chooses from the messengers, that is some of the messengers, not all of the messengers, to inform them of the unseen, so as to give them assurance that they are connected to the One who sent them. He, glory be to Him, did not send them so as to abandon them; no, they are connected to Him; therefore He informs them of the unseen. We have said that the unseen is of kinds: the absolute unseen is that which is hidden from you and from everyone else.

But there is an unseen that is hidden from you and known to others, and this is not unseen.

An example of that: if the wallet of one of you is lost, and the thief is unseen, and its place is unseen to its owner, but the one who stole it knows its place. So this is unseen to the one robbed, but it is not unseen to the thief, because it is not absolutely unseen. This is what the charlatans use to deceive the naive people: some charlatans and sorcerers may contact the devil or the jinn, and tell the victim a story about the thing that was stolen from him. These sorcerers do not know the unseen, for the absolute unseen is that which no one knows, for Allah has reserved it for Himself.

Another example: the inventions that humans discover in the universe, which were a secret, but Allah revealed those things to them; and their discovery may also have been made by disbelievers. Did anyone say that they knew the unseen? No; for such knowledge has preliminaries, and they researched the secrets of Allah, and Allah granted them success in taking up its causes, as long as they exerted effort, and Allah gives people, believer and disbeliever alike, its causes. And as long as they take hold of them, He gives them their reward for that. And to Allah belongs the highest likeness, and He is exalted above every comparison. I say this example for the sake of approximation:

A teacher who gives a geometry exercise to a student to solve: is the arrival of the solution an unseen matter? No; for the student knows how to solve the geometry exercise, because in it are the given data which he reflects upon in a particular manner, and the result is produced. And as long as the student arrives at a result for an exercise after taking the given data, that is not unseen.

Therefore we must realize that the unseen is what is hidden from all, and this is what Allah has reserved the knowledge of, the absolute unseen; and He, glory be to Him and exalted, makes some of His creation from among the messengers know it, and He, glory be to Him, the Sayer

Almighty God says next: "And let not those who are niggardly with what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty think that it is better for them. Nay, it is worse for them. They shall have the collar of what they were niggardly with around their necks on the Day of Resurrection..."

Some of the hypocrites and disbelievers thought that long life was an advantage for them. And here we are, dealing with another people who thought that the wealth they accumulate is good, so that whenever it increases, they rejoice. Thus God says: "And let not those who are niggardly with what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty..." The wealth has come to them from the bounty of God. That is because they entered this world without pockets. None of us has seen a shroud that has pockets. None of us has seen the swaddling cloth of a newborn baby that has pockets. A person enters the world without a pocket and leaves it without a pocket. Everything that comes to a person is from the bounty of God. No one has invented the things from which provision comes. One may develop from existing provision: one may advance in means and causes, and a person has a share in the movement that God gave him to "travel in the earth" (yadrib fi al-ard, a phrase meaning to travel or work in the land). But no one brings land from his own possession to plant in, no one brings seeds from himself that did not exist before and plants them, and no one brings water that did not exist before to irrigate with. The earth is from God, the seeds are a gift from God, the water is God's provision, and even the movement by which a person moves is from the bounty of God.

So, by God, if a person wanted to lift an axe to strike the earth with one blow, does the person know how many muscles move in order to raise the axe? And how many muscles move when the axe comes down?!!

And when a person strikes with the axe, he strikes it into God's earth. Whoever wants an axe for himself goes to the blacksmith to have it made for him. But has the person asked himself where the iron came from? On this God said:

﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]

So what, then, do you create, O human?

You take the raw primary materials from God, and you expend in them the movement granted to you by God, and you do not create anything from nothing; rather, you create from something that already exists. Everything is from the bounty of God. You, O human, are a "mudarib" (one who travels/works) in God's creation. Your mind that thinks: who created it? It is God. Your limbs that act at the command of the mind: who created them? It is God.

Your limbs act upon a medium, which is the earth, with a tool, which is the axe, and then you irrigate it with water that comes down from the sky. So what is yours, O human? You must know that you have nothing at all in all of this; you are merely a "mudarib" for God. So give Him His due in this "mudaraba" (partnership/working share).

God, glorified is He, asks only a modest portion of the yield and fruit of the earth. If it is irrigated with rain water, then the due is a tenth of its produce; and if the land is irrigated by a water-wheel (tanbur) or a waterwheel (saqiya), then the due is half a tenth.

The one who farms land plows it on one day and irrigates it every two weeks.

As for the one who trades in commercial transactions, these require action at every moment, so God set the zakat on him at the rate of two and a half percent.

So the more a person's movement increases, the more God reduces the rate of zakat. This process is the reverse of human practice: the more his movement increases, the more they take from him!!

God, glorified is He, wants movement to exist in the universe, because if movement exists in the universe, people benefit even if one did not intend to move. After that, where does what God takes from you go? He gives it to your brother and to others. Since He, glorified is He, gives your brother and your colleague from the fruit and result of your movement, in this there is assurance and security for you, because others will give to you if you become incapable and unable to earn. In this there is reassurance regarding the calamities (aghyar) of God in you. If calamities come upon you, you will find people who help you, and thus society is united, and this is social insurance in its noblest meanings. So all of this is from the bounty of God.

"And let not those who are niggardly with what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty think that it is better for them. Nay, it is worse for them." Those who are miserly with God's bounty think that miserliness is good merely because it piles up wealth for them, and that is not correct, because the Almighty says: "They shall have the collar of what they were niggardly with around their necks on the Day of Resurrection." That is, what they were miserly with, God will make into a collar around the neck of the miser, and when people see the collar on the miser's neck, they will say: "This is one who withheld God's right from his wealth."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) depicts this matter precisely when he explains to us that whoever is required to give God's right and does not pay it, the wealth he withheld and clung to and was miserly with will appear to its owner on the Day of Resurrection as a "shuja' aqra'" (a bald, huge serpent), and it will encircle his neck. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever God gives wealth to and he does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be depicted for him as a bald serpent with two black spots over its eyes; it will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, seize him by his two cheeks (lahzimatayn, meaning his jaws), and say: 'I am your wealth, I am your treasure.'" Then he recited the saying of the Exalted: "And let not those who are niggardly with what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty..." to the end of the verse.

So whoever hoards out of miserliness toward God, he increases the collar that coils around his neck on the Day of Resurrection.

"And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and God is Acquainted with what you do." Yes, to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth; then He places it with whomever He wills. Everything in the universe is ascribed to God, and God distributes it as He wills. Faith calls us not to postpone charity until the state when the soul reaches the throat. It has been narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: A man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, which charity is greatest in reward?" He said: "That you give charity while you are healthy and miserly, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth, and do not delay until, when you reach the throat, you say: 'To so-and-so such-and-such, and to so-and-so such-and-such, and it has already belonged to so-and-so.'" Because when the soul reaches the throat, one no longer has wealth.

The saying of the Almighty: "And God is Acquainted with what you do" is a matter that makes the heart tremble with fear and dread. A person may deceive other people: you find someone who evades taxes and falsifies two ledgers for taxes, one for genuine earnings and another for false losses, and this tax evader owns the wealth and then denies it. This person must know that God is Acquainted with everything he does.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 181:

Then the Truthful Lord says: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich..."﴾

It is related, concerning the occasion of revelation of this noble verse: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that when the saying of the Exalted was revealed, ﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾, the Jews said: "O Muhammad, has your Lord become poor, so that He asks His servants for a loan?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich."﴾

Those who lived alongside Islam in Medina were Jews. The Jews, as we know, used to boast and take pride before the world that they were the People of the Book, of knowledge and understanding, and they would claim, in the environment in which they lived, that they were the masters of the economy, as they say of themselves now.
