Whoever wanted something would take it from the Jews. They would build fortresses and acquire weapons to display strength. Islam came and took from them all these forms of dominance, and then they enjoyed the benefits of Islam: the protection of their wealth, their security, and their lives.

Would Islam leave them thus, enjoying what the Muslims enjoy of security, tranquility, physical safety and the safety of property, and yet not take anything from them? Indeed, Islam took from them the jizya (poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Islamic rule). It was not acceptable that a Muslim should pay the zakat while the Jews sat within the community of faith without paying the cost of their protection. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent our master Abu Bakr al-Siddiq to the Jews in the place where they studied. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq entered the House of Study (bayt al-midras), and found many people of the Jews gathered around a man among them called Finhas, who was one of their scholars and rabbis, and with him a rabbi called Ashya'. Abu Bakr said to him: "Woe to you, O Finhas! Fear Allah and embrace Islam, for by Allah you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, who has come with the truth from Him; you find him written with you in the Torah and the Gospel." Finhas said: "By Allah, O Abu Bakr, we have no need of Allah on account of poverty. Rather, it is He who is poor toward us; we do not humble ourselves to Him as He humbles Himself to us, and we are free of Him. If He were rich of us, He would not borrow from us as your companion claims, forbidding you from usury while giving us [loans]; if He were rich, He would not have given us usury." Abu Bakr became angry, struck Finhas's face a severe blow, and said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would strike off your neck, O enemy of Allah! Deny us as much as you can, if you are truthful."

Finhas went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, and said: "O Muhammad, look at what your companion has done to me!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What prompted you to do what you did, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy of Allah said a monstrous thing, claiming that Allah is poor and they are rich. When he said that, I became angry for the sake of Allah at what he said, and so I struck his face." Finhas denied this and said: "I did not say that."

So Allah revealed, concerning what Finhas said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich."﴾

Those who did not grasp the secret of the beautiful expression in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ [al-Hadid: 11]

This saying is a mark of respect from the Truth, glorified is He, for human initiative in ownership. Why did Allah honour the human right to ownership? He, glorified is He, wants to entice the active person to increase his activity, and to move the inactive to become active. So if He, glorified is He, asks for something of this wealth, He does not say to the person: "Give back what I gave you." Rather, it is as if He, glorified is He, were saying: "I will honour your sweat, I will honour your movement, I will honour your thought, I will honour your limbs, your capacities and everything that is in you. If I take anything from you, I will not say to you, 'Give me what I gave you,' but I say to you: 'Lend it to Me.' And if you lend it, you will lend it not for My benefit, but for your brother's. And later He will lend to you from the Capable One, which is for you when need befalls you." Why? Because I am Allah, who summoned My creation into existence; and since I am Allah who summoned creation into being, their provision is incumbent upon Me.

When one of the human beings invites two of his friends, he prepares food sufficient for five or ten people. Since Allah is the One who summoned creation into existence, He is the One who guarantees their provision. And when He guarantees their provision, they must move. And when they move, He, glorified is He, guarantees the effects of movement, so that each one attains what pleases Him, or at least what suffices him of necessities.

Therefore, when the effects of movement from wealth came, and human intervention in it through nationalization and other measures occurred, movement decreased. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows the human eagerness for the benefit of his own self, so He entices him with that, so that he moves, and society will benefit from his movement, whether the person intends it or not. Thus, when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, borrows from some of His creation for some of His creation, He, glorified is He, does not retract what He has granted. Rather, He, majestic and exalted, says:

﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him, and he will have a noble reward?﴾ [al-Hadid: 11]

I cite this example, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: we humans may be compelled into this situation. When one of us gives his children pocket money, each child saves what remains of it. Then a circumstance arises for some of the children requiring money that the father does not have at hand at the moment the event occurs. So the father says to his children: "Lend me what is in your piggy banks, and I will return it to you multiplied." He has taken it from their brother, but because he is the one who gave it first, he did not retract the gift; rather he asked for it as a loan. And when the first of the month comes, he returns the loan multiplied. If this is what happens in human affairs, what then of what happens from the Creator, the Giver, to His servants?

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾

But the Jews did not take the matter with this understanding; rather, they took it with the dullness of materialism, and said: "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich." Therefore the Truthful Lord said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich. We will record what they have said."﴾

Why would Allah record that, when He is the Knower of all things? This statement came also to indicate documentation: when this man comes to read his book on the Day of Resurrection, he finds it written; for writing serves to document what might be denied (the verb being in the passive form: "is denied"). If knowledge were from Allah alone, the servant might say: "You, O Lord, are the One who punishes; You may say what You say." But when it is written against them for them to read, this is a documentation that cannot be denied.

The Jew did not understand that lending to Allah is a gentle kindness from the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and an appeal to evoke human tenderness toward humans. The Truth willed to honour the effect of your effort and sweat, O human: if you come to some wealth, it is your property. Allah did not say to you: "Give to your brother." Rather, glorified and exalted is He, in gentleness toward His creation, says: "Lend to Me," so that the person may be assured that what he gave is with One who is solvent. But the manners of the Children of Israel toward Allah are lacking, for they said earlier:

﴿The Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained up." Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outspread; He spends as He wills.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64]

The cause of this was that drought and famine afflicted them, because of their denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah had expanded provision for the Jews in this world until they were the most wealthy of people. When they disobeyed Allah, disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ and denied him, Allah constricted [their provision] during his lifetime, peace be upon him. Finhas ibn 'Azura' and those with him among the Jews said: 'The hand of Allah is chained up,' and so Allah revealed this verse." They said: "The heaven has withheld from us, and the hand of Allah is chained up, so He has not given us provision." Thus they had dared against Him with a word, or against His companions with mockery. Glorified is He clarifies to His Messenger that they did not do this to you or to your followers; this is their stance toward Me. If their stance and bad manners reached the point that they dare against the sacred, exalted Essence, saying ﴿Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ and saying ﴿The hand of Allah is chained up﴾, will you grieve and sorrow that they say to you or to your followers anything that may harm you?

How excellent is this consolation from Allah to His Messenger, and how excellent is this solace. The Truth adds: ﴿We will record what they have said.﴾ Why would Allah record what they said, when His knowledge is eternal and does not forget?

﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 52]

The word "We will record" came so that the Exalted would not hold them to account on the Day of Resurrection for what He Himself says they did, but for what was written against them, so that they might read it themselves, and so that it would be proof against them. As if writing is not only as we imagine, but a recording of voices and breaths; and on the Day of Resurrection each person will find what he did inscribed:

﴿Read your book; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ [al-Isra': 14]

This saying indicates that at the moment a person sees what was written in the book, he will know that it is from him. If we now record the breaths and words of our adversaries, do you find it far-fetched that the One who taught us this should record breaths, voices and movements, so that when a person reads them and sees them, he cannot contend or deny them? ﴿We will record what they have said.﴾ And they said: ﴿Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich.﴾ This is disobedience at its peak and insolence against the Exalted Essence. Nor were they content with that, but they killed the prophets whom Allah sent to guide them. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿We will record what they have said, and their killing of the prophets without right.﴾

When this news reaches the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is a consolation to him from the Truth, glorified is He. They said about your Lord, O Muhammad, what they said, and they killed the prophets, your brothers. If they have done to you what they have done, do not grieve, for they will be recompensed for what We have recorded against them by their own testimony, and We will say: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ Burning produces a sensory pain in the soul.

Sensation differs from one sense to another: sometimes it is by sight, sometimes by hearing, sometimes by smell, or by touch, or by taste.

Taste is the lord of the senses; it is never lost from anyone. We may find a person who is blind, another who is deaf, or a third who has been struck with paralysis so that his hand cannot touch, and one who suffers from constant congestion so that he is no longer able to smell. But taste is a sense that does not disappear from any person. Therefore taste is a matter from within the self, and so it is more intense in causing pain. And we find the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, saying:

﴿Allah struck a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the blessings of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾ [al-Nahl: 112]

Consider the Qur'anic expression ﴿Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear.﴾ The expression uses "making to taste" (adha), and it applies it to something that is not tasted, namely a garment. Is a garment tasted? No, but He, glorified is He, wants to alert the human being that all the senses within him feel, even that hidden sense inside the soul; this encompasses every part of the human being.

Thus "making to taste" envelops the human being in this noble Qur'anic imagery: ﴿Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear.﴾ So it is an intensity of the impact of pain, and the comprehensiveness of painful torment for all parts of the body, until tasting becomes everywhere.

Thereafter the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿That is because of what your hands have sent before,...ﴩ

﴿That﴾ refers to the torment of the Burning. Allah, glorified is He, did not wrong them; rather, they were the ones who wronged themselves. ﴿Because of what your hands have sent before﴾. Does this mean that all sins are things sent forth by the hand? There is disobedience of the eye, disobedience of the tongue, disobedience of the foot, and disobedience of the heart, and the sins cannot be counted. Why, then, did the Truth say: ﴿because of what your hands have sent before﴾?

The Truth said that because outward deeds are usually carried out by the hand; the hand is the limb with which we perform most of our affairs. Accordingly, the Truth's words ﴿because of what your hands have sent before﴾ are meant to say: because of what you have sent forth with any of the limbs.

Then He, glorified is He, informs us: ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. He made them taste the torment of the Burning as a result of what He had prescribed for them, of speech and deed. The speech was the slander with the tongue when they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich﴾. The deed was their killing of the prophets. So they deserve that torment.

The general principle concerning God and the justice of God is that He is not unjust to the servants.

Here is a pause for the opponents of Islam among the Orientalists. They say: Allah says in their Qur'an ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, and the word "ẓallām" is an intensive form of "ẓālim." So there is "ẓālim" and there is "ẓallām," and "ẓallām" is one who wrongs with strong and repeated injustice; "ẓallām" is an intensive form of "ẓālim."

When we respond to them, we must know that intensive forms (ṣīghat al-mubālagha) are many. The linguists know them to be: fa''āl, fa'īl, mif'āl, fa'ūl, fa'il, so ẓallām is like our saying "akkāl" and like our saying "qattāl" instead of saying "qātil." The qātil has committed the crime of killing once, but the qattāl is one who has committed the crime many times and killing has become his trade. Likewise "nāhib" (plunderer), and one for whom plundering has become his trade is called "nahhāb," meaning that if he plunders, he plunders much and multiplies plunder among people.

This is called the intensive form. When an intensive form occurs in an affirmative statement, that is, in an affirmed matter, it affirms the lesser. When it is said: "So-and-so is ẓallām," it is established that he is also ẓālim, because as long as we have affirmed the intensity, we affirm the lesser. Likewise we say: "So-and-so is allāma" or "allāma," meaning that this person is a scholar. But if we say: "So-and-so is ʿālim," that does not establish that he is "allāma." So the intensive form does not mean merely "active participle"; it is also an active participle in which exaggeration is present, because the act comes from him strongly, or because the act is repeated and multiplied from him. If we affirm the intensive attribute, then by greater right the non-intensive attribute is affirmed. If someone says: "So-and-so is akkāl," it establishes for us that he is an eater; this is in affirmation.

The matter differs in negation. If we negate the intensive attribute, the attribute without intensity is affirmed by greater right. But if the intensive attribute is negated, that does not necessarily entail the negation of the lesser attribute.

The clarification of the verse we are now dealing with is: ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾.

The Orientalists understand from this saying that it is merely a negation of exaggeration in injustice, but that it did not negate that He is unjust, and the Orientalists did not understand why the exaggeration is here. The Truth has said: He is not ever unjust (ẓallām) to the servants (ʿabīd), and He did not say He is not unjust to the servant (ʿabd). This means that He is not ever unjust to the servants from Adam until the Hour is established. For if He were to wrong all of them — God forbid — He would be called ẓallām, even if He wronged each one with the slightest wrong. For injustice is repeated, and that repetition comes from the number of those wronged, who are the servants. So if one wants to multiply the argument, let the dull-witted among them notice that Allah said: ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ and did not say He is not unjust to the servant.

And if the wrongdoer must be stronger than the wronged, then every injustice is qualified by the strength of the wrongdoer. If God had permitted Himself to wrong, He would not be a wrongdoer merely; because the greatness of His power would not make Him ẓālim but ẓallām.

So if the event is intended, it is ẓallām, and if we intend the repetition of the event, it is ẓallām. When some Orientalists try to object to the Truth's saying ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, this objection shows an inability to grasp the purposes of the words in the language, or these people know the purposes of the words and try to deceive people who do not possess a linguistic stock by which they can understand the purposes of words. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, makes available for His Book those who draw attention to the manifestation of its miraculousness in its verses.

After the Truth had finished with the Battle of Uhud, He, glorified is He, wanted to establish principles that clarify the camps of hostility to Islam: the camp of the People of the Book, the camp of the Quraysh polytheists in Mecca, and the camp of the polytheists around Medina who used to raid Medina.

So after the Battle of Uhud, which sorted, refined, tested, and afflicted, and made the people know the matters of religion, the Truth then wished to lay down the principles.

The Qur'an made clear: these are your enemies; remember them well. They said such-and-such about your Lord, they say such-and-such about your Messenger, and they killed your prophets.

Then, after that, the Truth (Allah), glory be to Him, says: ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from us that we not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which the fire devours..."﴾

They claim this and say: "Our Lord told us this in the Torah: beware of believing in a messenger who comes to you until he brings you a tangible miracle. This tangible miracle is that the messenger offers a sacrifice (qurban) and fire descends from the sky and consumes it."

This was true, and we all hear the story of Qabil and Habil:

﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when each offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous. If you extend your hand toward me to kill me, I will not extend my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 27-28]

And we want to turn to the Qur'an and reflect: why did this expression come: ﴿it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other﴾? Acceptance comes from Allah, and it is a secret matter with Him, so how do we know that Allah accepted or did not accept? There must be that Allah has set for acceptance a tangible sign. We know that a person may do a deed and Allah accepts it, and we find another person who does a deed and Allah does not accept it, may Allah protect us. So who informed us that Allah accepted one person's deed and offering and did not accept the other's offering?

Since acceptance is one of Allah's secrets, we will not know the sign of acceptance unless it is something tangible, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other﴾. And the one whose offering was not accepted by Allah said: ﴿I will surely kill you﴾. It is as if the one whose offering was accepted had known, and the one whose offering was not accepted had also known. Therefore, there must have been a tangible matter that occurred.

We have said that Allah addresses His creatures according to the measure of the maturity of their minds, both tangibly and in meaning. For this reason, the miracles of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, given to the earlier prophets before the Messenger of Allah, were tangible matters. The miracle Allah gave to Ibrahim was fire that does not burn, the staff of our master Musa turned into a serpent, and our master 'Isa, peace be upon him, healed the blind and the leper and raised the dead by Allah's permission. A tangible miracle has the feature that it convinces the senses, but it ends once it has occurred one time. But the intellectual miracle that suits the maturity of humanity is the lasting miracle, and for it to remain a lasting miracle it cannot be tangible.

So when a lasting miracle comes for a messenger who is the Seal of the Prophets, and by whose method the Hour will stand, this miracle must have an extended duration, and extension contradicts tangibility, because tangibility remains confined to the one who saw it, and whoever did not see it does not relate it or believe in it except when he has great trust in the one who reported it. Adam's sons, Qabil and Habil, each offered a sacrifice.

"Qurban" in language is like "ghufran" and "udwan," and qurban is a thing or deed by which the servant draws near to Allah.

Acceptance of this deed from the righteous is one of Allah's secrets. What informs these people that Habil's offering was accepted by Allah and Qabil's offering was not accepted by Allah? The matter must be tangible. Certainly Qabil and Habil disagreed, but the Qur'an did not tell us what they disagreed about. It is only a claim that one of them was closer to Allah, but in what form? The Qur'an did not show us that. If the matter were important, Allah would have shown it to us in the noble Qur'an. So do not say the dispute was about marriage or otherwise. What appeared to us from the Qur'an is that a dispute occurred between them, or that they both appealed to heaven for judgment. The principle of appealing to heaven for judgment no one can annul. Each of them had a doubt (shubhah). When Qabil's doubt stood against Habil's doubt, there was no persuasion from one holding a doubt, and therefore they went to arbitration.

In our modern age, when we disagree about something, we say: let us draw lots. This is so that no person submits to another person's desire, but both submit to fate: each writes a paper, then they leave a third person to draw one of the two papers. As for Habil and Qabil, the noble Qur'an mentions: ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when each offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other﴾.

So each of them had a doubt, and neither was able to persuade the other; therefore, after Allah accepted Habil's offering, Qabil said: ﴿I will surely kill you﴾. Then what did Habil say? He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous﴾.

So the one from whom Allah accepts the offering is the one who will be killed, and the one filled with rage is the one whose offering Allah did not accept, and he is the one who will kill. So what did the owner of the accepted offering say?

﴿If you extend your hand toward me to kill me, I will not extend my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 28]

So this one deserves that Allah accept his offering, because his conscience is awake with the method of heaven, and this is the basis for the acceptance of the offering.

Lest we think that the other, Qabil, was entirely evil merely because desire dominated him, the Truth shows us that there is some good in him, and the evidence for that is the saying of the Truth:

﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother, and he killed him, and he became among the losers.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 30]

This phrasing indicates that he hesitated, for one does not say "tawwa'at al-ma'" (she made the water submissive), but says "tawwa'at al-hadid" (she made the iron submissive). It is as if faith was opposing the soul, but the soul prevailed and made the murder of his brother submissive to him. When Qabil killed his brother and the fury of anger and the frenzy of vengeance subsided, he saw his brother lying in the open:

﴿Then Allah sent a crow searching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's corpse. He said, "Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's corpse?" And he became among the regretful.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 31]

On this same pattern the Jews said: Allah has enjoined on us that we not believe in a messenger unless he brings a miracle of tangible things.

Why did they say that? They said it because the greatest miracle of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, which is the noble Qur'an, was not of the tangible kind, and the era of miracles through tangible things alone has ended. Our Messenger has many tangible miracles, and since these end with their occurrence, the Qur'an became the lasting miracle, and it suits the final message. They demanded that the miracle be tangible so that they could make for themselves a semblance of an excuse for not believing, so they said what the Qur'an recorded:

﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from us that we not believe in any messenger until he comes to us..."﴾ etc.

The Truth in this verse taught us that the sacrifice is consumed by fire, and from this we deduce how Allah accepted Habil's offering and did not accept Qabil's, so that we understand that there is no repetition in the Qur'an. And the Truth shows us His persuasive and delightful divine replies:

﴿Say: "Messengers before me have certainly come to you with clear proofs and with what you say..."﴾ etc., the verse.

Messengers came to you before the Messenger of Allah with the offering that fire consumed, and yet you disbelieved. So if your statement, O Jews, were true, you would have believed in the messengers who came to you with the offering consumed by fire. Thus the Truth reveals that they deceive themselves and deceive the Messenger of Allah, and that it is merely "mumahakat" (contentious quibbling), obstinacy, and persistence in dispute and enmity.

The Truth commands His Messenger to ask: ﴿Why then did you kill them, if you are truthful?﴾

He, glory be to Him, wants to set before us a matter that makes clear that the era of tangible miracles alone has ended, and the maturity of humanity and the intellect's attainment of perfection has begun. Therefore He brought an intellectual sign to remain with the method until the Hour arises. Had the sign been tangible, it would have been limited to the contemporaries who witnessed it, and would have left those who came after without miracle or proof. But the coming of an intellectual miracle lets any believer in our age say: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that is his miracle. But if the miracle were tangible and a sacrifice consumed by fire, what would the believer after that era rely on and depend upon?

The Truth wants to teach us that it is He who brings the signs, and He does not bring signs according to human whims, but brings the signs that establish proof; therefore it is not for humans to propose the sign. He, glory be to Him, is the One who brings the sign, and in it is the proof. Why? Because some said to the Messenger:

﴿They said, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I not but a human messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 90-93]

All these were tangible signs they demanded, and Allah, glory be to Him, responds to that when He said to His Messenger that what prevented Him from sending such signs was the denial of the earlier peoples of them: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ [al-Isra': 59].

So even those who said, "We will not believe until you bring an offering that fire consumes," had messengers come to them before bearing the miracle of the offering consumed by fire, and yet they denied. Therefore the matter is contentious quibbling and obstinacy in dispute. And Allah consoles His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and this consolation here is a consolation by the parallel and example of the messengers. As if the Truth were clarifying: if they have denied you, do not grieve; for they denied many messengers before you, and you are not without precedent among the messengers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 184:

﴿If they deny you, then [know that] messengers before you were denied too, who came with clear proofs, and the Psalms, and the Book giving light.﴾

Exalted be the Truth, glory be to Him, with the spirit of our master, the Messenger of Allah, to a rank of elevation that no human other than him can reach, so He says:

﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you, but it is not you they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ [al-An'am: 33]

So the matter is not your matter. They know that you, O Muhammad, are truthful and never lie at all. ﴿But the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ That is, this matter is not specific to you; rather it refers back to Me. No one says you are a liar; they deny Me. The wrongdoers deny and reject My signs. So the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, here for consolation, and gives him an example that keeps him from grieving over what the Jews and those who deny do. So He says: ﴿If they deny you, then messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs and the Psalms and the Book giving light.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 184]

We know that the condition is the cause of the existence of its answer (jawab al-shart, the consequent of the conditional). So if the answer has occurred before the condition, what is the situation? The Truth clarifies: "If they deny you, O Muhammad, then they have denied messengers before you." That is, the "answer of the condition" has occurred here before the condition. When one of the superficial people, the pretenders to Islam, or one of the orientalists who do not grasp the aims of the language, seizes upon this, he may say:

"The answer in this verse has occurred before the condition." Here we respond to him, saying: Is His saying, ﴿then messengers before you were denied...﴾, the answer of the condition, or is it the evidence of the answer? The Truth has brought this verse to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him:

"If they deny you, then do not grieve, for a people denied their messengers before you." It is a reason (ʿilla) for the answer of the condition, as if He says:

"If they deny you, then do not grieve." Thus what is mentioned is not the answer; rather it is the aspect (ḥaythiyya) of the answer: ﴿then messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs...﴾ etc.

When we say, "So-and-so came to me with such-and-such," it may be that he is the one who brought it, or it may be that he is merely an companion of the one who brought it.

Let us strike this example for clarification — and to Allah belongs the highest similitude — suppose an employee was sent by his superior with an envelope to another person; the employee is the companion of the envelope.

So the clear proofs came from Allah, but these messengers came accompanied by and supported by the clear proofs, so that they would be a proof for the truthfulness of their conveying from Allah: ﴿If they deny you, then messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs.﴾ That is, they came with signs clearly indicating the intended meaning. The signs may be the pointing to cosmic signs, and they may be miracles.

We know that each messenger among those who preceded our master, the Messenger of Allah, had a miracle separate from his methodology. The miracle is one thing, and the book of method is another. The "Scrolls of Abraham" contain the method, but they are not the miracle; the miracle was the fire not harming him and his deliverance. Moses, peace be upon him, had the staff that turned into a serpent and the splitting of the sea, but the book of his method was the "Torah." Jesus, peace be upon him, had the "Gospel" as the book of his method, and his miracle was healing and raising the dead by Allah's permission. Thus the miracle was separate from the method, except for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him; his miracle is the Qur'an, and his method is in the Qur'an. Why?

Because he came as a messenger bearing the complete method, which is the Noble Qur'an. Yet he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is the Seal of the Messengers, so the miracle must remain with the method, so that it may be a proof. Thus the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿came with the clear proofs﴾ means the miracles that indicate their truthfulness.

﴿and the Psalms and the Book giving light﴾: that is, the books that brought the method. They need two things: a method and a miracle.

The "clear proofs" are the miracle, that is, matters clear from Allah and not from any one of them. Then "the method" came in ﴿the Psalms and the Book giving light﴾. The meaning of "zubur" (Psalms/scriptures) is "book," and whatever has been written has been "zabara," that is, written down; this is evidence of documentation, that it is written and so is not obliterated or erased. So "al-zabr" is writing. "Al-zabr" also means admonition, because it prevents the one admonished from doing what he has been warned against, that is, it keeps him from error and from committing deviation. "Al-zabr" also means reason ('aql), because it prevents a person from entering the places of destruction.

To those who wish to take reason as an opportunity for liberation and license, we say: understand the meaning of the word "reason" ('aql). The meaning of 'aql is restraint. Reason restrains you from doing any matter without studying its consequences. "'Aql" derives from "'aqala," meaning to tie, so that one says this and does not say that, and it prevents a person from doing things for which he would be blamed. Also "al-zabr" means the lining of a well: when we dig a well to bring out water, we do not leave it, but make for it an edge of stone and build it from within with stones, so that it is not filled up with dirt. All the meanings of "zabr" converge: it means the written things, and written things have a description: they are luminous, and this illumination means that they show the traveler the obstacles and hindrances of the path, so that he does not stumble.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, consoles His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and clarifies to him: do not grieve if they deny you; for messengers before you were denied, and the messengers came with the method and with the miracle. And after Allah gives the believers and the Messenger of Allah immunity against what the rumor-mongers among the Jews spread and what they say, the cultivation of faithful immunity in the soul requires that Allah inform us through His Messenger of what the call may face, so that confrontations do not surprise us, and He reveals to us what they will say and what they will do.

We do this in the material world: if we fear a certain disease such as cholera, for example, what do we do? We take the very microbe and weaken it in a specific form, then inoculate the healthy with it, so that immunity is cultivated in him and the body can resist the disease.

Then after that the Truth, glory be to Him, brings a matter of faith that must remain in the mind of the believer always. This matter is: if they deny you, their denial is not eternal, for they will end with death. The matter's battle is timed, and the reckoning in the end is with the Truth, glory be to Him; therefore He says: ﴿Every soul shall taste death, and you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 185:

﴿Every soul shall taste death. And you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed. And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾

We note that the word ﴿ذَآئِقَةُ﴾ (tasting) appears here as well. We know that there is "qatl" (killing) and there is "mawt" (death), and "mawt" is the more general term, meaning the ending of life, whether by breaking the body's structure, as in killing, or without breaking the structure, as in the soul's departure and its taking away by natural death (ḥatf al-anf). Therefore, scholars who examine words precisely say: if this person who was killed had not been killed, would he have died? We say: Yes, because the one who was killed dies at his appointed term (ajal). But the one who killed him, did he know the appointed time? No. Thus he is punished for committing the crime of taking a soul, while the one who was killed had God decree that he would part from life through this act.

So every soul will taste death, either by natural death or by being killed. And because most of those who are killed are martyrs, and martyrs are alive, yet all will die. The Exalted says:

﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom God wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]

Look at the precision of the expression: ﴿And you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection⦆. That is, beware lest you expect the result of your faith in this world, for if you were to receive a reward for your faith in this world, it would be a time that passes and ends. So your reward for faith must be in the Hereafter, so that it will be a reward that does not end.

We know what happened at the Second Pledge of al-'Aqabah, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took covenants from the Ansar. They said: "What shall we have for this, O Messenger of God, if we are faithful?" He (ﷺ) did not tell them, "You will be victorious or you will rule the world," but said: "Paradise." They said: "Extend your hand," and he extended his hand and they pledged allegiance to him. Had he promised them anything of this world, any shrewd one among them would have said: "How trivial it is." Therefore, when one man said to his companion: "I love you as much as the world," the other replied: "Am I so worthless in your eyes to this degree?" It is as if the Exalted, glory be to Him, says: Beware lest you understand that the reward of faith is in this world, for if it were in this world it would be transient and would be a small reward for faith, because faith is connected to the One who has no end, which is God. So the reward must be endless, which is Paradise. Thus He said: ﴿And you will only be paid your full rewards﴾.

Those of subtle insight have derived from the word "tuwaffawna" (you will be paid in full) that there are preliminaries, because the meaning of "wafaytuhu ajrahu" is "I gave him his wage and nothing remained owed to him, and I completed it for him." Indeed He, glory be to Him, gives them the needs of faith, and the radiance of faith in the soul of the believer suffices. The answer must accord with the logic of the one who hears this verse; for one who hears it may die shortly after in a battle, and since he died in battle, he did not see victory, nor spoils, nor anything else, so what is his share? He takes his share on the Day of Resurrection: "tuwaffawn." Whoever attains something of it in this world, through victory, through spoils, through the pride of faith in having triumphed over disbelief, that is part of the reward. But the complete payment of the full reward will be in the Hereafter, because the word "tawfiyah" indicates that the full payment and completion of the rewards will be on the Day of Resurrection, and that what comes before that is part of the rewards that those who act deserve.

The Truth says: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed﴾. On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. Recite if you wish: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed﴾."

When you say "zuḥziḥa fulān" (he was drawn away), it means that he was halted in terror. So how does this happen near the Fire? We know that the cause of the Fire is disobedience, and disobedience has an allure for the disobedient, and faith comes to pull them back, so the allure of disobedience takes them. Likewise the recompense is the Fire. So the Fire has an allure, because it will be in a state of rage... And therefore our Lord says:

﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾ [al-Mulk: 8]

The Fire bursts with rage against the disbelievers. And what is the meaning of "bursting with rage"? Have you not seen a pot boiling? When the pot boils, some bubbles come out of it and separate from what is in the pot, and this is "tamayyuz", that is, they separate. And when one of us is in a state of rage, things come out of him like the bubbles of a boiling pot; he foams and froths, meaning his anger has intensified, and these bubbles burn whoever stands before them or touches them, and from the intensity of the boiling some of them separate and break away from the pot. Likewise the Fire. And why does it burst with rage? It bursts with rage against the disbelievers, because its origin is glorifying, praising and thanking. Then the Truth says to it: ﴿Are you filled?﴾ [Qaf: 30], and it says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ [Qaf: 30].

This indicates that the phrase ﴿it almost bursts with rage﴾ is literal. Therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) explains to us that the Fire has an allure, for the Fire is only the result of disobedience in this world, and disobedience in this world is what draws the disobedient. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said about this: "My example and your example is like a man who kindled a fire, and moths and locusts began to fall into it while he was driving them away from it, and I am holding you by your waistbands from the Fire, and you are slipping from my hand." Look at the beautiful comparison: when you kindle a fire in an open space, the first thing you see is that moths, insects and gnats come to the fire, and so they say: "Many a soul has fallen in love with its own destruction."

Those insects came because they were drawn to the light. We see this when we light a fire in an open area: you find many of these insects around it dead. Those insects loved their own destruction; they came to the light, but the fire burned them. Likewise the disobedient person loves his own ruin, because he does not know that this desire will lead him into the Fire.

﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire﴾: that is, the Fire has an allure like the allure of disobedience when it takes hold of a person, and merely being drawn away from the Fire, even if he stands between them, neither in the Fire nor in Paradise, is good. So what of one who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise? He has been freed from harm and given good.

This is a good need, and this is the reason that the Sirat is laid over the Fire, which we will cross. Why? So that the believer sees the Fire while he walks upon the Sirat, into which, had he not been a believer, he would have fallen, and so he says: "Praise be to God who saved me from that Fire."

﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed﴾. Triumph (al-fawz) is deliverance from what you dislike and attaining what you love. Mere deliverance from what you dislike is a blessing, and that you go after deliverance from what you dislike to a blessing, this is triumph. We notice in ﴿zuḥziḥa﴾ that someone other than him has drawn him away. Yes, because God honoured him first in his life with the outpouring of faith, and it is He who also drew him away from the Fire.

The Truth concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, describes the life we know as "dunya" (the nearer, lower world), this indicates that there is a life described as "not dunya," and the non-dunya is the "ʿulyā" (higher). Therefore the Truth says in another verse:

﴿And indeed the Last Abode, that is the true life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64]

That is, it is the life that deserves to be called life, because the worldly life is not measured by its duration from its beginning until the Hour, for that life is for the whole universe. Rather, for each individual, the "dunya" is not that length, but the "dunya" of each individual is the measure of his life in it. And the measure of his life in it is not known: whether it is a moment, a day, a month, or a century. In short, it is limited by a specific limit for each lifespan and a general limit for all lifespans.

Enjoyment in this world is in proportion to a person's share of pleasures, and is according to his capacities. If we look at the world by this measure, its enjoyment is small, and therefore it is not right or proper for a person to be deceived by this enjoyment, recalling God's saying:

﴿Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6-7]

So delusion is that a short-lived enjoyment distracts you from a high enjoyment whose end has no limit. Therefore, so that the one who lives in this world is not deceived and does not play with its little for the sake of the much with God in the Hereafter, he must compare an enjoyment whose term is limited, however long its duration, with an enjoyment whose end has no limit: an enjoyment according to your capacities and an enjoyment according to the vastness of God's bounty. Therefore the life of this world is the enjoyment of delusion, for it deceives the one who is deluded by the trivial and little, away from the great and glorious.

God did not wrong the world when He described it as an enjoyment, but He alerted us that it is not the enjoyment by which one should be deceived and be distracted from a more lasting enjoyment, which is eternity. Then the Exalted, glory be to Him, says to His Messenger and to the followers of His Messenger a matter that establishes in them and assures them that faith alone is the best reward for the believer, even if he does not obtain any of the bliss of this world. Therefore He wanted to settle them in the understanding that those who enter faith should not settle themselves into believing that faith is always victorious, for if it were always victorious, each one would settle himself upon it and be content, because it would guarantee him a tranquil life. Therefore it was necessary to clarify for them that there are trials. The matter of faith is that you will be tested, and the place of the trial is in your souls or in your wealth. So He said:

﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons, and you will surely hear much hurtful speech from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate partners with God...﴾

I need to translate this passage faithfully, following the given rules.

**Translation:**

The trial in wealth: in what does it consist? It is that a blight comes upon it and consumes it, and if it is found, there is a trial of another kind in it, and it is your test: whether you spend this wealth in the channels of good or do not give it to the needy. So sometimes the trial in wealth is by its loss, and sometimes in its existence and the watching of how you dispose of it. The Truth in this verse placed wealth before the self, because the trial of the self is by killing, or by wounding, or by sickness. As for killing, not everyone will be killed; rather, each one will be struck by a trial in his wealth.

﴿And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associated others with God much hurt﴾. So these are two camps of disbelief: the camp of the People of the Book and the camp of the polytheists. These two camps are the ones who opposed Islam, and the much hurt was represented in the attempt to harm the Messenger (ﷺ), and the hurt of mockery of the believers; the people of disbelief and polytheism say to the believers what they dislike. So prepare your resolve, O Muslims, to receive that from them and from the trials of the heavens with acceptance and contentment.

People err and think that trial in itself is evil. No. Trial is merely a test, and a test is subject to your succeeding in it or failing. When God says "﴿la-tubla-wunna﴾," meaning "I will test you" – God's is the highest likeness – just as the teacher says to the student: "I will examine you," "﴿fa-nabtaliyka﴾" means "we will test you in the examination." So does this mean that trial is evil or good? It is evil for the one who does not handle it well. The one who succeeds in the trial of wealth says: "It is all perishable," and God has lightened my responsibility, because I may have wealth and not manage it well in its lawful places, so the wealth would become a temptation upon me. God has taken wealth from me so that it does not enter me into the Fire, and therefore He said in Surah "al-Fajr":

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honours him and blesses him, he says: "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me."﴾ [al-Fajr: 15-16]

Here are two matters: the man is given wealth and says: "My Lord has honoured me," and this is better than the one of whom the Word of Truth said:

﴿He said: "I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess." Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in gathering?﴾ [al-Qasas: 78]

So the one who looked at wealth and thought that richness is honour, and looked at poverty and restriction and thought it is humiliation, this person does not perceive the reality, and the reality is stated by the Truth: "﴿Kalla﴾," meaning this assumption is not true; wealth is not proof of honour, nor is poverty proof of humiliation. But when does wealth become proof of honour? Wealth is a proof of honour if it comes to you and you are successful in rendering what is due from your wealth to the one in need of it; and if you do not render God's right, wealth is a disgrace and humiliation to you. You may be rich and not give what is due, so poverty in this case is better. Therefore God said to both: "﴿Kalla﴾," meaning: giving wealth is not proof of honour, and poverty is not proof of humiliation.

He, glorified is He, wished to demonstrate this and said:

﴿No! Rather you do not honour the orphan. And you do not urge one another to feed the needy. And you devour the heritage with greedy devouring.﴾ [al-Fajr: 17-19]

"﴿Nay, rather you do not honour the orphan﴾": and since you do not honour the orphan, how can wealth be a proof of honour? Here wealth is a burden, and how, if it is taken from you, O you who do not honour the orphan, would that be humiliation? He, glorified is He, has exempted you from being humiliated, so you do not bear the responsibility of wealth. Thus wealth is not proof of honour, nor is poverty proof of humiliation.

"﴿Nay, rather you do not honour the orphan, and you do not urge one another to feed the needy﴾": Even if you do not own and do not give, do you not urge the one who has to give? You are stingy even with a word; so "to urge upon the feeding of the needy" means to urge others. If you are stingy even with advice, how can you say wealth is honour and poverty is humiliation? "﴿Nay, rather you do not honour the orphan, and you do not urge one another to feed the needy, and you devour the heritage with greedy devouring﴾": that is, you eat the inheritance and in your eating you combine your share of the inheritance and the share of others, without any one of you investigating whether this wealth is lawful or unlawful. If the matter is like this, how can giving wealth be an honour, and how can poverty be a humiliation? Neither this nor that.

﴿And you will surely be tested in your wealth and your selves, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associated others with God much hurt﴾: The One who says this is God, so it must come to pass. You, O Lord, said to us that this will happen and your word will be fulfilled; so what have you given us to confront that? Listen to the remedy: "﴿But if you are patient and mindful of God, then that is among the matters requiring resolve﴾." You endure the trial in wealth, and you endure the trial in yourself, and you endure the harm of the opposing camp of those who were given the Scripture before you and of those who associated others with God; if you are patient, then that is among the matters requiring resolve. Resolve is the strength gathered for action. You intend to act, and then you resolve, meaning you gather strength; so His saying "﴿fa-inna dhalika min ʿazm al-umur﴾" means it is among the things that require firmness from you and strength in gathering and mustering all your capacities to act.

So the matter is a test which contains a trial in wealth, a trial in the self, and much harm from those who associated others with God and from those who were given the Scripture, and all of that requires patience. And "patience" – as we have said – is of two kinds: "patience upon" and "patience from", and patience varies with the variation of the preposition. Patience from the desires of the self, which make it appear attractive to a person to do this and that, so he is patient from them; and obedience may be burdensome for the servant, so he is patient upon it. Thus in obedience the believer is patient through hardships, and in disobedience he is patient from temptations.

And "﴿you will surely be tested in your wealth and your selves﴾" clarifies that there is no clearly defined opponent in the matter: the blight comes to wealth, or the affliction comes to the body and it falls ill, so there is no specific adversary for you that has been identified. But His saying "﴿and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associated others with God much hurt﴾" is the identification of an adversary for you. So when you see this adversary, he stirs up in you the hidden urges of vengeance. The Truth made clear: beware lest you let them make you react; postpone the act of anger, and do not let every matter provoke you. Rather, be calm, and beware of being provoked except when you are certain that you will prevail; and therefore He said: "﴿But if you are patient and mindful of God, then that is among the matters requiring resolve﴾."

"Ittaqu" (be mindful) is like "ittaqu Allah" (be mindful of God), meaning guard against the attributes of majesty, by placing between yourself and what angers God a shield. "On the authority of Usama ibn Zayd that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rode a donkey with a Fadakiyya cloth on it, and he had Usama ibn Zayd riding behind him, visiting Sa'd ibn 'Ubada among the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj before the battle of Badr, until he passed by a gathering in which was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and that was before Ibn Ubayy embraced Islam; and in the gathering were mixed people of Muslims and polytheists, idol-worshippers, and People of the Book, Jews and Muslims; and in the gathering was 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha. When the dust of the animal enveloped the gathering, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his garment and said: 'Do not raise dust over us.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) greeted them with peace, then stopped, dismounted, and invited them to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and recited the Qur'an to them. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: 'O man, there is nothing better than what you say, if it is true, so do not trouble us in our gatherings; return to your saddle, and whoever comes to you, relate it to him.' 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, may God be pleased with him, said: 'Yes, O Messenger of God, bring it to us in our gatherings, for we love that.' The Muslims, polytheists and Jews then quarrelled until they nearly came to blows, and the Prophet (ﷺ) kept calming them until they fell silent. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) mounted his animal and went until he entered upon Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: 'O Sa'd, have you not heard what Abu Hubab said?' – meaning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy – he said: such and such. Sa'd said: 'O Messenger of God, pardon him and forgive him, for by Him who revealed the Book to you, God has brought you the truth that was revealed to you, and the people of this valley had agreed to crown him and put a headband on him; but when God refused that, through the truth He gave you, it choked him, and that is why he did what you have seen.' So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) pardoned him."

Almighty Allah says: ﴿And remember when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it..."﴾

We already know that Allah took a covenant and pledge from all the Prophets that they would believe in the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), in His saying:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on this condition?" They said, "We affirm it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 81]

Here we come to another covenant and pledge that Allah took from the People of the Scripture who believed in their prophets. This covenant is: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it."﴾

So what is it that they make clear, and what is it that they conceal?

Do they conceal the Scripture? Yes, because they forget part of the Scripture, and as long as they forget part of the Scripture, this means they are preoccupied away from it:

﴿But they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 14]

As for what they did not forget of the methodology, what did they do with it? 

﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance, after We have made it clear to the people in the Scripture — those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 159]

They concealed the clear proofs that Allah sent down in the Scripture. Concealment is a deliberate act, whereas forgetting may be an excuse for them, since they forgot it; yet they bear sin from another direction, for if the methodology had been on their minds and they were living by it, they would not have forgotten it. What they did not forget, they concealed in part; and what they did not conceal, they twisted with their tongues and distorted.

Did they limit themselves to that? No. Rather they brought something of their own and said: it is from Allah:

﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 79]

Their saying ﴿This is from Allah﴾ is something that could only be said of a truthful message from Allah. The phrase ﴿to exchange it for a small price﴾ must have its meaning broadened somewhat, and it has a general sense. We know that a price is what one buys with, so how do you buy the price? If you make the price a commodity, and since the price is made a commodity, this would be the first violation of the logic of exchange, because the original purpose of prices is that things be bought with them. The root of the matter is that the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was present among them in the books, and then they denied it:

﴿And before this, they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved. But when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 89]

So His saying ﴿You shall make it clear﴾ means: you shall make clear the matter of the Messenger (ﷺ), as it exists with you without change or distortion. When they make clear the matter of the Messenger by his attributes and descriptions, they are making clear what came as truth in the Scripture that came to them from Allah. Thus we find that the meanings converge: if they make clear the Scripture that came from Allah, then the Scripture that came from Allah contains the description of Muhammad, and so we find that the meaning of making the Scripture clear and making the description of the Messenger of Allah clear through the Scripture are two converging matters.

﴿You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it, but they threw it behind their backs﴾. It is said: "nabadha al-shay'" meaning "I threw the thing away forcefully," and this is evidence of aversion, because one who dislikes something wants its existence to be brief. An example: suppose someone gave another a need, then found it a burning ember stinging him; what does he do? Without thinking, he throws it far away. Throwing away has directions: he throws it to his right, he throws it in front of him, he throws it to his left; but if he throws it behind him, this is evidence that he casts it off with a throw to which he never turns back. Look at the Qur'anic expression ﴿they threw it behind their backs﴾.

Throwing alone is evidence of aversion to the presence of the thing one hates; it is an intensification of hatred and detestation. If a person throws something in front of him, he may feel drawn to it when he sees it or remembers it; but if he throws it behind his back, this is exactly the evidence of casting off and aversion. This is why they say: "Do not make my need behind your back," meaning do not make a matter I want from you something behind your back. And the Truth says: ﴿they threw it behind their backs﴾, meaning they are a group, and "ẓuhūr" is the plural of "ẓahr," as if each one of them threw it behind his back. It is as if there was a consensus on this narrative, as if they agreed upon misguidance and exchanged it for a small price; wretched is what they buy. The buyer here is the price, and the price is bought with; let us examine the Qur'anic expression carefully: one person buys this matter for a meal, another buys this narrative for a robe or garment, and there are those who buy it for a need and it ends; they are saying: we want money and we buy with it what we love. This is the meaning of ﴿and they bought with it a price﴾.

The Truth comments on what they buy, saying: ﴿wretched is what they buy﴾. Why? Because you may think that with wealth — which is the price — you can buy everything with it, but money does not benefit a person as direct need does; as we said earlier: suppose a person is in a desert place and has a mountain of gold but no cup of water. It is true that wealth brings things, but there may be some trivial thing that suffices where wealth and gold do not suffice, so a cup of water, for example, is worth the whole world, and no wealth equals it. ﴿Wretched is what they buy﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 188:

Then, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought, and love to be praised for what they did not do...﴾

Al-husban (supposing, or reckoning) with regard to a matter is that the listener thinks of it other than as it really is. Matters that the listener supposes first proceed in the light of the apparent thing, without reflecting on what lies behind the façades of things. Those who rejoice in what they have brought are of two kinds. One kind rejoices in what it has brought in opposition to the call of truth, like the hypocrites who rejoiced that they had deceived the believers and feigned faith, so the believers treated them with the rights of faith-brotherhood. This happened before Allah revealed these hypocrites to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to the believers afterwards.

Another kind rejoices in what it has brought and what it has come with, in support of the call of truth. So the first rejoicing, which is the rejoicing of the hypocrites, is blameworthy, and the second rejoicing is lawful. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Say: In the grace of Allah and in His mercy, so in that let them rejoice﴾ [Yunus: 58]

So Allah did not forbid rejoicing in general, but rather that they should rejoice in the grace of Allah. He, glory be to Him, has forbidden one kind of rejoicing in the matter of Qarun:

﴿When his people said to him: Do not exult; indeed Allah does not love the exultant﴾ [al-Qasas: 76]

Thus we find verses that forbid rejoicing and verses that affirm that rejoicing for the believers and command it. So rejoicing in itself is not abhorrent, but what is abhorrent is some of the motives for that rejoicing. Its lawful motives for the believer are that he rejoices in the victory of Allah and in the exaltation of the word of truth, and these are lawful motives. Its forbidden motives are that he rejoices at standing in the face of one of the principles of Allah in order to refute that principle, and this is what the disbeliever rejoices in. But true rejoicing is the rejoicing that is not followed by regret, for the rejoicing of the believer is connected until the Hour arises, and connected after the Hour arises. But the rejoicing of the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the People of the Book who depict Allah other than as He truly is, is temporary and abhorrent. So that does not count as rejoicing, because regret after rejoicing yields an evil outcome, since the regretful one is constantly grieved over his deed and is in distress and sorrow.

So the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wants to give the believer immunity. You, O believers, face camps that are hostile to you. These camps will rejoice in what they have brought against you, so that must not weaken your resolve, and do not suppose that they, if they do that, are beyond punishment; and since their rejoicing will lead them to punishment, it is foolish rejoicing.

And what did those about whom the saying was revealed, ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾, do? It may be that the intended ones are the People of the Book who concealed the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because the preceding verse says: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, you shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it, but they threw it behind their backs﴾. What did these people do then? They concealed the attributes of the Messenger of Allah and his description present in their books, and rejoiced in what they had concealed. After that they loved to be praised for what they had done by those who were on their path of disbelief and misguidance.

A person may commit a sin but then regret it after doing it; but when he persists and rejoices in what he has done, that is another sin. Thus the act of doing becomes a sin, and rejoicing in it another sin, because if he had regretted what he did, the regret would have been evidence of repentance. As for doing the deed, then afterwards rejoicing in it, and then, after that, the worse: loving to be praised for what he did not do, that is among the complete foolishness. It is a crime and a sin composed of a sinful act, then rejoicing in it, then loving to be praised for a thing he did not do.

Should he be praised for what he did or for what he did not do? For what he did not do, because he has put on his affair something untrue. And if someone says: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah, the saying is plausible, because those people stayed behind from war with the Messenger of Allah and rejoiced that the hardships of travel and the hardships of jihad had not touched them, and afterwards they offered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) false excuses. Had they regretted, it would have been better for them, and the Muslims did not become clear about their lying, so they praised them for that excuse. They committed the sin and rejoiced that they had committed it, and escaped the burdens of war, and afterwards they also rejoiced that they loved to be praised for what they had not done, because their excuse was hypocrisy. Whether it was this or that, the verse is general: for those who rejoice in what they have brought of opposition to the truth, and that is an act; and rejoicing in it is another sin; and the desire to be praised for it is a third thing. So the sin is compound: they conceal the matter and display its opposite, so that we praise and thank them, and the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, gives through this a faith-based constitution for all of life.

﴿And love to be praised for what they did not do﴾. Is the reproach against them that they love to be praised, or is the reproach and the thing they are held to account for that they love to be praised for what they did not do? The reproach against them is that they love to be praised for what they did not do, because if a person loves to be praised for what he did, there is no objection. The Qur'an, when it addresses a human soul which Allah created with faculties, knows the requirements of those faculties. Some faculties may need something, and Allah does not overlook that thing. Man is naturally disposed to love praise from others, because love of praise establishes for him a second existence, and your second existence is to express yourself through your deed, which becomes the source of praise for you; people do not praise your existence, but they praise your action.

As long as a person loves praise, that will tempt him to do what earns him praise, and as long as he is tempted by what earns him praise, he will work with greater excellence. When he works, those around him benefit from his work, and Allah wishes the spread of benefit, so He, glory be to Him, does not prohibit love of praise in order to increase the active energy of things; for if He forbade that praise, only those whose faculties were sound would work, and society would lose the energies of those whose faculties were weak. So the one with weak faculties wants to be praised, and there is no objection to praising him to increase his work, and he is praised a second time, and people benefit. And the one who awaits praise from people is lowered in rank and station below one who awaits appraisal from Allah, and he has brought harm upon himself in that.

But we must praise him so that he works with the instinct of love of praise that is in him, and so we increase the number of energies of those who work.

Accordingly, we find that when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addressed this matter, which is the matter of commending the righteous and condemning the corrupt wrongdoer, in the story of "Dhu al-Qarnayn," He, exalted, says:

﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a remembrance of him. Indeed, We established him in the earth and gave him of every thing a means﴾ [al-Kahf: 83-84]

So that you know that the one who is empowered is not empowered by his own essence, but is empowered by the One who empowered him. If he had a faith-based way of thinking, the causes would not have tempted him to rebel, because faith teaches him that causes are not self-existent. And in order to establish that causes are not self-existent, He takes away dominion from whom He wills and grants dominion to whom He wills. We say to him: were causes self-existent, then hold fast to them; but causes are a gift from Allah: ﴿and We gave him of every thing a means﴾. When Allah gives him the means, then means are of kinds: a direct means of the act, and a means preceding the direct means. If you wear a beautiful garment, behind that is that you have obtained the cloth which the weaver wove, and the weaver was able to perfect his work after the spinner spun the cotton, and the cotton was produced because a farmer sowed the seeds and tended the land by ploughing and irrigation. So if you look at the direct, successive means, look to the end of the causes, and you will arrive at a thing that has no cause except the highest Causer, who is Allah, may His power be exalted.

And trace any thing in existence and you will find that you are finally before a cause created by Allah. An example of that is the electric light you enjoy. You will find that the factory made the glass for the electric bulbs, and a kind of factory makes the wires within the bulb, and you will end at a thing that exists in which there is no human being, and you arrive at the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted.

For example, you are sitting on a chair. You may say: the carpenter made it, and the carpenter got the wood from the seller, and the seller got the wood from the forest; so where did the wood come to the forest from? You say: I do not know. But if you have a faith-based sense, you say: Allah brought it into being. When the causes and their chain end, we find Allah the Creator: ﴿Indeed, We established him in the earth and gave him of every thing a means. So he followed a means﴾. When Allah gave him the means, he came only with the intermediaries. So the origin of all of it is from Allah.

The Truth continues: ﴿until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring﴾. This is in the eye of the observer only. For when you board the sea and see the sun at sunset dip into the sea, and when you go to the place where the sun dipped, you find the sun present, because it never sets; rather ﴿it sets in a murky spring﴾, meaning that he found the sun in his sight at its setting from him as if it set in a place with a spring of hot water and black mud.

The Truth continues: ﴿And he found beside it a people. We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them, or you take towards them a goodly course﴾.

People understand this as an option, meaning either you punish them or you do good to those whom you were punishing. But careful reflection makes clear to us that the Truth gave Dhu al-Qarnayn a delegation of authority by His saying: ﴿either you punish them, or you take towards them a goodly course﴾. Dhu al-Qarnayn understood the delegation from Allah and did not take the delegation and invent, but said: ﴿As for he who does wrong, we shall punish him﴾. This is not the punishment he deserves; no, we will punish him in our world so that evil does not spread in it. And beyond that Allah will punish him with another punishment: ﴿As for he who does wrong, we shall punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a dreadful punishment﴾. First, he did not describe his punishment as dreadful; rather he described the punishment of Allah, saying: ﴿He will punish him with a dreadful punishment﴾, because the punishment of humans by humans is according to human measure, but the punishment of Allah is commensurate with the power of Allah. Do we have the strength for this punishment, and Allah forbid? We have no strength for it. And what of the stance of Dhu al-Qarnayn toward the one who believed? It is a different stance.

The Truth says: ﴿And as for he who believes and does righteousness, he shall have a goodly reward, and we shall speak to him of Our command with ease﴾. He rewards him with the goodly reward, gives him rewards and honours him. When one who loves praise asks: why was this one honoured? and sees the causes of the honouring, he says to himself: I will do likewise so that I too may be honoured. That is why you find the youth eager to play football; why? Because they see that whoever scores a goal in football is honoured, so he says: I want to score a goal.

Moreover, our noble religion calls us to thank those who have done good or conferred a favour, as an incitement to aspirations and encouragement to expend energies, and it is related: "Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah." So love of praise is part of human nature, and in order to motivate people to work, you must provide them with work that absorbs their diverse energies. If the excellence of work is confined to those who do not love praise, we will reduce the hands that act. That is why you find work where there is an encouraging reward, which is taken by the one who deserves it, and is matched by blame and punishment for the one who neglects his work. A head of an enterprise does not give a reward to those who worked according to their whims, but must give it to the one who performed his work with excellence. When people know that he does not reward with good nor honour with words except one who has done a truly real deed, then everyone does a truly real deed; but when you find people

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 189:

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things Competent.﴾

He, glorified is He, judges concerning what He owns, and no one can step outside of His dominion. Since the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, when He says: ﴿So do not think them to be safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment﴾, this threat will certainly be fulfilled, because no one escapes from it. For this reason, the people of unveiling (kashf), the people of insight (lamahiyyah), and the people of overflowing grace (fayd) say: Make your obedience to the One whom you cannot do without; make your gratitude to the One whose blessings never cease to reach you; and make your submission to the One from whose dominion and authority you can never get out.

So ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ indicates that when Allah makes a threat, He, glorified is He, is able to carry out what He has threatened, and no one will ever escape from Him. This reinforces the meaning. So when the enemies of the religion rejoice in a surge of delusion that they have won, the believer looks to the end and to what it will be. For this reason you find that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! * His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. * He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, * And his wife, the carrier of firewood, * Around her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber.﴾ [al-Masad: 1–5].

This surah was revealed concerning the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And this surah was a proof among the proofs of the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Allah, because Abu Lahab was a disbeliever, and there were many other disbelievers besides him. Was not Umar ibn al-Khattab among them? Was not Khalid ibn al-Walid among them? Was not Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl among them? Was not Safwan among them? All of these were disbelievers and then believed.
