Who was it that could tell Muhammad (ﷺ), after he said: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! * His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. * He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, * And his wife, the carrier of firewood, * Around her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber﴾, who could tell him that this would be a Qur'an recited and memorized by many believers? And after all that, who could tell him that Abu Lahab would come and say: "I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and perhaps add: "If Muhammad said that I will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, here I am, I have believed," who could tell him that he would not do so, just as Ibn al-Khattab did, and as Amr ibn al-As did? The One who informed Muhammad knows that Abu Lahab will never choose faith, so the Qur'an records it against him, and then Abu Lahab dies a disbeliever.

As if Allah wanted to confirm this, He clarifies for you: beware lest you think that this threat will fail, because I am "One, Eternal Refuge," and no one opposes Me in this judgment. Therefore He says in Surat al-Ikhlas:

﴿Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One. * Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1–2].

Since "He is Allah, One," what He said first will not be annulled by any other god, and His word will remain forever.

So the words of the Truth, glorified is He, after His saying ﴿So do not think them to be safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment﴾, namely ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, clarify for us that He has joined this threat to that new articles of faith: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. He brought in the two sides, because the sky shades and the earth bears, so each of us is confined between two things owned by Allah; and since each of us is confined between two things owned by Allah, where will you go? ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. There may be a king who has no power to rule, so He, glorified is He, clarifies: No, to Allah belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the power.

﴿And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ Then He moves on to another article of faith, to establish it in souls after the premises that have proven the truthfulness of what Allah said in the reality of life:

Subhanahu wa ta'ala wants to build the faith-based outlook on roots fixed in the human soul, because a person who is confronted with this universe, with a sky of this form, without pillars, with stars beneath it and a settled earth, will he not, by God, reflect on who made this? By God, if a man woke from his sleep and found that a pavilion had been erected in the square during the night, he would stop and ask: what is the story? So what of someone who opened his eyes and found this orderly universe that provides him with the means of life?

For this reason the matter comes in another surah to explain this question in a way that clarifies the issue of faith through human reflection. We do not wait only for the preacher who brings us the message and prophethood to indicate the path intended by the One who created us. Rather, it is incumbent upon us to become aware, by innate nature (fitra), of who created us. As we said before: if a person's plane went down in a desert, and he found there no water, no trees and no people, and he was exhausted and overcome by sleep, then he woke and found a table upon which were the finest foods, by God, before he stretched out his hand to benefit from it, would his thoughts not wander to who prepared this? His astonishment at the event makes him think about who brought it before he tastes the food, even though he is hungry. So likewise are people who opened their eyes and found this wondrous universe. After that, none of them claimed that he created it. Had someone claimed to have created it, the matter would be easy, but no one claimed to have made it. This universe that we all see, with its wonderful regularity and fixed laws: has anyone said, "I made it"? No. Then whoever says, "I made it," his claim goes unchallenged, until another comes and says, "I am the one who made it." This has never happened, despite the existence of atheists and those who slander God. Therefore the words of the Exalted came:

﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth?﴾ [an-Naml: 60].

It is as if the Truth were saying: if I am not the one who created, then who created? No one dared to attribute the universe to himself, because the disbelievers and atheists cannot create even a trivial thing out of nothing. An example of this is the drinking glass (the cup of water), which God did not create in the form it has so that they might make it, in order to understand that everything was accomplished by His creation, glory be to Him. This glass of water is a trivial thing that adorns life. Before the glass was manufactured, we drank, and there was no tree that bears and fruits glasses; rather, a human made it, a man who wanted to embellish life. So if this small thing has a maker who traversed the realms of various sciences and of matter, then looked at the earth until he found the material which, when melted, gives this transparency and sheen, and experimented with the elements of the earth until he found nothing but sand.

He discovered this material and mixed it with other materials to melt and dissolve it, and making the glass required factories and scientists. All of this for the small cup which you might dispense with. Look at what it needs to be made! It needed energies that roamed through all the materials of the earth, industrial capabilities, and people who devise chemical formulas. So what of the original things, and how much do they need?

Every craft requires in proportion to its worth. No one has said, "I made them," so the Truth says: who made all this? Whenever He poses a question, He does not want to make the matter one of His own announcement, though He is capable of saying, "I am the One who created the heavens and the earth." So what does the one questioned do? He stumbles in his answer, and in the end he finds nothing but God.

It is as if the questioner would not pose this question unless he were certain that the answer would only be in accordance with what he wants:

﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delightful beauty﴾.

Here He brings in the direct need: ﴿We caused to grow thereby gardens of delightful beauty﴾, meaning they delight the eye with their greenery, freshness, pleasantness, shade, flowers and fruits. He did not limit the matter by saying "that you may eat from them," because the one who eats is the one who owns, but the beauty of the scene is not withheld by anyone from whoever sees it and takes pleasure in what he sees. When any of us sees a beautiful garden that pleases him with its appearance, it is true that you do not stretch out your hand to eat from it because it is not yours, but does anyone prevent you from enjoying it with your sight, or from delighting your nose with its beautiful fragrance? No.

Thus the Truth brought the common blessing for the one who owns and the one who does not own, saying "delightful beauty." We know that when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, bestows favours upon things, He makes clear to you: beware of understanding that the purpose of this matter is only that you eat them to fill your belly, because there are beautiful things from which we benefit not by eating. There are kinds of trees that have no fruit but must have a use; their beautiful leaves may give shade, and the fragrance they spread perfumes the air, and some have wood we need. Besides this, we find trees with beautiful fruits from which we benefit.

For this reason the Truth says:

﴿And it is He who sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby the growth of all things. From it We bring forth green [foliage], from which We bring forth grains piled up; and from the palm trees, from their spathes, clusters hanging low; and gardens of grapes, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Look at their fruit when they bear fruit and [at] its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-An'am: 99].

And He, glory be to Him, asks man: ﴿Is it that you could not make its trees grow? Is there a god with God? Nay, but they are a people who deviate (ya'dilun)﴾ [an-Naml: 60, cf. the verse of an-Naml 27:60 in the Arabic text].

With superficiality, one of the orientalists began to repeat: does God rebuke creation and blame them for deviating (ya'dilun)? That is because he did not understand the correct meaning, for "al-'adl" here means turning away from the truth or inclining away from it. He says:

﴿Or who made the earth a stable place and placed within it rivers and made for it firm mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a god with God? Nay, but most of them do not know﴾ [an-Naml: 61].

It is He, glory be to Him, who created the earth and placed within it the rivers, and placed in it the firm mountains. The Truth clarifies the reason for the existence of the firm mountains in another place in the Holy Qur'an:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed firmly on the earth mountains from above it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat: 9–10].

Why, O God, did You bless? God blessed the mountains and determined their sustenance therein, for qut (sustenance) is that by which life is preserved. We know that sustenance is taken from crops, and crops grow always in fertile land, and the fertility of the land is in the valleys, and the valley is the place that lies between two mountains. And why is the valley fertile between two mountains? Because when rain falls from the sky, it falls upon the mountains, and mountains, as you know, are exposed to the agents of erosion: heat comes after cold, heat makes the earth expand, and cold contracts the material, and between contraction and expansion surface cracks occur in the mountains. When the rain falls, it washes these cracks away, and they descend from the mountaintop by the force of momentum, becoming fine particles, which we call ghirin (silt) or tamy (alluvial mud), like that which used to come to us from Abyssinia (al-Habasha), which produced the fertility of the Nile Valley (Wadi al-Nil).

So the mountains are the storehouses of sustenance. It is one of God's favours that He made the mountains hard. Had they been brittle from the outset, a single rainfall would have been enough to remove them all, and He would have made the earth one flat surface, and mankind would not have benefited from half a metre of fertility. After that comes barrenness. We know that the Truth made, alongside human multiplication, a multiplication of the causes of sustenance, so how would the Truth, glory be to Him, increase sustenance?

We see that mountains have a summit and have a base, and between each mountain and another is a valley. We know that the narrowness of the valley is at its bottom and its breadth is at its top, while the mountain is the opposite of the valley: the narrowness of the mountain is at the summit and its breadth at the base, that is, the summit of the mountain is less broad than its base. When the ghirin descends by means of the rain from the mountain, it descends into the valley, raising the level of the valley's floor, and the area of the valley widens. Whenever rain falls on the mountains, the area of the valleys between the mountains expands, because the rain carries with it parts of the mountains, which is what is called ghirin. When the Truth, glory be to Him, wills the announcement of the end, all the mountains will be crumbled, and He will say to the Hour: "Arise now."

And He says:

﴿And He made for it firm mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier. Is there a god with God? Nay, but most of them do not know﴾.

In another place the Truth says:

﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side; between them is a barrier they do not transgress﴾ [ar-Rahman: 19–20].

Water has a way of seeping through, so God channelled it as springs in the earth. A person digs in one place in the earth and finds the water sweet, and in another place a person strikes the ground and digs and finds the water salty. Why then did the salt water not seep into the sweet water, when both are beneath the earth? It must be that salt water has channels different from the channels of sweet water, and neither overwhelms the other.

Why? Because we find that sweet water comes from above. We always find the sources of rivers high, and they pour into the sea. The Truth did not make the level of the salt water higher than the level of the sweet water, lest the salt water overwhelm the sweet water, because He, glory be to Him, wants people to be relieved of thirst with water, and wants crops to grow, and wants the surplus of sweet water to flow toward the storehouse of water, whether in the belly of the earth or in the seas. After that comes the process of evaporation, so the water rises as vapour to become clouds, and then rains down again as sweet water. The quantity of water that God created from the beginning is itself, neither increasing nor decreasing.

If a person has drunk tons of water throughout his life, do those tons remain in the human body, or have they left in his excretions? A person stores only the water present in him now. The human body is about ninety percent water in its constituents, and after a person dies, the water evaporates from him and the remaining elements descend to the earth. So the quantity of water is one, but it is subject to a cycle that God willed.

After that the Truth says:

﴿Or who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil and makes you successors upon the earth? Is there a god with God? Little do you remember﴾ [an-Naml: 62].

The meaning of al-mudtarr (the distressed one) is the person who has exhausted the causes of his human capacity and has not reached what would preserve his life. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove from him his harm, he passes on as if he had never called Us for a harm that touched him. Thus is made attractive to the wasteful what they used to do﴾ [Yunus: 12].

And likewise the Truth says in another place in the Holy Qur'an:

﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful﴾ [al-Isra': 67].

That is because when a person is struck by a grave calamity, he does not deceive himself. Even the disbeliever in God, when he finds that all the material means before him do not benefit him, turns to Him and acknowledges that there is one God, the Creator. He says: "O Lord."

So then, the Truth, glory be to Him

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 191:

So who are the people of understanding (*ulu al-albab*)?

The answer of the Truth is: ﴿Those who remember Allah, standing, sitting, and on their sides...﴾.

They say:

﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain.﴾ For You are the Truth, and You created the heavens and the earth with truth, and You set down for them their laws (*nawamis*) and their regulations with truth. So we must receive the blessing You created for us with truth. If some people receive it without truth, it becomes a burden upon them. It is said that a truthful believer among the Children of Israel, before the mission of Jesus, peace be upon him, was such that if he worshipped Allah sincerely for thirty years, a cloud would shade him wherever he went. So when they saw one of these people walking with a cloud shading him, they knew that he had worshipped Allah sincerely for thirty years.

One of them worshipped Allah for thirty years and did not see the cloud shading him. He complained of this to his mother, and she said to him: "Perhaps something has slipped from you." He said to her: "O mother, I do not remember." She said to him: "Perhaps you once looked at the sky and did not reflect." He said to her: "Perhaps that happened." She said: "Then it is from that." This story reminds us of the need to reflect upon Allah at all times.

It is related from our master, the Imam 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him and ennoble his face, that he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke up at night, he would use the siwak, then look up at the sky."

So looking at the sky is looking at what is above. Looking at the earth is also reflection on the wisdom of the Creator, but looking at the sky makes a person aware of the exaltation of the Creator. Therefore, an Arab who lay on his back sleeping, then woke and became aware of the wondrous blue color of the sky with the stars sparkling in it, said: "I testify that You have a Lord and a Creator. O Allah, forgive me." That man knew when to call upon Allah and how to call upon Him, so Allah forgave him.

The books of biography (*sirah*) relate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he came one night and lay down, and it was the night of 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her. 'Aisha said to him: "He lay down beside me until his skin touched my skin, then he said: 'O 'Aisha, will you permit me tonight to worship my Lord?'"

The Messenger of Allah asked her permission regarding her right, because that night was her night. 'Aisha added: "O Messenger of Allah, I love your nearness and I love your company, and I have given you permission."

She took the beautiful precaution, for she loves the Messenger and says: "And I love your nearness," and this statement has a beautiful meaning. It happened that some of the extremists in the religion of Allah said: "The Messenger of Allah was elderly, with a great difference in age between him and 'Aisha, and her saying that was only out of indifference toward him."

But 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, responded to that before it was said. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love your nearness and I love your company, and I have given you permission." This is a lesson that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives us so that we learn how to treat our families, even if the matter that occupies us away from them is worship. He does not want the believer to be occupied away from caring for his family after performing what is obligatory upon him, even if it is worship, except after seeking the permission of the family.

Why? Because Allah requires the wife, in non-obligatory worship, not to perform voluntary (*tatawwu'*) worship until she seeks her husband's permission. So if the wife prays voluntarily or fasts voluntarily, she must seek her husband's permission. If he grants it, well and good, and if he does not grant it, she has no right to perform this non-obligatory worship.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of you... the best of you is the best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family."

Because when a husband approaches his wife, he wants to keep her from worldly longings. Therefore, when the wife wants to take her time, especially if she has co-wives, this time is her right. If the husband wants it for non-obligatory worship, he must ask her permission. The psychological state of a woman without co-wives may be more capable of accepting her husband's request to devote himself to worship. Therefore, you see among the jurists (*ahl al-fatwa*) the successful clarification of such a matter.

A woman went to complain about her husband to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. The substance of her complaint was that her husband did not approach her. A noble companion was with 'Umar, and 'Umar said to him: "Give her a ruling (*aftiha*)." The companion said to the husband: "Sir, let us suppose you married four wives; then your wife would have a night after every three nights." And since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked 'Aisha's permission for worship of his Lord, this means a lesson for husbands to treat their families with such kindness that it gives the wife no cause for longing.

But we find people who do not seek their families' permission, neither for worship nor even for evenings of sin. This is what corrupts homes and families. What corrupts homes is that the husband is preoccupied away from his wife and goes to his friends at the café or some other place, and does not care for the members of his family.

Why does he not go home to keep his family company, to fulfill their desires, to sit with his wife, his family, and his children, so that the wife is reassured that her husband is with her and not somewhere else, and so that affairs settle? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and she gave him permission. 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said:

"He got up to a waterskin (*qirbah*), performed ablution, then stood and wept; then he recited and wept; then he praised Allah and glorified Him and wept, until the ground was wet. Then Bilal came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the dawn prayer.' He saw him weeping and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you weep when Allah has forgiven you what is past and what is to come of your sins?' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Shall I not be a grateful servant? O Bilal, there was revealed to me tonight:

{Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding. Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You; protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, whoever You admit to the Fire, You have truly disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers. Our Lord, we heard a caller calling to faith, 'Believe in your Lord,' so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and make us die with the righteous. Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection; indeed You do not fail in the promise." So their Lord responded to them: "I do not let the work of any worker among you be lost, whether male or female; you are of one another. Those who emigrated, were expelled from their homes, were harmed in My way, fought, and were killed, I will surely remove their misdeeds from them and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah; and with Allah is the best reward." Do not let the movement of those who disbelieve through the lands deceive you. It is a little enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place. But those who fear their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, as a welcome from Allah; and what is with Allah is best for the righteous. And among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submitting to Allah, not selling the signs of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord; indeed Allah is swift in reckoning. O you who believe, be patient, endure, stay stationed, and fear Allah that you may succeed.}" [Al 'Imran: 190-200].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) added: "Woe to the one who recites it and does not reflect upon it, and woe to the one who chews it between his jaws and does not contemplate it."

This is what came from our master, the Messenger of Allah, at the end of Surat Al 'Imran, those final verses that begin with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day﴾.

In those verses are the method, the argument, and the companionship of the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, and His remembrance in every state: standing, sitting, and on the side. The Truth says: ﴿Those who remember Allah, standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You; protect us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾

Here we see that what is required of people of understanding is that they remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides. Some scholars, interpreting the Truth's saying ﴿Those who remember Allah, standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾, said that what is meant is the prayer: whoever cannot pray standing prays sitting, and whoever cannot pray sitting prays lying on his side.

We say to these scholars: you have restricted this meaning, while the context calls for generality. Why? Because the Qur'an does not contradict itself, but explains one part by another. And the Truth says regarding the prayer of fear:

﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. When they have prostrated, let them be behind you; and let another group who have not prayed come and pray with you, taking their precaution and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings so they could attack you in one assault. But there is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill, but take your precaution. Indeed Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ [An-Nisa': 102].

And so that the believer does not think that the five obligatory prayers are the only occasions on which Allah is remembered, He, Glorified is He, said:

﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides. And when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times.﴾ [An-Nisa': 103].

That is, the prayer took place first, and the prayer took place second, as if the remembrance of Allah is a continuous and obligatory matter in prayer and outside it, and after it the believers reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth and acknowledge that He, Glorified is He, did not create this in vain. And what is required is that they say:

﴿Glory be to You; protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191].

Why? Because all this remembrance does not fulfill the right of our Lord upon us. Therefore they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire...﴾.

It is greatness indeed. They do not mention the punishment of those who enter the Fire, but they mention the disgrace (khizy) of Allah toward whoever enters the Fire. It is as if disgrace is a rank worse than the torment of the Fire. So who has given us all this favour? It is He, glory be to Him, who has given us the success of remembering Him, and the success of reflecting on the creation of the heavens and the earth. Is it right, then, that we should meet this with ingratitude for the blessing? And what happens to those who enter the Fire?

It is disgrace, and we seek refuge in Allah from it. ﴿And the wrongdoers will have no helpers﴾, meaning: there will be no helpers for them to ward off the torment of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 193:

Then the Truth says: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we believed﴾.

So the human being, with his heart and his mind, before a messenger comes to him, must become alert to the signs in the universe, and he must anticipate that behind the universe there is a power. But this power is vague in his mind. What is it? He sees the wondrous universe and says to himself: it is impossible that this universe should be without a creator. Behind it is a power that has wisdom and has ability. This is the utmost the intellect can reach. But can the intellect comprehend that the power's name is Allah? Can the intellect comprehend what the power requires of him?

No. Therefore there must be a messenger who conveys from that power. That is why we said: this is the slip into which the philosophers fell, because the philosophers are the ones who investigated beyond matter. We know that knowledge divides into two parts: a material part founded on experiment, and a metaphysical part (ma ba'd al-tabi'ah) that investigates what is beyond matter. This knowledge is the labyrinth of the philosophers, the misguidance in which no school ever met another school, nor a student in one school met another student in another school.

Why did they not meet? Because they investigate beyond matter. What is beyond matter is unseen (ghayb). The unseen does not enter the laboratory. But matter enters the laboratory. And the laboratory, when it gives the results of analyses, does not flatter these results. Whoever enters scientific experiment in the laboratory with integrity, the laboratory gives him. And whoever enters without integrity, the laboratories give him nothing.

That is why we always say: in the material sciences we find no difference between a Russian communist science and an American capitalist science. There is no capitalist chemistry or communist chemistry, and there is no Russian electricity and another American electricity. It is one chemistry and one electricity, because it is the child of the laboratory and the daughter of material experiment.

And among the wonders that the arrogant creatures among them do not notice: we find that material science, the child of experiment, the laboratory, and the deaf matter that does not flatter, each camp tries to steal it from the other. We find spies travelling from one camp to another to steal the designs of aircraft and missiles, and some of them spy on others so that they may know the material science.

But what of the science of desires and theories? We find that each side erects a wall so that the science of desires does not penetrate the society.

They erect barriers in matters of desire, but in material science they turn into thieves. So why do they not take desires along with material science? Each camp is eager for enmity with the doctrines of others in government, society and economics. But in material science they steal from one another, because theoretical doctrines follow desires, whereas material science, as we have said, follows the laboratory truth that does not flatter.

So when a person thinks with his intellect, he must say: behind the creation of the universe is an extraordinary power. The Arab knew it by his nature and said: the dung indicates the camel, and the footprint indicates the walking; does not all of that indicate the Subtle, the All-Aware?!

It is a natural proof, which guides you to the existence of the power, but what is the name of this power? We do not know.

So the ear longs for someone who will tell it the name of this power. When someone comes and says: I am sent from the side of this power, and its name is Allah, people should have rushed to him, because he will solve for them the riddle that preoccupies them. Therefore the believers say: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we believed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 193].

It is as if the mind of each one of them was preoccupied with the necessity of recognising the Creator. And after that:

﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit into the Fire, You have truly disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 192].

So the first thing they reflected upon is the averting of harm, because the best of people always accuse themselves of shortcoming. Therefore they said: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds﴾.

When we look at the indications of the Qur'an, we find that "dhanb" (sin) is one thing and "sayyi'ah" (misdeed) is another. Sin needs forgiveness, and misdeed needs expiation (takfir). For example, the "expiation of the oath" (kaffarat al-yamin) is obligatory if the believer swears an oath and breaks it, and this expiation is the counterpart of breaking the oath. As for the matters that concern disobedience between the servant and his Lord, these are sins; and the misdeed is the matter that contradicts the method of God with the servants of God. When you commit disobedience in a matter between you and God, you have not harmed God, for who are you, O human, in the station of God? But by disobedience you sin, and after sin comes punishment. As for contravening the method of God with the servants of God, it is a misdeed, because by it you have done wrong.

Therefore the believers said: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds﴾.

And who guided them to know that there is a difference between sin and misdeed, that sin needs forgiveness and misdeed needs expiation? It is the Messenger (ﷺ), the bearer of the message from God. He is the one who taught us the difference between sin and misdeed. He was sitting among his companions when drowsiness overcame him, then he woke and laughed.

It is narrated on the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting, we saw him laugh until his front teeth showed. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Two men from my nation knelt before the Lord of Might. One of them said: O Lord, take for me my right from my brother. Allah said: Give your brother his right. He said: O Lord, nothing of my good deeds remains. He said: O Lord, let some of his burdens be borne for me. The eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) overflowed with weeping, then he said: That is indeed a great day, a day on which people need to have their burdens borne for them. Then Allah said to the claimant: Raise your gaze and look at the gardens. He raised his head and said: O Lord, I see cities of silver and palaces of gold, crowned with pearls. For which prophet is this? For which truthful one is this? For which martyr is this? He said: This is for whoever pays the price. He said: O Lord, and who possesses its price? He said: You. He said: With what? He said: With your pardoning your brother. He said: O Lord, I have pardoned him. He said: Take your brother by the hand and enter him into Paradise. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Fear Allah and set right your relations with one another, for Allah sets right between the believers on the Day of Resurrection."

This is the meaning of expiation, namely that we bear (the burden). Therefore we say in supplication as we have been taught: "O Allah, whatever of it is Your right, forgive me; and whatever is the right of Your servants, bear it on my behalf." That is, the servant asks that the Truth satisfy His servants on his behalf, and what is with Him never runs out.

And the believing servants say: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous﴾, that is: conclude for us, O Glorified One, with this conclusion among the righteous.

After that comes His saying, may He be exalted, relating their words: ﴿Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers...﴾

That is, "Our Lord, give us what You promised us through the tongue of Your messengers."

ولتسمع قول الحق استجابة لهم :

﴿So their Lord responded to them: "Indeed, I will not allow the work of any worker among you, male or female, to be lost; you are of one another. So those who emigrated, were expelled from their homes, were harmed in My cause, fought, and were killed, I will surely remove their misdeeds from them and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the best reward."﴾

ولْنر اللفتة الجميلة في الاستجابة : " فاستجاب لهم ربهم أنّي لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم من ذكر أو أنثى بعضكم من بعض " لقد كانوا يذكرون الله قياماً وقعوداً وعلى جنوبهم، ويتفكرون في خلق السماوات والأرض. ويخشون الدخول إلى النار. ودعوا الله بغفران الذنوب وتكفير السيئات. ودعوا الله أن يأتيهم ويعطيهم ما وعدهم به على ألسنة الرسل.

Let us observe the graceful point in the response: "So their Lord responded to them: 'Indeed, I will not allow the work of any worker among you, male or female, to be lost; you are of one another.'" They used to remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and they reflected on the creation of the heavens and the earth. They feared entering the Fire. They called upon Allah for the forgiveness of sins and the expiation of misdeeds. They called upon Allah to grant them what He had promised them through the tongues of the messengers.

لم يقل الحق سبحانه : استجبت لكم، لكنه جعل الاستجابة هي قبول العمل فقال :﴿أَنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى﴾ فليست الحكاية كلاما يقال، إنما يريد الله أن تدخل هذه المسائل في حيز التطبيق والنزوع العملي ؛ فالمسألة ليست بالتمني فقط، فقد وضع سبحانه الشرط الواضح وهو العمل، فمن يريد استجابة الحق فلابد له من العمل. إن التفكر في بديع صنع الله لا يغني عن العمل ؛ لأن الحق سبحانه يريد التفكر فيه وأنت تعمل في أسبابه. فأسباب الحق لا تشغلك عنه ﴿فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى بَعْضُكُم مِّن بَعْضٍ فَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ وَأُخْرِجُواْ مِن دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُواْ فِي سَبِيلِي وَقَاتَلُواْ وَقُتِلُواْ لأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأَنْهَارُ ثَوَاباً مِّن عِندِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عِندَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّوَابِ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٩٥].

The Truth (al-Ḥaqq, may He be exalted) did not say "I have responded to you." Instead, He made the response the acceptance of the work, saying: ﴿I will not allow the work of any worker among you, male or female, to be lost﴾. The matter is not a narrative to be recited; rather, Allah wants these matters to enter the realm of practice and concrete action. The matter is not by wishing alone. He, glory be to Him, set a clear condition, which is work, so whoever seeks the response of the Truth must act. Reflecting on the wondrous creation of Allah does not replace action, because the Truth wants you to reflect on it while you work within its causes. The causes of the Truth do not distract you from Him. ﴿So their Lord responded to them: "Indeed, I will not allow the work of any worker among you, male or female, to be lost; you are of one another. So those who emigrated, were expelled from their homes, were harmed in My cause, fought, and were killed, I will surely remove their misdeeds from them and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the best reward."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 195].

فالذين هاجروا من بلادهم ومن أهلهم ومن أوطانهم ومن أحبابهم، دون إكراه فهجرتهم هذه هي نزع وجودي، وانتقال من مكان إلى مكان جديد وكان ذلك في سبيل الله أي، فالذين هاجروا وخرجوا بجزء من إرادتهم، وكذلك الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم، وقاتلوا في سبيل الله وتحملوا الإيذاء وقُتلوا - هؤلاء - ينالون التكفير عن السيئات ويدخلون الجنة.

Those who emigrated from their lands, their families, their homelands, and their loved ones, without compulsion, their emigration is an existential uprooting and a move from one place to a new place, and it was in the way of Allah. That is, those who emigrated and went out with part of their will, and likewise those who were expelled from their homes, and those who fought in the way of Allah, endured harm, and were killed — these attain the expiation of their misdeeds and enter Paradise.

لقد جاء الحق هنا بالعملية التي تتضح فيها الأسوة الإيمانية ؛ لأن الإنسان ينشغل بماله وأهله ووطنه وباستبقاء الحياة، فإذا ما ضحى الإنسان بهذا كله في سبيل الثبات على كلمة الله أولا، وإعلاء كلمة الله ونشرها ثانيا. فالمؤمن من هؤلاء لم يكتف بنفسه بل جاهد في سبيل الله لتنتقل الحياة بحلاوتها إلى غيره، وبذلك يكون قد أحب لغيره ما أحبه لنفسه.

Here the Truth has brought the practice in which the exemplary faith becomes manifest, because a person is preoccupied with his wealth, his family, his homeland, and preserving his life. When a person sacrifices all of this, first for steadfastness upon the word of Allah, and second for raising the word of Allah and spreading it, then the believer of this kind does not suffice with himself but strives in the way of Allah so that the sweetness of life passes to others. Thereby he has loved for others what he loves for himself.

نخرج من كل هذا برؤية واضحة هي أن الفكر وحده لا يكفي وإذا قال واحد : إن إيماني حسن فلا تأخذني بالمسائل الشكلية، نرد عليه قائلين : إن الله ليس في حاجة إلى ذلك، ولكنه يطلب منك أن تعمر الكون بحركتك، وأبرك الحركات وأفضلها أن ترسخ منهج الله في الأرض ؛ لأنك إن رسخت منهج الله في الأرض، أدمت للوجود جماله.

From all of this we draw a clear insight: thought alone is not enough. If someone says, "My faith is sound, so do not hold me to formal matters," we reply: Allah has no need of that, but He asks you to make the universe flourish through your movement. The most blessed and virtuous of movements is that you establish the method of Allah on earth, for if you establish the method of Allah on earth, you perpetuate beauty for existence.

And after that, the Truth says: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you﴾.

When we hear the phrase ﴿the movement of those who disbelieve through the land﴾, know that movement requires the ability to move. That ability exists within a person's own place and homeland. When your capacity for movement expands and you travel to another country, people then say of such a person, "His activity is wide-ranging," meaning that the environment in which he lives is not equal to his capacity; rather, his capacity is greater than his environment, and so he leaves his homeland. This used to happen. The disbelievers of Quraysh would travel from their homeland on journeys beyond it. Therefore the Truth said:

﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you﴾ [Al-Imran: 196].

As we have understood, movement arises from: capacity, motion, and the expansion of ambition. He, glorified is He, wants to show us that the adornments of life may come to those who are not believers. Every adornment is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and it is tied to the human lifespan in existence. Whatever they take, they have taken only the adornment of life and its deception. He, glorified is He, is the one who said:

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [Al-Imran: 185].

It is a life that has an end. As for the one who wants to increase the blessing and increase the benefit, he does the deed for the sake of a life that does not end. The disbelievers may take the hasty, finite life, but the believers take the deferred life that does not end.

When we compare the seeker of this world with the seeker of the Hereafter, we see that the transaction deserves to be examined from its aspects, which are as follows: Do not measure the age of the world in relation to itself, but measure its age in relation to the lifespan of the individual, because the age of the world for each person is the duration of his stay in it. Suppose the world lasts for others; what is it to me? The age of the world is short in relation to a person's stay in it. Beware of comparing it by saying, "The world will remain for millions of years," because it will remain for millions of years for millions of creatures other than you. The age of the world for you is your age in it, and your age in it is limited, and this is on the assumption that a person lives the average lifespan. How much more so when your age in it is uncertain, because death comes without warning and is not tied to a cause or a time. Therefore a person cannot guarantee the average lifespan. The age of the Hereafter is certain, and it is eternal.

So the human lifespan in this world is uncertain, his lifespan in the Hereafter is certain, the world is limited, and in the Hereafter there is eternity. Your bliss in this world depends on your capacity to conceive of blessing and its possibilities, but your bliss in the Hereafter is according to the greatness of your Lord and His abundant bounty. Therefore the Truth said about it that it is the enjoyment of delusion. He did not give it a name less than the name "the world." Is there a name that is lesser and more contemptible than this? Those who are deceived by what is gained by those who step outside Allah's method through their movement in the lands must remember that all of that is heading toward disappearance and loss. We must compare the movement in the lands with what Allah has prepared for us in the Hereafter. When you make this comparison, the comparison is sound.

Therefore the Truth continues His words about the movement of those who disbelieve in the lands:

﴿A brief enjoyment; then their refuge is...﴾

﴿A brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.﴾

The mihad (resting place) is the place where a child sleeps. The meaning is that al-Haqq (the Truth, God) turns them over in Hell as He wills, because they have no power over anything. Their situation in this is like that of a child, who remains clinging to his bed and cradle until someone else turns and moves him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 3, verse 198:

Opposite these are the believers, and so He says:

﴿But those who have feared their Lord, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, as a provision (nuzul) from Allah. And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous.﴾

The nuzul (provision, lodging prepared for a guest) is the place prepared for the arrival of a guest. Nuzul, when it is provided by human capabilities, varies according to what people are able to afford. On one journey we stayed in a luxurious hotel, and my colleagues and brothers said to me: "This is a kind of human magnificence!"

I said to them: "This is what humans have prepared for humans, so how much more so is what Allah has prepared for the believers?"

And when you see the disbelievers moving freely about the lands, know that they cannot feel secure that Allah will seize them in their movements. About this He says:

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah came upon you suddenly or openly, would any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ [al-An'am: 47].

He - glorified is He - also says:

﴿Or He seizes them in their going back and forth, and they cannot escape.﴾ [al-An'am: 46].

The disbeliever among these is seized by arrogance, and while he moves about, the punishment of Allah comes upon him suddenly. The punishment comes sometimes suddenly (baghtah), and sometimes openly (jahrah). It comes suddenly so that a person is always expecting it at any moment, and it comes openly so that it terrifies and frightens a person before it occurs. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿"We will never believe you until we see Allah openly (jahrah)," so the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55].

So death, if it comes to them suddenly, they may not feel its horror except at the moment it occurs; but when death comes to them while they are looking on, they see it in terror and dread.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 3, verse 199:

And the Truthful (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God...﴾.

Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, records faith with a truthful and trustworthy account. The Qur'an does not deal unfairly with the People of the Book because they opposed the Messenger of God, confronted his call, and did with him everything that could thwart the call and bring it to an end.

Rather, the Qur'an says, speaking fairly on behalf of some of them: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God﴾. This, as we have said, is called "preserving the possibility" (ṣiyanat al-iḥtimāl). When al-Haqq says: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God﴾, at the moment this speech is revealed, some of the People of the Book hear it, those who in their inner selves have been occupied with confirming the Messenger and who put the question of faith before their own souls. If they are in this state, what will their position be, they who are thinking about faith in what Muhammad has brought? At that point they say to themselves: "This is a matter within our depths; who has informed Muhammad of it? That is evidence that Muhammad does not speak from his own desire, and that God knows him what is in our souls, which has not come forth into existence. And since al-Haqq informs him of what has not come out into existence, he must be truthful." Had the verse been revealed after they had believed, it would not have had this effect.

Therefore, this statement must be a good tiding that many of the People of the Book are thinking about confirming the Messenger of God in the message from God, and are on the verge of believing. God's saying that makes the process of faith in their souls confirmed, for they say: the Messenger who says this is a reporter from a God who knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed...﴾.

This verse is the conclusion of Surat Al-Imran. Surat Al-Imran came after Surat Al-Baqarah. The two surahs share a first doctrinal matter, which is faith in Allah and belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what he brought from Allah as the seal of the messages and as the one who watches over them (muhaymin). Therefore Allah spoke of the matter of faith, the matter of guidance and the matter of the Book. Then He addressed the remnants of earlier religions that had turned away from the way of Allah toward the desires of men: in Surat Al-Baqarah He disputed with the Jews, and in Surat Al-Imran He disputed with the Christians.

After that He presented a matter of faith concerning the stance of the believing Muslims, who trust in Allah and affirm His Messenger, in the struggle of life, and He presented one of the battles in which the believers were severely tested. Then He addressed the matter of faith when the faltering believer returns to the way of his Lord. After He finishes with these, Allah says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: you who have believed in what has preceded, believing in Allah, affirming His Book, affirming His Messenger (ﷺ), and testing the truth with the Jews and testing the truth with the People of the Book altogether, a testing not merely theoretical argument but practical, in one of the most important battles of Islam, which is the Battle of Uhud. So, O you who have believed in Allah with a sincere and pure faith, listen to me, O you who have believed in me: ﴿Be patient﴾ (isbiru). This is one command. ﴿And endure﴾ (wa sabiru) is a second command. ﴿And be stationed at the frontier﴾ (warabitu) is a third command. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ (wattaqu Allah) is a fourth command.

These are four commands, and the purpose of these commands is ﴿that you may succeed﴾. So whoever loves success must carry out these four: be patient, endure, be stationed at the frontier, fear Allah, that you may succeed.

When Allah, glory be to Him, expresses success, He expresses it through something visible and perceptible to all people. He did not say to you: do that so that you may pass or win. Rather He used the word "al-falah" (success). As we have said, "al-falah" is derived from "falaha al-ard" (he tilled the land). Tilling the land is splitting it so that it is exposed to air and becomes soft and easy under the simple shoot that emerges from the seed. When the land is tilled with this hardship, through plowing, sowing and tending its irrigation, what happens to you from the land? It gives you visible, noticeable material good.

So Allah has struck the example for immaterial matters with a visible matter that all people experience. And what is this success that Allah, glory be to Him, intends? It is the success of this world and the success of the Hereafter: the success of this world is that you defeat your enemies and live a secure, stable, comfortable life; the success of the Hereafter is that you take your share of eternal immortality in lasting bliss. And since He, glory be to Him, says "be patient," this must be an indication that there is hardship in it. Faith leads to Paradise, and Paradise is surrounded by hardships; therefore there must be hardships in it.

If you look at these hardships, you find them sometimes within the self, separate from society, and sometimes within the self together with society. As for within the self, separate from society, patience requires that you be patient in carrying out Allah's command in performing acts of obedience, and in bearing the pain of abstaining from sins, even if that prevents you from the pleasure of a desire you love; you are patient against that desire which presses upon you. The believer's striving is to be patient against the desires which Allah has forbidden, and patient over things that befall a person: a calamity in the self is endured with patience, and what one is patient against among the prohibitions are the desires and pleasures which Allah has forbidden.

It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, says: I created you and I know that your self inclines toward desire because you love it, so be patient against it. And the matters of obedience, if you do them, will bring you hardship in your being; be patient over them. So in commands there is patience in carrying them out, and in prohibitions there is patience in refraining from committing them. All of this concerns the self. Then, if the matter goes beyond the personal to the external environment, Allah says:

﴿And the patient in adversity and hardship and at the time of violence; those are the ones who have been true, and those are the righteous﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 177].

He says "patient in" (sabirin fi). So we have "patient upon" (sabara ala), "patient against/from" (sabara an), and "patient in" (sabara fi). "The patient in adversity" is the adversity that falls upon them from the society outside them. How does adversity befall them from the society outside them? Yes, because the way of the truth comes to correct the error in the movement of society. And the error in the movement of society is a source of benefit to some people, who strive eagerly to prevent those who want to establish the way of Allah. So they do not fall short in harming them, mocking them, wearying them and fighting them. This is patience in adversity, hardship and at the time of violence. And if your enemy, whom you came to refute with your true way against his false way, is patient with you and also patient in harming you, then you must be patient with him.

What does that mean? It means that "isbir" (be patient) differs from "sabir" (endure/be patient with another). Isbir is a command concerning yourself, which you will endure. But suppose your opponent also endures your harm and has the stamina to stand before you here.

Allah commands you here to endure him, meaning: if your enemy endures a little, then you must be able to endure against him, that is, bring a patience above the patience that opposes you. And every form of the pattern "fa'ala" is like this.

An example: when you say, "So-and-so competed with so-and-so" (nafasa). Competition (munafasa) happens between two who need and aim at a goal, and each wants to reach it, and the one who wants to reach it wants to reach it eagerly. If your opponent strives for it with one step, you strive for it with two steps; this is competition. Competition is a contest for victory. And Allah says:

﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 26]. Its root is: prolonging one's breath when a person dives under water. Our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to al-'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): "Are you competing with me?" meaning: he proposed that the two of them go down together under water and see which of them has the longer breath.

So the shrewd and intelligent person is one who trains himself in this practice and does not go down into the water with a hesitant spirit, but takes in an amount of air with an inhalation that fills his whole chest, so that he has a reserve by which he can remain under water longer than the second. As for one who dives without this reserve, he will take only the amount of inhalation and exhalation. "Fanafisni" (compete with me) means that we dive into the water together to see which of us has the longer breath. That is, he is able to keep a quantity of air that can perform the function of his life for a long time, and this cannot be achieved except by taking an inhalation that fills the chest so that you cannot increase it. Therefore, when a doctor wants to examine the condition of the lungs, he tells the patient: take a long breath, because he wants to see the patient and his capacity.

So "mosabara" (mutual endurance) means: if your opponent endures against you, then you endure and he endures, so you endure more. For this reason the matter requires that the whole society unite in endurance. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said:

﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [Al-'Asr: 1-3].

That is, if you see a brother among your believing brothers weakening and faltering in his endurance, you encourage him to endure and say: beware of faltering. Why? Because the human self is subject to changes, and an event may come upon it that overpowers it. The believer who does not have these changes breathes resolve into the one who falters. Therefore Allah said "tawasaw" (advised one another), and did not say: a group advising a group. No. "At-tawasi" means that you are at one time one who advises, and at another time one who is advised. When you do not have the weakness of changes, advise; when you have the weakness of changes, be advised. Each one advises at one time and is advised at another time, and we do not advise one another to patience in this way unless we had first advised one another to the truth for which the battle arose between one enduring and another enduring.

"O you who have believed, be patient, endure, be stationed at the frontier, and fear Allah, that you may succeed." We have understood patience and we have understood endurance. So what is ribat (being stationed at the frontier)? It is that you make your enemy feel that you are always ready to meet him. This is the meaning of ribat. Allah says:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of force and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ [Al-Anfal: 60].

These are horses kept tethered for jihad in the way of Allah, ready. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of you is one who holds the reins of his horse, whenever he hears a cry he flies to it."

That is, we should be prepared before the attack occurs, and when pressing matters come, we set out to face them. But our preparation must come before the pressing matter. Therefore, when your enemy knows that you are stationed against him and ready to move at any time, he fears and dreads you; but if you are relaxed and heedless, he will ambush you, and before you prepare he will have taken the first round from you. So what is the benefit of ribat?

The benefit of ribat is that it is known you have not been heedless of your enemy and that you will not abandon equipment and readiness against him until he comes with a surprise attack; rather you are ready for it at all times. And ribat is not only that you station horses against an enemy attacking physically; rather, mura bata means preparation for everything that could turn back the outcry of falsehood from the truth. Among ribat is that you prepare Islamic youth against the incursions of atheism before they arrive. Why?

Because the matter is not entirely an invasion with horses, weapons and equipment; the invasion may be by thought that seeps into souls without their noticing. Therefore there must also be a ribat that provides the believer with the power and capacity of confrontation, so that when a matter of atheism comes which may arrive among believers, each one of them has immunity against it and the ability to confront it.

We have said: the affliction of the scientific methods is that they took their methods from the West. They studied history as the West studies it, and studied nature as the West studies it, and forgot that we have a religion that protects us from all these things. When a man of history comes to me with his method from the West and says: the French Revolution is what proclaimed human rights, here we must have immunity and ribat, and we say to him: in what year did the French Revolution arise?

It arose some years ago, perhaps more or less than two hundred years, and you are ignorant that the Islamic religion came fourteen centuries ago with human rights, and read the Qur'an. So if every pupil, when he hears that the French Revolution proclaimed human rights, says to them: No, you know that this happened in the seventeenth century; but why do you not notice that fourteen centuries ago Islam came with this principle, and notice the misuse of right? If you are ignorant of Allah's legislation, this ignorance should not lead you to obliterate the landmarks of truth in the way of Allah.

And if a student of nature says: nature supplied the particular animal with the color that suits the environment in which it lives so that its enemy does not devour it, and in doing so he misleads, we say to him: nature does not supply; nature is supplied by Allah. Do not say: nature supplied. So ribat is not only by military strength but also by scientific strength. The enemies of Islam have despaired of defeating Islam by military force after they concentrated all their strength in the Crusades, and nothing remained for them except to enter upon us through their methods and through the orientalists there and the Westernized among us, so they transmit to us foreign cultures far from our method; and they are excused, because they do not know the method of Allah in the religion of Allah.
